author: rlronan
body:
Frozen-contract-change: spec/design/runtime_extents.md

Part of #1277. Addresses #3347 and #2644 (design only; no behavior change).

## Problem

spec/04 §4.7.2 and [04-ADT-4] require a runtime check whenever a declared literal or named extent meets a computed one, including a dimension supplied by a nominal type argument. Every claim source in the implementation derives obligations only from a top-level tensor type: the entry contract's `EntryPattern` (`Tensor`/`List`/`Other`), the host and Eval result-claim plans, and `LocalAscriptionClaim`. The exported-C aggregate walk (#2506) reads the host ABI type, which has no representation for ADT dimension arguments. A tensor reached through a tuple, `Option`, `List`, record or constructor field therefore carries no obligation. On Eval at 0.19.1, all of the following check clean and return 5 elements under a 3-element claim: `-> Box[3]` built from `insert(.., 5)`, generic `make[n] -> Box[n]` called under `Box[3]`, local `b: Box[3]`, formal `width(b: Box[3])`, a recursive `Pair[3]`, a named `Box[k]`, and `(tensor[3], i64)`, `List[tensor[3]]`, `Option[tensor[3]]` and record results. The bare-tensor equivalents trap.

## Change

`spec/design/runtime_extents.md` gains C6.5. It derives one claim pattern from each authored claim type by a total structural walk (tensor, tuple, List, and every nominal application with its type and dimension arguments substituted into its constructor fields). The pattern is memoized per (type, argument tuple), so recursive types are finite. Placement reuses the existing rules: entry obligations go through the #1788 contract, and result and ascription obligations are producer-owned through the #1771 origin transport, with a boundary observation when the activation has no producer. Both lanes migrate their consumers to the shared pattern together. The section adds an exit matrix for #3347 and #2644, a Part II owner row, and a pointer from the #2751 receipts' "general aggregate result guards" disclaimer.

## Evidence

- Reviewed head: `6c6a0ac825261656583733e8ef13f04d0f2bec31`
- Docs-only; `dtype_phase4b_oracle.py`'s required `runtime_extents.md` substring is untouched.
- Red-team round 1 (fresh local reviewer, head `f49c9f047`): P1 exit-matrix outcome contradicted spec/04 §4.7 lowered-graph rejection (class: required outcome contradicts spec rule); P2 pattern finiteness claimed for all recursion (class: unbounded claim); P3 absent-variant-only binders; P3 unobservable ordering. Repaired at `9221de11a`, verified closed by the same reviewer; its new P3 (recursion definitions leave a gap) folded at `6c6a0ac82` and verified closed. Round closed, no open findings. Compiled C was not probed; Eval only.

## Summary
- Adds a new **Environmental Control Systems** module and a **Cabin Pressurisation System** lesson, registered in `catalogue.js`.
- Files are in `items/environmental-control/cabin-pressurisation/`: `cabin-pressurisation.html`, `.css`, `.js`, plus an `index.html` redirect because the portal links every item to `index.html`.
- Vanilla HTML, CSS and JS only. Works from `file://` and on GitHub Pages, with relative paths and no external requests.

## What it contains
Five tabs, one section visible at a time:
1. **Overview**: plain-English introduction and a summary box of the five key components.
2. **Air Circulation Explorer**: labelled SVG with animated blue (pressurised) and grey (return/exhaust) flow, and a click-for-details pop-up for each of the seven components.
3. **Pressure Simulation**: altitude and outflow valve sliders, live cabin altitude and differential pressure, a green/amber/red status bar and an explanation sentence.
4. **Fault Scenarios**: three cards with instrument readings, three options each, feedback and a Maintenance Action note.
5. **Competency Check**: five questions, pass mark 4/5, Try Again. Results are saved through `tracker.js` (on the device only), guarded with `if (window.Tracker)`.

## Decisions to review
- The outflow valve counts as in its normal range when it is at least 50% closed. Further open than that, cabin altitude rises toward aircraft altitude.
- Differential pressure is capped at 8.6 PSI as specified, so green means cabin altitude no higher than 8,000 ft and differential pressure not over 8.6 PSI.
- The back button goes to the home page module list, not the module page.
- The quiz shows instant feedback after each answer, like the other portal quizzes.

## Testing
Checked in headless Chromium at 1200px and 360px wide: all sections work, no console errors, no horizontal scroll. Not yet checked in a real browser or on GitHub Pages.

author: leelu74
body:
## What this adds

Some sites have workers who do not own smartphones, so they cannot clock in with the ERP app. This lets an admin nominate a supervisor for such a site. That supervisor uses a new, separate attendance-only Android app to photograph each worker; the backend recognises the face and clocks the worker in or out.

This is an additional feature. The existing ERP app, the existing web attendance screens and the existing `/api/attendance/*` endpoints are unchanged.

## How it works

- **Admin (web)**: new page **Workforce → Physical Attendance** (admin and master only). Pick a supervisor and a site, then enable. The site can be changed or removed at any time. "Add supervisor" creates a supervisor account and assigns the site in one step.
- **One site per supervisor.** A supervisor is enabled exactly when a site is assigned, so it cannot be enabled without one.
- **Location only.** The server rejects a scan unless the supervisor's phone is inside the site's radius (plus the existing 25 m GPS buffer). A scan with no GPS position is rejected.
- **Face match only.** Workers must have a face registered on their employee record.
- **App "ERP Attendance"** (`com.econetvision.erp.attendance`, installs alongside the main app): sign in, **Scan worker** (rear camera, blink liveness check), and **On site today** (who was marked at the site, with in and out times).
- First scan of the day clocks in, the second clocks out, a third is refused. A second scan within 5 minutes of clock-in is refused as an accidental re-scan.
- A supervisor who is demoted or moved to another company loses the site automatically. The app refuses mock (fake) GPS locations.
- Records are ordinary `attendance` rows, so they appear in existing reports and payslips. They also store the site and the supervisor who scanned.

## Changes

- **Database** (migration `0032_physical_attendance`, mirrored in `db/init.sql`): `users.physical_attendance_site_id`, `attendance.site_location_id`, `attendance.marked_by`. All nullable; existing rows are unaffected. The migration runs on deploy.
- **Backend**: new router `/api/physical-attendance`, service `physical_attendance_service.py`, guard `require_physical_attendance`. Login and `/api/auth/me` responses gain `physical_attendance_site_id`.
- **Existing backend code touched**: the `User.attendance` / `Attendance.employee` relationship now names its foreign key (needed because `attendance` gained a second link to `users`); no behaviour change.
- **Frontend**: new page, route and sidebar item.
- **Mobile**: new module `mobile/attendance`. No file under `mobile/app` is changed; `mobile/settings.gradle.kts` registers the module.
- **CI**: new workflow `build-attendance-apk.yml` builds the APK on this PR and uploads it as an artifact. It also builds the main app to confirm the new module does not break it. Existing workflows are not edited.

## Things to know before merging

- An independent review of the branch found no critical defects; its four important findings are fixed or listed here. Location is still reported by the phone, as in the existing face scan, so a modified app could forge it.
- `PUT /api/auth/users/{id}` (existing endpoint) now also clears the site when a user's role or company changes.

- A new supervisor must sign in once on the web portal to set their own password before the app accepts them. This is the existing first-login rule.
- After merge, the existing "Build Dev APK" workflow runs `assembleDebug` for the whole Gradle project, so it will build both modules.
- The APK is debug-signed, like the current dev APK. It is not a Play Store release build.

## Testing

- Backend: 106 tests pass (`python -m pytest tests -q`), 72 of them new. They cover the rules, the guard, request validation, and the assign / scan / today-list flows on an in-memory SQLite database with only face matching stubbed.
- Frontend: `npm run build` compiles with no warnings. There is no frontend test framework in this repo.
- Android: unit tests and both APK builds run in this PR's CI.
- **Not tested**: the migration against a real PostgreSQL database (Docker was not available on the dev machine), and anything on a real phone.

## Manual test on a phone (before merge)

- [ ] Admin: Workforce → Physical Attendance → enable a supervisor with a site
- [ ] Supervisor signs in once on the web portal and sets a password
- [ ] App: sign in; site name shows in the header
- [ ] App: scan a worker with a registered face at the site → "Clocked in"
- [ ] App: scan the same worker again after 5 minutes → "Clocked out"; a third scan is refused
- [ ] App: scan away from the site → "You are N m from <site>…"
- [ ] App: scan a person with no registered face → "No matching employee found…"
- [ ] Admin disables the supervisor → app signs out on next refresh
- [ ] Main ERP app still installs and its face scan still works

Design: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-09-physical-attendance-app-design.md`
Plan: `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-10-09-physical-attendance-app.md`

body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"dihoyt"} -->
_Requested by **Daniel** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_014VPbDqzYvt1cxNyhZfrqoX?thread=cmsg_014VPbDqzYvt1cxNyhZfrqoX19ZqEYwG5f9Jzgs1ULxe1m)_

Before: every install is set up by clicking through the console after it comes up.

After: `install.sh --env <file>` (or `/etc/<slug>/install.env` when it exists) checks the file, stores it as the `install-seed` Secret for the console to apply on first boot, and shreds the file once the install succeeds. `--keep-env` keeps it. With `ADMIN_PASSWORD` in the file, no generated password is printed. The console side that applies the Secret is F11, the next PR.

How:
- `read_env_file` runs before the installer looks for a cluster. It accepts blank lines, comments, `export KEY=value` and quoted values. It stops on an unknown key, a key set twice, a line that isn't `KEY=value` or an `ADMIN_PASSWORD` under 10 characters, naming the line and key and never the value. It warns when the file can be read by other users.
- The allow list `SEED_KEYS` mirrors `INSTALL_SEED_KEYS` from #129; `test/install/seedKeys.test.ts` keeps them identical in install.sh and update.sh.
- Values go base64 into a 0600 manifest, then `kubectl apply`. They never go on a command line or into the output.
- `shred -u` removes the file, or where `shred` is missing it is overwritten with zeros and then `rm`'d. Both run with sudo when the file is root's.
- `--env` is refused on a cluster that already has the release, unless the `install-seed` Secret is still there (an earlier `--env` install that never finished). update.sh refuses `--env` and `--keep-env`. update.sh is regenerated with `gen-scripts.sh`.
- Docs: a new section "Unattended setup from an env file" in `docs/install.md` with every key, plus a pointer in `scripts/install/README.md`.
- CI (install-test): the lint job checks that an unknown key stops the installer with the key named and the value not printed, and that update.sh refuses `--env`. The kind job purges, reinstalls with `--env`, and checks the Secret was stored, the file was shredded and no password was printed.

Local checks: shellcheck and `gen-scripts.sh --check` are clean. The parser was run under dash and bash against good, unknown-key, duplicate, malformed and short-password files. Lint, typecheck and `seedKeys.test.ts` (3/3) pass.

author: mattadurham
body:
## Problem

A live session that launched background subagents could hang for good, and nothing on screen said so.

The runner read the Claude CLI's stream only between its own query and the next result. When the main agent ended its turn "waiting on the agents", the runner parked and stopped reading. The agents kept producing messages into the Agent SDK's 100-message buffer until it filled. Then the SDK's reader blocked, the CLI's permission requests went unread, and the session froze mid-call. Meanwhile the status bar read "complete - nothing pending". Every agent's lines had also been blended into the main agent's output with nothing saying who was talking.

Separately, sessions ran the SDK's bundled CLI (2.1.206). That build resolves the `opus` alias to an older model than the installed CLI does, so sessions ran a generation behind one-shot calls on the same machine. The status bar was reporting that accurately.

## What changed

- **Runner**: one pump reads every message for the whole session. A turn the CLI starts by itself (an agent reporting back) is handled as a real turn. A turn that ends with background work still running holds as `agents` (working): no landing card, not marked finished, and the reply box stays live. This also applies to machine-dispatched runs, so their output comes from the turn after the last report. If the report turn never arrives, the boundary is decided again after a short grace period. Stop also stops background agents.
- **Agent tracking**: each subagent is recorded in `state.agents` (label, type, status, tool calls, current step, report). Resumed agents (same task id started again) reopen. Agent lines are written in their own lane and never reach the main answer stream.
- **CLI**: sessions run the installed Claude CLI (`models.find_binary`). If none is found they fall back to the SDK's bundled copy.
- **Timers off**: `ScheduleWakeup` and `CronCreate` are disabled in sessions, because the session state has no way to show a timer waiting to fire.
- **Terminal UI**: agent lanes in the feed, coloured by launch order. An agents strip above the reply box shows each agent's progress and expands to its full report. The status line now reads "working - N agents running".
- **Instructions**: the Claude session preamble explains how agents report back. The map prompts no longer contradict branch placement, wait for subagents before saving, list slugs already in use, and say how a refresh should close.

## Verification

- New `tests/test_runner_agents.py` drives the real `run_session` loop against a scripted CLI stream using the message shapes the CLI emits. The two regression tests fail when the old stop-reading-at-the-boundary behaviour is put back.
- New `tests/session_agents_ui.js` runs the shipped lane and strip code in a VM.
- Full suite: 4858 tests, OK.
- End to end on a test instance with the real CLI: three background agents, including agents that resumed after backgrounding their own shells. Checked at desktop width and at 402px.

## Restart

This changes `server/` (`session.py` snapshot field). Runner changes take effect for new sessions without a restart. The `agents` field in `/api/jobs/{id}` needs a server restart.

After: `db/pxr_ctoken_ledger/001_tables.sql` を追加します。スキーマ `pxr_ctoken_ledger` と、5 表（ctoken、ctoken_history、cmatrix、row_hash、document）を作ります。

How:
- 出どころは MIT 表記の pxr-ctoken-ledger-service の TypeORM エンティティ 5 つだけです（Copyright 2022 NEC Corporation、NOTICE に表示済み）。ライセンスのないリポジトリの内容は、コピーも参照もしていません。
- 旧実装は `synchronize: false` で DDL を持たないため、エンティティの定義から起こしました。TypeORM の既定（nullable 指定なし = NOT NULL）に従います。列名が数字で始まるものは二重引用符で囲みました。
- 外部キー制約は、他の単位と同じく起こしていません（エンティティの OneToMany / ManyToOne のみ）。
- ローカルの PostgreSQL 16 に 2 回適用して、エラーなく通ること（冪等）と、列数を確かめました。

満たしていない終了条件（Issue #9）:

body:
## Sprint 9 — Offensive adjustment and Custom Adjustment triggering

Stacked draft on **PR #32** `madden-ml/full-book-inventory` (confirmed full-playbook ML). No automatic merge or changes to laptop/database.

### Goal
The trained model remains the primary **play** caller. The pre-snap action policy then chooses one **sourced, compatible action or NO ADJUSTMENT** based on the selected play, situation, credible coverage evidence, research and manually approved/armed macro state. Research-prior action scores are not fabricated learned uplift.

### Changes
- Make no action a first-class scored candidate. Uncertain, generic or unsupported actions are suppressed rather than always selecting an available option.
- Live/repeated credible coverage can trigger researched pass protection/hot routes or compatible coverage macros. A prior single-snap coverage observation never fires these on its own.
- Red-zone/goal-line/third- or fourth-and-short **situation** macros may fire without falsely inventing a coverage look, but cannot auto-trigger on every generic open-field snap.
- Verify settings, compatible exact formation/play, researched controller sequence, protected/cooldown state, selected active loadout and any explicit model-created macro attestation. Suppress unverified controls; no fabricated route assignment.
- Remove 80-play macro compatibility truncation, so relevant macros can apply to plays late in the complete installed inventory.
- Add `ml offense-actions -o cpu` read-only readiness report with current selected macro slots, compatibility, researched editor gaps, verified generated macros and unverified drafts; link it from the Madden-style designer browser.
- Existing live UI remains *Formation — Play* with actions in collapsed details, plus explicit applied/not-applied outcome logging.

### Evidence and limitations
The 28–7 CPU game produced zero recommended offensive actions. This PR improves controlled opportunities and observability, not causal action-value estimation. A prep-selected macro is not necessarily installed in Madden; the readiness report distinguishes that from explicitly verified model-generated macros. Actual action-specific learned value will require verified application/outcome records.

### Tests
`test_sprint9_situational_actions.py` and `test_sprint9_action_readiness.py`: no-look, no action, last-snap suppression, live blitz protection, researched controller safety, red-zone macro, open-field macro suppression, >80 plays, installed-book check, verified/draft macro diagnostic. Full suite CI enabled for branch.

Do not deploy for games until both CI checks pass. Stacked on #32; merge parents before children.

author: leet-c1
body:
## Why

Without a usable OS keyring, c1i caches one access-token file per set of credentials under `<UserConfigDir>/c1i/tokens/`. The file is named by a hash of host, client id and secret. When credentials are replaced or removed, their token file stays on disk forever. #150 stopped leftovers piling up in `~/.c1i/cache/`. This PR applies the same idea to the token cache, and documents what an uninstall leaves behind.

A `c1i clean` command was ruled out. go-keyring can't enumerate keyring entries and c1i keeps no list of tenants, so such a command couldn't truthfully claim to remove everything.

## What

**Token file sweep** (`internal/tokensource/cache.go`): after a token file is renamed into place, `pruneTokenDir` deletes the other files in `tokens/` that no load would serve.

- **What counts as unservable:** a token that has expired or expires within the 60s skew, and a file that is corrupt, unreadable, group/other-accessible, or over the 64 KiB bound. A corrupt file is deleted rather than kept, because no load can use it. The worst a transient read error costs is one re-mint.
- **Temp files:** `.tmp-` files older than one minute are deleted. Younger ones are kept, so a concurrent write isn't broken.
- **Only c1i's own files:** the sweep removes only regular files named exactly as this package names them: a lowercase 64-hex key plus `.json`, or the matching `.<key>.json.tmp-*`. A user's `backup.json`, an uppercase-hex name, a directory or a symlink is never touched.
- **Trust checks kept:** `trustedCacheDir` on `tokens/` and its `c1i` parent, plus `Lstat`. The read path is now shared with `loadFileCachedToken` through `readCachedTokenFile`. The sweep only reads `tokens/` and never `credentials/`.
- **Keyring tokens aren't swept:** they can't be enumerated, so they're only ever overwritten. A code comment says so.

**README "Uninstalling"** lists what c1i leaves behind:
- `~/.c1i/`
- `~/.c1i.yaml`
- `<UserConfigDir>/c1i/` (credentials and tokens)
- keyring entries under `c1i/<host>`, the legacy `c1i/<name>`, and `com.conductorone.c1i.tokens`

It explains that `c1i auth logout --url <tenant>`, once per tenant before removing the binary and with `C1I_CLIENT_ID`/`C1I_CLIENT_SECRET` unset, is the only way c1i can remove keyring credentials. It gives the manual removal steps for macOS (`security delete-generic-password`), Linux (`secret-tool clear`) and Windows (Credential Manager). It also notes that `~/.sigstore/root/` is shared with other Sigstore tools. `cmd/agents.md` is unchanged, because agents don't uninstall c1i.

**CHANGELOG:** one entry. With main merged in, `[Unreleased]` also carries the entries for #148, #149 and #150. I checked each against its PR's diff.

## Verification

- **Tests:**
  - `TestStoreSweepsExpiredTokenFiles` drives the sweep through `storeCachedToken`. It checks that removed files are gone and that kept files survive.
    - **Removed:** expired, near-expiry, corrupt, loose-permission, oversized (valid JSON padded past 64 KiB) and stale-temp files.
    - **Kept:** fresh files, young temp files, an uppercase-hex name, a token-named directory, a token-named symlink with its target, and near-miss names that are expired and old (a short or truncated key, a temp name without its leading dot, its `.json.tmp-` marker or the marker's dash, and user files).
  - `TestStoreSweepKeepsTokenJustWritten`, `TestStoreSweepLeavesCredentialsDir`, and `TestTokenSweepSkipsSymlinkedDir`, which covers a symlinked `tokens/` and a symlinked `c1i/`.
- **Mutation testing:** with the sweep reverted to a no-op, the removal test fails.
  - An independent reviewer ran 48 mutants against the sweep. Every survivor was either equivalent or is now killed by a fixture added here.
  - I also mutated each guard myself, and each one turns a test red. The guards: the trust checks on the dir and its parent, keep-the-written-file, the temp grace period, the regular-file check, the name checks (key length, case, leading dot, marker, dash), the 64 KiB bound, and a sweep pointed at `credentials/`.
- **Live sweep:** a built binary ran against a lab tenant on Linux, using the file cache. Fixtures were seeded into the real `tokens/` dir, and one mint was forced by removing the current token file.
  - **Deleted:** the expired, corrupt, oversized, 0644 and stale-temp fixtures.
  - **Kept:** the fresh, uppercase-hex, symlink, directory, user-file and near-miss fixtures. The real token was rewritten.
  - **Untouched:** `credentials/` did not change. The fixtures were removed afterwards.
- **Linux keyring commands, tested live:** gnome-keyring on a private D-Bus session with a throwaway HOME. Entries were written through go-keyring v0.2.8 under c1i's service and account names. `secret-tool clear service …` removed both credential entries and both cached tokens, and an unrelated app's entry survived.
- **macOS and Windows steps, not run:** there's no Mac or Windows machine available. They come from go-keyring v0.2.8's source: its macOS `DeleteAll` loops the same `security delete-generic-password -s` call, and its Windows target names are `<service>:<account>`.
- **Gates (`GOTOOLCHAIN=go1.27.2`, at `d47fa8c`), all passing:**
  - `go build`, `go vet`, `go test`, `go test -count=1 -shuffle=on`
  - `golangci-lint`, `go mod tidy` diff, `gosec`, `gitleaks`
  - `govulncheck` for linux, darwin and windows: no vulnerabilities.
- **Dependency scan:** no outdated direct dependency, and every workflow action and `go install` pin is at its latest release.
- **Adversarial review:** independent reviewers covered six axes:
  - invariants and correctness
  - every claim checked against the c1i, go-keyring and sigstore-go source
  - test sensitivity
  - the live run
  - publication hygiene
  - each fix round

  Each fix round was re-reviewed and approved. No blocking findings remain.

## Known trade-offs

- **Race with a concurrent write:** if one process deletes a stale token file just as another renames a fresh token over it for the same credentials, the fresh token is lost. The same happens if a transient read error hits a fresh file. Either way the cost is one extra mint, which is one audit-log event.
- **Machines that gain a keyring:** the sweep runs only on a file-cache write. A machine that later gains a usable keyring stops writing token files, so files left from before are never swept. The Uninstalling section covers removing them.

author: aaronlippold
body:
## Summary

The deprecated `Hdf*` type aliases exported from `@mitre/hdf-schema` (`HdfResults`, `HdfBaseline`, `HdfComparison`, `HdfSystem`, `HdfPlan`, `HdfAmendments`, `HdfEvidencePackage`) have resolved to `any` for every consumer since 3.3.0.

`dist/index.d.ts` is generated by `hdf-schema/src/create-index.ts`. The template re-exports the combined types with `export * from './ts/hdf.js'` and then declares `export type HdfResults = HDFResults;`. `export *` re-exports names but does not bind them in the module's own scope, so each alias referenced an undefined identifier. Consumers compile with `skipLibCheck` (the workspace default), which turns that into a silent `any` instead of an error:

```ts
import type { HdfResults } from '@mitre/hdf-schema';
const x: HdfResults = 42; // compiled without error on 3.3.0–3.7.2
```

With lib checks on, `tsc --skipLibCheck false hdf-schema/dist/index.d.ts` reports `TS2552: Cannot find name 'HDFResults'` for all seven aliases, plus `TS2308` because `src/helpers.d.ts` declared a top-level `type Identity` that a `.d.ts` module implicitly exports, colliding with the schema's `Identity`.

Introduced in #77 (combined TypeScript output), first published in 3.3.0. No in-repo TypeScript uses the aliases, and `create-index.test.ts` only asserted that the alias text was present, so nothing exercised them.

## Changes

- `create-index.ts`: `import type { HDFResults, … } from './ts/hdf.js'` above the alias block, with a comment explaining why `export *` is not enough.
- `helpers.d.ts`: drop the top-level `Identity` type and inline the (intentionally looser, `type: string`) shape at its two `appliedBy` sites. The schema's `Identity` uses the `IdentityType` string enum; switching the helpers to it would reject the plain-string callers the helper tests use.
- `create-index.test.ts`: two regression tests — `dist/index.d.ts` must produce zero diagnostics with `skipLibCheck: false`, and a virtual probe assigning `42` to each deprecated alias must be rejected on every line.

## Audit of the other packages

Every package's emitted declaration entry (`dist/index.d.ts` for all 11 TS packages, plus `hdf-converters` `detect`/`registry`, `hdf-schema` `helpers` and `testhdf`) was type-checked with `skipLibCheck: false`. Before this change the only diagnostics anywhere were the eight in `hdf-schema/dist/index.d.ts` (the five packages that depend on it inherited them transitively); after it, zero across all fifteen entries.

## Verification

- `pnpm --filter @mitre/hdf-schema test`: 21 files, 1147 passed, 5 pre-existing skips; the two new tests fail on `main` and pass here
- `pnpm -r --filter=!hdf-cli run type-check`: all packages pass
- `pnpm lint`: clean
- hdf-schema coverage: 98.8% statements / 93.3% branches

author: adelagranados
body:
## What this changes

Adds `.gitattributes` declaring `* text=auto eol=lf`, plus explicit `binary` for assets.

## Why

`npm run format:check` failed on Windows for three files it passed on in CI — on the same commit. `core.autocrlf=true` writes CRLF into the working tree on checkout, while Prettier defaults to `endOfLine: "lf"`.

Git stores LF either way, so the repository content was never wrong and CI was never lying. But a check that reports differently depending on who runs it is a check people learn to ignore, and the gate was only introduced two PRs ago — worth fixing before anyone builds that habit.

Declaring it in `.gitattributes` rather than telling each developer to set a local git config is the point: it also works for a fresh clone by someone who has never configured git.

`*.svg` is kept as text because it is source, not an asset blob.

## How it was verified

`git add --renormalize .` staged nothing beyond the new file, confirming the stored content was already LF and only the checkout differed.

After re-checking-out the tree with the attributes applied:

```
before:  .github/workflows/ci.yml: ASCII text, with CRLF line terminators
after:   .github/workflows/ci.yml: ASCII text
```

All four checks now pass locally, which was not true before this change:

```
format:check  All matched files use Prettier code style!
lint          clean
typecheck     clean
test          25 passed
```

Closes #17

author: valleedgar085-rgb
body:
### 💡 What
Optimized `createMemoryMap` in `src/music-engine.js` by replacing linear array searches (`find`) inside `.map()` with a pre-computed lookup Map (`Map.prototype.get`).

### 🎯 Why
In `createMemoryMap`, `source?.memoryMap?.find(...)` was called inside `structure.map()`, causing $O(N \times M)$ linear searches when populating inherited section memory entries. Constructing an $O(M)$ lookup map prior to iterating over structure sections achieves $O(1)$ lookups per section item, improving scaling to $O(N + M)$.

### 📊 Measured Improvement
- For typical structure sizes (32 sections), `createMemoryMap` execution time dropped from 4,771 ns/op to 3,122 ns/op (**1.53x speedup**).
- For larger song structures (160 sections), execution time dropped from 96,193 ns/op to 18,411 ns/op (**5.22x speedup**).
- Full quality checks (`npm run quality`) passed with zero test regressions and all quality gates intact.

## Context and summary

Carry forward #341 on a repository-owned branch, preserving the original
commits, and fix expired-session recovery during project refresh. A method-local
Clippy allowance handles the redundant must-use annotation emitted by
async-trait under the CI compiler without changing authentication behavior.

## Affected areas

- [ ] Rust daemon/runtime
- [x] Server/API
- [ ] macOS app
- [ ] MCP, CLI, or agent protocol
- [x] Storage, configuration, or schema
- [x] Windows/Linux desktop client
- [ ] Documentation
- [x] CI, deployment, or release

## Behavior and evidence

Retain #341's Windows startup/browser fixes, foreground membership refresh,
and uncached project loading. A refresh returning 401 now saves pending
edits before showing sign-in and invalidates old project/checkout reads.
Failed preservation retains editors and retries on a subsequent refresh.
Network failures and HTTP 403/500 do not interrupt editing or end a session.

## Verification

- [x] Local fix verification: cargo fmt -p desktop --check and git diff --check passed.
- [x] Local cargo test --locked -p desktop: 48 passed, 2 existing Dev Instance tests ignored.
- [x] New regression checks cover save-before-reauthentication, failed preservation,
  and transient errors that must not interrupt editing.
- [x] cargo clippy --locked -p server --all-targets -- -D warnings passed locally.
- [x] RUSTDOCFLAGS="-D warnings" cargo doc --locked -p server --no-deps
  --document-private-items passed locally.

No API, schema, or stored-data migration. Existing daemon IPC is reused.
Legacy missing-token errors remain recognized. macOS is unchanged.

## Risk, security, and privacy

Flush edits under the old session before replacement credentials can reload
the workspace. Busy mutations or failed saves defer recovery and retain
editors. Credentials stay daemon-owned; OAuth state, PKCE, and server
authorization remain unchanged.

- Observability: Existing refresh/checkout/save logs and HTTP request IDs.
- Rollback: Revert these changes; no stored-data migration needs undoing.

Runtime 401 recovery, edit preservation, cold-checkout readiness, selection
and session invalidation, and delayed saves. Original contributor commits
from #341 are preserved.

author: dylan-conway
body:
### What does this PR do?

JavaScriptCore hashes strings and numbers the same way in every process. Keys that share their low hash bits therefore share them everywhere, and n of those cost O(n²) to put into an object, a `Map`, a `Set` or the table of interned strings.

`BUN_CONFIG_RANDOMIZE_HASHES=1` makes Bun pick new secrets for both hashes each time it starts (https://github.com/oven-sh/WebKit/pull/783). Without it the secrets, and so every hash, are the ones used so far. `main()` makes the choice before anything can hash.

32,768 16-character keys that share one hash under the default secrets, next to 32,768 that do not (macOS arm64, release):

| | ordinary | default | `BUN_CONFIG_RANDOMIZE_HASHES=1` |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `JSON.parse`, as object keys | 3 ms | 2471 ms | 3 ms |
| `JSON.parse`, as array values | 2 ms | 2047 ms | 2 ms |
| `new Set(strings)` | 1 ms | 1541 ms | 1 ms |
| `new Set(integers)`, 16k | 1 ms | 134 ms | 1 ms |
| `JSON.parse`, 16k index-like keys | 2 ms | 106 ms | 2 ms |

On this side:

- `bun build --compile` stores `StringImpl::stableHash()` (the same function, keyed with the default secrets) where it stored `StringImpl::hash()`: per module source and per import/export name of the prelinked module graph. By default the two are the same number and it is used as before. With the variable set, a module's source starts out without a hash.
- Bytecode is the same bytes however it was built, and loads either way.
- `mapKeyHash()` in `bun:internal-for-testing`.
- Three things came out in hash order, which differs from run to run once hashes are randomized. They come out in insertion order: the keys of a `Worker`'s `env` option, the keys of an env shared with a `Worker` (`SHARE_ENV`), and `performance` entries with the same start time.

### How did you verify your code works?

`test/js/bun/jsc/hash-secrets.test.ts`:

- by default a key hashes the same in every process
- with the variable set:
  - a key hashes differently in each process and the same on every thread of one
  - keys built to collide under the default secrets are spread out
  - script-level globals are listed in the order they are without it
  - `--bytecode` output is byte for byte what it is without it
  - an executable compiled with it runs without it, and the other way around
- the three orders above are insertion order (each of these fails on `main`)

### Still to do

- Pin `WEBKIT_VERSION` to the merged commit.

## Change

- **Spec with typed credentials** (`packages/fansly/src/wire/`): every page spec is now `credentials: "session"`. The new `accounts.public_by_ids` lives in its own table (`FANSLY_PUBLIC_WIRE_SPECS`, `wire/public.ts`), is `credentials: "none"` and is no page route (no actor, plan or `sync probe` can name it).

The page builder refuses a session-less spec in turn.
- **Egress kind `fansly_public`** (`services/egress/fansly-public.ts`, resolver branch): the reader's own proxy, stored like a page's (`fansly_public_egress`: URL + encrypted auth with key version); never a page's (same address **and** user refused at set and again at resolve); never direct (no row → `FanslyPublicEgressUnavailableError(not_configured)`, nothing sent); private/loopback targets refused; the dispatcher lets through `https://apiv3.fansly.com` only — any other origin is refused in the dispatch itself, before a connection or tunnel.

- **Journal source**: `FANSLY_SEND_SOURCES` + `public_lookup`; registry disposition `pageless`.
- **Migration `0258_fansly_public_lookup_egress.sql` (M5)**: `fansly_public_egress` (singleton, no FK, no grant) and `fansly_send_log_source_check` replaced by the 0225 list + `'public_lookup'` (NOT VALID → VALIDATE, `lock_timeout 5s`; ≈17.5k rows).

body:
b2: the slow C2 save (~12 s before "Pronto!" on 13's Preview) must be understood and fixed before the C2 flip.

**Cause:** saveSelfFields (and dismissSelfFields) called `revalidatePath("/my-appointments")`. A server action that revalidates returns only after Next re-renders that page on the server, and its new tree ships in the same response. /my-appointments does about a dozen mostly sequential reads to Supabase (sa-east-1): auth, role, country, the linked doctor, appointments, each doctor's public info, flags, My doctors, document doctors, the self-field prompts, privacy… So "Pronto!" waited for the RPC plus that whole render. On a cold Preview that's ~12 s.

**Fix:**
- The actions just call the RPC; no revalidatePath.
- `CompleteRegistrationCards` shows "Pronto!" as soon as save_my_fields answers (its done state already lives above the cards since #473), then `router.refresh()` runs in a background transition, so the rest of the page catches up without blocking.
- "Agora não": the card hides itself; the server already recorded it for the next load, so there's no refresh.
- conditions.json `c2-patient-step-live`: "Before the flip (b2, 10-09): the save must show \"Pronto!\" promptly … confirmed by a tester row on www."

**Tests (c2-self-fields):** saving shows "Pronto!" and calls router.refresh exactly once, and the actions file has no `revalidatePath(`. The existing #473 tests still pass ("Pronto!" survives the prompt disappearing). tsc OK; full vitest 1799/1799.

Not changed: the page's own sequential loading (a broader perf item, worth a separate look post-cut).

**Row (13 or 49, short):** C2 card → complete → "Pronto!" in ~1–2 s (time it), it stays, and the card is gone after the background refresh. Plus smoke.

body:
## Summary
The isolated installed-wheel FastAPI and Starlette consumers created DIContainer/CapabilityRuntime at module scope before asyncio.run. They now create those live owners inside the native host lifespan and retrieve them through explicit host state. An async singleton resource probe verifies the same loop and exactly one cleanup on normal and exceptional host exits.

## Issue / Backlog
Closes #569. BACKLOG.md records the implementation awaiting review/merge, reconciles delivered #565/#568 and records closure of redundant Dependabot #567: its action pins already match merged #525. No promotion to main or retrospective review is performed.

## Architecture impact
Preserves ADR 0094 and explicit DI/lifecycle ownership. Immutable declarations/plans remain separately compiled. Raw native Request objects stay in host endpoints. No runtime/public API, dependency/version, authority, support-tier, release or governance changes.

## Implementation
- Construct runtime/container in FastAPI/Starlette lifespan; close the runtime after awaited invocation and remove live handles from host state at exit.
- Exercise normal and exceptional exits in the same installed consumer, with a fresh singleton resource per lifespan.
- Assert construction, invocation and resource/runtime shutdown loop identity and event order, and absence of stale host state.
- Preserve wheel builds, first-party installation without index resolution, core-only import isolation and external isolated Python execution.
- Assert HTTP 200 and the expected JSON body on both paths.
- Save consumer.py outside the checkout and audit its canonical public imports before running it with Python -I.

## Validation / Tests
Python 3.14.4; first-party packages 1.0.3; FastAPI 0.141.1; Starlette 1.6.0.
- Focused FastAPI/Starlette: 13 passed.
- Full uv run python -m pytest -q, including architecture: 3853 passed, 38 skipped.
- uv sync, ruff check ., ruff format --check ., ty check: passed.
- Current-stage read-only version check (release 1.0.3 --check) and git diff --check: passed.
- Both installed consumer public-import audits run and pass in their integration tests.
Local validation uses UV_CONSTRAINT pinning pydantic==2.13.5 and pydantic-core==2.46.5 from uv.lock. Windows application control blocks the newly resolved pydantic-core 2.50.0 DLL; the prior task reproduced that import-only restriction. No dependency metadata or Windows policy is changed. Python -m pytest is equivalent to the pytest launcher blocked on this host. Browser tests run in the explicit required CI lane.

## Security impact
No runtime security behavior changes. Existing host authority, error, context and isolation assertions pass. No native host object enters core DI.

## Performance impact
None expected: fixture evidence and contributor records only; no performance claim.

## Documentation / Changelog
BACKLOG.md and an Unreleased CHANGELOG.md entry record corrected integration/lifecycle evidence. Runtime guides and support declarations need no change.

## Breaking changes
None.

## Authorship
Codex <codex@openai.com> materially authored implementation, validation and supplementary self-review. Exact identity verified against ADR 0092 and .github/ai-agent-identities.toml. Commit 6dfd6395114b5a817667294abe43a9755300ad34 author and complete message checked before push. No other agent participated, and Blandskron has no implementation author/co-author credit.
The GitHub CLI authenticates as Blandskron, so the PR creator is that account; commit authorship remains Codex. Existing #524 owns the review identity discrepancy; no governance change or fabricated review is included.

author: zackees
body:
Part of #4801. Fixes #4796.

## Root cause (linker map)
```
main.o → fl.channels+ (IChannelDriver::waitForReady) → fl.system+ (delayMicroseconds)
  fl.system+ also contains fl::analogRead → adc_oneshot_new_unit (strong ref)
  → libesp_adc.a(adc_oneshot.c.obj) → adc_common.c.obj
```
`adc_common.c.obj` carries a `.ctors` constructor, `adc_hw_calibration`. Constructors are always kept, so every ESP32-S3 sketch ran ADC self-calibration at boot and linked the efuse calibration path:
- `adc_hal_self_calibration`, `adc_hal_arbiter_config`, `read_cal_channel`;
- `esp_efuse_utility_*`, `esp_efuse_rtc_calib_*`.

Archive extraction follows any undefined symbol in an extracted object, even when `fl::analogRead` itself is later discarded by `--gc-sections`.

## Fix
Move the `fl::analogRead` wrapper into its own unity object, `fl/build/fl.system.analog+.cpp` → `fl/system/analog/`. This is the same pattern as the #4726 Wi-Fi/OTA split. The declaration stays in `fl/system/pin.h`.

## Evidence (dashboard protocol, fbuild 2.5.38)
| | flash before → after | RAM before → after |
|---|---|---|
| esp32s3 Blink | 401,876 → **397,480 (−4,396)** | 77,936 → **77,760 (−176)** |
| esp32s3 APA102 | 409,656 → **405,244 (−4,412)** | 77,864 → **77,672 (−192)** |
| esp32dev Blink / APA102 | unchanged | unchanged |

- A sketch calling `fl::analogRead(4)` still links `fl::analogRead`, `adc_oneshot_new_unit`, `adc_oneshot_read` and `adc_hw_calibration`.
- `bash test --cpp`: 319/319 unit, 95/95 examples. `bash lint` passes, with the new unit added to the unity-build list. `/code-review`: no findings.

author: juan-pablo-lopez-laszuk
body:
## Qué resuelve

Closes #43

Permite crear los sprints de un proyecto con Sprint Goal y fechas: el número lo asigna el sistema (correlativo por proyecto), nace en estado Planificado, tiene que quedar dentro del proyecto y empezar después del último sprint.

## Trazabilidad

| Artefacto | Enlace |
|---|---|
| Historia | HU-11 (#43) |
| Especificación SDD | `specs/HU-11-crear-sprint.md` (con la tabla criterio → escenarios → tests) |
| Escenarios BDD | `features/hu-11-crear-sprint.feature` · pasos en `features/hu11_steps_test.go` |
| Tests | `internal/domain/sprint/sprint_test.go`, `internal/store/memory/sprints_test.go`, `internal/service/sprints_test.go`, `internal/server/sprints_test.go` |
| Código | `internal/domain/sprint/sprint.go`, `internal/store/memory/sprints.go`, `internal/service/sprints.go`, `internal/server/sprints.go`, `web/templates/paginas/sprints.html`, `sprint_nuevo.html` |

## Decisiones de la spec (revisadas antes del código)

1. **Los sprints se crean en orden:** el nuevo empieza después del día en que termina el último. Así no se superponen (CA-11.2) y el número sigue el orden de las fechas, que es lo que usan la velocidad (HU-31) y la lista de HU-15.
2. Los bordes del proyecto valen (un sprint puede empezar y terminar el mismo día que el proyecto).
3. El fin tiene que ser posterior al inicio (como en HU-01).
4. Sprint Goal obligatorio, de hasta 500 caracteres.
5. El número es el más alto del proyecto más uno; cada proyecto tiene su numeración.

## TDD (commits)

- Antes de empezar, un `refactor` que pasa `ErroresValidacion` y `SoloFecha` a `internal/domain` (los comparten proyecto y sprint; HU-01 no cambia).
- Dominio: 6 ciclos RED → GREEN (primer sprint, Sprint Goal, fechas, dentro del proyecto, en orden, número correlativo) y un REFACTOR.
- Después un ciclo por capa: repositorios en memoria, caso de uso y pantallas, y los pasos de godog.

## Para TEC-03 (@MarianoPiastre)

El repositorio Postgres va a necesitar:
- `BuscarPorID(ctx, id) (project.Proyecto, error)` en el de proyectos, devolviendo `project.ErrNoEncontrado` si no existe (interfaz `service.BuscadorProyectos`).
- Un repositorio de sprints con `ListarPorProyecto` y `Guardar` (interfaz `service.RepositorioSprints`).

La restricción única `(proyecto_id, numero)` del modelo de datos cubre el caso de dos altas al mismo tiempo.

## Checklist (Definition of Done)

- [x] La spec SDD está completa y actualizada (estado Implementada).
- [x] Los escenarios BDD cubren caso normal, alternativo, límite y error (6 escenarios, 11 con los ejemplos).
- [x] Los tests se escribieron primero (hay commits `test(...): RED` antes de `feat(...): GREEN`).
- [x] `go test ./...` pasa localmente (34 escenarios BDD en verde).
- [x] `go vet ./...`, `gofmt` y golangci-lint sin problemas.
- [ ] Probé la funcionalidad en el preview de Vercel → lo probé en local; falta el preview de este PR.
- [x] Registré el uso de IA en `docs/ia/registro.md`.

Cobertura de lo nuevo: dominio y repositorios 100 %, caso de uso 97,5 %, pantallas 95,1 %.

## Cómo probarlo

1. En el preview: **Proyectos → Nuevo proyecto** (por ejemplo del 05/10/2026 al 01/11/2026).
2. En la lista, botón **Sprints** del proyecto → **Nuevo sprint**.
3. Probar: Sprint Goal vacío y una fecha fuera del proyecto (se muestra cada error en su campo); un segundo sprint que empieza el día que termina el primero (error de superposición); uno que empieza al día siguiente (se crea el Sprint 2).
4. `/proyectos/99/sprints` da 404.

> Los datos todavía se guardan en memoria: en Vercel pueden perderse entre pedidos hasta que esté TEC-03.

author: danteps97
body:
## Qué resuelve
Hoy una desconexión solo cambia el estado del dispositivo a `desconectado`: no se crea ninguna alerta, así que **nadie recibe un aviso** a menos que esté mirando el dashboard. RF-016 pide *informar* cuando un sensor deja de comunicarse, y `ALERT_TYPES` ya tenía `dispositivo_desconectado` sin usar. La Cloud Function `notificarAlerta` manda un correo a los administradores cuando se *crea* una alerta, así que crear la alerta cierra el circuito.

## Qué hace
Todo dentro del rastreador de conexión del Servicio de Integración (`iot-integration-service/lib/estado-conexion.js`):
- **Crea la alerta** cuando el rastreador marca `desconectado`: `tipo: "dispositivo_desconectado"`, `estado: "activa"`, `titulo`, `mensaje`, `ultimaSenalEn` y `creadaEn`. **Sin** `variable`, `valor`, `limite` ni `medidoEn`, así que la resolución automática de umbrales (#26), que consulta por `variable`, nunca la toca. Se crea dentro de su propio manejo de errores: si falla, el cambio de estado ya guardado no se deshace.
- **No duplica**: antes de crear consulta si ya hay una alerta abierta (`activa` o `reconocida`) de ese dispositivo y tipo.
- **Reintenta** si la creación falla: mientras el dispositivo siga desconectado vuelve a intentarlo en cada ciclo del vigilante, con una sola línea de error en el log y sin intentos concurrentes. Si el dispositivo se reconecta antes de lograrlo, esa caída no genera alerta; la siguiente caída avisa con normalidad.
- **Se resuelve sola cuando la reconexión es estable**, para que un dispositivo con WiFi inestable no mande un correo por cada cortecito: la alerta se cierra cuando el dispositivo lleva `LATIDO_ESTABILIDAD_SEGUNDOS` (60 por defecto) comunicándose. La estabilidad se mide por el tramo en que realmente se recibieron señales, no por el reloj; la resolución puede tardar hasta un período de latido más (unos 64 s con latidos de 8 s). Si se corta antes, sigue la misma alerta y no se crea otra. Los latidos **no** hacen ninguna lectura a Firestore.
- **`incubadoraId`**: sale del tópico MQTT (`index.js` lo pasa al registrar la señal) o, para los dispositivos recuperados al arrancar, del documento en Firestore. Sin él no se crea la alerta y se avisa una sola vez.
- **`notificarAlerta`**: solo se agregó `dispositivo_desconectado` al mapa de nombres legibles. Se leyó el armado del asunto y del cuerpo de punta a punta: una alerta con `titulo` y `mensaje` pero sin variable, valor ni límite no produce "undefined" ni "NaN".
- **Documentación**: `docs/contrato-mqtt.md`, `docs/modelo-datos.md` (el tipo de alerta, sus campos y su ciclo de vida) y `.env.example` (solo la clave `LATIDO_ESTABILIDAD_SEGUNDOS`).

## Qué encontró la revisión
- **Una fuga real**, reproducida con arnés propio: con la ventana medida por reloj, un dispositivo que estuvo vivo entre 30 y 55 s tras reconectarse y luego se calló se resolvía a los 60 s y volvía a alertar unos segundos después (2 alertas, un correo de más). Mi primera propuesta solo la reducía; la que quedó (medir por las señales vistas) la cierra y la revisión confirmó que el caso legítimo sigue resolviendo.
- **La falta de reintento**, que quedó implementada como se describe arriba.

## Orden de merge
Depende de #26 (esta rama está apilada sobre ella y lleva sus commits): mergear después. Es independiente de #27. La parte de interfaz está en #29.

## Verificación
Arnés de 40 casos con un Firestore y un reloj simulados (alerta con exactamente los campos esperados, sin duplicados, estabilidad a 50 s contra 60 s, dispositivo inestable, dispositivo recuperado al arrancar con una alerta vieja, `incubadoraId` desconocido, fallos de creación y de resolución, latidos sin consultas, y el correo) más una revisión independiente con arnés propio. **No se probó contra Firebase, un broker ni un navegador.**

## Riesgos conocidos
- Si el Servicio de Integración está caído, nadie detecta desconexiones (ya estaba documentado).
- Una caída de 30 s o más después de resolverse una alerta crea una alerta nueva y un correo nuevo: es lo esperado.
- Si la creación falla de forma persistente, se reintenta una vez por ciclo (5 s por defecto) sin retroceso progresivo; solo registra el primer error.
- Para los dispositivos recuperados al arrancar el servicio, `ultimaSenalEn` es la hora de arranque, no su última señal real (está documentado).
- Dos instancias del servicio corriendo a la vez podrían competir en el deduplicado.
- La consulta de igualdades más `in` sin `orderBy` no requiere índice compuesto según la documentación de Firestore, pero no se pudo comprobar contra un proyecto real.

body:
## 요약
EKS coredns 애드온에 `topologySpreadConstraints`(hostname, `DoNotSchedule`, maxSkew 1)를 추가해 CoreDNS 2개가 같은 노드에 뜨지 않게 한다. Closes #154

## 배경
- 애드온 기본값은 hostname anti-affinity가 **preferred**뿐이라, 스케줄 시점에 노드가 1대면 2개가 같은 Spot 노드에 몰린다(2026-10-07 실측).
- 그 노드가 통지 없이 사라지면 클러스터 DNS 전체가 중단되고, API의 RDS·Redis·외부 API 이름 해석이 실패한다.

## 설계 선택
- **hostname 분산 필수화**: 노드가 1대뿐이면 두 번째 Pod는 Pending이 되고, Karpenter가 노드를 띄워 해소한다. 롤링 중에는 maxSurge 25%라 막히지 않는다.
- `configuration_values`에 값을 주면 기본 zone 제약이 **대체**되므로, 기본값(zone, `ScheduleAnyway`)을 함께 다시 적었다.
- 기각한 안: "1개는 코어 노드에 고정". Deployment는 레플리카마다 다른 위치를 지정할 수 없고, 코어 노드 CPU 요청이 이미 85%다.

## 검증 (apply 완료, 2026-10-09)
- 전체 `terraform plan`: `aws_eks_addon.this["coredns"]` 제자리 변경 1건만 나옴
- apply 후 애드온 `ACTIVE`, 롤아웃 완료, Pod 2개가 서로 다른 노드(ap-northeast-2a / 2c)에 배치됨
- 클러스터 내부 `nslookup kubernetes.default.svc.cluster.local` 정상, prod·staging `/health` 200

author: devlikebear
body:
## Why

While any session sat stalled or failed, pulse asked the LLM to classify the same signals on every 1-minute tick. On a `claude-code-cli` setup that was a full Claude Code run per minute on the **standard** tier (`pulse_decider` had no code default and fell through to the default tier), and every call failed with `decider response had no tool calls` — a CLI provider cannot be handed the `pulse_decide` tool.

Measured on one machine, 2026-10-08 18:00 → 2026-10-09 10:00 KST: 870 calls, 20.3M cache-write + 107M cache-read + 1.2M output tokens, 0 notifications delivered.

## What

- **Rules by default.** `pulse.DecideByRules` classifies a tick from what the signals already carry (severity, autofix candidate, whether it may run): ready allowed autofix → autofix; disk warning with log compression allowed → compress; at or above `min_severity` → notify; otherwise ignore. No model call.
- **Act on a situation once.** `pulse.Fingerprint` hashes kinds, severities and the non-numeric details (ages, counts and percentages drift every minute). Unchanged signals are skipped (`skip_reason: signals_unchanged`) for 6h; a tick that failed or whose autofix changed nothing retries from 5m, doubling.
- **`automation.pulse.decider: llm` is opt-in.** It runs on the light tier by default, is called only when the fingerprint changes, and asks CLI providers for a JSON reply in a decision-only call (no tools, one turn).
- Signal details sort their sessions: the store lists them in no fixed order, which a live run showed as a repeat notification on the third tick.

## Verification

- `make test`, `make fmt-check vet arch-check api-check security-scan`
- `make test-cover-diff DIFF_BASE=origin/main`: 92.9% of changed lines
- Ran the built binary against the real workspace (3 stalled sessions + 1 failed): 5 ticks → 1 notification, 4 `signals_unchanged`, `total_decisions: 0`, no new usage rows.

Not run locally: `make lint-diff` (no golangci-lint on this machine).

author: joncallim
body:
## Summary
#183 F10 extension from the tenth review's persistence cross-check (P2). `DocumentWriter.save` registers its pending source, follows the accepted lineage after acquiring the lane and inherits the encoding an earlier save already made; `saveAs` acquired the same lane but did none of that, passing the original snapshot straight to `writeSaveAs`. A Save As built from a snapshot that predates an accepted Save-with-Encoding (UTF-8 → UTF-8+BOM / Latin-1) therefore wrote the destination in the OLD encoding and rebound the visible document to it, silently undoing the explicit choice. `saveAs` now registers its source before waiting (so an ordinary save's acknowledgement cannot compact the lineage first), computes the inherited encoding once the lane is held, and passes it to `FileDocument.saveAs(encodingOverride:)`; the pending source is released on exit. The separately captured destination baseline is unchanged.

## Tests
A Save As from a stale UTF-8 snapshot after an accepted Latin-1 save writes Latin-1 bytes and returns Latin-1 metadata (fails on master); a Save As with no earlier change keeps the source encoding. Workspace suite passes (253). The gated end-to-end schedule (publication barrier + Save As panel timing) is not separately exercised.

body:
Arreglos de frontend antes de la demo, encontrados en la integración con el backend (Feature 7). Sin cambios en el contrato: `ApiService`, `HttpApiService` y `MockApiService` quedan igual. Nada fuera de `frontend/`.

## Qué cambia

1. **Cerrar sesión deja datos en pantalla.** El botón del header borraba la sesión y te dejaba en la misma página, en todas las pantallas. Ahora, cuando la sesión termina (por el botón o por un 401 del backend), se vuelven a correr los guards de la pantalla abierta: las protegidas (`/inicio`, `/test`, `/resultados`, `/resultados/:id`, `/perfil`) mandan a `/ingresar` y las públicas se quedan donde están. Para eso las rutas protegidas tienen `runGuardsAndResolvers: 'always'`. Medido contra `main`: no agrega pedidos a la API ni al responder ítems en `/test` ni al pasar entre resultados.
2. **El texto premium se podía leer sin pagar.** Sin tier pago, el texto real ya no está en el DOM: bajo el desenfoque hay un relleno (`aria-hidden`). La condición es la misma de antes (`attempt.tier === 'paid_full'`). En el build real el tier viene del backend. En el build demo vive en `localStorage` y se puede forzar desde el navegador; queda pendiente porque requiere tocar `MockApiService`. El texto sigue viajando en el bundle, y eso se resuelve en el backend.
3. **Largos máximos.** Nombre 100, email 254 y mensaje 5.000 en `/contacto`; comentario 2.000 en el feedback (cierre del test y `/perfil`). Son los valores de `backend/app/blueprints/feedback/schemas.py`. Cada campo muestra el mensaje en el mismo estilo del formulario y no se envía nada.
4. **`/resultados/:attemptId` no recargaba al cambiar de intento.** El router reutiliza el componente, que leía el snapshot una sola vez: al pasar de A a B se seguía viendo A. Ahora sigue `paramMap` y cancela la carga anterior si sigue en curso.
5. **Tests.** El spec por defecto de `AppComponent` (que ya fallaba en `main`) ahora pasa. Se suma un test de cierre de sesión que usa la configuración de rutas real; `routes` está exportado para eso.

## Verificación

- [x] `npm test`: 4 tests en verde (Edge headless vía `CHROME_BIN`). El de cierre de sesión falla si se saca `runGuardsAndResolvers`.
- [x] `npm run build` y `npm run build:demo` en verde.

- [x] Backend local: en un resultado de tier gratuito, buscar en Elements "En crecimiento," o "Bajo estrés," no encuentra nada; aparece el relleno "Este párrafo es un relleno…".

body:
## Quick summary

Full-document highlighting builds a large set of text keys to remove duplicate captures. This change groups captures by their text spans and keeps one deduplication entry per capture name, while preserving styles, equal-span precedence and injected-language output.

## Changes

- Sort only the worker's freshly returned compact capture array. The runtime API keeps its accepted-match ordering.
- Keep stable ordering within equal spans and deduplicate each language layer independently.
- Leave range highlighting, injection discovery and fold queries on their existing paths.
- Add a patch changeset, focused regressions and lossless shipping-source correctness evidence. Package version numbers are unchanged.

## Verification

From `editor/packages/tree-sitter`:

```sh
bun --bun vitest run test/treeSitter-worker.test.ts test/runtime-identity.test.ts
bun run typecheck
bun --bun vitest run --browser.enabled --browser.headless test/native-coverage.browser.test.ts test/markdown.browser.test.ts
```

Passed 30 focused tests, package types and 47 real native browser tests. The grouping regression failed before the source change. New cases cover separated duplicates, overlapping spans, empty/inverted spans, equal-span precedence and independent languages/invocations. Native full versus whole-range results agree on captures, tokens, injections, folds and errors for TypeScript documentation/regex, HTML script/style, Astro and fenced Markdown with Unicode and CRLF.

The complete-document build and a fresh 10 MiB shipping-source smoke passed. Every canonical proof field equals the compact consumer: 1,198,376 tokens, identical token/style/structural hashes, full root coverage through 10,485,760, 42 query calls and no exceeded match limit. The screenshot was read back. [Source-smoke evidence](https://github.com/ShaulLavo/fregat/tree/lane/plan-339-span-map/editor/docs/performance/singapore-full-parse-2026-10-08/normalization-span-map-source-smoke) includes exact source, observation, trace, screenshot and checked artifact hashes. Its single noisy sample is a correctness check, not a speed claim.

## Earlier paired experiment, not qualification

The prospective span-map experiment used compact ranges on both sides, identical lockfiles and the same 10 MiB complete-document fixture. Cold ran baseline then candidate; warm reversed that order. Each sample parsed a fresh document. Strict comparison passed environment and canonical-output guards.

| Diagnostic clock | Cold keys | Cold span map | Warm keys | Warm span map |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Complete highlighted frame | 4,144.9 ms | 3,820.3 ms | 4,046.0 ms | 3,630.4 ms |
| Worker parse plus query | 3,956.2 ms | 3,646.2 ms | 3,894.6 ms | 3,503.6 ms |
| Main-thread union work | 23.959 ms | 15.675 ms | 10.267 ms | 10.140 ms |

These are one observation per side and condition. [Raw paired observations, traces, source transforms and comparison](https://github.com/ShaulLavo/fregat/tree/lane/plan-339-capture-profile/editor/docs/performance/singapore-full-parse-2026-10-08/normalization-span-map-experiment) were preserved separately in the compact consumer PR. They do not establish distributions, whole-job memory or physical presentation.

M1 remains unpassed. Cold diagnostic work is 3,661.875 ms, above the frozen 3,539.053 ms ceiling. No qualified acceptance window was run. The next bounded experiment must close that gap before qualification.

This PR targets main after #1087 merged. Merge head `cccec9923e7c1e514c99a819c2d57221a0abdc2f` is byte-identical to independently approved `f24e3861`. Worker/runtime tests, package types and fresh complete-document canonical proof passed again. Browser screenshot and cold-optimizer repairs are separate in #1088.

body:
## What
Adds `.github/workflows/codeql.yml` — runs CodeQL analysis (Go, `autobuild`) on push/PR to `master`/`main` plus a weekly schedule, and uploads SARIF to GitHub code scanning.

## Why
The OpenSSF Scorecard **SAST** check currently scores **0** ("0 commits out of 26 are checked with a SAST tool"). SAST has weight 3 and feeds the LFX Insights *Security & Supply Chain* dimension via the Scorecard band. This is step 1 of the Scorecard improvement plan (target raw score ≥ 7.0).

## Design notes (deliberately avoids worsening other Scorecard checks)
- **Least-privilege permissions** — top-level `permissions: contents: read`; the `analyze` job adds only `security-events: write` (required for SARIF upload). Keeps *Token-Permissions* clean.
- **Actions pinned by commit SHA** — `checkout` v4, `setup-go` v5, `codeql-action` v3, each annotated `# vX`. Keeps *Pinned-Dependencies* clean.
- **`setup-go` pins Go 1.25** to match `ci.yml`'s `GO_VERSION`, so `autobuild` uses the toolchain the module requires.
- **Apache license header** copied verbatim from `ci.yml` to satisfy the `hawkeye` `strictCheck` gate in CI.

## Validation
- License header byte-identical to `ci.yml` (`diff` clean).
- YAML parses; single job `analyze`; triggers `push` / `pull_request` / `schedule`.
- This PR's own CI run executes CodeQL end-to-end (the real validation).

## Note for maintainers
Please review before merge. After merging, subsequent `master` commits carry the CodeQL check run and the Scorecard SAST score climbs as recent commits accumulate SAST coverage.

author: vercantez
body:
Follow-up to #96 (the side finding there). If a node is lost after a run's turn ended (its reply written, the turn closed) but before the run recorded its end, the next owner lost the outcome:
- **prompt:** ended `uncertain` with "The runtime restarted during this request", even though the reply was in history;
- **resume** (an answered approval or question): ran again from its answers, settled nothing, and completed with no `reply`.

## Root cause
The agent host's start reports a hand-off only for a turn that is still active (continue it, or take its final answer) or suspended. For a turn that had already ended, it reported nothing. `ClientSessions.resume()` then had nothing to go on:
- a prompt fell through to "uncertain";
- a resume re-ran `resume` with nothing left to settle, which returns no answer.

## Fix
- **Agent host** (`src/agent-host.ts`, `endedTurn`): when it starts to resume runs and its last turn has ended, it reports that turn:
  - the prompt ids its user messages carry;
  - the tool calls whose results it holds;
  - what it ended with: reply, structured output, or suspension.
- **`ClientSessions.resume()`**: a resumed run takes that outcome when the turn is its own.
  - A prompt matches when its request id is on the turn's user message.
  - A resume matches when every answered call of its suspension has its result in that turn.
- Otherwise nothing changes. For example, a prompt whose message was never written still ends uncertain.

`continue` runs carry no id in the transcript, so they cannot be matched and keep today's behaviour.

## Tests (deterministic sim scenarios, using `pauseAtDbAnswer(nth)`)
- **Prompt:** a stops right after its turn ends, past its lease. b ends the run with reply "the answer", and the model is not asked again. Before the fix it ended uncertain.
- **Approval resume:** a stops after the resumed turn ends. b ends the resume with the reply; the approved call ran once. Before the fix the reply was missing.
- Both assert the new goal `reachable("a resumed run took the outcome of its turn that had ended")`, so drift in the pause point fails loudly.
- Random sim seeds also reach this goal.

## Verification
- `npm run typecheck`: passes.
- `npm test`: 1199 tests, 0 failed.
- `npm run sim -- --seeds 1-200 --jobs 6`: 200 runs, 0 failed.
- After rebasing onto main (with #96): `sim-scenarios`, `human-input` and `cluster-handoff` pass, 40 of 40.

Release notes: `docs/operations/unreleased/fix-resume-outcome-reply.md`.

author: justin13888
body:
## Summary
- `crates/kynos-openapi/src/validate/rules/paths.rs`: `Validator::check_item` now descends into each operation's inline `callbacks`, calling itself on every inline callback Path Item with no path template and the location `<operation>/callbacks/<name>/<expression>`. Before this, `check_paths` reached `components.callbacks` but never an operation's own `callbacks`, so a duplicate `operationId`, an undeclared security scheme, a missing `responses` or any other operation-level rule written there passed `validate`. OpenAPI says `operationId` is unique "among all operations described in the API" (`references/3.1.2.md:979`, `references/3.2.0.md:680`), and an inline callback describes operations.
- `crates/kynos-openapi/src/validate/tests.rs`: `an_operation_inside_an_inline_callback_is_validated`, next to `an_operation_outside_paths_is_validated_too`. It checks a duplicate `operationId` in an inline callback at its exact location, and a responseless operation one callback deeper. It was committed red first (13e72d8, which failed with `got []`) and passes at the fix.

## Validation
- `cargo nextest run -p kynos-openapi -E 'test(/inline_callback|outside_paths/)'` at 13e72d8: the new test fails (`an inline callback describes an operation; got []`) and the two existing ones pass.
- `cargo nextest run --workspace --all-features` at 04643f9: 1682 passed, 0 failed.
- `cargo clippy -p kynos-openapi --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`: clean.
- `cargo clippy -p kynos-openapi --all-targets --no-default-features --features openapi31 -- -D warnings`: clean.
- `cargo fmt --all`: no changes.
- Not run locally, left to CI: the full `mise run check` set (features, docs, msrv, containment, publish, coverage).

## Risks and rollout
- A document that already has an invalid operation inside an inline callback now fails `validate`, and therefore fails at router build. That is the intended correction. No public API changed.
- Coverage gap: the test covers `operationId` uniqueness and `NoResponses` only. The other rules run through the same `check_operation` call, so they are reached by construction and have no case of their own here, following the reasoning in the existing test that the route to the operation is what was broken.

## Issue
Closes #428

## Decisions taken
Issue 428 - fix(validate): operations inside inline callbacks are never validated

1. **Where the recursion lives.** Taken: in `check_item`'s per-operation loop in `paths.rs`, which already owns the walk and its shared `operation_ids` map. Rejected: putting it in `check_operation` (`operations.rs`), which would have had to widen `check_item`'s visibility so another module could call it, for no change in behaviour. To reverse: move the loop into `check_operation` and make `check_item` `pub(in crate::validate)`.
2. **Referenced callbacks.** Taken: only `RefOr::Item` callbacks and callback Path Items are walked. A `$ref` is skipped, the same way the existing `components.callbacks` walk skips it. Its target is a component that is already validated once, and following references would visit it once per reference and report duplicate `operationId`s against the component itself. Following only inline items also keeps the recursion bounded by the document's depth. To reverse: resolve the reference instead of `continue` in the new loop.
3. **No path template for a callback.** Taken: `None`, as for `components.callbacks`. A runtime expression is not a path template, so the path-parameter correspondence rule is skipped there rather than given a made-up template. To reverse: pass a template built from the expression.
4. **Diagnosis.** The issue asked for diagnosis before fixing. The gap was confirmed by the red test, which produced no violations, before any code changed.

## Unresolved review notes
### V1
Coverage of decision 2's `$ref` skip (`paths.rs:194`, and the Path Item skip beside it): repaired by `a_referenced_callback_is_not_walked_again_from_its_operation` in `crates/kynos-openapi/src/validate/tests.rs`. An operation whose callback is a `$ref` to `components.callbacks`, and an inline callback whose Path Item is a `$ref` to `components.pathItems`, report no error, so neither component is visited again from the operation and no duplicate `operationId` is reported against it. `cargo nextest run -p kynos-openapi -E 'test(/callback|outside_paths/)'`: 5 passed; `cargo clippy -p kynos-openapi --all-targets -- -D warnings` under `--all-features` and under `--no-default-features --features openapi31`: clean; `cargo fmt --all --check`: clean. Remaining coverage gap: the crate has no reference resolver, so the test cannot be run red against a walk that follows references; it asserts the invariant rather than reproducing a regression.
Resolved at: a6c464f4f3e1d27d8f5273829c1d18c9ff14ca83

### HTTP/2 server memory exhaustion due to Trailer headers in net/http
[CVE-2026-78659](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-78659) / [GO-2026-6603](https://pkg.go.dev/vuln/GO-2026-6603)

<details>
<summary>More information</summary>

#### Details
When "Trailer" headers are sent by a client, the HTTP server internally uses the header values to populate the Request.Trailer map passed to the server handler. Because Request.Trailer is a map, each entry incurs memory overhead. For HTTP/2 servers, a malicious client can exploit this by sending a "Trailer" header that declares a large number of fields, causing the server to allocate a disproportionate amount of memory while bypassing Server.MaxHeaderValueCount and Server.MaxHeaderBytes limits. This exploit is not applicable for HTTP/1 servers, which do not support multiplexing a large number of requests over one TCP connection, and whose Server.MaxHeaderBytes are calculated differently.

#### Severity
Unknown

### Double flow control refund on HTTP/2 server streams in net/http
[CVE-2026-78663](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-78663) / [GO-2026-6612](https://pkg.go.dev/vuln/GO-2026-6612)

<details>
<summary>More information</summary>

#### Details
The HTTP/2 server can refund connection-level flow control twice for the same data: Once when a client resets a stream (refunding data for any sent-but-unread portion of the stream), and again when a request handler reads the buffered data. A malicious client can exploit this to bypass the configured connection-level flow control limit (MaxReceiveBufferPerConnection). Total buffered data is still limited by the concurrent stream limit and stream-level flow control.

#### Severity
Unknown

#### References
- [https://go.dev/cl/847187](https://go.dev/cl/847187)

</details>

### HTTP/2 server crash due to HPACK encoder race in net/http
[CVE-2026-97032](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-97032) / [GO-2026-6617](https://pkg.go.dev/vuln/GO-2026-6617)

<details>
<summary>More information</summary>

#### Details
HTTP/2 servers could end up crashing due to inadvertently modifying its HPACK encoder concurrently. This happens because the server modifies the HPACK encoder from two goroutines without synchronization: one uses the encoder to encode a HEADERS frame as part of a response sent to a client and the other modifies the encoder's table size when handling a SETTINGS frame containing SETTINGS_HEADER_TABLE_SIZE that a client sends. A malicious client can repeatedly send a request while changing the header table size to crash the server.

#### Severity
Unknown

author: lingduoduo
body:
Spec and plan only. The code PR will target `master` directly (not stacked on this one).

**Spec:** `.superpowers/docs/specs/2026-10-09-diversity-dashboard-design.md`
**Plan:** `.superpowers/docs/plans/2026-10-09-diversity-dashboard.md`

## The gap
- **The long-tail KPI is circular.** Its cutoff is the 80th popularity percentile taken *over exposures*, so about 80% of exposures fall below it by construction, whatever the recommender does. It was 0.796 on the last run; with the cutoff taken over distinct items it is 0.760.
- **Every KPI is a per-slate average.** A recommender that showed every user the same five genre-diverse items would score perfectly.
- **The table's 10 slate rows are an arbitrary sample** out of 16,726 slates.

## The plan
1. Take the long-tail cutoff over distinct served items, each counted once.
2. Add catalog-level fields: coverage, exposure Gini, the top decile's share of exposures, median distinct items per user, and the user repeat rate.
3. Replace the sampled slate rows with histograms of per-slate entropy and intra-list distance, plus a chart of each genre's share of exposures against its share of the items served.
4. Add diversity over time, reusing the satisfaction whole-second bucketing (pulled out into a shared `_time_buckets`).

The sim serves near-uniform slates, so every figure will sit near its ideal. The section is built to catch a recommender that narrows what people see, and the page says so.
