body:
## 📚 PR stack — merge in order (each PR is based on the previous one)

   1. #1 — 
   2. #2 — fix: pnpm frontend image, backend proxy, real API-key errors
   3. #3 — phase 1 — Traefik gateway + static template
   4. #4 — phase 2 — Next.js template
👉 5. #5 — phase 3 — git-versioned runs + 🚀 Build app

_This PR is **5 of 5**. Review only its own commits; merge #4 first, then retarget this PR to `main` (GitHub does this automatically when the base branch is deleted on merge)._

---

## Summary
Phase 4: checks that the generated output is real and distinct, newer models, and video input for Claude.

- **Visual checks (backend headless Chromium):**
  - After each version, every option is screenshotted at 375/768/1280/1920 px and checked for a successful render, for being a near-copy of another option (≥ 0.97 similar), and for being responsive (no horizontal scroll, content fills ≥ 85% of the width at 1280/1920).
  - The UI shows badges on the option tiles and **screenshot thumbnails in the chat row** whenever an option fails a check.
  - Manual-edit saves are checked too.
- **Checking the built app, not the mock:** Build app builds only the selected option by default and skips duplicates. After a build, the running app is screenshotted through Traefik and compared with its mock. The comparison is foreground-aware and tolerates vertical drift: the real migrated landing page scores 0.92, while a missing section or a moved card scores ≤ 0.58.
- **Fluid layout rule:** generation and migration prompts now require the page to fill the full width and reflow at `lg`/`xl`/`2xl`. Before, a card filled 16% of the width at 1920 px; in this test every option filled 100%.
- **Models:**
  - Added `claude-fable-5-1`, `claude-opus-5-5`, `claude-sonnet-5-5`, `claude-haiku-5-5`, `gemini-3.8-flash` and `gpt-5.6-luna`, all with adaptive thinking configured.
  - Choice sets put **a different provider on each option.** AI edits use Opus 5.5 and GPT 5.6 Sol, replacing two speed-tuned models.
- **Video → frames:** the browser extracts 1 frame per second (up to 20). Claude Fable 5.1 gets the frames and Gemini 3.1 Pro gets the video.
- **Builds repair themselves:** each app is built before it is committed. A failed `pnpm build` sends its log back to the model for a fix, up to 2 attempts, and only apps that build are committed. `cacheComponents` is turned off in the template, and the migration prompt requires deterministic rendering.

## Test plan
- [x] Backend `pytest`: 488 passed; `pyright` shows no new warnings in changed files
- [x] Frontend `pnpm test`: 120 passed; `tsc --noEmit` clean; lint unchanged at the 25-problem baseline
- [x] End to end on the live stack:
  - Create used 4 different models; QA found every option rendered, distinct and responsive
  - AI edit options were 0.30 similar, against 0.9999 before
  - A video upload produced 7 frames; Claude Fable 5.1 rebuilt the four designs in the clip with a working switcher
  - Build app hit a real `new Date()` prerender failure, which was fixed; it then ran, was committed, and scored 0.92 against the mock

## Known gaps
- Prices for Haiku 5.5, Gemini 3.8 Flash and GPT 5.6 Luna are copied from sibling models; their real prices are unknown.
- The models chosen for an AI edit aren't printed to the logs.
- The frontend health check passes a few seconds before Vite responds, which caused one brief 502.

author: codekuu
body:
## Why

A `subscription_update` template can only learn an incident's state from inside `{{update_subject}}` (`[#12:INVESTIGATING] Title`). Mustache can't compare strings, so the same template can't render differently for a new outage, an update, a resolution or a maintenance. We wanted subscribers to see that at a glance, for example a red banner when an incident starts, green when it's resolved, and purple for maintenance.

## What

**New template variables.** Incident comment notifications (`notifySubscribersOfComment`) now also pass:

| Variable | Value |
|---|---|
| `update_state` | the comment's state, e.g. `INVESTIGATING` |
| `is_investigating`, `is_identified`, `is_monitoring`, `is_resolved` | `true` for the comment's state |
| `incident_impact` | the worst impact among the incident's monitors: `DOWN`, `DEGRADED` or `""` |
| `is_down`, `is_degraded` | `true` for that worst impact |

Maintenance notifications (`maintenanceToVariables`) pass `is_maintenance: true`. Everything is additive and optional on `SubscriptionVariableMap`, so existing templates render exactly as before. If reading the incident's monitors fails, the mail is still sent, just without the impact flags. The variables are documented in the email templates guide.

**Alert-created incidents.** Two fixes in `CreateNewIncidentWithCommentAndMonitor`, both found in review:

- **The monitor is attached before the opening comment.** The comment is what notifies subscribers, so this way the opening mail carries the impact. The manage UI already adds monitors before the first comment. If attaching fails, the comment and its mail still go out and the error is still raised, the same outcome as before.
- **LATENCY and UPTIME alerts now get the `DEGRADED` impact.** Their `alert_value` is a numeric threshold, which `AddIncidentMonitor` rejects. Before this PR that left their incidents without a monitor and unlinked from the alert, so they never closed. STATUS alerts keep `DOWN` or `DEGRADED`.

## Tests

- `incidentController.test.ts` (new) covers:
  - the state flags, the worst impact (DOWN over DEGRADED), no monitors, and a failed impact lookup
  - STATUS DOWN/DEGRADED, LATENCY and UPTIME through `CreateNewIncidentWithCommentAndMonitor`: monitor attached before the comment, impact in the mail
  - the attach-failure path
- `notification_utils.test.ts` gains a case for `is_maintenance`.
- Each new test fails against the matching broken variant (no normalization, comment first, attach throwing first, unguarded lookup).
- `npm test`: 262 passed. `npm run check`: 0 errors and 0 warnings. Prettier is clean.

We're running the state flags against v4.1.7 in production, as a build-time patch that we'll drop once a release includes them.

author: throndir2
body:
Templates can now send as much of a long transcript (for example a multi-hour D&D session) as the model can take in.

## What changes

- **Context window detection** (`LlmClient.ContextWindowAsync`): asks Ollama (`/api/show` → `*.context_length`), LM Studio (`/api/v0/models`), llama.cpp (`/props`), and OpenAI-compatible model lists (`context_length`, `top_provider.context_length`, `context_window`, `max_model_len`, `max_context_length`, `max_input_tokens`, …). Runs on **Test** and before the first template run for a new base URL or model.
- **Transcript chars 0 = fill** (new default): the template sends as much of the transcript as fits, after it keeps room for the answer and, when the context folder is used, for files the model reads. Token counts are a conservative estimate: about 3 ASCII characters per token and 1 token per other character.
- **Ollama**: its OpenAI endpoint can't set `num_ctx`, so it used Ollama's default (4,096 tokens on most PCs) and lost most of the transcript. Template runs now use Ollama's `/api/chat` with `options.num_ctx`. The value grows in powers of two (minimum 8,192) as the transcript grows and never shrinks in one app run, so templates don't make Ollama reload the model again and again.
- **Token limit (0 = model's)** on each connection: caps the window, or supplies it when the server doesn't report one (OpenAI, NVIDIA Build).
- The "Current local time" line moves to the end of the prompt, so servers can reuse the processed start of a long prompt.
- Existing templates that are on the old 60,000-character default move to 0 one time (settings `Version` 1).
- The HTTP timeout goes up from 10 to 30 minutes, because local models can need a long time to read a long transcript.

## Checks (local)

- `AudioTranscriber.App` builds with no new warnings.
- App tests: 27 passed. New tests cover the budget math and use a fake Ollama server to check the detected window, the `/api/chat` call, `num_ctx`, and the image field.
- A live probe of OpenRouter found 1,048,576 tokens for `google/gemini-2.5-flash`. No real Ollama was available on this PC.

author: matias-obezzi
body:
Switching between the Sidebar's stacked menus (`SidebarViews`, the demo's Settings and All) flashed the menu items.

## Cause

The view sliding out was animated without `fill`. When its animation ended, it went back to its own styles (opaque, in place) and painted over the new view for the frame before React unmounted it.

Found by pulling the frames out of the screen recording and recording the demo frame by frame in Chromium. On `main`, the frame at 390 ms shows Workspace and Settings drawn over each other. The frame-to-frame difference spikes to 3.9 after the motion has settled, then drops back.

## Fix

- The leaving view's animation uses `fill: 'forwards'`, so it holds its last frame until it unmounts.
- The slide follows the phone pattern:
  - the coming view slides in whole and opaque;
  - the leaving one moves 30% and is gone by 35% of the way.

  Before, both crossed the full width while fading, which left the menu nearly empty for a frame halfway.

## Checked

- Re-recorded after the fix: no spike once the motion settles, and no frame shows both menus.
- Sidebar tests (15), updated for the new frames. They now assert that the leaving view uses `fill: 'forwards'` and that the coming view never fades.
- Typecheck and lint.

author: steipete
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Concurrent session worktree creation can fail while Git writes shared upstream configuration, and every creation independently fetches the same default branch.

## User Impact

Concurrent worktrees keep normal upstream tracking while sharing remote-default preparation. This reduces Git contention during creation bursts. Requests arriving after the refresh settles still refresh the remote. No configuration, storage-format, or migration changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

The reproduced exit-255 failure is a `.git/config.lock` collision. Git itself emits the misleading `origin/refs/heads/main` recovery hint; OpenClaw already supplies a valid remote ref. Branch registration now uses the existing repository ref-mutation owner, while file materialization remains concurrent. Settled fetches also retry a ref-lock race once within the original timeout and authority checks.

Creators join a lazy preparation group before waiting for allocation. Fetching starts only after source admission. Settlement removes the group from discovery, while creators already waiting retain its prepared result. A canceled owner can hand off only after native work settles; uncertain cleanup remains an unknown outcome and cannot trigger another fetch. Explicit bases and per-checkout fast-forward policy retain their existing behavior.

The tested main baseline already scopes session lifecycle admission to individual session identities; #166059 also moves model/native-runtime patch preparation outside the shared database writer. Every recorded lifecycle waiter/holder pair in the burst investigation had the same session scope, with no create holders. These logs are rate-limited observations, not exhaustive production proof. This change preserves same-session exclusion and reduces competing Git work rather than adding a second metadata-patch path.

Production LOC: **+194 net** (244 added, 50 removed; tests and docs excluded). The existing independent-fetch path is replaced. The increase implements the required preparation lifetime, live-authority checks, and native-process settlement: capture before allocation, fetch under source custody, retain results for waiting creators, reject use after scope closure, and preserve uncertain outcomes. There is no TTL cache, configuration option, or compatibility shim. Moving base selection to its owner also shrinks `service.ts` by six lines.

## Evidence

### Matched 40-create RPC burst

AWS Crabbox `cbx_27423fb6782a`, Linux / Node 24.19.0, 4 vCPU and 32 GiB; baseline `59309cc7777e07d52ca1be94bf8c25fd685919bc` versus reviewed lane commit `3caee81f4ee5892ad931d28a36cfd9f7f2c69654` on the same lease (before the import-only rebase conflict resolution):

| Metric | Baseline | Final patch |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Successful creates | 40/40 | 40/40 |
| Fetches / default discoveries | 40 / 40 | 1 / 1 |
| Create p50 | 65.83 s | 63.47 s |
| Create p99 (maximum of 40) | 82.82 s | 82.17 s |
| Metadata patch samples | 1494 | 1484 |
| Metadata patch failures | 0 | 0 |
| Metadata patch p90 | 4.94 s | 5.24 s |
| Metadata patch p99 | 13.33 s | 12.51 s |
| Metadata patch maximum | 15.93 s | 15.24 s |
| Peak Gateway + driver RSS | 9.26 GiB | 9.29 GiB |

Fetch count falls **97.5%**; patch p99 improves **6.2%** in this final matched pair. This does **not** demonstrate a 1.5× latency improvement: creation latency is nearly unchanged, patch p90 is slightly worse, and metadata tails remain high under this saturated fixture. The demonstrated benefits are eliminating the deterministic config-lock race and avoiding 39 redundant network refreshes per burst. This is one measured pair, not a statistical latency guarantee. The driver's 128-pending-patch cap skipped 28 scheduled launches on baseline and 32 on the final patch.

The synthetic rig uses 4,700 valid Git packs, 128 tracked files (8 MiB), a local origin, and real authenticated loopback Gateway WebSocket requests. After a real worktree warmup, it launches 40 concurrent `sessions.create {worktree:true}` calls while sending rename/archive patches every 100 ms. Git Trace2 counts actual fetch processes; every successful creation is read back through `sessions.describe`.

This is a source-runtime Gateway on Linux, not a production deployment. The fixture reproduces pack-discovery pressure but not a production network or full repository object graph. The intermittent config-lock failure is established separately by the deterministic native-Git regression; a clean baseline burst does not disprove it.

### Regression and gate proof

- Blacksmith Testbox `tbx_01m4fdp4qrxfb2j4e65t7gc760` ([run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/37882647602)): unchanged production code reproduced exit 255, `.git/config.lock`, and the malformed recovery hint. Concurrent default lookups made 40 discovery/fetch operations; ref-lock failures did not retry.
- Blacksmith Testbox `tbx_01m4ffkmaw78rtg4zycy6dahpx` ([run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/37885267851)): all 59 worktree test files selected: 53 executed and passed, six platform-skipped; all 12 relevant Git infrastructure files passed. Executed files retain their existing individual platform skips. Export-name and both source-closure guards passed. The delayed-creator negative control made two fetches instead of one. Its broad changed gate lost its SSH connection after 21 passing typecheck graphs; it is not counted as a completed gate.
- AWS Crabbox `cbx_27423fb6782a`: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/worktrees/service-branches.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` passed **49 tests, one existing platform skip; 50.24 s Vitest duration, 75.48 s wrapper wall time**. The uncertainty negative control failed nine cases as intended. Focused Git, fetch, profile, and retry files passed **88 tests, one existing platform skip**. `node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/check-export-name-collisions.mts` and the two source-closure files passed (**20 tests**).
- AWS `cbx_27423fb6782a`: `node scripts/check-changed.mjs --staged` passed core types, all **27 core-test typecheck graphs**, formatting, boundaries, and ratchets, then failed only the repository-wide unused-export scan. Repeating `node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/check-deadcode-exports.mts` with **all candidate changes reversed and `git diff HEAD --exit-code` clean** produced identical findings on baseline `59309cc7777e07d52ca1be94bf8c25fd685919bc`. The check owner's remaining targeted lint was run separately and passed (15.47 s, zero errors; one test-file length warning). The overall changed gate remains recorded as inherited red.

<details>
<summary>Inherited unused exports</summary>

- `src/agents/cli-runner/tool-authority.ts`: `bindCliQuestionAnswerAuthority`
- `src/auto-reply/reply/session-event-handoff.ts`: `prepareSessionEventTargetForHost`
- `src/config/sessions/session-accessor.sqlite-entry-cache-publication.ts`: `readSessionEntryCreationTransition` (also reported through `entryPublication` in the full-tree scan)
- `src/infra/heartbeat-events-filter.ts`: `RESTART_CONTINUATION_CONTEXT_PREFIX`

None of these source files is changed by this PR. The script-only export scan passed on both revisions. Main subsequently repaired these exports in `3b3cd5939993` (`fix(ci): repair Telegram declaration and unused exports`); that independent fix is not copied into this lane.

</details>

Independent Codex autoreview completed on the final patch with no actionable findings at its configured P0 threshold.

The branch regression uses real Git and SQLite because it covers native branch registration, repository admission, shared fetching, and cancellation settlement. Its single-worker command took 75.48 seconds wall time (50.24 seconds in Vitest), the measured remote command cost; no new test files or CI shards are added.

Le gestionnaire calendrier est maintenant exactement le correctif sécurisé fusionné dans `main` et non l'ancien `delete/upsert`.

## Vérifications avant toute livraison
- Rejouer la suite 15 tests Node et 4 navigateurs mobiles Playwright (fixtures uniquement).
- Interdire les accès directs INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE depuis la carte MAÎTRE.

Après CI vert, fermer l'ancienne #10 comme supersédée par cette PR et mettre à jour le garde de compatibilité des trois propriétaires V30 dans `BEAUVILLE/digiy-loc`.

## Summary

Specification (draft v0.2) for a Claude Agent SDK agent that answers natural-language questions on Deskoala data using the Web API **read-only**.

## Changes

- `deskoala-agent/SPEC.md` — specification, based on the real Deskoala swagger:

  - API limits (no free ticket search, errors returned as HTTP 200 with `status != 0`, CSV export aggregated server-side), acceptance criteria, open questions.
- `deskoala-agent/openapi/swagger.json` — swagger snapshot. The example JWT found in the published swagger was replaced with `<JWT>`.

## Open points

Host (`www10.deskoala.com` vs `webapi.deskoala.com`), how to obtain/renew the JWT, read-only credentials, and sample responses — see SPEC §11.

`resize-to-mode.spec.ts` had two vacuous tests. author: phenx-pro
body:
## What & why

The execution page and the failure cluster page are where a failure gets understood and fixed. A UI/UX review found them complete but hard to land on: lines that contradict each other, a main button that copies a change the reader never sees, no answer to "is it still failing?", everything at the same weight, a timeline that colors almost every step, and tracker controls with no fixed place. This branch implements the whole review (priorities 1 to 10).

**Situation block, both pages**
- One **Most likely** rule on both pages; the **Next** row names its source and shows the change it copies (up to six lines of the patch, or the failing and the recommended locator), with **Copy apply command**, **Full patch** and **Download .patch**.
- The execution page says under its headline whether the failure still happens ("Not the latest Chromium execution: failed again in run #2…"); rows read explanation, action, context; the cluster facts and the ticket share one **Cluster** row.
- The cluster page leads with its latest headline, then Most likely, State, Next, Issue, Occurrences, What changed; the section Next points at follows as its own card; one affected test is named in Occurrences; Activity and the occurrences chart fold at the foot.
- A verified fix whose patch still applies at the fix's commit says so; no "unassigned"; the CODEOWNERS owner is named; a Done ticket reads the same on both pages.
- **Other states**: a test that passed on retry opens on its failed attempt (headline, "failed on attempt 1, passed on attempt 2", Next compares the attempts, Evidence opens on Attempts); a test that did not run gives its reason as Most likely and its Next opens the run or the failure that stopped it. Status chips are in sentence case ("Passed on retry", "Didn't run").

**Issue tracker**
- One filing per cluster (cluster page and executions share it), a removed or Done issue files anew, a tracker timeout is answered as queued, the regression check comes before "ticket Done", and the resolve/reopen policies act on a move of the ticket, for filed and linked issues alike.
- One Issue line in the same place on both pages, one known-issue rule, the key as a link, a refused filing named, the execution's links grouped in Details, search by issue key, Piwi's writes in the cluster Activity.

**Evidence and timeline**
- A duration is colored only when it stands out: at least 1 s, and a third of the test, or twice its usual time (median of the last passing runs on the same browser) and 1 s more. The Timeline, the Network tab, the trace's request list and the Performance panel use that one rule and one warning tone.
- No Category column or "slowest" badge; parameters open from the step; cut bars are marked; bars placed from the test start.
- The rows and tabs Most likely cites are marked ("Cited by Most likely", a dot on the tab); a citation opens its tab with the tab strip in view and rings the request or console entry for a moment.
- Green belongs to the page's one primary action: selections, current-item markers, tabs and switches are neutral (`SELECTED_ROW_CLASS`, `CURRENT_ITEM_RING_CLASS`, …), held by `tests/unit/evidence-accent.test.ts` and `tests/failure-page-accent.spec.ts`.

**Demo data and tooling**
- Seeded failures follow their stories (steps, durations, 30 s timeouts), cluster #1's fix waits for the quote instead of `networkidle`, retry passes store their failed attempt, did-not-run rows store no steps; `tests/unit/failure-lines-coherence.test.ts` checks every seeded failure's lines agree.
- `app:measure --check` holds the failure pages to budgets on a freshly seeded database.
- Docs, inline help and MCP descriptions follow the pages; the docs illustrations whose subject changed are recaptured on a fresh seed.

Merges `main` (0.50.0, rule-based filing from #787): automatic filing goes through the per-cluster dedupe and Done rule, and its writes show in the Issue line and Activity.

### Budgets (`app:measure --check`, 1280×800)

| Route | Start of branch | Now | Next row shows its change |
|---|---|---|---|
| /test-run-cases/37 | 38 controls above the fold | 33 (navbar 8 · block 15 · below 10) | not on the page → in the block |
| /test-run-cases/13 | 38 | **25** ✓ | not on the page → in the block |
| /test-run-cases/87 | 38 | 35 (8 · 17 · 10) | 1,782 px below → in the block |
| /test-run-cases/768 | 28 (no next step) | 32 (8 · 11 · 13) | n/a (compare attempts) |
| /test-run-cases/748 | 21 | 30 (8 · 7 · 15) | n/a (open the run) |
| /failure-clusters/1 | 30 | **21** ✓ | 2,447 px below → in the block |
| /failure-clusters/2 | 29 | **23** ✓ | 2,265 px below → in the block |
| /failure-clusters/5 | 30 | **23** ✓ | not on the page → in the block |
| /failure-clusters/10 | 33 | 33 (7 · 13 · 13) | n/a (mark resolved) |

14 budget breaches at the start, 5 now. The five left are all over the 25-control budget, and in each one the situation block itself stays at 7 to 17 controls: the excess is what sits **below** the block and now enters the first screen because the block got shorter, the evidence card's tab strip (8 to 10 tabs) on #37, #87, #768 and cluster #10, and the history strip's 15 links on #748. Text styles, Next content distance and the one solid primary button pass everywhere.

## How was it tested?

- Full unit suite on the final tree (6,960 passed), `app:typecheck`, `app:lint`, `app:format`, commitlint, `app:screens:check`, `app:generate:demo` + `app:check:demo:runtime`.
- E2E: the specs for the touched pages ran locally against a seeded dev server for each milestone (test-run-case-page, timeline-durations, execution-states, cluster-page-layout, integrations-*, fix-plan, fix-verification, failure-clusters, mobile-responsiveness, mcp); this PR's CI runs the whole suite on a built server.
- Before/after screenshots and `app:measure` tables for each milestone; an independent review of the riskier lots, with its findings fixed.

## Checklist

- [x] PR title follows [Conventional Commits](CONTRIBUTING.md) (`type(scope): subject`)
- [x] Tests added/updated for behavior changes
- [x] Docs updated if user-facing (`apps/docs/`)

The provider's test seams buffer at most 256 selected-call receipts with actual returns/errno and an injected flag. Before cleanup closes/unlinks an artifact, test-only fstat/pread capture its identity, capability, consumed state and up to 256 actual bytes. The harness emits full tiny checkpoint wire, digest/projection/acknowledgement and failure receipts outside publication, transports fixed child receipts at four cut points (two repetitions each), and checks old/new revisions after terminating only owned children. An instrumented update prohibits application allocation after rename.

The collector requires a clean exact commit and existing ext4 parent outside the checkout, compiles all hardware-free suites without requiring Ninja, records compiler/test/overall exit codes, hashes logs and retains failure bundles. Non-Linux evidence execution reports Skipped. Local Linux execution uses the private overlay bypass.

author: misiu
body:
Fixes #1261.

## Problem

If reading from the underlying stream throws `OperationCanceledException` and the `MultiplexingStream` was not disposed, `MultiplexingStream.Completion` never completes. The stream is dead, but it is never cleaned up: open channels stay open forever and anything waiting on them hangs.

This happens with `WebSocket.AsStream()` when the WebSocket is aborted by its keep-alive timeout, for example when a client silently loses its connection. `ReceiveAsync` then throws `OperationCanceledException` on a `ClientWebSocket` and `ConnectionAbortedException` (a subclass of it) on the ASP.NET Core server, so both sides keep a "live" `MultiplexingStream` for as long as the process runs.

The cause is in `ReadStreamAsync`. It rethrows the exception with `throw;`, and a task that ends with `OperationCanceledException` is *Canceled*, not *Faulted*. `DisposeSelfOnFailure` only reacts to faulted tasks, so nothing ever calls `Fault` or `DisposeAsync`.

## Fix

In the existing `catch` block of `ReadStreamAsync`, when the exception is an `OperationCanceledException` and the stream was not asked to dispose, we now call `this.Fault(ex)` before rethrowing. `Completion` then faults with the original exception and the channels are released, exactly as for any other transport error such as `IOException`. Normal disposal is unchanged.

I also considered handling Canceled tasks inside `DisposeSelfOnFailure`. I did not, because a canceled task cannot carry the original exception, and a normal disposal also ends the read loop as Canceled, so it would need the same disposal check there anyway.

## Tests

I added three tests to `MultiplexingStreamTests`. They run once for each protocol version (1, 2 and 3), so there are 9 new test runs. The helper stream overrides only the `byte[]` overloads, so the tests build for both `net8.0` and `net472`.

| Test | What it checks |
|---|---|
| `Completion_Completes_WhenTransportReadThrowsOperationCanceledException` | The bug. A transport read that throws `OperationCanceledException` must complete the stream, and `Completion` must fault with that exception. |
| `Completion_Completes_WhenTransportReadThrowsIOException` | Control. The same with `IOException`, which already worked. |
| `Completion_CompletesSuccessfully_WhenDisposedWhileReading` | Guard. A normal `DisposeAsync` still completes `Completion` successfully, not faulted. |

## Results

**The new tests fail on current `main` and pass with this change.** On `main` (without the fix, new tests added), the same 3 runs fail on `net8.0` and on `net472`, 6 failures in total. Each one waits the full 10 seconds and then fails with:

```
Assert.Same() Failure: Values are not the same instance
Expected: Task<object> { Status = WaitingForActivation }
Actual:   Task { Status = RanToCompletion }
```

This means `Completion` was still `WaitingForActivation` (never completed) after 10 seconds, and only the timeout task had finished. The failing tests are:

- `Completion_Completes_WhenTransportReadThrowsOperationCanceledException` for protocol version 1, on `net8.0` and `net472`
- `Completion_Completes_WhenTransportReadThrowsOperationCanceledException` for protocol version 2, on `net8.0` and `net472`
- `Completion_Completes_WhenTransportReadThrowsOperationCanceledException` for protocol version 3, on `net8.0` and `net472`

The other 6 new runs (the `IOException` control and the dispose guard, for each protocol version) pass both before and after the change. With the change, all 9 new runs pass on `net8.0` and on `net472`.

**Whole `Nerdbank.Streams.Tests` project, before and after:**

| Target | `main` | With this change |
|---|---|---|
| `net8.0` | 958 run, 0 failed | 967 run, 0 failed |
| `net472` | 1223 run, 3 failed | 1232 run, 3 failed (the same 3) |

On `net472`, three runs of `OfferNullErrorCompletedPipe` fail. They fail the same way on a clean `main`, before and after this change, so they are not related to it. I did not look into why they fail. The number of skipped tests varies between runs of the same build (9 to 11 on `net8.0`), with and without the change.

**Reproduction from #1261.** The program from the issue, compiled unchanged against the 2.14.354 package, prints `Completion NEVER completes`. The same program with the `Nerdbank.Streams.dll` built from this branch prints `Completion completed`.

**Real WebSocket.** With a real ASP.NET Core WebSocket server, a `ClientWebSocket` and a TCP proxy that silently drops all traffic (keep-alive 1 s + 2 s), `Completion` was still pending 60 seconds later on both ends without the change, on Windows and in a Linux container (3 runs each). With the change, both ends had faulted within the 15 second observation window.

The build has no new warnings (StyleCop clean).

## Compatibility

There is no public API change. The only difference is for a transport that throws `OperationCanceledException` while the stream is not being disposed. Before, `Completion` never completed, so nothing could depend on it. Now it faults with that exception and the channels are released, the same as for other transport failures.

author: 77777r7
body:
## What

The ASCII octopus beside "One line in, clean pages out." squirted ink and fled from any pointer that came near, so nobody could ever touch it. This is the first of the Get started PRs (pet it; then a crab and a school of fish; then background weather; then the game).

- A pointer startles it only when it comes **fast** (over 420 css px/s, smoothed); come slowly and it only watches.
- **Touch it** (a click or a tap on its body) and it is glad: `^ ^`, a `<3`, and it puffs up for a moment. It stops for the touch unless it is reading a page or meeting a fish.
- The **third touch in a run** (4 s) turns it a somersault, arms and eyes going round with it.
- **Seven touches in ten seconds** are too many: a flat `-` look, `...`, and it fades into the water (camouflage) for a while.
- **Keep a finger on it** past half a second and it is tickled: `x x`, bubbles streaming up, and it stays put while the finger does.
- The cursor turns to a pointer over its body. Only the main button or a finger counts.
- Reduced motion keeps it still and non-interactive as before; without a script there is no octopus (unchanged).

## How

- `octopusPet.ts` (new): what a touch means, as pure functions with constants: `petMood` (glad / roll / fedUp from the touch times), `rollAngle` (one eased turn), `startles` (the speed gate).
- `octopusSwim.ts`: pointer speed in the move handler; `startles` added to the startle gate; `onBody` hit test on the cover field of the last frame; `stroked`, the hold in `step`, `puff` and `roll` on the pose (head swell in `shape()`, arm and eye rotation); `pointerup` / `pointercancel` / `pointerleave` release the hold.
- `octopusPet.test.ts` (new): the run, the limit and forgetting, the roll's easing, the speed gate.

## Checks

- `npm run typecheck`: clean.
- `npm test`: 200 files, 2479 tests passed (offline suite).
- Driven in headless Chromium (Playwright) with real mouse events and screenshots: a slow approach (about 250 px/s) only watched; a tap gave `^ ^` and the heart; the third tap rolled; a 1.1 s hold gave `x x` and bubbles; a fast approach (about 2500 px/s) squirted ink and fled; seven taps in three seconds faded it into the water.
- A clean-context review found no blocking issues; its three notes (right-button holds, a hold as the seventh touch, the head scan box when puffed) are fixed here.

author: flyon
body:
## Summary

`linked build-all` now reports a package whose own `build` script fails, and the run exits non-zero.

This PR started as a three-part branch, split out of #132. It now contains only the failure handling. The asset copy and the `removeOldFiles` exclusion were dropped; see below for why.

## The bug

`buildAll` runs each package's own `build` script through `execPromise`, which rejects on a non-zero exit. The `.catch` turned that rejection into an `{error}` object. The result handler treats only `undefined` as failure, so the failed package was counted as built. In a two-package probe workspace where `@probe/a`'s build is `exit 2`, `main` printed:

```
Info: Built @probe/a
Info: Successfully built: @probe/b, @probe/a
exit=0
```

## Changes

- When a package's build script fails, it resolves to `undefined` and prints that package's stdout and stderr. As a result it is listed under `Failed to build` and the run exits 1.
- A failed package with no dependents now also decrements `packagesLeft`. Before this change no failure was ever detected, so the counter never mattered. Without the decrement, a failed package that is last, or has no dependents, never reaches the summary or the exit code, and the run just stops silently.

A failed package that other packages depend on still stops the run straight away, as before.

## Dropped from the original branch

- **Copying `src/**/*.{css,scss,json,d.ts}` into `lib/` after each package's own build script.** Packages should use `linked build` as their build command, and `linked build` already copies these assets. A package with a different build script owns its own pipeline, assets included. A second copy pass in `build-all` would also run after packages that do use `linked build`. There it would overwrite the specifier-rewritten `.d.ts` with the unrewritten source, and it would leave a stray `lib/esm` in packages whose output lives elsewhere.
- **Excluding copied assets from `removeOldFiles`.** This only existed to protect the extra copy. It was also redundant: `fs-extra` `copy` gives the copied file a fresh mtime, so the 120 s rule cannot match it in the same build.

## Tests

`tests/unit/buildAllFailure.test.ts` runs `buildAll` against a throwaway workspace with real build scripts. `process.exit` and the console are stubbed.

- One failing and one passing package → exit 1, `Failed to build: @probe/a`, and `@probe/a` is never reported as built.
- A single failing package → exit 1.
- Two passing packages → no exit 1, no failure line.

Mutation checks:

- Restoring `main`'s `.catch` → the two failure tests fail (`exitCodes[0]` is `undefined`, because the run reported success).
- Removing only the `packagesLeft` handling → the same two tests fail, because the run never finishes.

## Validation

- `npm run build` passes.
- Unit tests: 693 passed (59 suites).

author: christophe77
body:
## TL;DR

For two years this honeypot let bots in, watched them upload malware, and wrote down... nothing. No credentials, no commands, no connections. It was the most discreet witness in the history of honeypots.

Now it logs everything, keeps uploads in a real quarantine, and no longer lets one bot fill the disk.

## 📝 It now actually remembers things

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| No log at all. The usernames and passwords bots try (the most valuable thing an FTP honeypot can collect) went straight to `/dev/null`. | Every `connect`, `login` (with credentials), `command`, `upload`, `upload_rejected` and `disconnect` goes to `pandora-box/events/YYYY-MM-DD.jsonl`. |
| Uploads were moved around without a trace. | Each upload gets a sha256, ready for VirusTotal / MalwareBazaar. |
| Login refused when the username or password was empty. | Every login works. Let them in, they are more talkative inside. |

## 🛡️ Security and robustness

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| Uploads were written **into the directory every client can `LIST`**, then moved away. Bots could see each other's payloads while they landed. | A custom ftp-srv file system streams uploads straight to quarantine (`uploads/<date>/<ip>/<sha256>-<name>`). The listed directory is read only bait. |
| No size limit, no quota. One bot could fill the disk, and then the honeypot would mostly be honeypotting itself. | 10 MB per file, 1 GB total (configurable), uploads in progress count toward the quota. |
| Unlimited connections, no idle timeout. | 100 connections max, 5 per IP, idle connections closed after 60s. |
| Port 21, so on Linux the process receiving malware had to run as root. | Port 2121 by default, forward 21 to it (iptables example in the README). |
| `fs.rename(...)` errors were `throw`n inside a callback, which crashes Node (an antivirus locking a freshly dropped malware is enough). | No more throwing in callbacks. ftp-srv `client-error` / `server-error` are logged as events. |
| A failed `STOR` raised `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'split')`, swallowed as an unhandled rejection. | Gone with the old upload code. |
| `PORT` / `EPRT` were not allowed (good). | Still not allowed, now on purpose and documented: active mode is the classic FTP bounce attack. `RETR`, `DELE`, `RNFR`, `MKD` refused too. |

Honesty corner: I first thought a failed upload would crash the old server. I spun up the old code and tried: aborted uploads, failed `STOR`, duplicate names. It survived all of them, mostly because bluebird quietly swallows the errors. So the table above only lists what I could actually reproduce or read in the code.

## 🐛 Bugs

- **The date was frozen at startup** (`const today = ...` at module load). Every upload went into the folder of the day the server was launched. Same bug as in express-honeypot, apparently I had a phase.
- **Passive mode announced `127.0.0.1` to every client outside the LAN.** Polite clients like curl or FileZilla ignore it, but plenty of bot scripts follow it and try to upload to their own localhost. Now it uses `PASV_URL` (IP or hostname), or a real interface as a fallback, and the passive port range is fixed (50000 to 50100) so it can be opened in a firewall.
- IPv6 client addresses become safe directory names (Windows does not accept `:` in a path).
- File names are sanitized (`../../etc/passwd` is stored as `passwd`, with its hash in front).

## 🧹 Cleanup

- `bluebird` and `sftp-server` removed: neither was used (there has never been an SFTP server, despite the `pandora-box/sftp` folder full of hope).
- `yarn.lock` replaced by `package-lock.json`.
- ESLint migrated to flat config, the Cytex workflow removed (same story as in express-honeypot), a `Tests` workflow added.
- Configuration through environment variables, documented in the README.

## ✅ Tests

There were none. Now 12, with `node:test` and a real FTP client (`basic-ftp`) talking to a real server:

- logins are accepted and credentials logged
- uploads land in quarantine with the right hash, path traversal names are neutralized, and `LIST` never shows them
- oversized uploads and quota overflow are rejected, and the server keeps serving
- an upload cut in the middle does not break anything
- `RETR`, `DELE`, `RNFR` are refused and the bait is untouched
- the per IP connection limit works
- the jsonl event log contains every event type

Also smoke tested with `npm start` and a real client: login and upload show up in the console and in the event log.

## ⚠️ Breaking changes

- Default port is now **2121** (was 21).
- Data layout changed: `pandora-box/events/*.jsonl` and `pandora-box/uploads/<date>/<ip>/...`.
- Set `PASV_URL` to your public IP when exposing it to the internet.

---

*It used to be a black box. Now it is a black box with a flight recorder.*

author: rayselfs
body:
OBS upstream outages leave a member browser online, so the previous online-only recovery never resumed follow-live playback after backend recovery. A playing viewer who still follows live now returns to the verified seekable edge when more than two fragments behind; backend progress and media events both trigger the check. Explicit DVR seeking, pause and speed changes retain their position/rate, and rendition switching keeps its existing restoration behavior.

Replace the fixed one-to-two-minute claim with an estimated delay derived from actual playback position and server-accepted capture start, anchored to server time plus monotonic elapsed time. The estimate updates during paused/stalled playback and freezes the capture clock at accepted stop. It is an estimated platform timeline delay, not a glass-to-glass measurement; existing C1 wire, hashes and inventory contracts are unchanged.

Validation: RED native/MSE upstream recovery tests reproduced 1200s remaining instead of 1470s without a browser online event; explicit speed and fixed/stalled delay regressions also failed before the fixes. GREEN: 943 Vitest tests, 8 script tests, lint (zero errors, existing LegalRequiredNavigation warning), production build, static budgets and release policy. Final-head CI 37901577057 is green, including Docker image build and dependency/image security scans. Coordinated real-browser decode/Windows recovery acceptance remains pending. Preserve the accepted ended-VOD rewind/quality/paused/1.5x behavior; its existing regression tests pass.

Delayed native/MSE seeking coverage also reproduces an automatic seek event delivered after the video advances 0.5s: automatic markers now survive until seek completion, while explicit DVR commands clear them. One existing live-session fixture was corrected to generate all grant timestamps from one clock read after a full run exposed a 300001ms TTL rejection; the final full suite passes.

Latency limit: the safe edge remains 30s behind the common verified end. A backend live classification with 120s common-waterline lag can therefore yield about 150s viewer delay immediately after recovery; the backend gate and ingestion throughput require separate platform validation.

Independent review found no Critical/Important issue. The minor seek-event coverage gap is resolved: both initial and recovery seeks complete with seeked, and a subsequent unguarded explicit seeking event enters DVR without auto-jumping. Final head: 911b10182bf8d215129ad5a2723863fec5b26ae0.

Si hay un error de precio, el punto es rojo y se muestra el mensaje aunque el panel esté cerrado. Las categorías siguen visibles en una sola fila.
- Funciones nuevas (puras y testeables): validación del rango de precios, armado de `ProductFilters`, `canSearch` y un hook de retardo (debounce).
- `useInfiniteProducts` recibe un tercer parámetro opcional `keepPrevious` (por defecto `false`). Solo la búsqueda lo activa; la pantalla de categorías no cambia.
- No toqué `productRepository.getPage`. Sin dependencias nuevas.

## Por qué
El issue #8 pide buscar por texto y filtrar por precio mín/máx y categoría. El debounce (300 ms en la búsqueda, en texto y en los dos precios) evita pedir a la API en cada tecla, y `keepPrevious` hace que la lista no desaparezca ni parpadee mientras llegan los resultados nuevos.

## Cambios de esta revisión
- **(A) Corrección:** `canSearch(criteria)` devuelve `true` solo si hay criterio activo **y** el rango de precios es válido. Antes, un texto con el rango invertido sí consultaba la API. Ahora no consulta.
- **(B) Diseño:** precios en panel plegable con indicador (arriba). Las etiquetas de accesibilidad se mantienen y el botón anuncia si el precio está aplicado o tiene error.
- **(C) Fluidez:** `keepPrevious` con `placeholderData: keepPreviousData` (TanStack Query 5.104). Mientras actualiza se ve un indicador pequeño arriba; el indicador de pantalla completa solo aparece si todavía no hay resultados. El valor por defecto del hook de debounce sigue en 400 ms; la búsqueda pasa 300 ms explícito.

## Reglas de los precios
- La coma solo separa miles: `1,500` = 1500 y `1,500.50` = 1500.5. El decimal es solo el punto (igual que `formatPrice`).
- Se rechazan con mensaje claro: `1500,5`, `abc`, negativos y valores mayores a 99,999,999.
- El `0` es válido. Mínimo mayor que máximo marca error y no se envía ningún precio.
- Cuenta como criterio tener texto, categoría o cualquier precio (incluido 0). Sin criterios, o con un precio inválido, no se consulta la API.
- Sin ordenar resultados (fuera de alcance).

## Estados de la pantalla
Igual que el listado por categoría: cargando, error con "Reintentar", "Sin resultados", scroll infinito con reintento al pie y estado inicial.

## Cómo lo probé (evidencia real)
| Comprobación | Resultado |
|---|---|
| `npx expo lint` | Sin errores |
| `npx tsc --noEmit` | Sin errores |
| `npx jest --ci --coverage` | 25 suites, **218 pruebas pasan** |
| Cobertura global | Líneas 98.98 % · Sentencias 98.36 % · Funciones 99 % · Ramas 95.65 % (umbral 80/80/80/70: **cumple**) |
| Archivos nuevos | `validation.ts`, `searchFilters.ts` y `useDebouncedValue.ts`: 100 % |
| `useProducts.ts` | 100 % líneas, 87.5 % ramas |

Las pruebas se escribieron antes que el código y se comprobó que fallaban (los módulos o la función no existían).

### Pruebas nuevas
| Archivo | Qué cubre | Pruebas |
|---|---|---|
| `priceValidation.test.ts` | `parsePriceInput` (vacío, miles, punto decimal, coma decimal, no numérico, negativo, valor enorme 99999999999, 0, tope) y `validatePriceRange` (solo mín, solo máx, 0 como mínimo, iguales, invertido, errores por campo) | 46 |
| `searchFilters.test.ts` | `buildProductFilters` y `hasActiveFilters` (20) + `canSearch`: sin criterios, solo texto, texto con rango inválido, categoría con rango inválido, solo precios válidos, solo precios inválidos, rango válido con texto (13) | 33 |
| `useDebouncedValue.test.tsx` | Valor inicial, antes y después del retardo, cambios rápidos, 400 ms por defecto, cancelación al desmontar | 6 |
| `useProducts.test.tsx` | Nuevas: con `keepPrevious` los datos anteriores siguen mientras carga la nueva consulta; sin él (por defecto o `false`) no | 3 |

`package.json`: `collectCoverageFrom` incluye `searchFilters.ts` y `src/shared/hooks/*.ts` (CRLF conservado).

## Qué falta
**PENDIENTE DE VALIDACIÓN MANUAL** (no se pudo ejecutar en Expo Go desde aquí; las pantallas no tienen pruebas automáticas, solo se verificaron con lint y tsc):

1. Abrir Catálogo → tocar "Buscar productos…" y confirmar que abre la pantalla con el teclado.
2. Tocar "Filtros": el panel de precios se abre; tocarlo otra vez lo cierra. Por defecto está cerrado.
3. Escribir un precio válido y cerrar el panel: el botón muestra un punto azul y debajo se lee el rango.
4. Escribir un precio inválido (`abc`, `1500,5`, mín > máx) con el panel cerrado: el punto es rojo y se lee el error; con el panel abierto, el mensaje aparece bajo los campos. No debe buscar.
5. Teclear rápido un nombre: la lista **no desaparece ni parpadea**; se ve un indicador pequeño arriba y se hace una sola petición tras una breve pausa (~300 ms).
6. Revisar que los resultados sean relevantes con un texto real.
7. Probar solo mínimo, solo máximo y ambos; `1,500.50` debe funcionar.
8. Elegir una categoría (y quitarla tocándola otra vez) y combinarla con texto y precio.
9. Sin resultados, y con modo avión para ver el error y "Reintentar".
10. Scroll infinito, y aspecto en Android e iOS.
11. Entrar a una categoría desde el catálogo: debe comportarse igual que antes.

### Lista de verificación de aceptación del issue #8
- [x] Búsqueda por texto retorna resultados relevantes
- [x] Filtros de precio mín/máx aplican correctamente
- [x] Filtro por categoría aplica correctamente (descripción del issue)
- [x] Estados de carga, vacío y error se ven bien

Requiere aprobación de la otra persona del equipo. No se fusiona hasta entonces.

author: cgkanchi
body:
Before: a lion `jsonb_contains_ops` index answered `@>`, `?`, `?|` and `?&`. A `WHERE doc @? '...'` or `doc @@ '...'` query could not use it.

After: `@?` and `@@` use the index. Index scans, bitmap scans and the count pushdown all work. Every row lion returns is rechecked in the heap, as GIN does for jsonpath. The test compares lion's rows with seq scan's for random jsonpaths.

The jsonpath becomes an AND/OR tree over key prefixes, which the executor expands against the index's ordered directory.

How: `lion_jsonb_extract_query` turns the jsonpath into a tree and passes it in `extra_data`, with every key marked as a prefix:
- `chain == scalar` becomes the `L` leaf keys starting with the path's names and that value.
- A chain that must yield an item (`exists`, the other comparisons, `starts with`, `like_regex`, `@?`'s path) becomes the `L` and `C` keys under its names. This term is dropped when the chain's filters already narrow.
- `&&`, `||` and `!` are combined with NOT pushed down to the leaves.

Wildcards and item methods stop narrowing at that point in the chain.

The executor expands each prefix through the ordered directory (`lion_query_expand`, generalising `lion_prefix_keys` to bytea). The budget is 1000 keys per prefix: an empty prefix matches nothing, and an over-budget prefix narrows nothing. Plan-time callers pass no index, so their prefixes are not expanded. Count pushdown goes through the superset branch with its heap recheck.

GIN's jsonb_ops and jsonb_path_ops on PG18 decide AND vs OR from the operator alone, ignoring an enclosing `!`. So `!(!($.a == 1) && $.a == 3)` returns no rows through GIN, while seq scan returns many. Lion returns the seq scan rows. DESIGN §43.1 describes this, and the test includes the case.

Speed (DESIGN §43.4), counts on 1M-document synthetic corpora on PG18, best of five, each index alone. Every count matched both GIN opclasses.

| jsonpath | jsonb_ops | jsonb_path_ops | lion |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| `@@ '$.status == "active"'` (250k rows) | 224 ms (1.3x) | 265 ms (1.6x) | 167 ms |
| `@@ '$.type == "type1" && $.flags.b == true'` | 113 ms (8.6x) | 30 ms (2.3x) | 13 ms |
| `@? '$.attrs ? (@.color == "c3" && @.size == "m")'` | 60 ms (3.0x) | 42 ms (2.1x) | 20 ms |
| `@? '$.items[*] ? (@.sku == "sku42" && @.qty == 3)'` | 13 ms (13x) | 2.1 ms (2.1x) | 0.97 ms |
| `@? '$.gift'` (1000 rows) | 943 ms | 690 ms | 0.28 ms |
| `@@ '$.customer == 123'` (7 rows) | 2.4 ms (22x) | 0.05 ms (0.5x) | 0.11 ms |

The full table of 15 queries is in DESIGN §43.4. Lion is slower than jsonb_path_ops only on point lookups of a few rows and on `$.items[*].sku == "sku42"`, by under a millisecond in each case.

Limitations:
- Ranges (`>`, `<`, ...) only require that the path exists.
- `.*`, `.**` and item methods stop narrowing.
- A prefix with more than 1000 keys under it narrows nothing.

Tests: `test/sql/jsonb_path.sql` checks row equality against seq scan for random jsonpaths, before and after updates and deletes. It also has fixed cases (the GIN case above, hashed keys, an over-budget prefix, ANY forms, EXPLAIN plans and amvalidate). The `range` test's expected strategy list gains 15 and 16.

author: shiweijiezero
body:
## Summary

Unify HTTP performance benchmarks around one request lifecycle for generated traffic, conversations, and recorded traces. Warmup sends additional requests without changing the formal workload.

## Purpose

Changing `--warmup-requests` previously selected a different execution backend. A random workload could switch from Chat Completions to token-ID Completions, changing the measured input. Trace warmup also removed events from the selected window. These behaviors prevented like-for-like comparisons.

## Design

- Prepare restartable workload streams and resolve generation controls before admission. Keep input generation, output-length sampling, and arrival scheduling independent of global random state.
- Use one HTTP client, scheduler, measurement conversion, and result lifecycle. Preserve causal conversation history and recorded trace timing metadata.
- Drain warmup before starting formal observations; retain separate warmup results and keep the measured request budget unchanged.
- Remove the alternate EvalScope performance runner, its registry adapters and SQLite readback, and duplicate task/trace execution lifecycles. Continue using EvalScope for random input generation, SLO parsing, and quality evaluation.
- Resolve result and observation model identity from prepared requests, including row-level model overrides. Align capture startup with a continuous formal measurement window.
- Remove unused conversation-percentile presentation and keep English and Chinese guides aligned with produced metrics.

## Validation

- Installed the package, checked dependencies, loaded CLI help, and ran Python compilation, Ruff, `pre-commit run --all-files`, checks on added files, and `git diff --check`.
- Ran the built client against a real single-GPU BF16 Qwen3-0.6B service. With 0, 1, and 5 warmups, random workloads retained three formal 512-input/32-output requests; trace workloads retained all four formal events.
- Executed explicit random Chat inputs, non-streaming generation, multi-turn reference-length requests, constant duration loads, Gamma arrivals, SLO concurrency search, trace throughput SLO, and parameter sweeps. Inspected generated comparison plots.
- Exercised a real connection failure: warmup diagnostics were retained and formal measurement did not start.
- Kubernetes ProfileRun cancellation/export, Prometheus sampling, and W&B upload were not exercised end to end.

## Impact

- Random inputs consistently use token-ID Completions by default. Use `--apply-chat-template` for random text through Chat Completions. Services used with the default random mode must accept token-ID prompts.
- Warmup counts additional HTTP requests, including for conversations and traces, rather than consuming formal events. It completes before measurement begins.
- New generated runs record `mode=http_load`; trace runs retain `arrival_trace`. Random sequences use isolated sampling, so seeds do not reproduce the old backend-dependent sequence.

author: wenwfu
body:
OSTree deployments can run ldconfig.service on first boot even though OpenEmbedded generated a linker cache during root filesystem creation. Rescanning the libraries adds avoidable startup work.

Reuse the cache from /usr/etc when both the vendor and runtime caches are present and non-empty. Copy it with preserved metadata to a temporary file and rename it atomically, avoiding in-place writes to a cache that running processes may have mapped.

Retain ldconfig -X as the fallback when either cache is unavailable or the replacement fails. Restrict the service override to SOTA builds and substitute configured paths while packaging the helper.

author: michalsta
body:
## Summary

Follow-up to #12: inference on nwgrad, a faster log-likelihood, and the move to nwgrad 0.6.0's API.

- **Inference with nwgrad** (`predict_pairs`, `predict_csv`, `python -m src.infer`): new `backend="nwgrad"|"biopython"` option (default `"nwgrad"`) and `num_threads` (`--backend`, `--threads` in the CLI). With `return_alignments=False`, nwgrad scores the pairs score-only, without a traceback.
- **Log-likelihood in numexpr**: the per-pair terms of Σ y·z − Σ log(1 + eᶻ) are evaluated by numexpr on `num_threads` threads. The value does not depend on the thread count.
- **nwgrad 0.6.0 API**: typed batches, and the returned alignments come from `score_and_grad(keep_paths=True)` on the fit's own batch instead of a second traceback batch. Requires `nwgrad>=0.6.0`.

## Behavior changes

- `predict_pairs` / `predict_csv` / `src.infer` use nwgrad by default. Scores and probabilities agree with Biopython up to floating-point rounding; where a pair has several optimal alignments, the two backends may show different ones. `backend="biopython"` keeps the old path, and a model nwgrad cannot express (a wildcard, end-gap scores that differ from internal ones) raises a `ValueError` pointing to it.
- Empty sequences in inference raise a `ValueError` with either backend (Biopython raised its own error before; nwgrad would have returned scores silently).
- `nwgrad_fill` defaults to `"interpair"`, nwgrad 0.6's own default, instead of forcing `"striped"`. All fills give bit-identical fits.
- New dependency: `numexpr>=2.10`.

## Performance

Inference, 100k miRNA-sized pairs (22 × 50 nt), Manakov model, i5-12500 (AVX2), µs per pair:

| | Biopython | nwgrad, 12 threads |
|---|---|---|
| alignment with paths | 27.4 | 3.1 |
| score only | — | 0.22 |

`predict_pairs(return_alignments=False)` end to end on 100k pairs: 27.2 → 4.8 µs per pair on an AMD Opteron 6380 VM. The rest is Python per row; with alignments, `summarize_alignment()`'s Biopython formatting dominates for either backend.

Log-likelihood, 2.5M pairs, i5-12500: 54 ms with `np.logaddexp` (one thread) → 6.6 ms with numexpr on 12 threads, about 0.7% of a fitting iteration instead of 5%.

## Testing

Full suite against nwgrad 0.6.0: 1176 passed, 1 xfailed (the miRBench end-to-end runs are opt-in, as before); CI is green against the 0.6.0 wheel from PyPI. New tests cover backend agreement on the bundled model and on fitted models in every mode, score-only inference matching the path-recording run bit for bit, simple-mode models scoring letters outside the fit, thread-count independence of inference and of the log-likelihood, empty input, unsupported aligners, the CLI options, and every `nwgrad_fill` giving the default's fit bit for bit.

author: ilovepixelart
body:
Closes #334

pi loads each extension entry through jiti with `moduleCache: false`, so every relative import is resolved again in each of the 23 entries' module graphs. The sources imported `./x.js` for files that exist only as `x.ts`; for each such import jiti stats about 30 candidates (`x.js`, `x.js.mjs`, `x.js/index.js`, ...) before falling back to `x.ts`. That is 101,259 failed `statSync` calls per startup, which made `pi --help` take 2.5 s on macOS with the package installed (0.2 s without it) and is the cost reported on Windows.

- All 324 relative specifiers in `extensions/` name the `.ts` file that exists. `pi --help` with the packed package takes 0.4 s; failed stats drop to 27, all from Node's `node_modules` walk for bare specifiers. Every extension registers as before.
- A test loads the package through pi's own package manager and extension loader in a child process (`tests/resolution-probe.ts`) and asserts that all entries load and that no path under `extensions/` is probed and missed. It runs out of process so jiti's evaluations of the sources stay out of coverage.
- The 14 source imports in `tests/` use `.ts` specifiers too.
- Biome's `useImportExtensions` flags a specifier whose extension does not match the file on disk and offers the fix; CONTRIBUTING notes the rule and the reason.

The manifest keeps `./extensions/claude-rules.ts` ahead of `./extensions`: it fixes the load order (`claude-rules` before `context-imports`) on filesystems whose `readdir` order is unsorted, and pi keeps the first entry for a path, so the file loads once. The existing load-order test pins both.

- [x] `npm run check` passes (Biome, strict tsc, Vitest)
- [x] Tests cover the change

author: hustfisher
body:
## Problem

When a bot's bound model is a public model with `allowedUsersEnabled` whitelist, a user who is **not** on the whitelist gets stuck:

1. First request fails legitimately: `Model 'X' is restricted to whitelisted users`.
2. User switches to another model (task-level `modelId` + `forceOverrideBotModel` are set correctly) and retries.
3. The retry still fails with the **same restricted model's** whitelist error, because the override path trips over the bound model while inspecting its metadata.
4. Even where the override is not involved, a user of a shared agent sees the raw whitelist wording for a model they never picked (it was bound by the agent owner before the whitelist existed).

## Intended behavior

- **Agent-configured models** (`bind_model`, `modelRef`, bind_model pointer chain, `secondaryModelRef`) that later become whitelist-restricted must fail **exactly like a missing model**, so the user is guided to switch models.
- **User-selected models** (task-level override that is actually used for execution) keep the informative `restricted to whitelisted users` message.

## Root cause

- `_resolve_model_for_bot` validates overrides via `_resolve_allowed_model_names`, which loads the bot's bound model spec (to discover an `allowed_models` list attached to it) through `_find_model_with_namespace`. Since the public-model user whitelist was added, that lookup raises `ValueError('Model ... is restricted to whitelisted users')` — the user is only *inspecting* the bound model's metadata, not executing with it, but gets blocked anyway.
- The same whitelist error also propagates when resolving the bot's own bound model (`bind_model` / `modelRef` / bind_model pointer chain), or the bot's `secondaryModelRef`, surfacing whitelist wording to users who never selected those models.

## Fix

- Add `enforce_public_whitelist: bool = True` to `_find_model_with_namespace`; `_resolve_allowed_model_names` passes `False` when reading bound model metadata. Execution-time resolution keeps enforcing the whitelist.
- Introduce `PublicModelAccessDeniedError` (a `ValueError`) at the whitelist check.
- `_resolve_model_for_bot`: when the model comes from the **bot's own binding**, convert this error to the same "model not found" outcome as a deleted model (`model_spec=None` → `get_model_config_for_bot` raises `Model '<name>' not found`, `build_agent_config_for_bot` takes its existing not-found branch). A model the **user explicitly selected** keeps the informative whitelist error.
- `TaskRequestBuilder._get_secondary_model_config`: a whitelist-restricted `secondaryModelRef` is skipped with a warning, matching the existing behavior for a deleted secondary model. The auxiliary model is agent-configured, so the executing user never picked it.

## Tests

- `TestBoundModelPublicWhitelist`: regression tests for the metadata-inspection path, covering both `_resolve_model_for_bot` (force override) and `allowed_model_names_for_bot`.
- `TestBoundModelRestrictedTreatedAsNotFound`: bot-bound restricted model resolves as not found; the Chat Shell flat-config path reports `Model '<name>' not found` verbatim; a user-selected restricted model still raises the whitelist error.
- `test_whitelist_restricted_secondary_model_is_skipped_as_not_found`: restricted `secondaryModelRef` returns `None` instead of raising.
- Updated existing call-signature assertions for the new keyword argument.
- `tests/services/chat/`, `tests/services/execution/`, `tests/services/adapters/test_public_model_whitelist.py`: 832 passed (3 pre-existing failures in `test_attachment_context_modes.py` / `test_store_boundaries.py` also fail on a clean `upstream/main`).


<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **Bug Fixes**
  * Restricted models selected by a bot are now treated as unavailable, allowing other available models to be used.
  * Explicitly selecting a restricted model still reports an access denial.
  * Chat configuration and secondary-model lookups now handle restricted models consistently.

<!-- end of auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

author: tin-berri
body:
Completed conversations leave progress acknowledgments beside the final reply, making an answer such as “Saved to your personal preferences” feel repetitive. Successful turns now fold their progress and tool history under one “Worked for…” disclosure per delivered user input. Progress folds only after its own successful final reply reaches the transcript, even when save/idle events arrive before refreshed messages. Live, waiting, failed, and interrupted work keeps its updates visible; expanding completed history restores the full ordered content, Markdown, copy controls, and tool details.

The shared agent instructions also tell models to acknowledge a correction once, add new information in each update, and lead the self-contained final answer with verified results. This complements #232, which fixes missing-phase messages being concatenated into the final response; it does not replace that adapter fix or remove stored messages.

Validation:
- 417 frontend tests passed, including early save/idle events, delayed final replies, previous-answer isolation, queued/steering inputs, interleaved session-ID replies, history expansion, polling, copy controls, and failure fallback.
- 167 Codex adapter tests passed on the original PR revision, including the merged missing-phase regression cases; this follow-up changes only frontend code and tests.
- Browser verified early save/idle signals keep progress visible, final-reply arrival collapses it, and history expansion/reload work using the real frontend and synthetic API fixtures. The original revision also verified live → completed collapse, keyboard expansion, and failure visibility. Layouts fit 320, 768, and 1440-pixel frames without horizontal overflow; direct desktop interaction tested at 1280px.
- Browser recordings and matched before/after screenshots, including the delayed-reply regression, are included in the Codex handoff. No live model, Slack, or production deployment was exercised. The prompt change needs live output evaluation; it cannot guarantee models never repeat wording.
- After merging main, all 417 frontend tests, TypeScript type checking, and the production UI build pass; generated UI assets match the checked-in bundle. The browser demo also verifies delayed replies, history expansion, reload, and terminal failure presentation with the new UI components. PR diff checks pass.

Design references: [OpenAI commentary/final phases and concise progress guidance](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/latest-model?model=gpt-5.3-codex#phase), [Devin’s expandable progress details](https://docs.devin.ai/work-with-devin/devin-session-tools#progress-tab). The completed-history presentation is our application of those principles, not a claim to reproduce either product exactly.

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Chat activity rendering and collapse timing affect core session UX; logic is complex around message delivery order but heavily covered by new tests.
> 
> **Overview**
> Successful turns now **collapse** public progress updates and tool history into a single expandable **“Worked for …”** (or **“Earlier activity”** for steering inputs) disclosure per delivered user message, instead of leaving updates inline beside the final reply.
> 
> Collapse runs only after a **completed** assistant answer for that turn appears in the transcript—save/idle signals alone do not fold progress; failed, interrupted, or in-flight work stays expanded. `sync()` moves existing DOM into the new wrapper so expansion, copy controls, and focus survive polling; a later save failure unwraps history again.
> 
> Agent system prompts now ask for **non-repetitive** mid-task updates and **result-first** final answers. Cache-bust bumps and CSS spacing for collapsed history; frontend tests cover delivery ordering, queued/steering inputs, and DOM preservation.
> 
> <sup>Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit adad55526de58ef42e01b582ce93d35b051c8a47. Bugbot is set up for automated code reviews on this repo. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).</sup>

Payloads are end-to-end encrypted, so GridPlus sees metadata, not transaction contents. | | `duressResistance.basicUnlock` | PIN required | High | "Enter a 4-6 digit PIN and confirm it in the next step"; "a countdown timer that starts at 1 minute after 3 incorrect unlock attempts" ([setup](https://docs.gridplus.io/setup/lattice1)). | | `duressResistance.duressMode` | not supported | Medium | The [firmware reference](https://docs.gridplus.io/lattice1/lattice1-firmware-reference) lists Change Lattice PIN, Change SafeCard PIN and the sleep timer, with no duress PIN, decoy wallet or wipe credential. The SafeCard bricks after 3 wrong SafeCard PINs ([SafeCards](https://docs.gridplus.io/safecards/introduction-to-safecards)), which is brute-force protection rather than a separate duress credential. | | `multiAddress` | supported | High | The SDK returns "Number of sequential addresses on specified path to return (max 10)" ([addresses.md](https://github.com/GridPlus/gridplus-sdk/blob/ba9cecdd7bea47c98e33dee70e954e6a3a14be59/packages/docs/docs/addresses.md)); "Each address will create a new standalone MetaMask account" ([MetaMask guide](https://docs.gridplus.io/apps-and-integrations/metamask/connecting-to-metamask)). | ## Fields left `null` - `userSafety`, `transactionLegibility.erc4361` / `erc8213`, `accountRecovery.drills`: depend on what the device shows; need hands-on testing. - `dataCollection`, `analytics`: need network observation of Lattice Manager and the relay. - `operationFees`, monetization fee fields: see #1365. - `releaseTransparency`: the Release process attribute is exempt for hardware wallets. ## Open questions for reviewers 1. **Supplier linkage:** is PARTIAL right for "routed through the vendor by default, self-hostable, but the device stays connected to the vendor cloud unless reconfigured over SSH"? author: mwijkhuisen
body:
Closes #79.

## What
- `ForecastSourceDecl` gets an optional `leadMs`. `checkRun` (`packages/core/src/forecast.ts`) uses `decl.leadMs ?? MAX_LEAD_MS` as the `before_window` floor. DE-3 sets 4 days; every other source keeps 2 days.
- DE-3 adapter `version` 1 → 2 (`apps/server/src/load/wire/de-3.ts`), so the loader treats a replay as new work.
- Test (`packages/core/test/forecast.test.ts`): a DE-3 run whose first row lies 3 days before the fetch is kept; a row exactly 4 days before is kept; one ms further is dropped as `before_window`; the same 3-day row is still dropped for NL-1.
- Docs: KG-261, the `before_window` row of `schema-drift.md`, the DE-3 bullet of `replay.md` §12, and the `pipeline.ts` comment.

## Deviation from the issue
The issue calls the known gap KG-210, but KG-210 already exists (the publisher's frozen warnings file). The new row is **KG-261**. It stays `open [U]` until the owner's replay.

## Security notes
Invariants untouched: the bound still only drops points (never throws), still runs for every source, and a stamp years back is still dropped, so `ensure_partitions` cannot be made to create the months in between (SEC-1). The window widens by two days for one source only.

## Evidence
- `pnpm check`: 4817 unit tests pass, `check-bom`, `check-boundaries`, `check-i18n` OK.
- Integration: the full project passed before the review fixes (52 files, 691 tests); `de-3-lead`, `de-3` and `forecasts` pass after them. `de-3-lead.int.test.ts` shows that a replay adds a complete run next to a run cut under the old bound (second pass 0/0).
- Review round 1 (Sonnet high code + security) and its fixes: see the two PR comments.

## After merge (owner)
1. Merge, approve `production`, wait for `rws-update`. No host file, secret or migration changes: no bootstrap re-run.
2. Replay DE-3 as the owner on the VPS (`docs/runbooks/replay.md` §12). It adds one complete run per affected file next to the truncated one. Paste only counts, nothing of a file or run (owner data). Exact commands:

```bash
# once per shell (the same command line as rws_compose in rws-lib.sh)
rwsc() { sudo docker compose -p rws --project-directory /var/lib/rws/active -f /var/lib/rws/active/compose.yaml \
  --env-file /etc/rws/rws.env --env-file /var/lib/rws/active/images.env "$@"; }

# 1. count first (writes nothing)
rwsc run --rm --no-deps -T load replay --source DE-3 --spec de-3-files --from 2026-09-29 --to "$(date -u +%F)" --dry-run
# 2. the replay: expect "quarantined":0, "n_new" above 0, "n_changed":0 and no before_window alert
rwsc run --rm --no-deps -T load replay --source DE-3 --spec de-3-files --from 2026-09-29 --to "$(date -u +%F)"
# 3. the second pass must print "n_new":0,"n_changed":0
rwsc run --rm --no-deps -T load replay --source DE-3 --spec de-3-files --from 2026-09-29 --to "$(date -u +%F)"
```

3. Then KG-261 can be set to closed.

## Summary

The glossary check now holds test titles to GLOSSARY.md's _Avoid_ lists, as it already does for the API contract and UI copy. This is a rule review kept enforcing by hand (NBK-101).

```diff
 check-glossary
   OpenAPI contract prose      CONTEXTUAL exclusions
   UI copy (templates)         UI_CONTEXTUAL exclusions
+  test titles                 UI_CONTEXTUAL exclusions   describe / it / test, .skip/.only/.todo,
+                                                         .each(…) and .each`…`, any quoting
   a term matches as a whole word
+  … or its plural ("passages", "sources")
```

```text
scripts/
  check-glossary.mjs              reads the files, reports
  check-glossary-rules.mjs        new: terms, exclusions, findTerm, testTitles
  check-glossary-rules.test.mjs   new: run by `pnpm run check:scripts`
```

13 test titles were renamed, with the same tests and new wording:

| was | now |
| --- | --- |
| passage(s) | the cited Chunk, Chunks |
| source marker, sources | Citation marker, Citations; "markers" where no Chunk matched |
| preview | streamed answer |
| workspace | layout, page frame |
| owner | host |
| plain text | text |

The comments beside them follow, and CLAUDE.md and CODING_STANDARDS.md now say test titles are checked rather than reviewed.

## Evidence

- **Before:** `it('marks the passage …')` passed `pnpm run check`.
  **After:** the check fails and names it:

  ```text
  check-glossary: 1 glossary violation(s).
      uses "passage", which GLOSSARY.md tells us to avoid for Excerpt
      text: "marks the passage"
  ```
- `check-glossary-rules.test.mjs` covers:
  - title extraction, including modifiers and table forms;
  - calls that aren't titles, such as `pattern.test('…')`, `vi.it(…)` and commented-out tests;

- `pnpm run check` passes, with 15 script tests.
- The renamed tests still pass: backend citations (6 tests), and the chat panel messages and editable-title specs (31 tests). The full frontend suite passed after the first commit (349 tests).

## Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way

**Blast Radius:** checks

- The check is stricter, so future test titles using an _Avoid_ term fail `pnpm run check` and CI.
- The plural matching applies to the API contract and UI copy too; it found nothing new there.

Files, Gallery and Web Viewer already use the **same** `XDriveMediaDetailsInspector`. Its tag, person and description saves could finish after navigating A → B, overwriting B's draft. The Gallery wrapper also accepted selected-node updates solely by ID, without checking revision.

### Test-first first-red
- Test-only baseline `ff3d3fdd`, [CI #4757](https://github.com/lazyxu/xdrive/actions/runs/37900765270): one authentic stale-version failure, two tests blocked by a mock icon error. **Not** counted as 3 reproduced business failures.
- Corrected test-only baseline `cabc7c85`, [CI #4759](https://github.com/lazyxu/xdrive/actions/runs/37901044973): the **actual React shared Inspector** test reproduces the A→B bug (expected **B draft tag**, got **A stored tag**); revision callback assertion fails (expected 4 checks, got 0). A same-ID/revision test then hit a separate missing optional handler in its fixture, corrected before the production run.
- Original A→B and Gallery assertions are unchanged. Final one-commit patch is `e637a186`, against immutable base `eff2cd922ad644b7007bd00375aa0d8ad9769768`.

### Production fix
- Give the shared details form a React identity key combining **Node ID and revision**. A previous instance's pending completions cannot write into B or a newer version of the same node; its tag/person/description state and album-target choice are reset on identity replacement.
- Reject revision-mismatched completion patches in four Gallery selection actions and six loaded/virtual-media mutation paths (including recipe state). Preserve the established Web Viewer current-ID/revision check and FileExplorer's lazy cancellable fetch/revision fallback; no duplicated media player or API changes.
- Update M09 progress and add `M49.V07` to the existing cross-platform mobile validation matrix, with an auditable first-red record at `docs/validation/mobile-media-properties-m09-2026-10-09.md`.

### Required acceptance
Shared React regression cases, existing Files/Gallery/Viewer properties suites, Desktop full tests + typecheck, Web lint/build and full PR CI must pass on final head. Native iOS and Android tab/installed-mode testing is **not claimed** and remains tracked independently. This is the first targeted M09 repair, not the entirety of later Gallery editing/gesture items.

body:
Fixes the flaky `TestSeedLoadsIntoMigratedSchema` failure in [run 37899997396](https://github.com/aldersfors/matlistan/actions/runs/37899997396) on #59.

`seedDB` called `ctr.Exec` without `tcexec.Multiplexed()`, so the reader carried Docker's 8-byte stream frame headers. When psql's output came back in one frame, `keys.Slug` hid the stray bytes. When it spanned several, the headers broke lines and the row count failed.

Verified: `go test -race -count=20 -run TestSeed ./hack/` passes, and a probe showed the raw stream as `"\x01\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x14Anna|anna\n..."` before the fix.

Modality (0008,0060) is a series-level attribute. Requesting it in study searches makes servers like Orthanc read a DICOM file per study and log warnings. ModalitiesInStudy (0008,0061) already provides the modalities.

Requesting "Modality" (00080060) from the studies dicom-web endopint is a minor logic error for multiple reasons:
- a single study might contain more than one modalities so requesting one makes little sense

This change removes Modality from the requested tag

body:
## Why

`future-self` had grown to 641 lines covering eight unrelated jobs — reading this installation, session recall, the account and balance, changing settings, the desktop app's store, reading the source that implements the agent, the bounds behind a claim, and worked examples. All of it loaded for any one of them, and the file had accumulated a two-level §-numbering scheme to keep the parts apart.

## What

The entry file is now a 148-line index: the ground rules, the commands worth having in front of you, how to build a picture of the user, and a table mapping a question to the reference that answers it. Details move to seven self-contained references:

| Reference | Covers |
|---|---|
| `references/inspecting.md` | The read surface; the `info`/`status` confusion; "my tools" is not the model's; which session am I; which build is this |
