| `references/settings.md` | Changing global/session/skill settings, stopping runs, approvals, refreshing the model registry |
| `references/desktop-app.md` | The app's own store: its preferences, and its workspaces |
| `references/source.md` | Reading the code that implements the agent, and attributing a behaviour to the right build |

`references/desktop-app.md` also records the workspace capability added in futuregene/future-os#951/#952 — `future workspace list|add`, and that `future session set <id> --cwd` files the conversation under the directory's workspace — so the skill knows the feature exists rather than reporting it missing.

author: mdarooka
body:
## Problem
After signing in, every marketing page still said "Sign in" and there was no way to sign out from the site header.

## Cause
The server only accepted Hexclave sessions from a request header. The planner adds that header, but marketing pages call `/api/auth/me` with a plain fetch, so they always looked signed out.

## Fix
- **Server:** `GET /api/auth/me` (and only that route) may also read the Hexclave session cookie. Every other route still requires the header, so cookie-based CSRF stays closed.
- **Header / menu / footer:** signed in shows the first name (→ Preferences), "Account (Name)" in the mobile menu, "Account" in the footer, plus a Sign out control in the nav and menu.
- **Sign out:** loads the Hexclave SDK only on click, with analytics and replay off, then refreshes the header.
- Root HTML regenerated from `build/templates.js`.

## Testing
- `npm test`: 388/388 pass after merging latest main.
- New tests: the cookie works on `/api/auth/me`; with only the cookie, `/api/trips` and `/api/itineraries` return 401.
- Browser check on a local server with local auth: the header switches between signed-in and signed-out states, and Sign out works on desktop and in the mobile menu.
- Not yet checked against live Hexclave: needs one sign-in/sign-out on production after deploy.

author: tristan-stoltz-erc
body:
## Summary

Add a SQLite-backed local witness adapter and deterministic crash/recovery model for CIV-013. This is research/qualification code, not production trust infrastructure.

## Exact topology

- Base branch: `research/sym-civ-012-independent-receipt-tail-anchors-v3`
- Base SHA: `8ce1bd36c6e34a145bd765fc0b3fcb0b2d8fc6a8`
- PR branch: `research/sym-civ-013-durable-witness-crash-recovery-v1`
- Current adapter commit: `d76ddc77f4ac325b75450241f705d548c7835e77`
- Adapter file blob: `5af3c4c375f5b4a7698435984f34cff42921b90d`
- Workspace dependencies: rusqlite 0.40.2, libsqlite3-sys 0.38.2, bundled SQLite 3.53.2; Rust 1.96.0.

## SQLite adapter

The crate persists accepted/prepared records and the accepted head in SQLite. Each connection verifies WAL mode, `synchronous=FULL`, foreign keys, busy timeout, and linked SQLite runtime. The adapter refuses to open below SQLite 3.51.3, the fixed-version floor for the WAL-reset corruption issue documented by SQLite: [WAL documentation](https://www.sqlite.org/wal.html#the_wal_reset_bug), [3.51.3 release notes](https://www.sqlite.org/releaselog/3_51_3.html).

Local acceptance is the SQLite transaction that marks a record accepted and advances `witness_meta`. The `IndependentAnchor` trait requires durable reads and linearizable compare-and-advance in a separate trust/failure domain, but this PR does not provide a production anchor. Callers remain responsible for authenticating and authorizing the genesis checkpoint before `initialize()`.

## Integrity and recovery hardening

- Same-generation retries and late historical finalization verify the exact candidate and validate full accepted/prepared history before returning idempotent success.
- Current-head field tampering fails closed even when the metadata pointer and stored digest column still agree.
- An anchor already past the candidate is classified as rollback/missing-history state, not a false same-generation fork.
- Fork evidence is committed with a per-log row-count/tail-digest commitment. Reads validate it; appends fail closed when it is corrupted. Valid legacy evidence is checked before an atomic `user_version=2` migration; malformed legacy evidence blocks migration.
- The latest change moves SQLite structural checks, foreign-key checks, log enumeration, and per-log semantic history checks onto one deferred read snapshot. The helper is typed as `&Transaction<'_>`, so these multi-query integrity checks cannot be accidentally called through an arbitrary connection. The regression now invokes it as `SqliteWitnessStore::integrity_check_from_transaction(&tx)` from the test module, rather than using `Self` outside an `impl`.
- Regression `integrity_check_uses_a_consistent_snapshot_during_concurrent_advance` establishes a generation-one snapshot, lets a separate WAL connection commit generation two, verifies that the old snapshot remains coherent, and then verifies the fresh snapshot. This is a test definition, not yet a test-pass claim.
- The subprocess crash fixture exits after external-anchor commit but before local finalization. It verifies the split state (anchor at generation two, local head still generation one, generation two still prepared), then requires a fresh process to recover the exact candidate. Its second SQLite file is on the same host; this is a process-restart fixture, not a production independent anchor or power-loss test.

## Rust test inventory

The source currently defines **31 unit tests**, covering WAL/FULL configuration and reopen, receipt rollback/equivocation, prepared recovery, anchor outages and divergences, late-finalize interleavings, concurrent connections, integer boundaries, fork evidence/tail corruption, legacy migration, process-restart recovery, SQLite version-floor enforcement, and consistent-snapshot integrity checking.

These are definitions only. No current-head Rust test PASS is asserted.

A separate JavaScript SHA-256/canonical-encoding/outcome evaluator matched 46/46 expected results, including DA046's integrity-snapshot contract. It verified the canonical bootstrap and fork digests and was checked against the standard SHA-256 `abc` vector. This does not mean the committed Python checker, Rust tests, or Actions passed.

## Mycelix conformance profile

Mycelix draft PR [#4918](https://github.com/Luminous-Dynamics/mycelix/pull/4918) is pinned to this exact adapter revision and source blob. Its 46 ordered reference vectors DA001–DA046 cover canonical encodings, adapter state outcomes, anchor/race cases, fork-tail integrity/migration, SQLite version policy, overflow preflight, and DA046's consistent-snapshot contract. The Mycelix profile is reference conformance only; it is not a substitute for executing the Rust tests or Actions.

## Claim ceiling / merge gates

This PR is not production-qualified. It does not provide a production independent anchor, bootstrap authentication, signing/key lifecycle, operational witness independence, quorum safety, hardware/power-loss validation, or production anti-rollback. The local fork-evidence commitment is in the same SQLite rollback domain as the evidence rows; coordinated deletion of both remains outside the current accepted-head-only anchor contract.

At the latest status check for `d76ddc77f4ac325b75450241f705d548c7835e77`, workflow syntax, governance, broad CI, backend regression, feature-matrix/measurements, and smoke checks were queued/pending. Queued or pending is not PASS. Do not merge until exact-head format, compile, crate tests, CIV smoke, and their outputs complete and are reviewed.

body:
## Summary
This PR introduces a new React application for displaying real-time currency exchange rates against the Brazilian Real (BRL). The application fetches live quotes from the AwesomeAPI and displays them in an interactive dashboard with visual indicators for price movements.

## Key Changes
- **useQuotes hook** (`src/useQuotes.js`): Custom React hook that manages fetching and caching currency quotes with automatic polling every 5 seconds. Includes:
  - Support for 4 major currencies (USD, EUR, JPY, CNH)
  - Direction tracking to detect price movements (up/down)
  - Smart polling that pauses when the page is hidden
  - Proper cleanup and abort handling for fetch requests

- **App component** (`src/App.jsx`): Main application component featuring:
  - Card-based layout displaying each currency's bid/ask prices, highs, lows, and percentage changes
  - Visual trend indicators (▲/▼/■) with color coding
  - Real-time status indicator showing last update time and connection state
  - Responsive grid layout

- **Styling** (`src/styles.css`): Dark theme CSS with:
  - Animated flash effects for price updates (green for up, red for down)
  - Pulsing status indicator for active connection
  - Responsive grid layout with mobile support
  - Tabular number formatting for consistent price display

- **Build configuration**: Vite setup with React plugin for development and production builds
- **GitHub Pages deployment**: Automated workflow to deploy the application on push to main
- **Project setup**: HTML entry point, package.json with React dependencies, and .gitignore

## Notable Implementation Details
- Uses `AbortController` to cancel in-flight requests when component unmounts or new requests are initiated
- Tracks previous quote values to determine price direction changes
- Pauses polling when page visibility changes (using `visibilitychange` event) to reduce unnecessary API calls
- Formats all currency values using Brazilian locale (`pt-BR`) with proper BRL currency formatting

author: hyper-ff
body:
## Why I'm doing:

A query that mixes a dictionary-capable aggregate with one that is not, over the
same low-cardinality string column, is rejected by the plan validator in the
default configuration:

```sql
select g, min(s), group_concat(s, ' ')
from t where s is null or s != 'x' group by g;
```

```
ERROR 1064 (HY000): Invalid agg function plan: min with
    (arg type VARCHAR, serde type INT, result type INT, nullable true) backend [id=10001]
```

or, depending on which validator runs first,

```
ERROR 1064 (HY000): Invalid plan: Type check failed. the type of arg 10: min in
    expr '10: min' is defined as VARCHAR, but the actual type is INT
```

The user sees `Unknown error` for a query that is perfectly legal. Found by the
cluster fuzzer.

## What I'm doing:

`DecodeCollector.visitPhysicalHashAggregate` judges each aggregate function on
its own, against the input columns **as they stood before any disable was
known**. `min(s)` is in `LOW_CARD_AGGREGATE_FUNCTIONS` and is accepted;
`group_concat(s)` is not, and disables the very column `min` reads. The loop that
follows only skips a function whose *output* ref is disabled, so `min` stayed
registered as producing a dictionary value while its input had already been
materialised as strings — the plan then carried `min` typed INT under a VARCHAR
column ref.

This asks `shouldProcessAggFunction` again once the decode set is known, and
keeps going until nothing changes.

Re-asking the same question is what makes this safe, rather than adding a second,
hand-written rule. An accepted `array_agg` disables its own non-string first
argument on purpose — that is the sort-only encoding — so a rule phrased as "a
function that reads a disabled column is disabled" switches that `array_agg` off.
The first revision of this PR did exactly that and `LowCardinalityStructTest`
caught it with four failures; running the acceptance predicate again instead
leaves `array_agg` accepted, because its candidate columns already exclude that
argument.

A dictionary-capable aggregate that has no such sibling is untouched — the
`min(s), max(s)` control statement in the new test keeps its `Decode` nodes.

Fixes #issue

Does this PR entail a change in behavior?

If yes, please specify the type of change:

- [ ] Interface/UI changes: syntax, type conversion, expression evaluation, display information
- [ ] Parameter changes: default values, similar parameters but with different default values
- [x] Policy changes: use new policy to replace old one, functionality automatically enabled
- [ ] Feature removed
- [ ] Miscellaneous: upgrade & downgrade compatibility, etc.

## Checklist:

- [x] I have added test cases for my bug fix or my new feature
- [ ] This pr needs user documentation (for new or modified features or behaviors)
  - [ ] I have added documentation for my new feature or new function
  - [ ] This pr needs auto generate documentation
- [ ] This is a backport pr

## Bugfix cherry-pick branch check:
- [x] I have checked the version labels which the pr will be auto-backported to the target branch
  - [x] 4.1
  - [x] 4.0
  - [ ] 3.5

## Verification

Bidirectional, on a real cluster, with the **only** difference between the two
runs being the FE jar:

| | without the fix | with the fix |
|---|---|---|
| `min(s)` + `group_concat(s)` | `Invalid agg function plan: min with (arg type VARCHAR, serde type INT, ...)` | passes |
| `max(s)` + `group_concat(s)` | same error | passes |
| `count(*), count(s), min(s), max(s), group_concat(s)` | same error | passes |
| `min(s), max(s)` (control) | passes | passes |

The plan really does take the low-cardinality path in both runs — the scan
carries `PREDICATES: DictDecode(12: s, [(<place-holder> IS NULL) OR (<place-holder> != 'V0')])`
and a `1:Decode` node — so the passing column is not "the optimization never
fired".

The new SQLTest was recorded on the fixed build and then replayed against the
unfixed one, where it fails with the error above.

Unit tests: all 274 tests in `LowCardinalityTest`, `LowCardinalityTest2`,
`LowCardinalityStructTest`, `LowCardinalityArrayTest`, `LowCardinalityJoinTest`,
`LowCardinalityAggStateTest`, `DecodeCollectorTest` and `DecodeRewriterTest` pass,
`LowCardinalityStructTest` 33/33 among them.

## Observability

Reviewed the signals on this path: `DecodeCollector` emits no metrics or logs,
and the failure already surfaces through the plan validator's exception, which
this change makes unreachable for this shape. No signal was removed, and none is
added — a plan that no longer throws is observable through the existing query
profile (`Decode` nodes appear in `EXPLAIN` exactly as before for the shapes that
still encode).

All pins are in one new pending test, `pipeline_sinks_and_wrapper_options_fail_closed`, with its behaviour-only row. The implementation, 3c-2b (about 339 non-test lines), follows once this merges.

**The rules pinned (DEC-851 item 6):**
- **(A) Rule 2 becomes a sink allowlist.** On a logical line holding `$` or a backtick, every pipeline sink, after its wrappers, must be one of:
  - `sha256sum`, `tee`, `tr`, `sort`, `grep`, `cut`, `tail`, `paste`, `cat`, `head`, `uniq`, `wc` or `while read`;
  - `put_file` or `sql`, only in a file under `deploy/`.

  A variable sink is refused, and so is an empty one, such as a sink swallowed by a comment.
- **Structural skip.** Every unquoted redirection word before the command word is skipped. Wrapper options are read by arity, matched by basename. An option of unknown arity is refused.
- **(C)** A sink must be one simple command: no `{`, `(`, `;`, `&&` or `||`.
- **(D)** `<(` and `>(` are refused on an expanding line, and on any line whose command word or sink is a shell.
- **(E)** awk and sed are allowed only on exact lines. `sort --compress-program` is refused.

body: ## Why Relevance reeval was still treating stored Facebook rows as posts when the URL is a normal web page. The listener schedule also missed 11:17 PM and 2:17 AM PT after it was re-enabled. Nothing here triggers production. Merging this workflow file is what re-registers the GitHub schedule. ## Root cause of the missed listener runs The workflow file on main is valid. There is no `if:` gate, the path and name are unchanged, and `workflow_dispatch` of the current file returns HTTP 200 (`mode=monitor` against `www.utahcity.app`). GitHub only registers cron from the default branch, and a UI re-enable does not pick up a schedule that changed while the workflow was disabled. - The last `schedule` events are 2026-10-08 00:37, 06:31, and 09:45 UTC. All three ran commit `09b64b0`, which still had `0 */3 * * *` and `30 */6 * * *`, posted to the apex host, and failed on HTTP 308. - No schedule event has been created since. `#15` (`a11e93c`, 2026-10-09 05:16 UTC) replaced those crons with `17 */3 * * *` while the workflow was off. - The workflow was re-enabled at 2026-10-09 05:24:31 UTC (`state: active`). The 06:17 and 09:17 UTC slots never started. The YAML was not the bug. The schedule registrar never saw `17 */3` after re-enable. This commit changes the workflow file on main so GitHub registers it again, and adds `47 1-23/3 * * *` (01:47, 04:47, … UTC) so a dropped `:17` slot still runs about 90 minutes later. `concurrency.cancel-in-progress` on `social-pulse-listener` stops a late run from overlapping the nudge. ## Stored URL reeval `RELEVANCE_VERSION` is 5, so the next `relevance-reeval` selects every older row. Before classification, a stored row is rejected (status `rejected_offtopic`, reason logged, comments left in the database) when: - its URL host does not match the platform (the Facebook rows on utahcity.com, utah.city, ksl.com, apartments.com, app stores, and instagram.com/popular) - it is an `instagram.com/popular/` page even if the platform is Instagram - it is a non-official Facebook row with no publish date Official Facebook posts on facebook.com may still omit a date. body:
## Verified validation — October 9, 2026

**Evaluation-only merge candidate; production activation is NOT approved.** Checkpoint `88c3559` was evaluated and rebased onto latest main as `7254435` (main's intervening change was docs/tests only).

- Focused native statement-policy, shadow, runtime and evaluator suite: **28/28 passed** on both checkpoints; required CI passed on `88c3559`, fresh strict-branch CI for `7254435` must pass before merge.
- Full synthetic prompt estimated savings: **26,344 → 18,768 tokens (28.758% aggregate; 26.767% case-weighted)**. Below 30% target, not provider-measured.
- Read-only live history metadata: **27,230 → 27,230 estimated tokens (0%)**, two safely-fallback sessions. One has 53 distinct mandatory historical Summary blocks (~32.1k chars) plus 224 retained source spans (~55.2k chars); an in-memory relaxed-bound probe still found no savings. The other has incomplete Summary coverage.
- No provider inference, transcript export, production DB writes, runtime activation, or live deploy. Continuity equivalence and independently blinded narrative quality remain unproven.
- Merge **only as an inactive, safe research foundation**; leave issue #421 open for a newly validated candidate and explicit gated production approval. Detailed diagnostics: [issue #421 checkpoint](https://github.com/cepeter-job/SillyTavern-Telegram-Bridge/issues/421#issuecomment-6079180295).

---

## Issue #421 — statement-level, source-proven continuity shadow (recovery checkpoint)

**Evaluation-only.** This branch is a separate recovery PR based on the verified merged whole-turn shadow PR #473 (main SHA `4e3b31a`). It does not merge/modify PR #467's frozen native experiment, enable history pruning, change live configuration, or send model requests.

### Why
The old hybrid retained entire turns whenever an anchor/neighbor was present, protecting all 73 sampled live turns and yielding **0% estimated savings**. A long turn may contain one critical refusal or promise and many unrelated descriptive paragraphs.

### Implementation
- Exact source-aligned statement slices with character offsets/SHA-256, chronology, speaker roles and robust fallback for unbalanced quotations, roleplay stage directions, code or unsupported scripts.
- Preserve first and recent eight historical turns verbatim, critical claims/choices/negations and neighboring statements **inside** a turn, plus bounded query-relevant statements.
- Reuse existing native SQLite source/reader proof and classified Summary-window validation. Retain all mandatory critical evidence or fall back rather than clipping it for a numeric token target.
- Keep fixed card/world/system/post-history/current inputs untouched. Mark every candidate shadow-only and reject candidate dispatch in all modes.
- Extend the existing lazy shadow-mode callback with scalar, whitelisted statement metrics. Off/enabled modes still do not evaluate the experiment.
- Offline evaluator uses the production `build_chat_messages` function for full **synthetic** prompts and retains six declared controls. Optional read-only live metadata emits no raw transcript.

### Tests and known limitations
Local test-driven development on vm148 observed **11 statement-source tests passed**, **15 statement/runtime tests passed**, and the first **3 benchmark tests passed** before a VPS memory-cgroup stall. Earlier unamended parser benchmark estimated **27.91% aggregate / 25.97% case-weighted synthetic savings**, with **0% initial live-history-only fallback**; those observations are *not final* for this recovery branch. A follow-up parser adaptation to preserve balanced quoted/italicized paragraphs has not yet passed full CI or been remeasured on live.

The VPS went offline and uncommitted work remained isolated. This GitHub-side reconstruction preserves the implementation on a new branch without clobbering the earlier local branch. **Treat CI as the required verification gate and do not merge if checks fail.** Report the actual measured results without upgrading estimates into provider-reported savings. A future representative matched NanoGPT A/B and independently blinded quality review remain mandatory for approval.

**No production activation or release is requested by this PR.** Issue #421 remains open.

author: yannicked
body:
Teams showed you as Away a while after starting NoSlacking, though Slack did not.

NoSlacking published its endpoint's presence once (`PUT …/me/endpoints/`, `activityReporting: "Transport"`), but with transport reporting Teams expects activity on the live connection itself. The web client sends a Socket.IO event on its Trouter socket right after connecting, and again while you use it (recorded, personal and work):

```
5:1+::{"name":"user.activity","args":[{"state":"active","cv":"…"}]}
```

answered `6:::1+[]`. NoSlacking sent only the `2::` heartbeat. Now it sends `user.activity` on connecting and every minute after, numbered per connection, with a correlation vector made as the web client's look (16 random bytes in base64, `.0`).

Not done here: `Busy` / `InACall` during calls, and going Away when you are idle at the computer; the app keeps saying you are active while it runs, as Slack's connection does.

Checked: fmt, clippy, tests, docs. Not yet watched for longer than a few minutes against a real account.

author: aesx9
body:
## Resumen

Módulo independiente `backtest/` (no importa ni modifica `src/copybot`) para decidir si la estrategia tiene ventaja real antes de construir nada más: régimen por SMA50, entrada por cruce del RSI estocástico (14, 14, 3, 3), stop 2×ATR y take profit 3×ATR, sobre `PF_XBTUSD`, `PF_ETHUSD` y `PF_SOLUSD` en velas de 4h.

**Veredicto: no supera los criterios de aceptación** (informe completo en `backtest/REPORT.md`).

| Criterio (funding pesimista) | Resultado | |
|---|---|---|
| Neto positivo en el reservado | −11,30 % (−62,16 USD) | ❌ |
| ≥ 50 operaciones en el reservado | 248 | ✅ |
| Drawdown máximo < 15 % | 26,41 % | ❌ |
| Positivo con parámetros ±20 % (desarrollo) | 0/20 variantes | ❌ |
| Percentil ≥ 90 frente al azar (reservado) | 53,8 | ❌ |

En el reservado el movimiento de precio da +32 USD brutos, pero comisiones y slippage cuestan −87 USD y el funding −7. La tasa de acierto (40,7 %) es prácticamente el punto de equilibrio de una relación 2:3, y la estrategia queda en el percentil 53,8 de 1.000 entradas aleatorias con las mismas salidas: indistinguible del azar.

## Datos y funding (ojo)

- Velas: 4,55 años por activo (2022-03-23 → 2026-10-09), 9.966 velas 4h sin huecos; se descarta la vela en curso.
- **El funding real de Kraken solo cubre ≈1,0 año** (2025-10-06 → hoy); el endpoint no admite rangos ni paginación. Cubre el 73,8 % del tramo reservado y nada del de desarrollo.
- Donde no hay dato se imputa y se informan dos escenarios: *central* (mediana horaria con signo del año real, por activo) y *pesimista* (siempre en contra de la posición, `|P75|` del año real). Los criterios se evalúan con el pesimista; el informe indica el % de funding real frente a imputado.
- Datos guardados en `backtest/datos/` para reproducir sin red.

## Decisiones de diseño a revisar

- «Habiendo estado por debajo/encima de 20/80» = `%K` de la vela inmediatamente anterior al cruce.
- Lectura literal de «valor absoluto del P75» = `|P75(tasa con signo)|`. La alternativa, `P75(|tasa|)`, es ≈12 % mayor en BTC/ETH y ≈78 % en SOL; se muestra en el informe como referencia.
- Robustez ±20 % **solo en desarrollo**, para respetar «el reservado una sola vez». El reservado se ejecutó una vez con los parámetros base (el código se congeló en el primer commit; el segundo solo añade resultados). Tras verlo corregí únicamente la presentación del informe y lo regeneré con una repetición determinista: los CSV de operaciones tienen los mismos sha256 antes y después.
- Umbral de «claramente por encima de la mediana del azar» = percentil ≥ 90, fijado antes de ver resultados.
- Cartera única con capital común (550 USD) y tope de 2× compartido; los datos «por activo» son su contribución. Slippage también en el take profit; gap a través del stop se ejecuta a la apertura.
- Otras limitaciones (drawdown a cierres de vela, funding con granularidad de vela, etc.) en la sección 9 del informe.

## Cambios fuera de `backtest/`

- `Makefile`: `make lint` cubre `backtest/` (ruff y mypy estricto).
- `pyproject.toml`: `testpaths` incluye `backtest/tests`.
- `.gitignore` y `.pre-commit-config.yaml`: excepción acotada a `backtest/datos/*.csv` y `backtest/resultados/*.csv` (datos públicos de mercado y operaciones simuladas) dentro de la prohibición general de CSV. Los CSV de ejecución del bot siguen ignorados y bloqueados.

## Verificación

- `make check` completo: ruff, mypy estricto, 716 tests (123 nuevos en `backtest/tests/`), pip-audit y detect-secrets, todo en verde.
- Tests: sin lookahead (alterar velas futuras no cambia señales ni indicadores pasados), costes en ambos lados (long y short), regla pesimista de stop y TP en la misma vela, hueco a través del stop, tamaño por riesgo y tope de apalancamiento compartido, funding real/imputado por signo y escenario, corte 70/30, robustez ±20 %, azar reproducible, que el reservado no contamina el desarrollo, y una prueba diferencial contra un simulador de referencia independiente.
- Reproducir: `.venv/bin/python -m backtest ejecutar` (sin red). `--solo-desarrollo` no toca el 30 % reservado.

author: abretonc7s
body:
The Command Center showed "This update changes dependencies ... Nothing was changed. 5fdac659 → d9e09b8f" for two days. `.git/farmslot-checkout-update.json` held a 10-07 error record (localSha 5fdac659), and `readCheckoutUpdate` (gateway-update.ts:26) kept returning it. The only filter, in gateway-status.ts:224, dropped an error only when HEAD equalled its targetSha, and the checkout had moved past that commit by other means.

- `readCheckoutUpdate`: a finished record describes one commit: the target for `complete`, the untouched localSha for `error`. If HEAD has moved off that commit, the record is no longer returned.
  - The file isn't deleted, so nothing races a new update that is writing its record.
  - Running records are unaffected, including the dead-worker path.
  - If HEAD can't be read, the record is kept.
- `gateway-status.ts`: the old error-only filter is removed; the new rule covers it.
- `scripts/update-checkout.mjs`: the dependency refusal now names the exact command: `cd '<checkout>' && git merge --ff-only <target> && yarn install --immutable`.

Trade-off: a "the local commit changed" error is written exactly when HEAD already differs from its localSha, so it is hidden at once. The banner then offers the update for the new HEAD instead.

Tests:
- New `gateway-update.test.ts`, 4 cases, 2.1 s for the file, each 118–289 ms:
  - an old error is hidden after HEAD moved;
  - it's shown while HEAD is unchanged;
  - a running record is shown;
  - a `complete` record is shown and then hidden.
- `scripts/tests/update-checkout.test.mjs`: 9/9 pass. The changed dependencies case asserts the command (1.80 s).
- Gateway typecheck passes, the lint ratchet has 0 new issues, and the changelog guard passes.

author: paodingo
body:
While fuzzing the converter I noticed that `process_symbolic_symbol` casts symbol addresses down to u32 without any range check — unlike `process_symbolic_functions`, which skips functions above `u32::MAX`.

Concretely: a symbol living entirely above the u32 range, say at `0x1_0000_0010`, gets its mapping and its "end of symbol" gap marker inserted at *truncated* low addresses — the end marker lands at `0x20`. If a real function's exact end address sits there, lookups for that address return no source location from then on, silently.

This skips symbols above `u32::MAX` the same way functions are skipped, and only inserts the end marker when the end address is actually representable, so a straddling symbol keeps its low mapping without the bogus marker.

Added a regression test (a high symbol plus a low one, then asserting the low lookup survives); `cargo test -p symbolic-symcache` passes.

author: menghun3-cn
body:
## 背景

微信的 token 早就在了，会话那几个界面也用了。但**导航栏和剩下的四个页面**（设备、传输、剪贴板、设置）仍然架在 Material 的默认值上。

问题不在于「页面写了 Material 的颜色」，而在于**页面不必提到某个槽位，那个槽位照样会被画出来**：`Chip`、`Switch`、`SegmentedButton`、`NavigationRail`、`NavigationBar`、对话框底色，读的都是没人写下来的槽位，于是它们按 Material 3 的调色板渲染 —— 一片灰色列表里的薰衣草色实心按钮、每条次要文字上的紫灰 `onSurfaceVariant`、把纯白卡片往种子色洗的 elevation tint。

这种 bug 能躲过 review，因为它**不出现在 diff 的任何一行里**。

## 做了什么

1. **`ColorScheme` 每个槽位都点名**，包括没有任何页面提到的：`surfaceDim` / `surfaceBright` / 四档 `surfaceContainer*` / `onSurfaceVariant` / `outline(Variant)` / `inverseSurface` / `inversePrimary` / `errorContainer` / `onErrorContainer` / `shadow` / `scrim`。规则是**谁都不许用默认值** —— 默认值就是 Material 的颜色。
2. **`surfaceTint: Colors.transparent`**。这是唯一一个默认值会主动破坏观感的槽位：Material 3 会把有高度的表面往种子色调，而微信的表面是平的灰与白。
3. **页面够得着的组件全部配上组件主题**：`appBar` / `card` / `divider` / `chip` / `listTile` / `progressIndicator` / `switch` / `checkbox` / `radio` / `segmentedButton` / `filledButton` / `textButton` / `navigationRail` / `navigationBar` / `dialog` / `inputDecoration`，外加 `iconTheme` 与 `textTheme`。开关类用 `WidgetStateProperty` 按状态取值，品牌绿只在**开着**或**当前**时出现。
4. **两个导航面故意分家**：侧栏 `sidebarBackground` + `listHover` 指示块；底栏 `toolbarBackground` + `indicatorColor: transparent`，靠给图标和标签染色标记当前页（手机尺寸的底栏很薄，实心指示器会压过整条栏）。
5. **四个页面不再各报各的数**：统一取 `WeChat.pagePadding` / `cardPadding` / `cardGap` / `sectionGap`。页面留白以前是四份独立意见。

## 会话列表收尾（三处）

- **行里有了时间**：右列把时间戳叠在「动作或摘要」之上，取 `latest?.at ?? peer.lastSeen`。为此新增 `TransferView.at` —— 由 `app_controller` 在 Tracking 那一刻从自己的时钟读一次传下来。引擎的 `Transfer` 是协议对象、本身没有时间，而在渲染时读时钟会让同一条消息每次重建印出不同的时间。
- **行与行之间有了一条内缩的细线**：从**头像左缘**起笔，而不是整行通栏 —— 通栏横线会把列表切成一块块，而参照物里它是一整片。
- **「怎么进去」是一个词，不是胶囊**：`TextButton` + 6×6 小圆点 + 动词，取代原来的实心/描边胶囊。用 `TextButton` 而不是手搓 `Material`+`InkWell`，是为了保住焦点环、键盘激活和 tooltip 语义。

## 测试

`test_flutter/support/ui_harness.dart` 的 `_pane` 原本自己搭了个 `MaterialApp`、塞的是 `ColorScheme.fromSeed(deepPurple)` —— 也就是说**每一个 widget 测试都是在一套应用从不使用的主题上跑的**，主题回归一个测试都不会失败。现在它用 `WeChat.theme()`，只覆盖页面转场。

新增测试：

- `shell_test.dart` 新增 `the WeChat theme` 组（不需要 widget 树）：断言 Material 本来会自己填的槽位与 `ColorScheme.light()` **不同**、`surfaceTint` 透明、卡片/脚手架/分隔线取 token、字体族从 `textTheme.bodyMedium` 读、两个导航面的配色与透明指示器。
- `pages_test.dart` 在真实会话行上新增三个用例，对应三处收尾各一个：行说出最后什么时候动的、行之间是内缩细线、入口是词而不是实心按钮。

## 门禁（本分支上，已并入最新 develop）

| 门禁 | 结果 |
| --- | --- |
| `verify-agent-notes.ps1` | 41 份活跃笔记 |
| `verify-translation-pairs.ps1` | 42 个配对记录一致 |
| `flutter analyze` | No issues found |
| `dart format --set-exit-if-changed .` | 0 changed |
| `dart test` | **428 / 428** |
| `flutter test test_flutter` | **65 / 65** |

## 附带

- 新增 Agent Note：`.agents/notes/implemented/feature/2026-10-09-wechat-theme-everywhere.{md,zh.md,i18n.yaml}`
- 本分支已经并入 `develop` 上的 PR #25（`fix(app): a renamed device kept its old name on connected peers`），合并 `lib/app/app_controller.dart` 时两边改动区域不同、自动合并干净，合并后两处改动都在（`fromDiscovery` 与 `_Tracked.at` 都已在位）。

## Problem
The native peer probe stops at the initial F_GETFD query before bind/listen or worker upload. The exact title's imports and caller ABI were inspected; no SceNet adapter substitution was found. This does not establish that all firmware fcntl operations are unsupported.

## Change
Replace peer AF_UNIX socket preparation with checked FIOCLEX(NULL), FIONBIO(&one), and the unchanged SO_NOSIGPIPE requirement. These BSD operations preserve unrelated flags. Stop on the first nonzero ioctl result; no fallback or ignored failure. Apply the same preparation to listener, accepted stream and worker socket. Append diagnostic API24/25, preserving saved code meanings. Keep inherited worker stdio fcntl and HELLO/FD modes unchanged. Pin exact peer worker imports including ioctl and fcntl.

## Evidence
Independent source review accepted tree 2d69fc5ce4156c13d2b3c298f68d668836511695. Retained test-only fail-before controls; 3627 target-ABI mock assertions, focused controller/worker checks and all 5 builder tests pass. Publication audit passes562 allowlisted files; whitespace check passes.

Local unchanged make all was attempted and stopped at the sandbox's ELF32 reference execution: OSError [Errno8] Exec format error. make sanitize with restored Clang19 stopped with LeakSanitizer fatal error (ptrace unsupported). No test or sanitizer option was weakened. Hosted CI must pass before the candidate is handed over.

## Limits
Experimental PS5 candidate: ioctl request acceptance remains a console gate. No worker launch, credentials, native exit, Windows child, Battle.net or gameplay success is claimed. A separately reproduced post-preparation deadline/Stop side-effect defect is being handled in its own follow-up, not hidden in this patch. Raw operator logs and SDK files are not included.

author: rwadada
body:
> Stacked on #255 (which is on #254): #254 → #255 → this. The base switches to `main` as those merge.

## Why

#255 sends a USB Android device's traffic through `adb reverse`. A reverse lives in the `adb` connection to the device, so it is **lost whenever the cable is pulled or the `adb` server restarts**, while the device's proxy setting (`localhost:<port>`) stays, pointing at nothing. Reported: having to redo it every time the USB cable comes out. `detour doctor` notices the loss but does not repair it.

## What

`detour start --adb-reverse` (off by default):

- runs `adb track-devices` as a child process and, for **every list it sends**, applies `adb -s <serial> reverse --no-rebind tcp:<port> tcp:<port>` to each ready USB device in it;
- `--no-rebind` makes "already in place" a harmless failure and leaves a port another tool forwards alone;
- if `adb track-devices` ends (the `adb` server restarted, or `adb` is missing) it is started again after 5 s, until the process stops; it is killed on shutdown;
- ignores emulators, `<ip>:<port>` devices, Android 11+ wireless-debugging (`adb-…`) names, and devices that are `unauthorized` or `offline`;
- prints one line when it restores a reverse (once per reconnect), and a line at startup saying it is on.

Off by default because it starts the `adb` server, which people who do not use Android do not want a plain `detour start` to do. The port it forwards is the proxy's real port, so `detour setup --port N` and `detour start --port N` must agree (README says so).

Code: the device classification (`isUsbDevice`, `parseAdbDevices`) moves to `domain/adbReverse/devices.ts` so the watcher and `usecase/setup/android.ts` share it (still re-exported from `android.ts`); the `track-devices` frame parser is there too and reads **bytes**, since the length counts bytes. The watcher is `infra/adb/adbReverseWatcher.ts`, with `adb track-devices` behind a small `StreamingProcess` seam so it is tested without `adb`.

## Verification

- `format:check` / `typecheck` / `eslint .` / `lint:fsd` / `dep-cruise` / `dup-check` / `test:web` / `test:coverage` (1410 tests) / `test:e2e` (153 tests): all exit 0
- New tests: frame parsing (empty list, one, several in a chunk, split across reads, garbage prefix, a multi-byte character), USB classification, and the watcher (applies on connect, re-applies after unplug and re-plug, logs once per reconnect, ignores non-USB and unauthorised devices, restarts `track-devices` and re-applies after it, stops cleanly and cancels a scheduled restart, failures are not fatal). Two end-to-end tests with a fake `adb` first on PATH: with the flag a USB device gets `reverse --no-rebind tcp:<real port> tcp:<real port>` and the emulator does not; without it `adb` is never called.
- Real things, no device: the real `adb track-devices` through `spawnStreaming` (the `0000` empty list is read as an empty list, and `kill()` ends it); a real `detour start --adb-reverse` shows the startup line, `adb track-devices` is running, and it is gone after `SIGTERM`.
- **Not exercised**: a real device being plugged and unplugged. I have no device here, and the body of a `track-devices` list with a device in it is not spelled out in Google's docs; it is read as the same `<serial>\t<state>` lines as `adb devices`, which is also what the existing parser assumes. A wrong guess would show up as the reverse not being restored; worth one plug/unplug check.

## Next

A toggle in the dashboard (it runs `adb` on the host, so it would be limited to a client that proved the password or token, like the one-click update). Separate PR on top of this one.

The empty composer expanded on any focus within it. Giving the mode button focus changed its rectangle from approximately (57,686,30,32) to (87,653,78,32), allowing a control to move before activation. The original quiet rules also repeated their long condition and added two important declarations.

Quiet phone composer presentation only. Consolidate the condition in a component stylesheet using native CSS nesting. Expand for textarea focus rather than toolbar focus, while retaining expansion for draft text, attachments, refinement and open menus. The existing scene-fold CSS owns the quiet state. No React state, transport or public API changes are needed.

## O que muda

- **Migra o repositório do portfólio estático para o app interno Autocontrole** — Next.js (App Router) com a API em route handlers Node e PostgreSQL (sem ORM). Cobre login por nome + cargo + senha, painel, e os módulos PACs, APPCC, PCCs (monitoramentos), rastreabilidade, temperaturas, laboratório, não conformidades, auditorias, documentos, treinamentos, produtos, alertas e usuários.
- **Permissões de cargos unificadas** (`src/lib/roles.js`): **Supervisor** e **Controle de Qualidade** passam a ter acesso total e idêntico (registros, alertas e usuários); **Funcionário** só visualiza; **Operador** visualiza e cria. A matriz é aplicada na API (`permissaoDoRecurso`) e na tela (`CrudResource`, `/usuarios`).
- **Identidade visual amarela** (`src/app/globals.css`): navegação, botões, abas e badges passam a usar `--brand: #eab308`.
- **Nova aba `/planilhas`** (`src/app/planilhas/page.jsx`): consolida os registros de execução dos PACs (`pac_registros`) e os monitoramentos de PCCs (`pcc_monitoramentos`) numa planilha única, com filtro (PACs e PCCs / somente PACs / somente PCCs), cabeçalho do estabelecimento e o botão **"Imprimir PDF de planilha"** (`window.print`), no mesmo padrão de impressão da ficha de produto.

## Problema resolvido

O repositório era apenas um portfólio estático, e o sistema de controle de qualidade (PAC/PCC/APPCC) existia somente numa branch legada. Além disso, "Controle de Qualidade" não tinha os mesmos acessos do supervisor, a identidade visual não seguia a marca amarela, e não havia uma visão consolidada e imprimível dos PACs e PCCs para os registros.

## Comportamento resultante

- Supervisor e Controle de Qualidade enxergam e fazem exatamente o mesmo (inclusive `/usuarios` e alertas); os demais cargos ficam restritos pela matriz de permissões.
- Toda rota de API exige login: sem sessão a API responde 401 e o shell redireciona para `/login`.
- `/planilhas` reúne PACs e PCCs e imprime pelo diálogo do navegador.

Smoke test com o stack no ar (`docker compose -f docker-compose.base44.yml ps` → serviços `db` e `web` healthy):

- `POST /api/auth/login` → 200, cria/entra a conta (`{"data":{"id":4,"nome":"Supervisor","cargo":"supervisor"}}`)
- `GET /api/dashboard` com sessão → 200; sem sessão → 401
- `GET /` → página renderiza (contém "Autocontrole")

author: stoptheworld-java
body:
## 概要

DOC-1 第 1 片后端：时间戳校验工具 `is_timestamp`（任务 DOC-1-03 / #702）。

job 的 GET / 取消 / 重试在返回前，要用它校验 `created_at` / `updated_at`。那个 PR（-45）加上它超过了 300 行，所以先把这个纯工具单独拆出来。

### 改动

- **`timestamp.rs`**：`is_timestamp` 只接受 OS 写入的那一种格式 `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS.sssZ`（即 `strftime('%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%fZ')`：24 字节、ASCII 数字），并按公历严格校验：
  - 闰年规则（含 1900、2000、0000、0300 这些世纪年）；
  - 各月天数；
  - 时 < 24、分 < 60、秒 < 60。
- **为什么不交给 SQLite**：它的日期函数往返时会保留不存在的时间：
  - 24 时；
  - 负年份；
  - 项目自带的 SQLite 3.46 还会把 `0300-02-29` 原样往返（300 年不是闰年），反而拒掉合法的 `0300-03-01`。

## 测试与证据

- **测试**：`a_timestamp_is_a_real_date_time_in_the_form_the_os_writes`。
  - 合法值：`now` 的输出、闰日、`0000-02-29`、`0300-03-01`、`9999-12-31`。
  - 非法值：
    - 日期：`0300-02-29`、`1900-02-29`、2 月 30 日、4 月 31 日、13 月、0 月、0 日；
    - 时间：24 时、60 分、60 秒；
    - 年份：负年份；
    - 格式：缺毫秒、缺 Z、24 字节但末位不是 Z、空格分隔、前导空格、NUL、全角数字、空串。
- **反面对照**：以下任一处放松都有测试变红：
  - 闰年规则改成儒略历；
  - 允许 24 时；
  - 允许 60 秒；
  - 30 天的月份放到 31 天；
  - 不查末位 Z。
- **本地门禁**：`cargo fmt --check`、`cargo clippy --all-targets -D warnings`、`cargo test -p agent24-documents` 共 120 个全部通过。
- **严格审查（Codex）**：这段代码是在 -45 的第 2–5 轮审查里成形的，第 5 轮 **APPROVE**。
  - Codex 独立核对了 3,960,000 个日期组合、全部两位字段值、全部 1000 个毫秒值、6,144 种字节替换，没有出入。
  - 并确认没有 panic 路径：先保证 24 字节再切片；每个参与计算的字节都是数字，减法不会下溢；累加值最大 9999。

## pre-pr-check

`pre-pr-check: 0 block / 0 review · 规模 38 行 / 2 文件 / 1 顶层目录（不计测试）· normal`

合并策略：等 PR-Daemon 评审、CI 全绿。

author: joshxee
body:
## What

Gesture start, the last parity gap before the KMP cutover. A guest holds a palm in a box on the right half of the attract screen. A green ring fills round the box while the hold completes, and a dot marks the hand on the live preview. A small "Tap here to start" button stays bottom-left as a fallback.

- **Core (pure Rust):** `PalmHold` (1.2 s hold, 500 ms gap tolerance, a latch so a raised hand cannot start a second session), `GestureTrigger` on the existing `StartTrigger` seam, a `PalmDetector` trait, and `run_sampler`, which publishes a `GestureUpdate` for the UI. `Settings.start_trigger = gesture` is now accepted; the default stays `tap`.
- **App:** live-view frames are teed into a keep-latest channel. `gesture_set_region` (WebView-callable) tells Rust where the box is in the *camera frame*; `gesture://state` carries `{palm, holding, hold_ms}`. A dev-panel `hold_palm` fault drives the whole path without a hand and lets go by itself after 5 s.
- **Plugin (Kotlin):** `gestureDetect` runs MediaPipe `GestureRecognizer` in IMAGE mode, so it never sticks to one hand. It crops the box plus a margin, requires the palm's centre to be in the box, and accepts only the classifier's own `Open_Palm`. It logs one diagnostics line a second.
- **UI:** the box is a window onto the preview (outside dimmed), with a solid white border flush with the box edge, a green ring from the top centre, no text in the box, and no brand line on the attract screen. There is an Open-Palm Start toggle in Settings. Tap-only and native-preview cameras keep the old layout and the "Tap to start photoshoot" pill the Maestro flows rely on.

## Why

The old Kotlin gesture start was unreliable (it kept jumping between hands and never started) and had no on-screen guide. The box gives guests a target and lets the detector ignore everything outside it.

## For reviewers

- **Verified on the tablet with the Sony:** the box-to-frame mapping (a saved crop matches the box), a real raised hand starting real captures, ~12 detections/s at 40-90 ms, and the layout at 5x zoom.
- **Not tuned:** recognition of blurred or tilted hands. A hand close to the lens is out of focus on the Sony live view, and about half the frames hit with a hand in view. A looser "4+ fingers extended" rule was tried and removed because it started sessions from the back of a hand or a hand at the guest's side. Hold and tolerance values (`DEFAULT_HOLD`, `DEFAULT_GAP_TOLERANCE` in `gesture.rs`) are my choices, not measured.
- **Bug found while testing:** a dev-panel fake palm that stayed on left the box green and, because of the latch, blocked every new start. It now expires after 5 s.
- Adds the 8 MB `gesture_recognizer.task` model to the plugin (the old app's file, same MediaPipe version), so the plugin no longer depends on `composeApp`.
- Debug aid: `adb shell run-as com.jc.photobooth.tauri mkdir cache/gesture-debug` keeps the last frame and crop for inspection.
- Checks run locally: `cargo fmt`, clippy on all four crates with `-D warnings`, all Rust tests, and `bun run typecheck` / `bun test` (130) / `bun run build`. CI was not run yet.
- Wiki updated: `Core-Domain`, `Tauri-App`, `Native-Camera-Plugin`, `Frontend`, `Tauri-Migration-Plan`.

author: victorsolaya
body:
Adds `npm run deploy`, which publishes the tool to npm in one step.

## What it does

From `main`, with no uncommitted changes:

1. `git pull --ff-only`.
2. `npm whoami`; runs `npm login` (browser) when there is no session.
3. `npm test`, before the version is touched.
4. If the version in package.json is already on npm, raises it (`patch` by default, `npm run deploy -- minor` or `-- major`) and commits `Release vX.Y.Z`. A version raised in its PR (like 0.3.6) is published as it is.
5. `npm publish`. `prepublishOnly` runs the tests, the build and `pptb-validate`, so a stale `dist/` can't be published.
6. Tags `vX.Y.Z` and pushes the commit and the tag to `main`.

ToolBox picks the new version up from npm at 00:00 UTC, or right away from **My tools → ⋯ → Trigger Update**.

## Other changes

- `@pptb/validate` is a declared dev dependency (it was installed but not listed).
- `publishConfig.access: public`, so a plain `npm publish` works for the scoped package.
- README: the Development section explains `npm run deploy`.

## Checks

- [x] `npm run deploy -- bogus` stops: unknown version bump.
- [x] `npm run deploy` outside `main` stops before touching anything.
- [x] `npm publish --dry-run`: the tests, the build and the validator run, and the tarball holds only `dist/`, README, LICENSE and package.json, with public access.
- [x] Version detection against the registry: 0.3.5 is published, 0.3.6 is not, so the first run publishes 0.3.6 without raising it.

## Thai-RAG Issue #2 — bounded cross-process workspace admission receipt revocation (after merged PR #313)

### Security scope
- Adds migration **036_workspace_admission_authority**. Transactional `AFTER INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE` triggers on `workspace_admission_receipts` atomically increment the persisted `workspace_authority_epoch` introduced by merged PR #312.
- When a different process invalidates an admission receipt through the **real** `SqliteWorkspaceRepository.invalidateAdmissionReceipt` API, the strict FD3 parent watcher from merged PR #313 observes the committed generation, aborts idle old Python workers, and denies subsequent calls **without requiring any workspace registry path/identity change**.
- Direct SQLite mutations also fenced. Rolled-back changes do not increase the observed committed generation, and update miss without matching row does not revoke.
- Explicit `strictWorkerAuthority` remains **OFF by default**. This adds generation invalidation of *old FD3 sessions*; it does **not** independently validate every new FD3 worker against application-level Goal/admission state. New-session admission policy, atomic in-flight side-effect barriers, and parity for standalone `local-*` remain separate Issue #2 work.

author: warehousevistar
body:
Wires the four new backend endpoints. I verified each against the module source rather than the spec — paths, role gates and payload shapes all match.

| Endpoint | Used by |
|---|---|
| `GET /employees/:id/deletion-impact` | opens the confirmation; deletes nothing |
| `DELETE /employees/:id/purge` | the confirm action |
| `DELETE /kra-assignments/:id` | per-assignment unassign |
| `DELETE /kra-assignments/employee/:employeeId` | "Unassign all KRAs" |

## Purge is a second action, not a replacement

Deactivate stays the primary removal — it refuses while reports or in-progress reviews exist, and that check is usually what you want. Purge never refuses and cannot be undone, so the two sit apart on the screen and read as different acts rather than neighbouring equals.

## The confirmation

Built around one asymmetry: the counts fall into **three groups that mean different things**, and summing them would hide the one that matters.

- **Their own records** — expected, and why the user is here.
- **Records belonging to OTHER employees** — the reviews this person rated for their team, the feeds they entered. *Deleting a manager takes their whole team's ratings with them*, and nothing about the word "delete" suggests that. Own heading, in red, with a sentence saying whose data it is.
- **Reporting lines** — reports are **detached**, not deleted. Reads as alarming unless it says so.

Zero counts are hidden rather than printed, so real figures aren't buried in ones that don't apply; an all-zero impact says so in a line instead.

The preview is fetched **before** the dialog opens, and the dialog isn't shown without it — confirming a deletion whose scope you were never shown is the failure this endpoint exists to prevent. A `404` on purge is treated as success: the employee is gone, which is what was asked.

## Unassign

"Unassign all KRAs" on the employee's KRA tab, shown only when there's something to clear. The server **keeps** a review that already carries scores, so the result is reported rather than assumed — an assignment going while its scored review stays is a half-done state the user would otherwise meet later.

`cycleId` is omitted entirely rather than sent empty, which would scope the call to a cycle with no id, clear nothing, and report success.

## Tests

17 new, covering the request shapes (GET for the preview, the `/purge` path rather than the deactivate one, `cycleId` omission), the `removes` / `removed` key difference, the three-way grouping, and the copy. `analyze` clean, **854 pass**.

author: szczepanov
body:
⚡ **[perf] Avoid string allocation inside frame decoding loop**

* **💡 What:** Refactored `MediaError::InvalidFrame` to store `openbar_tracking::TrackerError` directly rather than converting the error to a `String` via `.to_string()`.
* **🎯 Why:** Previously, `GrayFrame::try_new(...).map_err(|error| MediaError::InvalidFrame { index: decoded, detail: error.to_string() })` heap-allocated a `String` on frame decoding errors inside the loop in `read_gray_frames`. Storing `TrackerError` directly avoids unnecessary heap allocation during error mapping and defers string formatting to `Display`.
* **📊 Measured Improvement:** Eliminates string heap allocation overhead during error mapping when reading raw gray frame streams.

author: hunterdsp
body:
Closes #2163.

## What it does

`PYTEST_ISOLATED` now runs `uv run --no-project --isolated`. Without `--isolated`,
`uv run --no-project` still discovers a virtual environment (from `VIRTUAL_ENV`,
or a `.venv` above the cwd) and layers the `--with` env over it, so a
dev-group package imports on a laptop and fails in CI.

`--isolated` stops that overlay and keeps the interpreter request in force. An
explicit `--python <path>` also stops the overlay, but it overrides `UV_PYTHON`,
which setup-uv sets per CI matrix leg, so every leg would test one interpreter.
`BASE_PYTHON` is removed.

## The `.python-version` finding

The premise case of `tests/test_gh2163_isolated_test_env.py` built its leak venv
from the test's own interpreter. The checkout's `.python-version` is 3.12, and
uv's interpreter search skips a venv whose version does not satisfy that
request. Under a pinned 3.14 parent the sentinel was therefore invisible for a
version reason, not because of a leak. The test now builds the venv at the
version `uv python find` selects in the checkout, the one the probe's inner
`uv run` will request.

Measured with a bare `uv run` in the checkout (sentinel visible / interpreter):

| venv | invocation | sentinel | version |
|---|---|---|---|
| 3.12 | plain | yes | 3.12 |
| 3.12 | pinned 3.14 parent | no | 3.14 |
| 3.14 | plain | no | 3.12 |
| 3.14 | pinned 3.14 parent | no | 3.14 |

## The gate

`tests/test_gh2163_isolated_test_env.py` has three tests, none skipped. Each
builds a sentinel venv in `tmp_path`, so the gate runs on every box:

- premise: a plain `uv run --no-project` under `VIRTUAL_ENV` imports the sentinel
- isolation: `PYTEST_ISOLATED` does not import it
- version: with `UV_PYTHON` set to the venv's version, the isolated interpreter reports that version

The file has no skip condition, so it cannot skip in CI. CI runs the full suite
through `make coverage-shard`; I have not checked that this file is in a shard.

## Verification

Through make targets:

- `make test-fast TEST_FAST_CMD='$(PYTEST) -q tests/test_gh2163_isolated_test_env.py'` on the default interpreter: 3 passed
- the same under `UV_PYTHON=3.14`: 3 passed

Sabotage, via `scripts/sabotage.py`, Makefile restored byte-identical afterward:

- dropping `--isolated`: red on `test_the_isolated_suite_does_not_import_the_sentinel`
- pinning `--python /usr/bin/python3` in its place: red on `test_the_isolated_suite_runs_the_interpreter_uv_was_asked_for`

The premise has no Makefile sabotage. It is covered by the 3.14 run and the table above.

body:
## What this fixes (all reported behaviours)

1. **YouTube was open on the first visit; the option only appeared after a reload.**
   - Every `page.init` message now has its own 3s timeout (a dropped callback no longer stalls the page), the question is retried for up to 60s (the last pause repeats after the initial growth), and while waiting the page shows a fail-closed **"Checking this site…"** cover. The chooser and the YouTube filter attach on the **first** load — no reload. If the extension context dies, the cover removes itself.

2. **Force-played a video from an unproductive channel in Productive Mode and it counted as productive.**
   - The YouTube page kind is re-read on **every** scan (SPA navigation channel/home → watch is judged correctly), and a video's **`play` event triggers the channel check synchronously**: the channel name is read the moment the video starts, and a non-matching video is covered and paused on the first play — no reload. Covered time is reported as an intentional cover, so it neither earns nor spends.

3. **Don't remove unproductive channel results from Search.**
   - Search results are never filtered now; every channel stays visible. The check happens only while the content plays (see 2).

4. **No banner over the YouTube homepage in Productive Mode.**
   - The study-search cover is gone. The homepage simply shows **no videos**; search box and guide keep working.

5. **WhatsApp still blanked chats; make it a trust-based half-productive site.**
   - `web.whatsapp.com` is back on the default half-productive list (storage **schema 4**, re-added exactly once for upgraded installs, afterwards the stored list is authoritative). It is **fully visible in both modes** — nothing blanked — with the same Productive/Unproductive chooser as every other half-productive site. Productive earns at your ratio, Unproductive is charged to the balance. Legacy WhatsApp auto-reply data stays discarded.

6. **Timer must tick live and be exact (never 2s per 1s).**
   - The popup asks the worker for a checkpoint **every second** (`ui.tick`): Remaining, Earned/Used and the live role advance in real time instead of freezing between 30s alarm ticks. Remaining always shows seconds, plus a new **"This visit"** session timer ticking every second. Interpolation now works in both directions (spend down, earn up at the ratio). A new sim test checkpoints 30 simulated seconds and asserts a ~30s charge — a double charge would be ~60s and fail.

7. **Remove the greyscale in unproductive YouTube.**
   - Greyscale is gone entirely: the directive field, the injected style, and all tests asserting it.

## Verification

- `npm test`: **152 passing** — 106 unit + 13 jsdom DOM + 33 simulated-browser flow tests
- `npm run typecheck` (strict): clean
- `npm run build`: artifacts rebuilt at the repo root
- Browser (Playwright) suite updated for all of the above but **not run here** — no Chromium binary in this sandbox (`CHROME_PATH`); the real-Chrome checklist in `docs/TESTING.md` still applies.

## Release

- Version bumped to **2.3.0** (manifest, package).
- `source/RELEASE_NOTES.md` rewritten for 2.3.0 (used as the GitHub release notes).
- `.github/workflows/publish-release-v2.3.0.yml` added: after this PR is merged, pushing a commit containing `[publish v2.3.0]` to `arena/e5df21cc-earntime` builds `EarnTime-2.3.0.zip` from the merge commit and publishes it on the v2.3.0 release.

body:
Service status and application progress currently republish retained registration records, growing the entities stream during normal operation. Keep `_ServiceDetails` for registration, capability changes and reconnect; send runtime health/progress to the deployment's telemetry exporter.

Coordinated workers publish completion and live readiness through ordered `_ClockProgress` records. Readiness continues while factory time is paused; retained replay and duplicate markers do not refresh it. Noncoordinated workers report telemetry without starting a readiness heartbeat. An exporter failure cannot suppress functional completion.

Requires Colca/contracts 0.32.1 and coordinated upgrades of clock participants. CI is pinned to the merged Colca implementation. Mixed old/new coordinated workers are unsupported.

Validation: the full suite passed 905 tests against the matching broker and bundle; four focused integration tests, lint and mypy passed. Real broker paused-clock/reconnect/no-registration-heartbeat integration independently passed. Independent adversarial review found no remaining blocking issue. The integration fixtures now assert runtime telemetry instead of removed registration fields and use an explicit historical offset when probing retention; a fresh cursor correctly starts at the current low-water mark.

author: martinschmidt
body:
## Problem

When a client (commonly a TCP health probe) resets or aborts a connection while the server is writing to it — most often while sending the 220 banner — the write fails with an `IOException` wrapping a `SocketException`. `StreamPipeWriterService.ExecuteAsync` logged every one of these at Warning level, which is noisy for traffic that is entirely client-initiated and not a server problem.

This mirrors upstream FubarDevelopment/FtpServer#166, which addressed the same issue for `SocketError.ConnectionReset` on Windows.

## Fix

`StreamPipeWriterService.ExecuteAsync`'s existing catch block now chooses the log level based on the exception: if it's caused by the peer closing the connection (`SocketException` with `SocketErrorCode` of `ConnectionReset`, `ConnectionAborted`, or `Shutdown`), it logs at Debug; any other, unexpected exception still logs at Warning. The control flow itself — `_pipeReader.AdvanceTo(readResult.Buffer.Start)` followed by `throw;` — is unchanged from before this PR.

**Note on an earlier revision of this PR:** the first version of this fix had the peer-reset branch `return` early instead of falling through to the existing `AdvanceTo` + `throw`. That was wrong: skipping `AdvanceTo` leaves the `PipeReader`'s last read result unadvanced ("reading in progress"), and a later read on the same reader — e.g. the one `StopAsync`'s `SafeFlushAsync` performs during shutdown — then throws `InvalidOperationException` ("Reading is already in progress"), which gets logged as its own Warning in `SafeFlushAsync`. The rethrow was never actually the noisy part: `PausableFtpService.RunAsync` already catches `IOException` silently and completes the service normally either way. This revision keeps the original control flow exactly and only varies the log level.

I verified empirically on this machine (macOS) what a reset-while-writing actually surfaces as: writing to a stream whose peer reset the connection throws an `IOException` with an inner `SocketException` whose `SocketErrorCode` is `Shutdown` ("Broken pipe") — not `ConnectionReset`. The check therefore covers `ConnectionReset`, `ConnectionAborted`, and `Shutdown` to be portable across platforms/runtimes rather than assuming the Windows-specific code from the upstream PR.

I also checked the pre-existing `catch (Exception ex) when (ex.Is<IOException>())` in `SafeFlushAsync` (used during shutdown flush): it already swallows all `IOException`s silently with no logging at all, so its behavior is already at least as lenient as the new Debug-level path and needed no change for consistency.

## Test

Added `test/FubarDev.FtpServer.Tests/StreamPipeWriterServiceTests.cs`, a unit test that drives `StreamPipeWriterService` directly (it's `internal`, and the test assembly already has `InternalsVisibleTo` access) against a fake `Stream` whose `WriteAsync` always throws the `IOException`/`SocketException` shape under test, for each of `ConnectionReset`, `ConnectionAborted`, and `Shutdown`. A recording `ILogger` captures all log entries. After the simulated peer reset, the test also calls `StopAsync` (with a timeout) and asserts it completes and produces no additional Warning/Error entries — this covers the `AdvanceTo` regression described above, since skipping it causes `SafeFlushAsync`'s later read to throw and log a Warning. The test then asserts no Warning-or-higher entry exists overall and a Debug entry mentions the peer closing the connection.

I confirmed both regressions are caught by this test, each against the production file only:
- Reverting the whole fix (original `catch (Exception ex) { LogWarning; AdvanceTo; throw; }` only) → all three cases fail on `Assert.DoesNotContain()` because a Warning "Sending data failed ..." entry is present.
- Reinstating just the earlier `return`-without-`AdvanceTo` variant (keeping the rest of the current fix) → all three cases fail on `Assert.DoesNotContain()` because `StopAsync`'s flush produces a "Flush failed with: Reading is already in progress." Warning.

Both fail against their respective buggy variants and pass against the current code.

I initially attempted an end-to-end reproduction (connecting a `TcpClient` with `LingerState = new LingerOption(true, 0)` and closing before the banner is read, similar to `ConnectionCleanupTests`), but after the earlier connection-leak fix (#6), the connection's read side notices the closed stream and tears the connection down cooperatively before the write ever gets a chance to throw — so that path no longer reliably reproduces the Warning end-to-end. The unit-level test above reproduces it deterministically instead.

## Verification

- `dotnet build FubarDev.FtpServer.sln` — 0 warnings, 0 errors.
- `dotnet test FubarDev.FtpServer.sln` — full suite passes (43 passed, 18 skipped Windows-only path tests, as expected on macOS).
- `dotnet format FubarDev.FtpServer.sln --verify-no-changes --no-restore` — exit 0.

author: rchezhian81-prog
body:
## What this fixes (audit PF-06 · M12-FR-03 · D04-FR-02 · §4.3 · hard rules #1, #3, #6)
When the card machine did not answer, the till refused the sale and wrote **no record at all** (audit: "runtime-reproduced no-answer creates zero durable records"). If the machine had taken the money, nobody knew, and the next try could charge the customer again. The tested recovery rule `recoverPendingTender` was connected only to a head-office compute route.

## What changed
- **`edge/store-edge/src/payment-attempts.ts` (`PaymentAttempts`, `PaymentProviderPort`)**, an fsync'd append-only log:
  - **ask** records bill, kind, amount and who *before* the machine is asked. The id is the merchant reference. Card-number-like references are refused (rule #3).
  - **answer** records approved, declined or no-answer; the first answer stands.
  - **recover** settles a no-answer **only** against the provider's record, through the port and the `recoverPendingTender` rule:
    - an incomplete record means still unknown;
    - a complete record with nothing means not paid;
    - a capture means paid;
    - a double capture means paid, with the extra owed back.
  - While a no-answer is unresolved, a new attempt on that bill is refused. A confirmed-but-unused payment on the bill is handed back instead of charging again.
  - `checkTenders` runs at sale intake: each card/UPI tender must name an attempt recorded as paid, for that amount, on this till, and not used by another sale. Its use is recorded after the commit.
  - `status` returns three lists: unresolved, paid without a sale, and owed back.
- **Lane socket:** `POST /lane/payment-attempts`, `/answer`, `/recover`, plus `GET` for the account. Only the signed-in person may use them.
- **Start-up:** `startEdge` takes a `paymentProvider` port. None is live in this build; tests pass a stand-in.
- **Till**
  - `Tender.ref`; `PosSession.billRef()` (one reference per basket).
  - `bootPos` gains `startCardPayment`, `answerCardPayment` and `checkCardPayment`. The exchange top-up carries its `ref`.
  - `app.js` has a shared `cardAttempt`: record first, then the machine question. When an unresolved payment exists on the bill, the screen offers "Check that payment with the provider" instead of the machine.
- **Till-screen guardrail:** now follows the shared flow, which still asks the machine question.

## Proof
- **Integration on a real box with a stand-in provider** (8):
  - the attempt is recorded before the machine is asked;
  - approved → the sale carries the reference, and it cannot pay a second bill;
  - a card sale with no recorded payment is refused;
  - declined stands;
  - **the audit's no-answer case:** it is on disk, a second charge is refused, "no provider" is said, and a restart keeps it;
  - the provider confirms paid → the payment is used, not charged again;
  - a complete record showing no payment → the customer may pay again;
  - a double capture → the extra is owed back;
  - a card-number-like reference is refused.
- **Browser, through the till's real buttons:** Card → no answer → on disk → Card again offers a check, not the machine → an approved payment on a new bill carries its reference.
- **The new tests fail on the code before the fix.** On the old code, the browser case shows no record of the attempt at all.
- **Local gate:** 10,395 unit/integration, 31 performance and 258 browser tests pass. The store-day browser test was run with the database. Lint and secret scan are clean.

## Not yet
- No live payment provider is connected; credentials and certification are an external gate.
- The unresolved list stays on the box; it does not yet reach head office (Wave 5).
- Card refunds are not in this slice.
- Staff UAT (SP-10) is pending.

## For the owner (plain English)
Before the cashier asks the card machine for money, the store computer now writes the payment down. If the machine never answers, that is written down too, and the till will **not** let the cashier try the same bill on the machine again. Trying again is how a customer gets charged twice. Instead it offers to check with the payment company. Until a real payment company is connected, the screen says to take cash.

When a payment is confirmed, it can pay only one bill. If a customer was charged twice, it is listed as money owed back to them.

**What to check in the store (demo data):**
1. Ring an item and tap Tender → Card → "It has not answered". The screen says do not hand over the goods.
2. Tap Tender → Card again. The screen offers "Check that payment with the provider", not the machine.
3. On a new bill, Tender → Card → Approved completes the sale.

author: krantheman
body:
All accounts couldn't select threads: no checkboxes, no select-all, no bulk actions. It also didn't mark unknown senders and didn't put the subject in the tab title.

Selection now lives in one place that both lists use: `useListSelection`, `selectActions` and the `ListSelection` components. The single-account list drops its own copy (about 300 lines), so the two can't drift apart again.

- Bulk actions in All accounts run once per account, with that account's own folders. One Undo puts every account's mail back, after the action has landed.
- Bulk actions act on every copy of a message, so a mail you sent yourself doesn't leave its twin in Sent.
- On phones, All accounts gets the same selection header and action bar as a single account.

Not included: Outbox and New Folder in All accounts (a new folder has to go in some account, which needs a decision), Move To on a selection, and Shift+arrow range selection.

author: crowloki
body:
## Summary
Make direct CrowBot AI image requests work in standalone CrowClaw and run image generation without a mandatory extra approval popup.

## What changed
- Add CrowClaw-owned direct internet chat and image clients; no separate app or checkout is required.
- Connect the image operation to the actual model tool registry, retain JPEG/PNG/WebP output bytes and display generated pictures inline.
- Default image requests to automatic execution; offer extra confirmation only as an off-by-default owner preference.
- Add persistent automatic local-operation choices and honour saved denial without another confirmation prompt.
- Preserve current tool results in action framing and reject duplicate completed image requests before repeating generation.
- Preserve local personalities through the chat request and task snapshot, without bundling personal profile data.
- Ensure native main-window destruction requests shutdown while respecting background preferences.

## Why
Normal image requests previously returned descriptions/promises or failed because the operation was absent from the offered registry. A real JPEG then exposed a PNG-only settlement guard and repeated-generation proposals. Crow explicitly rejected mandatory per-image approval.

## How tested
- 205 frontend tests pass.
- 189 Rust library tests pass; four explicit live probes remain ignored by ordinary runs.
- 11 attachment integration tests pass, including original PNG and JPEG bytes across settlement and database reopen.
- Separate direct chat and image service probes pass without paid keys or membership fallback.
- Actual installed ordinary cat request completes with zero pending approvals, a real JPEG displayed inline and retained after full process restart. Automatic preferences and the selected provider/personality also persist.
- Type/production frontend, Windows NSIS build, installed binary identity and diff checks pass.

## Risk / out of scope
Local permissions are owner-configured; image confirmation is optional. Selected-folder boundaries remain. No physical printing, sibling edit, credential publication or paid API fallback is included. This PR is source delivery, not a claim that every service modality or Android CrowClaw packaging is complete, and not a new public installer release.

ComfyUI never removes its finished videos from `<ComfyUI>/output` on the network volume, and the volume is billed per GB, so every batch left its segment clips behind. New opt-in cleanup, off by default, deletes a result from the pod's S3 volume only after it is verified safe on disk.

- Settings → RunPod Volume (S3): "Delete each segment video from the pod volume after it is downloaded" (off by default) + Output Prefix.

author: ychampion
body:
## What changes

**Catalog apps that need no setup are ready.** Notion, Linear, Atlassian, Sentry and Stripe each answer dynamic client registration (checked against each server's protected-resource and authorization-server metadata), so the only thing a sign-in needs is somewhere for the browser to come back to. When `MELETE_PUBLIC_URL` is unset or unusable, the sign-in returns to the address the person opened Melete at:

- the web proxy states it in `X-Melete-Web-Origin` (replacing anything the browser sent), and the service believes it only from `MELETE_TRUSTED_PROXY`, like the client address header;
- it must be `https://` or on this machine (for example an SSH tunnel to `http://127.0.0.1:<port>`);
- the web proxy lets the return from the app's site through as a `GET` page load to `/api/oauth/callback` or `/api/oauth/<provider>/callback` only; every other cross-site request is still refused.

GitHub alone waits for an operator-registered OAuth app. Its card now says that in plain words; the operator also sees what to set (`GITHUB_MCP_CLIENT_ID` / `GITHUB_MCP_CLIENT_SECRET`). Account sign-ins (Google, Microsoft) are unchanged.

**Adding an MCP server by its address discovers its tools.** `POST /mcp-servers/discover` reads `tools/list` and suggests where each tool starts (read, a change that can be undone, asks first, spends); the person keeps or drops each and changes how far it may act, and the installation is built from that, one grant per tool. A server that wants a sign-in answers `needs_sign_in`; `POST /mcp-sign-ins` with `discover` signs in, reads the tools, and waits (`ready`) until `POST /mcp-sign-ins/{id}/install` names the tools kept. The Connect screen's "MCP server (HTTP)" form is now name, address, optional token, then the tool list.

**Failures say what went wrong.** New check codes `unreachable`, `not_mcp` and `tool_missing`. DeepWiki's "refused the credential" came from a typed tool name the server does not have (its tool is `ask_wiki_question`); the transport itself connects fine.

No migration.

## Verification

- Targeted tests: `mcp-discovery.test.ts` (readiness per catalog entry, return address, discovery and the discover sign-in, failure messages), plus `mcp-oauth`, `mcp-catalog`, `mcp-protocol`, `mcp`, `listener`, `serve-static`, `ConnectionInstall`, contracts, mock-api and client tests: all pass.
- `bun run typecheck` clean; Biome clean on changed files; OpenAPI and client regenerated.
- Connect screen checked with Playwright against the mock, fresh profile, 1440 and 390 px, light and dark: five apps offer Connect, GitHub says what is missing, a server's tools are listed and adjustable with nothing typed, a sign-in-first server offers its sign-in, no horizontal overflow, no console errors.

**Nachtlauf 8 · Nr. 46** · Kundensicht kinderleicht (Register N2; Geldpfad) · Basis **`main`** (9c7da65). **Migration: nein.** **Per Merge-Commit mergen, nicht per Squash.**

- **Kasse** (N2, FAGG § 9 Abs. 3):
  - Kein Bar-Haken und kein Neuigkeiten-Haken mehr. Der Kaufknopf bleibt „Zahlungspflichtig bestellen", die Bar-Bestätigung per Mail (H3) bleibt.
  - Abholtermine als Kacheln mit Datum („Sa, 10. Okt"; heute und morgen zusätzlich „Heute"/„Morgen").
  - **Beträge, Servicegebühr (E4) und B1 unverändert.** Der Checkout verliert nur zwei Felder und den Abo-Schritt 10b. Felder alter Tabs verwirft das Schema still.
- **Neuigkeiten auf der Bestätigungsseite:** Neu ist eine Karte mit dem Knopf „Ja, Neuigkeiten per E-Mail" und eine Server Action über `meldeEmailAboAn` (Double-Opt-in S11 bleibt).
  - Die Signatur wird vor jeder Abfrage geprüft. Die Adresse kommt nur aus der Bestellung, die Antwort ist immer gleich.
  - Die Karte erscheint nur bei einer laufenden Bestellung (online bezahlt, bar bestätigt oder bar offen bis zur Frist), nie bei storniert, verfallen, nicht abgeholt oder unbezahlt. Karte und Action nutzen dieselbe Regel (`neuigkeitenErlaubt`).
  - Höchstens drei Anfragen je Bestellung und Tag (Datenbank-Bremse aus Nr. 40), dazu ein Link je Abo und zehn Minuten.
- **Hofseite:** „Nächste Abholung" als Textzeilen mit Datum, in Wiener Zeit gerechnet (vorher in der Zeit des Geräts).
- **/hoefe:** ein Feld „Ort oder Produkt". Den Ort sucht es nur bei genau vier Ziffern oder auf ausdrücklichen Wunsch („Höfe rund um … zeigen"), nie beim Tippen.
- **Cookie-Hinweis:** am Handy eine flache Zeile über Unterleiste und Kaufknopf, damit der erste Hof bei 390 × 844 ganz zu sehen ist.

## Zur Freigabe
- **Mockup-Abweichungen (mit Bild):**
  - /hoefe mit einem Feld;
  - Hofseite mit Zeilen statt Kacheln;
  - Kassen-Kachel „Heute" plus Datum;
  - neue Neuigkeiten-Karte;
  - Cookie-Hinweis flach am Handy (kein Mockup, zur Kenntnis).
- **Restrisiko, bewusst so:** Bei bezahlten oder bestätigten Bestellungen bleibt „Neuigkeiten" ohne Frist erlaubt (die Signatur läuft nie ab). Wer online mit fremder Adresse bezahlt, kann bis zu drei Bestätigungsmails am Tag auslösen; das gibt es nur gegen echtes Geld.
- **Produktfolge:** Bei „Zahlung wird geprüft" fehlt die Karte, und die Seite lädt nicht von selbst nach. Online-Kundinnen sehen sie oft erst beim nächsten Öffnen des Links.
- **Für dich (nicht geändert):**
  - Datenschutzerklärung §9 („beim Abschluss einer Bestellung … E-Mail und/oder WhatsApp") passt nach dem Merge nicht mehr.
  - Der Knopf heißt dort „In meiner Nähe" statt „Standort nutzen".
  - WhatsApp-Neuigkeiten haben keinen Ersatz mehr; das ist eine Entscheidung fürs Register.

## Checkliste (freigabe.md §12, §3)
- [x] Register und Freigabe decken den Inhalt ab (N2, S11, H3, E4, B1; §12 „46")
- [x] origin/main vor dem Push hineingeholt (9c7da65, aktuell)

- [x] Axe ohne Fehler, Touch-Ziele ≥ 44 px, `loading.tsx` passend
- [x] Texte aus einer Quelle, Deutsch, per Du
- [x] tester und pruefer gelaufen, Befunde erledigt oder begründet (Nachprüfung siehe unten)
- [x] Entwurf, wenn eine Vorbedingung offen ist: keine

## Prüfung
- **`tester` grün** (e0a6b00): unit 290 / 5525; Integration 36 / 331; lint 13/7; eslint.config.mjs nur strenger (cookie-banner.tsx verlässt die Ausnahmeliste der Farbwerte); kein Diff unter `prisma/`.
- **`pruefer`:** kein Blocker. Drei „Sollte":
  - **Sicherheit:** Die Neuigkeiten-Action prüfte keinen Bestellstatus. Ein dauerhaft gültiger Link konnte für stornierte oder unbezahlte Bestellungen alle 10 Minuten Mails an eine fremde Adresse auslösen.
  - **Sicherheit/Doku:** Der Lese-Link erlaubt jetzt einen Schreibweg.
  - 1440-px-Bilder fehlten.

  Dazu vier Hinweise.
- **Runde 1 (ff52d03)** behebt alles:
  - Statusregel `neuigkeitenErlaubt` für Karte und Action, Bremse je Bestellung.
  - Ehrliche Doku samt Wache „3 Lesewege, 1 Schreibweg".

- **Nachprüfung (Geldpfad):** kein Blocker, kein „Sollte". Kasse, Checkout, Beträge und Bestand sind vom Fix unberührt; Abholfenster und Fristen rechnen unverändert. Die Hinweise (UTC-Tag der Bremse, Pfad in CODING_STANDARDS, eine Gegenprobe, `env` im Integrationstest) hat der Dirigent nachgezogen (**7397979**, nur Doku und Tests).
- **Selbst wiederholt:** Typecheck grün, `pnpm test` 290 / 5554, Integration der geänderten Datei 7 / 7.
