author: pavellnk
body:
## Summary

Follow-up to #1852 for [AYC-85](https://linear.app/ayunis/issue/AYC-85/type-safe-cls-rolesystemrole-reads-in-use-cases). Stacked on #1852.

#1852 left `required-context.ts` with two vocabularies for the same thing: `getRequiredUserContext` (`{ userId, orgId }`, 60 callers) next to `getUserPrincipal` / `getRequiredUserPrincipal` (`{ userId, orgId, role, systemRole }`, 16 callers). This PR unifies them on the word the codebase already uses everywhere else (`ContextService`, `UserContextInterceptor`, `getRequiredOrgId`):

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| `getRequiredUserContext(ctx): { userId, orgId }` | `getRequiredUserContext(ctx): UserContext` (now includes roles) |
| `getRequiredUserPrincipal(ctx)` | deleted, callers use `getRequiredUserContext` |
| `getUserPrincipal(ctx)` | `getUserContext(ctx)` |
| `interface UserPrincipal` | `interface UserContext` |
| `isSuperAdmin(ctx)`, `getRequiredOrgId(ctx)` | unchanged |

The ticket's `ContextService.requireUserPrincipal()` is not possible (see #1852: `ContextService` is a `useExisting` alias of `ClsService`), and the "principal" wording came from a planned `ResolvedPrincipal` type that never landed, so "context" is the vocabulary that matches the rest of the module.

A shared `src/common/context/testing/context.fixtures.ts` (`aUserContext`, `getFromUserContext`, `createMockContextService`) builds a complete user store. The workspace fixture delegates to it.

## Classification

**High-Risk Path** — trigger: change to the authorization accessors used by every user-only use case.

## Failure-mode matrix

| Failure mode | Check |
| --- | --- |
| `getRequiredUserContext` starts throwing for a real user login | Not possible: `UserContextInterceptor` sets `userId`, `orgId`, `role`, `systemRole` in the same block, so the two new conditions cannot fail where the old one passed. CI browser e2e exercises logged-in journeys. |
| API key or org-only background job gains a user context | `required-context.spec`: `getUserContext` / `getRequiredUserContext` return `undefined` / throw for api-key and org-only stores, including with leaked roles |
| A caller's authorization check changed semantics | No call-site logic changed; the diff at 16 sites is the identifier rename only |
| Pattern B (api-key reachable) sites affected | They use `getRequiredOrgId` / `isSuperAdmin`, both unchanged |
| Spec doubles model a state that cannot occur (user without roles) | 40 specs now build the store via `aUserContext` / `getFromUserContext`; the fixture is the single place that defines a user store |
| `testing/` fixture leaks into the production build | `tsc -p tsconfig.build.json --noEmit` clean (`**/testing/**` excluded) |
| New raw role read added later | ESLint rule from #1852 unchanged apart from the message text |

Persistence, transport contracts and frontend do not participate.

## Validation

Local, worktree on top of #1852:

- `pnpm exec tsc --noEmit` — clean
- `pnpm exec tsc -p tsconfig.build.json --noEmit` — clean
- repo-wide `pnpm exec eslint src eslint.config.mjs` — 0 errors
- `pnpm test` — 884 / 885 suites, 6042 / 6043 tests. The one failure is `src/common/util/msg.spec.ts` (Windows-1252 decoding), untouched by this PR and green on #1852 in CI; local Node ICU issue.
- Pre-commit hooks (staged ESLint, Prettier, typecheck, complexity, dependency, duplication, file size) all passed.

Spec changes are mock setup only; no assertion changed except `required-context.spec.ts`, which now asserts the four-field return shape and the per-key missing cases.

author: nothariharan
body:
Consolidates the outstanding fixes for three issues into one branch, rebased onto current `v8`. Every referenced PR was raised against an older `v8` revision and no longer applies; this is the single, current version. One previous version of this PR was self-reviewed and two real issues were found and fixed before opening (see **Review notes** below).

## What this fixes

### #2698 — classify `.gs`, `.css` and extensionless config files
- **`.gs` (Google Apps Script) is now code**: routed to the JavaScript extractor, the JS language/resolution family, the AST-cache bypass set and the rebuild hook. A GLSL/Gosu marker guard (`#version `, `gl_Position`, `EmitVertex`, `uses java.` …) leaves a real geometry shader / Gosu file without an extractor rather than force-parsing it as JS.
- **`.css` / `.scss` / `.less` are code.**
- **Well-known extensionless config/build files** (`.htaccess`, `Dockerfile`, `Makefile`, `Procfile`, `Vagrantfile`, …) are classified by filename as documents instead of being dropped as "not classified".

### #3473 — design-token systems were invisible to the graph
- New `graphify/extractors/css.py`: a brace-aware, comment/string-aware, dependency-free scan. It emits a node per custom-property definition in a root/theme context (`:root`, `:host`, `html`, `body`, `[data-theme…]`, `.dark`, `.theme-*`, `@theme`), a `defines_token` edge per definition, and collects `var(--x)` uses.
- Uses resolve to a same-file definition, or to exactly one cross-file definition; ambiguous or missing uses emit nothing (no fan-out).
- A custom property declared **locally** (outside a root context, e.g. a component overriding a theme token) shadows a same-named global, so no false cross-file edge is invented — while a file that also declares the token in `:root` keeps its own same-file edge.
- Wired through the incremental cache (`raw_token_uses`) and both id-remap passes; warm and cold extraction agree.

### #2498 — the filename-only secrets filter silently drops design-token files
The report has two distinct halves:
- **`.css` case (reporting defect):** `tokens.css` is now genuinely graphable, so the misleading "skipped as potentially sensitive" message for an unsupported extension is gone.
- **`tokens.json` / `tokens.contract.json` (real data loss):** `#3527` deliberately keeps bare plural `tokens` in data files excluded, so rather than weaken the default the fix is the **explicit override** the issue asked for (option 3): a wildcard-free `!path` entry in `.graphifyignore` (or `--exclude`) now overrides **only the Stage-3 name heuristic**.
  - A specific Stage-2 key file (`.env`, `id_rsa`, `server.pem`) or a credential-store directory is **never** rescued.
  - Glob entries (`!*.json`) are ignored, so a broad opt-in cannot silently start ingesting credential stores.
  - An entry is anchored to its own directory and matched case-sensitively; a leading `/` is anchor-exact, per gitignore semantics.
  - Only the **explicit** `.graphifyignore`/`--exclude` set is consulted — never `.gitignore`.
  - Default posture is unchanged: `tokens.json`, `oauth_token.json`, `api_token.txt`, `credentials.json`, `.token`, `secrets.json` all stay skipped unless explicitly overridden.
- **The skip is no longer silent:** `GRAPH_REPORT.md` gains a `## Skipped Files` section listing every excluded file by name, and the CLI skip notice names the escape hatch.

## PRs this supersedes

| PR | Subject | Status here |
|----|---------|-------------|
| #2747 | `.gs` only, minimal | superseded by the `.gs` support here |
| #3505 | `.gs` (comprehensive) | folded in |
| #3480 | CSS/SCSS design tokens | folded in, plus the local-shadow fix |
| #3067 | CSS/HTML UI + JS linkage | superseded by the token-focused design here |
| #2240 | Twig + SCSS | SCSS half superseded; Twig is out of scope for these issues |
| #1921 | `.graphifyinclude` override | superseded by `.graphifyignore` negation (`.graphifyinclude` was removed in #2112) |
| #3605 | closed omnibus | superseded |

All of the above no longer merge onto `v8`; this branch applies cleanly on `v8` @ `5b74d7d`.

## Review notes (self-review before opening)
Two independent verification passes were run. They caught and this branch fixes:
1. The override was initially reading the *merged* ignore set (including `.gitignore` and nested anchors) and matching case-insensitively — i.e. broader than the "exact `.graphifyignore` path" it promised. It now uses the explicit pattern set only, is anchor-scoped, and case-sensitive.
2. `var()` resolution initially ignored local custom-property shadowing, inventing false `EXTRACTED` `uses_token` edges between a component override and a theme token. Fixed, then narrowed so a file that also defines the token in `:root` keeps its same-file edge.

## Tests

New / extended:
- `tests/test_gs_apps_script.py` — `.gs` routing, GLSL/Gosu guard, node parity with `.js`.
- `tests/test_css.py` — CSS/SCSS/Less classification, token extraction, comments/strings/urls/nesting/themes, cross-file resolution, same-file precedence, local shadowing, warm cache.
- `tests/test_detect.py` — explicit-negation rescue, `.gitignore`-only negation does not rescue, anchor scoping, leading-slash anchoring, wildcard entries do not rescue, Stage-1/2 never rescued, dotfile classification.
- `tests/test_report.py` — `## Skipped Files` present/absent.

Local results (`v8` @ `5b74d7d`, Python 3.12, Windows):
- Focused suites: `test_detect.py` 304 passed / 1 skipped, `test_css.py` 25 passed, `test_report.py` 21 passed, `test_gs_apps_script.py` 10 passed, `test_extract.py` 289 passed / 4 skipped.
- `ruff check` on all changed files: clean.
- Full suite: **6699 passed, 24 failed, 184 skipped**. All 24 failures reproduce identically on a clean `v8` checkout — they are pre-existing Windows/environment failures (no `os.mkfifo`, read-only-file semantics, missing home dir under a stripped env, cp1252 unicode, and gemini/hermes install + watch/hook timing). None is in a file this branch touches.

## Known limitations
- The `.gs` sniff scans the first 256 KiB for GLSL/Gosu markers; a genuine Apps Script file that literally contains one of those substrings in a string or comment is left without an extractor (same outcome as MATLAB `.m`). Kept from #3505's conservative design.
- Tailwind-style utility-class → token inference is deliberately **not** attempted; only unambiguous `var()` references are resolved.
- The CSS extractor is `.css`/`.scss`/`.less`, not Sass indented syntax; `@import url(...)` prose is not resolved.

author: jdegreef
body:
Closes #5220.

## What ships
- **Book:** `content/books/how-to-bring-men-to-christ.fr.json` holds the book row and 13 chapters, all `ai_unreviewed`.
  - Title « Comment amener les hommes à Christ », subtitle « Manuel de l’œuvre personnelle », plus the description and 8 Q&A.
  - About 26.4k words, against 25.3k in English.
- **Notes:** `translation_notes/book/how-to-bring-men-to-christ.fr.json` has 483 rows: 46 mined, 437 self_rendered.
  - Torrey cites several hundred verses by reference, and only the ones he has the inquirer read are quoted.
  - So most printed references carry no verbatim Segond span, and the method's first pass marks them self_rendered.
- **Cover:** `localize_covers` points the row at the existing curated ground `/covers/art/how-to-bring-men-to-christ.jpg`. The French share card is drawn, with its one manifest entry.
- **Plan:** none needed; the book isn't in any plan.
- **Back matter:** this book has a `corrections.BODY_CORRECTIONS` back-matter seam. The French fixture is clean, and the existing English seam keeps the entry live, so no French seam is needed.

## How it was built
- **Units:** 9 parallel units worked from one shared brief. The brief fixed:
  - the 13 chapter titles (« Comment s’occuper de… »);
  - a glossary: « l’œuvre personnelle », « rétrograde », « le baptême du Saint-Esprit », which matches the shipped French Torrey books.
- **References:** every one is converted from Roman numerals to French form with Segond numbering. Each unit checked its reference count against the English. Examples:
  - Ps 84:11 → « Psaume 84:12 »
  - Ps 51:14 → « Psaume 51:16 »
  - Ps 19:1-2 → « Psaume 19:2, 3 »
  - Eccl 12:1 → « Ecclésiaste 12:3 »
  - Job 40:2 → « Job 39:35 »
- **Scripture:** Louis Segond 1910, pasted byte-for-byte by script. Torrey's scripted questions and answers are reworded to agree with the French verse the inquirer is reading, for example:
  - Jean 1:12 « enfants de Dieu », with « l’avez-vous reçu » about Christ
  - Galates 3:10 « Maudit »
  - Proverbes 29:1 « brisé »
  - Jean 5:40 « vous ne voulez pas venir »
- **Cross-reference:** ch09's pointer to the ch08 sections uses ch08's own French headings.

## Validation
- **Text:** the tag sequence is identical in all 13 chapters. There are no straight quotes, and the word ratio is 1.01–1.10 per chapter.
- **References:** the reference count matches the English in every chapter. The only `? ! ; :` without a space before them are inside verbatim Segond quotations.
- **Backend:** 242 tests pass:
  - `tests_fixture`, including `CitationRangeTests`
  - `tests_book_export`
  - `tests_mined_verification`
  - `tests_translation_markup`
  - `tests_translation_notes`
  - `tests_verse_consistency` (no re-pin)
  - `tests_sanitize`
- **Frontend:** `coverOgManifest` and `coverLayouts` pass (65 tests).

## Share cards
Same situation as #5795 and #5820. On `main`, `og:covers` redraws every card since #5782 moved the ungated `fonts` digest. This PR commits only its own card and manifest entry.

## Found, not fixed (the English source)
The French follows the English. References are converted but kept as printed.
- **ch08:** "2 John v. 10". 2 John has one chapter; the quoted words are 1 John 5:10. Printed as « 2 Jean 5:10 ».
- **ch08:** "Rev. xiii. 7-8" is probably 20:15, the verse tying the book of life to the lake of fire.
- **ch05:** "John ii. 1-2" (Cana) for 1 John 2:1-2 (pardon).
- **ch11:** points to a heading "Those Who are Afraid of Persecution". The ch05 heading actually reads "I will be persecuted if I become a Christian".
- **ch11/ch12:** "2 Tim. iii. 13-17". The Bible-study point starts at v. 14.
- **ch13:** "(ch. i. 4; ii. 16, 33.)". 2:16 doesn't contain "promise", though it introduces Joel.
- **ch05:** "Is. i. 18, and Rev. xxii. 17, can alone be used here". Read as "also", « peuvent aussi être utilisés ».
- **ch01:** "great heaviness and unceasing pain" mixes the KJV and the RV of Rom 9:2.
- **ch07:** "who do these verses say…" about one verse (John 3:36).
- **OCR slips**, read through:
  - "endured with power" for endued
  - "(i Cor." for 1 Cor
  - "Acts; i. 22"
  - "selfrighteous"
  - "according to his verse"
  - "Sceptics"/"skeptic" mixed

author: unjica
body:
Hermes frames such as `at r (address at index.android.bundle:1:165)` previously retained `address at` in the filename and could not find uploaded maps. They now resolve to the fixture throw site `checkout.js:7:14` and its original call sites. Native scheme filenames and iOS absolute paths also match; HTTP-to-HTTP matching keeps host/path checks.

React Native now chains its previous global handler, attempts fatal error delivery for at most one second, installs once per ErrorUtils instance, and defaults platform to `react-native` while preserving explicit overrides. Core error-object deduplication prevents duplicate manual/global reports. Eight RN tests cover this behavior, including a test with the actual core SDK.

OTA design: `buildBundleRelease(nativeVersion, bundleId)` validates and encodes bundle identity. Require a distinct release per JS bundle and separate app labels per platform, since artifacts are not platform-keyed. Match verified device sourceURL/path (or its basename); no single-artifact fallback for unknown OTA hashes and no cross-release fallback. Reject multiple matches and conservatively refuse releases at the 128-ref metadata cap. Release uniqueness cannot be inferred or guaranteed by the server; the guide states the operational requirement.

Function-name decision: retain existing labels, as explicitly permitted by the task when a reliable correction cannot be confirmed. Tests show `originalPositionFor` returns the callee token `computeTotal` at an `onPressPay` call site in both the Hermes composed map and the web packager map. Sentry uses scope information and caller-name heuristics, rather than blindly assigning each token name or shifting all names by one frame ([implementation](https://github.com/getsentry/symbolicator/blob/master/crates/symbolicator-js/src/symbolication.rs)). A universally safe enclosing-name recovery was not established for TT's map-only pipeline. This remaining limitation is documented.

Guide: `docs/expo-hermes-source-maps.md`, linked from SDK React Native docs, `/docs/react-native`, and `/error-tracking/react-native`. Covers SDK setup and identity convention, Android/iOS EAS Build maps and iOS SOURCEMAP_FILE, Expo Update exports and conditional Hermes composition, JSON API upload, an EAS success hook and existing GitHub Action, and runtime bundle URLs. Limits: JS errors only/no native crash capture, 10 MiB map JSON limit, no debug IDs, no automatic EAS integration, function-name limitations and best-effort fatal delivery. No claim of full Expo support. The action's existing `.map` filename fallback suffices for the staged maps; no extension change was needed.

Validation:

- `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`: passed after adding the RN test dependency to the lockfile.
- `pnpm lint`: passed, zero warnings.
- `pnpm test`: 1,435 passed, 128 DB-gated tests skipped, zero failures. API 1,060; dashboard 227; core 67; vite-plugin 14; node 27; next 15; RN 8; publish guards 17.
- Targeted symbolicator: 31 passed, including real Hermes CLI stack/composed-map throw and call positions, native URL variants, ambiguous maps, metadata cap, OTA paths, and web V8/Firefox regressions. Newer Hermes map composed with metro-source-map 0.87.1 resolves the throw using its own synthetic absolute offset (131); this is not a newly executed real device/CLI stack.
- `pnpm build`: passed for all workspace packages including Next production build.
- Production API `tsc -p tsconfig.build.json --noEmit` and RN `tsc --noEmit`: passed.
- Broad API `tsc --noEmit`: 106 existing test-file errors, identical error multiset with the original API test file (line numbers normalized); no new errors. Dashboard broad `tsc --noEmit`: six existing errors in unchanged google-analytics.test.ts and marketing-seo-head.test.ts. Production build type validation passes.
- DB integration attempt: local PostgreSQL initdb failed because sandbox disallowed shared-memory creation; no production database used. CI must run its PostgreSQL-enabled suite after publication.
- Self-review: `git diff origin/develop...`, full working diff/new files, `git status`, and `git diff --check`. HEAD and origin/develop are both 51e1d9d; the local develop ref is stale, so origin/develop was used for comparison. Generated build changes are excluded/restored, as required by the handoff.

CI/publication: pending runner publication. No git-state writes, PR writes, merge, deployment, package publication or EAS update publication performed. No existing branch PR was found with `gh pr list --head codex/hermes-sourcemaps --state all`. The runner should open one normal PR against develop and attach its URL; hosted CI/review cannot start before that step.

UNVERIFIED QA (must be checked on supported Expo/RN versions):

- [ ] Real Android release Hermes sourceURL strings and map offsets.
- [ ] Real iOS release sourceURL strings, SOURCEMAP_FILE output and map offsets.
- [ ] expo-updates OTA device paths and upload identity alignment (including embedded fallback/rollback).
- [ ] Actual composed-map JSON sizes against the 10 MiB cap.
- [ ] Live upload with a project key enabled for source-map upload.

- [ ] Real RN fatal crash/red-box behavior and best-effort delivery on device.
- [ ] Hosted CI including PostgreSQL integration tests and normal review flow.

author: ralayonizquierdo-alt
body:
## Descripción

El Arenal (AP-2-B) es el único inmueble cuyos importes no vienen en el Excel maestro: lo gestiona SOC Properties, se alquila por Airbnb y el dinero llega con las comisiones ya descontadas. Sus 17 reservas de 2026 estaban en la aplicación con importe 0,00 € y tres cobros no colgaban de ninguna estancia.

El informe anual de la gestora trae justo lo que faltaba —bruto, comisiones y neto por estancia—, así que ahora se sube desde Reservas y con él 2026 cuadra: ni una reserva sin importe, ni un cobro sin estancia, nada cobrado de más.

## Cambios principales
- `lib/importarAirbnb.ts`: lee el HTML del informe sin atarse a su maquetado (busca cada concepto por su texto), comprueba sus propias cuentas (bruto − ajuste − comisiones = neto) y cuadra cada estancia contra lo que ya hay — empareja reservas por fechas y enlaza los cobros cuyo importe es exactamente el neto.
- `components/ImportarAirbnb.tsx`: enseña todo antes de guardar nada (qué se crea, a qué se le pone importe, qué cobros se enlazan y qué estancias terminadas siguen sin cobro) y deja su línea en el registro de subidas. Se guarda el **neto**; la limpieza va a 0 y las comisiones **no** se dan de alta como gasto, porque con el ingreso ya neto se descontarían dos veces. **No inventa cobros**: una estancia terminada sin transferencia queda pendiente.
- Panel: solo avisan los **cobros ya vencidos**. Una estancia que aún no ha empezado y no está cobrada es lo normal, y mezclarlas tapaba los descubiertos reales (5 de 14 avisos).
- Descuadres: solo del ejercicio en curso. Los de 2022–2025 son años cerrados y sus cifras no son comparables; eran 6 avisos que nadie iba a mirar.
- `eur()` estaba roto en Reservas y en `priceCalc` —una sustitución en masa dejó `(x, 2)` en vez de `num(x, 2)`— y escribía «2 €» en lugar del importe.

## Tipo de cambio
- [x] Corrección de bug
- [x] Nueva funcionalidad
- [x] Documentación

## Checklist — Service Worker
- [ ] No aplica: no se ha tocado `Index.html` ni ningún asset estático de la raíz.

## Checklist — Seguridad
- [x] No hay claves API, passwords ni tokens en el código
- [x] No hay datos personales de clientes reales en seeds ni comentarios
- [x] Los cambios en localStorage son retrocompatibles (no se ha tocado)

## Pruebas realizadas
- `npm run lint` y `npm run build` limpios (quedan los 5 avisos preexistentes de `react-hooks`).
- Recorrido completo en navegador (Playwright) con los **datos reales** de producción: se sube el informe, se revisa la previsualización y se aplica. Volver a subir el mismo fichero dice «no hay nada que cambiar», así que no duplica.
- Comprobado contra Firestore después de aplicarlo: 2026 no tiene ninguna reserva sin importe ni ningún cobro sin estancia, y nada cobrado de más.
- Queda un único descuadre en 2026, que es dinero y no código: **1.609,17 €** de cuatro estancias del Arenal que el informe da por facturadas y de las que no consta la transferencia (ver DT-36).

author: iwanhae
body:
## Summary

`Controller.refreshObservability` runs on a 1-second ticker and called `Table.Snapshot()`, which copies **every retained RouterRef** (≈5,000 entries on a busy public reseed) just to compute two numbers: total routers and floodfill count. On a memory-constrained reseed host (951 MiB RAM) this per-second full-table allocation churn keeps GC headroom inflated (heap profile showed ~28 MB of live-but-transient `Snapshot` allocations at any instant, plus constant RLock traffic competing with `StoreVerified` writers).

This PR keeps an incremental floodfill counter on `Table` so the loop reads `Len()` / `FloodfillCount()` (O(1), existing RLock) instead of snapshotting.

## Changes

- `netdb.Table`: new `floodfills` counter, maintained under the existing table lock in every mutation path:
  - `StoreVerified`: insert, and transitions when a newer advertisement flips the floodfill flag (upgrade/downgrade)
  - `Remove`, `Expire`, `evictOldestLocked` (also covers `SetRouterLimit` truncation)
- New `Table.FloodfillCount()` accessor
- `runtime.Controller.refreshObservability`: replaces the `Snapshot()` + scan with `Len()` + `FloodfillCount()`

## Testing

- New `TestFloodfillCountTracksEveryMutation` covers insert, flag upgrade/downgrade, stale-update no-op, double remove, expiration, router-limit eviction, and a full-scan cross-check
- `go test ./controlplane/...` — all pass
- `go test -race ./controlplane/internal/netdb/` — pass
- `go test ./cmd/...` — pass

## Impact

- Removes a 1 Hz O(n) copy of the NetDB routing table (memory churn + lock contention on the admission path)
- Memory/CPU relief is most visible on unbounded long-running reseed routers

author: danielchalmers
body:
## Why

On Sep 24, CI runs 35951371383 and 35951360990 failed only on GitHub, because the runner's own environment leaked into the tests. The failing check was `env.test.ts`'s "GITHUB_REPOSITORY is not set" case: `@actions/github` had already loaded the push event's payload from `GITHUB_EVENT_PATH` when it was imported. That case is currently patched inside the test itself. Nothing stops the next test from hitting the same problem.

The test step also prints output that isn't test results. Every run shows 15 leaked `::group::` commands, Vite's "ESM syntax in a file loaded as CommonJS" warning and undici's `UNDICI-EHPA` experimental warning.

## What changed

- New `tests/setup.ts` deletes every `GITHUB_*`, `INPUT_*` and `RUNNER_*` variable in two places:
  - when the setup file loads, before the test file's imports run, so `@actions/github` never sees the runner's event payload;
  - again before each test, so a variable one test sets can't reach the next.
- `silent: 'passed-only'` is set, so only failing tests print console output. I removed the spies that only silenced console output (in runner, issueProcessor, executeOperations, prompts and storageArtifacts tests). Spies that assert on log lines stay. One of the removed spies was never restored, so it had been silencing `console.warn` for the rest of `issueProcessor.test.ts`.
- `issueProcessor.test.ts` mocks `core.group`, which writes `::group::` straight to stdout. `silent` can't hide stdout writes. The re-analysis test now checks the group title on the mock instead of spying on `process.stdout.write`.
- `runner.test.ts` now stubs `GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY` in `beforeEach` instead of `beforeAll`, because the setup clears it before each test. This matches what `summary.test.ts` already does.
- The config was renamed `vitest.config.ts` → `vitest.config.mts`. I confirmed this removes the Vite warning. `.gitattributes` gets `*.mts text eol=lf` so the config keeps LF line endings.
- Test workers run with `--disable-warning=UNDICI-EHPA`. This hides the warning from the proxy test in `tests/llm/chat.test.ts` without editing that file. `tests/llm/` is shared with Nuntia and stays unchanged.
- AGENTS.md now has three sentences on the setup file, the silent setting, and mocking `@actions/core` commands that write to stdout.
- The 2-second slow-header transport test is unchanged.

## Breaking changes

None. Only tests and test config changed, and `dist/` is the same.

## Verification

- `npm run verify` (typecheck, typecheck:test, tests, build, check:dist): passed. 341 tests, and `dist is up to date`.
- `CI=true npx vitest run --silent=false`: passed, 341 tests.
- A plain `npx vitest run` printed none of these: `::group::` lines, `stdout |` or `stderr |` blocks, the UNDICI warning, or the Vite warning. Before this change it printed 15 `::group::` pairs plus both warnings.
- I ran the suite with a fake runner environment: about 20 `GITHUB_*`, `INPUT_*` and `RUNNER_*` variables, with `GITHUB_EVENT_PATH` pointing at a fake payload for a different repo. It passed both with the normal output and with `--silent=false`.
- I also ran a throwaway probe test (not committed) in that environment:
  - with the setup file it saw no runner variables, an empty `github.context.payload`, and no variable set by the previous test;
  - with the setup file removed from the config, both of its tests failed (21 leaked variables, and `GITHUB_TOKEN` carried over from the previous test).
- A throwaway failing test still printed its `console.warn` output, and a passing one in the same file printed nothing.

## Not verified or follow-ups

- Not run on a real GitHub runner. I only tested with the simulated environment above.
- `tests/util.test.ts`, the example duplicate in the plan, was already deleted in "Delete the remaining dead code". No other small test file clearly duplicates another:
  - `parseAnalysisResult`, `additionalInstructions` and `promptLoading` each cover behavior nothing else asserts, so they stay;
  - `additionalInstructions.test.ts` goes away with that input in stack 2.
- Vitest's own "Transform … fsModuleCache" performance note still prints at the end of each run. It isn't test output.
- The roadmap's esbuild install-script approval wasn't part of this item, so I left it out.
- Nuntia stack #7 should do the same: the setup file, `silent`, the `.mts` rename and the `execArgv` flag. No shared `src/llm/` or `tests/llm/` files changed here.

author: mrodriguez1821
body:
## Resumen General
Se introduce la suite completa de componentes comunes en `src/common/`, se reestructura el enrutamiento con layouts protegidos y públicos mediante TanStack Router, y se refactoriza a fondo el componente de tabla [`Table.tsx`] para incluir encabezados flotantes de filtro/ordenamiento, contención de altura fija con scroll interno de registros y paginación completa con botones numéricos y de navegación rápida.

---

## Detalle de Cambios Principales

### 1. Tabla (`Table.tsx` & `Table.stories.tsx`)
- **Filtros y Ordenamiento en Flotante:**
  - Se eliminaron los campos de búsqueda incrustados en la fila de títulos que distorsionaban el ancho de columna.
  - Cada columna con `sortable` o `filterable` cuenta con un botón en el encabezado que despliega un **popover flotante anclado**.
  - El popover incluye opciones de ordenamiento (*Ascendente*, *Descendente*, *Limpiar*) y búsqueda/filtro contextual (texto con botón limpiar `X`, o selector para columnas de valores discretos).
  - Cierre automático al hacer clic fuera o presionar `Escape`.
- **Tamaño Fijo y Scroll Interno:**
  - Soporte de propiedades `height` (por defecto `"520px"`) y `maxHeight`.
  - El contenedor exterior de la tabla ya no crece verticalmente al aumentar el número de registros o cambiar el `pageSize`.
  - El área de registros (`tbody`) aplica `overflow-y-auto`, manteniendo el encabezado **sticky** arriba (`sticky top-0 z-20`) con fondo sólido y el pie de paginación fijo al fondo (`shrink-0`).
- **Paginación Avanzada:**
  - Grupo de botones de navegación:
    - **Primera página (`«` / `ChevronsLeft`)**
    - **Página anterior (`‹` / `ChevronLeft`)**
    - **Botones numéricos interactivos (`[1][2][3]...[N]`)** con ventana deslizante e indicador visual activo.
    - **Página siguiente (`›` / `ChevronRight`)**
    - **Última página (`»` / `ChevronsRight`)**
  - Selector de filas sincronizado dinámicamente (`effectivePageSizeOptions`) para que el valor de `pageSize` siempre coincida con la opción seleccionada.
  - Soporte tanto de paginación del lado del cliente como del servidor (`serverSide`).
  - Compatibilidad transparente con `totalCount` y `totalElements`.

---

### 2. Suite Completa de Pickers y Entradas de Formulario
Se crearon componentes atómicos y compuestos con historias de Storybook y soporte para temas claro/oscuro:
- [`DatePicker.tsx`]: Selector de fecha y variante fecha + hora (`datetime`).
- [`DateRangePicker.tsx`]: Selección de rangos de fechas (Desde / Hasta) con popover interactivo.
- [`TimePicker.tsx`]: Selector de horas y minutos con reloj o selector de lista.
- [`TimeRangePicker.tsx`]: Rango de horas (hora inicial y final).
- [`FilePicker.tsx`]: Subida de archivos con drag & drop, filtros MIME y previsualización.
- [`FolderPicker.tsx`]: Selección de directorios/carpetas con árbol de navegación.
- [`PasswordInput.tsx`]: Input de contraseña con toggle de visibilidad (ojo mostrar/ocultar).
- [`MaskedInput.tsx`]: Input para máscaras numéricas, teléfonos, identificaciones y patrones personalizados.

---

### 3. Arquitectura de Enrutamiento y Layouts
- **Rutas públicas y autenticadas (`src/routes/`):**
  - `_public.tsx` y `login.tsx`: Páginas y demos públicas con layout no autenticado.
  - `_authenticated.tsx`: Guard de autenticación con redirección automática a `/login` si no hay sesión.
  - `_authenticated/home.tsx`: Dashboard principal autenticado.
  - `_authenticated/users.index.tsx` & `_authenticated/users.$userId.tsx`: Gestión y detalle de usuarios.
- **Layouts base en `src/common/components/layout/`:**
  - `Sidebar.tsx`, `TopNav.tsx`, `PageLayout.tsx`, `PageHeader.tsx`, `TablePage.tsx`, `FormPage.tsx`, `AuthContainer.tsx`.

---

### 4. Storybook e Interactividad en Controls
- Todos los componentes en `src/common/components` cuentan con archivos `.stories.tsx`.
- Parámetros y propiedades configurables en vivo desde la pestaña de **Controls** (tamaños, variantes, estados de error, loading, `pageSize`, `currentPage`, `totalCount`, `totalElements`, `totalPages`, `height`, etc.).

---

## Archivos y Rutas Modificados

| Directorio / Archivo | Tipo | Descripción |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `src/common/components/Table.tsx` | Modificado | Encabezados flotantes, scroll de registros, paginador segmentado. |
| `src/common/components/Table.stories.tsx` | Modificado | Historias interactivas con controls reactivos y dataset de prueba. |
| `src/common/lib/types/index.ts` | Modificado | Tipos de `TableProps` (`height`, `maxHeight`, `totalElements`, etc.). |
| `src/common/components/DatePicker*` | Nuevo | Componente de selección de fechas e historias. |
| `src/common/components/DateRangePicker*` | Nuevo | Componente de selección de rango de fechas e historias. |
| `src/common/components/TimePicker*` | Nuevo | Componente de selección de tiempo e historias. |
| `src/common/components/TimeRangePicker*` | Nuevo | Componente de selección de rango de tiempo e historias. |
| `src/common/components/FilePicker*` | Nuevo | Selector y uploader de archivos e historias. |
| `src/common/components/FolderPicker*` | Nuevo | Selector de carpetas e historias. |
| `src/common/components/PasswordInput*` | Nuevo | Entrada de contraseña con máscara alternable. |
| `src/common/components/MaskedInput*` | Nuevo | Entrada de texto con formateo y máscaras. |
| `src/routes/_authenticated.tsx` | Nuevo | Layout protegido con validación de credenciales. |
| `src/routes/_authenticated/*` | Nuevo | Rutas de home y módulo de usuarios. |
| `src/routes/_public.tsx` & `login.tsx` | Nuevo | Layout público y pantalla de inicio de sesión. |
| `src/common/context/*` & `hooks/*` | Nuevo | Contextos de autenticación, tema, títulos y hooks utilitarios. |

Stacked on #121 (non-root user). I'll retarget it to master once #121 merges.

## Why
The runtime image was the Debian-based `aspnet:10.0`: a shell, a package manager and many OS packages the app never uses. Each one is something for scanners to flag and for an attacker to use.

## What
- `FROM mcr.microsoft.com/dotnet/aspnet:10.0-noble-chiseled-extra`. "extra" keeps ICU and the time zones (culture-aware text, SqlClient), which the plain chiseled image drops.
- The image has no shell, so #121's `RUN touch && chown` can't run there. The build stage now creates the empty `index.html`, and a `COPY --chown=$APP_UID` puts it in place. Ownership is unchanged: the `wwwroot` folder and `app.js` are root's, only `index.html` is `app`'s (checked in the exported image).
- CLAUDE.md: `az containerapp exec` gets no shell any more; debugging goes through logs and traces.

**Size:** 463 MB → 360 MB locally (uncompressed). ACR's compressed size will be smaller on both sides.

Checked locally: runs as uid 1654, writes the shell at startup, serves the page and `app.js`, `/healthz` answers. What I couldn't check here is managed identity, SQL with Entra auth and the OTLP exporter on Azure. That needs a **Deploy Branch to Staging** run (no migrations), and the smoke tests cover all three.

Closes #100.

author: vladf1
body:
Follow-up to 48bb12c (shell path replication tests). Comments only, in test files, so the content hash and the servers are unaffected.

**Rocks in the path tests are boulders, not blocks.** `rock()` in `net_timing.rs` said "rock block", but `CoverKind::Rock` is the quarry boulder's octagonal outline stretched to `w`×`d`. Its long faces cover only the middle of its length. A single 40 m rock let a ricochet miss its first bounce near the end. Two rocks laid end to end leave a V-shaped gap where their chamfered ends meet. This is the authored shape, not a collision bug. The comment now says so, and the ricochet corridor explains why its walls are overlapping rocks.

**What a mid-round joiner draws before its baseline.** The join test requires every flying shell to be drawn only from the baseline tick on, and the comment now gives the reason. The display starts one buffer (about 70 ms) behind the baseline. The baseline holds each shell's current path and the tanks' baseline pose. So until the display reaches the baseline, a shell that turned or ended just before it is missing, but never misplaced. Making it complete would mean sending each shell's recent earlier paths in the baseline, which changes the wire format and needs a server redeploy. It isn't worth that for a 70 ms window after a join or resync, and tanks have no history before the baseline either.

Checked: `cargo test -p sloppy-core --test net_timing --test net_client`, `cargo clippy -p sloppy-core --tests -- -D warnings`.

author: gfeitel1-maker
body:
## Summary
- New `reconnectCoordinator.js`: LAN, then rung 1, then rung 2, then rung 3 only if all fail. Rung 3 is never contacted when an earlier rung succeeds or when `SHORESH_RENDEZVOUS_URL` is unset. Total failure emits `SAME_NETWORK_REQUIRED`.
- Rung 3 is demand-driven with jittered exponential backoff (60s doubling to ~30 min); no publish or poll while every peer is reachable. The rendezvous record now carries this device's public reflexive addresses only.
- Production callers for `attemptRung1`, `attemptRung2`, the punch-signal protocol, gossip publishing and the coordinator, all inside the `SHORESH_PUNCH_ENABLED === 'true'` gate.
- Carried from S4b: `PUNCH_STORE_FAILED` event, `3fff::/20` rejected, revoked-mid-connection test tied to the revoked write. Doc fixes for the request-quota residual and ADR status.

## Testing
Red-first with planted defects: rung 3 first (5 ordering tests red), unfiltered record addresses (2 red), store event suppressed (1 red), 3fff cases (4 red before fix). Light focused runs green. Tests importing `node-datachannel` (punchTransport.sync, punchInertness, punchWiring, punchRung1/2) cannot run on the stale local node_modules, so CI is the gate for them; the planted-defect check for the revoked-write test is likewise pending CI.

The owner's two-device cross-NAT test is the real validation; S5 (packaging plus the T327 capability gate) follows.

author: scottkelly36
body:
## What
Costing, step 2: the firm's own costs, entered once, so the cost of a job can be worked out next. New **Costs** page under Operations.

- **Running costs:** a monthly amount for one vehicle (finance, insurance, road tax, a service plan) or, with no vehicle, for the firm (an overhead: office, software, the yard). Entered once; carries on until changed or stopped. Like the standing costs on the Finances page, **changing it from a later month closes the old row the month before and starts a new one, so earlier months keep what they had**.
- **Driver pay:** what each driver costs the firm an hour, from a day on. A rate applies until the next starts, so a pay rise never changes the cost of work already done.
- **Only `manage_billing` (the firm's money person) or WagonWise** can see or change either, because wages are private. A fleet manager without it cannot. Drivers never see it.

## The model for the next step (the cost of a job), so you can change it before I build it
- A job's time is from the driver accepting it to delivery.
- Wages: that time times the driver's rate on the day it was delivered.
- Fuel and a vehicle's running costs are spread over that vehicle's jobs in the month by their share of job time, so a vehicle's jobs together carry all of its costs for the month.
- Overheads are not added to a job; they are shown on their own.
- A driver or vehicle with no rate or cost adds nothing.

## Deploy
Migration 0057 (runs with core). Deploy core, staff-bff and dashboard together.

## Tests
The month and day rules, change/stop planning, validation, rate lookup, permissions and isolation (use cases and a real-Postgres/RLS end-to-end); `pnpm verify`.

> When your thoroughness is standard, you must make at least 5 rounds of searches before you apply the stop rule below, unless your budget ends first. Use a different query in each round. A first search that looks complete is not a reason to stop.

author: leynos
body:
Makes `install-mdtablefix` verify what it installs against the SHA-256 the release publishes.

## Why

`cargo binstall` checks nothing about the archive it unpacks, and the action only compared `mdtablefix --version`. A repository that moves from its own download-and-verify step to this action therefore loses an integrity check. leynos/whitaker#484 is the case that found it: it pinned `MDTABLEFIX_LINUX_X64_SHA256` and curl-verified the release, and CodeRabbit flagged the regression when it moved to the action (the user's rule is that every repository installs mdtablefix through this action).

## What publishes what

Every mdtablefix release from 0.5.1 (checked for 0.5.1, 0.6.0 and 0.6.1) publishes, beside each bare platform executable, a `<asset>.sha256` file (`mdtablefix-linux-x86_64`, `-linux-aarch64`, `-macos-x86_64`, `-macos-aarch64`, `-windows-x86_64.exe`). It also publishes per-target archives with their own `.sha256`. There are no attestations (the attestations API returns 404). For 0.6.1 the executable inside `mdtablefix-0.6.1-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu.tar.gz` is byte-identical to the bare `mdtablefix-linux-x86_64` asset (`e166e2da...`), so the installed binary can be compared with the bare asset's published digest.

## Change

- New step `Verify mdtablefix checksum`, between `Install mdtablefix` and `Verify mdtablefix`, run only when an install happened. It maps `runner.os`/`runner.arch` to the bare asset, fetches `.../releases/download/v<version>/<asset>.sha256` over HTTPS (`--proto =https --tlsv1.2 --retry 3`), requires a 64-hex digest, and compares it with the installed executable's SHA-256 (`sha256sum`, falling back to `shasum -a 256` on macOS).
- Fails closed with `install-mdtablefix.result=checksum-failed` on a mismatch, a failed download or a malformed file, and removes an executable that failed verification, so the version check never runs it. Success adds `install-mdtablefix.checksum=verified`. A cache hit downloads nothing.
- A missing executable is left to the existing version check, so "installed nothing" keeps its one outcome.
- README (new "Checksum verification" section, metrics table), CHANGELOG, and the developers' guide contract paragraph (seven steps become eight).

Limit, stated in the README and CHANGELOG: this is the release's own digest, so it catches a corrupt or substituted download but not a release replaced wholesale; only a digest pinned by the caller could catch that. I did not add a `sha256` input, because the request was verification against the published checksum; say if you want the pin as well.

## Tests

The scenario harness gains a `curl` stub and a `checksum` mode (`match`, `mismatch`, `unreachable`, `malformed`) and records the curl calls. New `TestChecksumVerification` cases: verified install reports the metric; each of the five platforms requests its own asset over `--proto =https`; a mismatch fails with `checksum-failed`, is annotated, removes the executable and skips the version check; an unreachable or malformed digest fails closed; a cache hit calls no curl; a missing executable keeps `version-mismatch`.

Mutation proofs: replacing the comparison with `false` fails the mismatch test; replacing the `rm -f` with `true` fails the same test (executable left behind). `.github/actions/install-mdtablefix` suite: 71 passed. `shellcheck` is clean on the new fragment; `ruff check` and `ruff format --check` pass.

## Follow-up

leynos/whitaker#484 (curl step replaced by the action) merges after this lands, pinned to the new revision. Other repositories pick the new revision up as Dependabot moves the pin.

## Summary by Sourcery

Add fail-closed SHA-256 verification for installed mdtablefix executables, supporting both release-published checksums and optional caller-pinned digests.

New Features:
- Verify installed mdtablefix executables against either the release-published SHA-256 or an optional caller-provided pinned digest.
- Add platform-aware checksum verification with HTTPS-only retrieval and checksum status metrics.

Bug Fixes:
- Prevent unverified, corrupt, substituted, or mismatched cached executables from being run by removing them and failing closed.

Enhancements:
- Validate the optional sha256 input and preserve cache behavior while checking pinned cached executables before use.
- Document checksum verification, metrics, inputs, failure behavior, and the expanded action contract.

Documentation:
- Update the action README, changelog, users guide, and developers guide with published and pinned checksum verification behavior.

Tests:
- Expand the scenario harness and test suite to cover platform asset selection, secure downloads, pinned digests, cache handling, malformed or unavailable checksums, hash failures, cleanup, and mutation proofs.

Update: added an optional `sha256` input (lead request). When a caller passes the digest of its platform's executable, the action verifies against it, downloads nothing and reports `install-mdtablefix.checksum=pinned`; otherwise it falls back to the release's published `.sha256` (`checksum=published`, renamed from `verified`). A malformed input is refused with `result=invalid-input`. The executable is now removed on every checksum failure, including a failed or malformed digest download (Codex P2). Tests: 78 passed; mutations proved (ignoring the pin fails 2 tests, removing the rm fails 3).

author: haowjy
body:
## Why

A stored internal link was only its path: an `href` format attribute on the label's characters. Every rename or move therefore rewrote the link formatting in every document that linked to the moved one, through a background worker. That rewrite was a second writer of the same formatting, concurrent with whoever was editing, and Yjs merges formatting marker by marker. Two settled rules broke:

- **#729:** words replaced during a move kept the old path: `[Renamed t](old.md)[arget](new.md) waits.`
- **#730:** an unlink lost to the rewrite, and the plain words after the link got linked: `[Target waits.](new.md)`

No arrangement of the rewrite could meet both rules (the redesign brief and seven design reviews show why), so the representation changed instead.

## Goal

- A stored link names its document. A rename or move writes nothing into any document that links to it, so a writer's or the AI's own edit is the only link operation in any merge.
- The model, Markdown export, plain-text copy and downloads still see `[label](path)` with the current, canonical path. No id reaches the model or any wire format, with no exception: an upload that cannot be spelled at its current path shows its last address, or an empty destination when there is none a reader may see.
- The AI's link writes keep the document they meant, even after a move, by matching what it was shown.
- Links written ahead of their document connect when it arrives (create, Apply, restore, move-in, upload).

## Summary

- **Stored identity.** The `link` mark, `image` and `figure` gain `ref`: `doc:<id>`, or `ahead:<uuid>` for an address where no document exists yet. `href` stays as an absolute fallback. Collab schema 1.0.0 (major: collaborative state is reset, Yjs history is not migrated).
- **Read side spells, never stores.** Every read door (model reads, hashlines, echoes, receipts, search, draft preview, download, projection, reversal) spells refs through one per-operation, holder-bound scope over the document tree. Paths are canonical (`ch1` reads back `ch1.md`). The model-facing revision becomes `y2:` (Yjs snapshot plus holder plus spellings), so a tree-only move counts as a change for freshness and compaction.
- **Write side assigns refs.** Every write door parses Markdown as pure syntax, then assigns refs: written links continue the old occurrences they replace (an exact, tuple-ranked correspondence), else take the ref the model was last shown at that address, else classify, resolve or mint. Images and figures go through the same continuation as links; the shipped `asset:` rule binds only fresh sources, and reads record a showing for uploaded pictures too, so a picture whose file moved keeps that file through an AI rewrite even when another file takes its old path. Bound ProseMirror nodes reach Yjs with no Markdown round trip, and unchanged links keep their attributes byte for byte. Whole-document saves and imports are base-anchored merges that certify their holder and authority generation.
- **Shown links.** Host-only evidence of which links the model actually saw (reads, search passages shown whole, echoes, receipts, references), kept per showing turn and recorded only when the host accepts the result that showed them. Never in model-visible bytes.
- **Ahead refs.** Registered durably before any lock; settled once, on the first document to arrive at the exact address, under the same namespace lock as the arrival. A settled ref behaves like a document ref: deleting the document makes the link gone, and a new document at the old path never captures it.
- **Moves write nothing into linking documents.** The rewrite worker, link redirects, the holder-redirect resolver path, the #728 marker cleanup and the `link-update` attribution row are deleted. "Updated N links" counts incoming links from live documents.
- **Client.** `@`, the link-ahead row, Ctrl+K, `[[…]]` paste and Markdown paste write refs without waiting on the network. Resolution is keyed by `(ref, href)`; a settled ahead ref never answers by its old address, online or offline. Gone links draw dashed, are not followable and say "No longer available". Link chips and pictures are drawn by their own mark and node views, which ask through one batched requester per editor. A paste assigns links and picture sources in one pass from the project catalog. Rich copy keeps refs within a project, including an upload's identity right after it is uploaded; plain-text copy spells full current addresses. A deleted upload says "This image is no longer available.", and a stored picture source never becomes a browser URL.
- **Chat references keep their identity from the first message.** The new-chat page posts the composer's exact reference blocks like any other send, and every writer row on screen is built from the submitted blocks, so a deleted document reads "No longer available" in chat at once, never followable to a new file at its path.
- **Pictures resolve like links (#734).** Images and figures that name a document by ref, or by a contextual address such as `uploads://seal.png`, are answered by the same `(ref, href)` cache, asked by the same document scan, and drawn through the existing signed-URL lifecycle. An image written ahead says it has not been uploaded yet and draws the moment a file arrives at its address; a deleted one says it is no longer available. Same-project paste keeps a picture's ref, and plain-text copy spells its current address.
- **Relabel is gone** (owner decision): link words never change automatically.

## Diff

- Non-migration total: 390 files, +22,315 / -6,518. Product code is 237 files, +11,019 / -4,231; tests, fixtures and harnesses are 108 files, +10,060 / -1,870; the rest is `.context`, docs, PR assets and the lockfile. The final-review fix round alone removed 970 product lines and added 618 (net -352), including the new upload identity behaviour.
- Breakdown:
  - Packages, contracts, schema and markup: 47 files, +2,517 / -480 — ref grammar, the shared resolution and speller, `ref` attributes and schema 1.0.0, the explicit-scope codec, occurrence walks and the shared link entry points.
  - Package, agent-edit: 54 files, +5,268 / -508 — ref assignment (correspondence, assignment, find-splice, shown facts), nodes as the write currency, the document-links port; about half is the correspondence fixtures and merge-matrix tests.
  - Server, collab domain: 77 files, +3,520 / -1,895 — the link scope doors, `y2:` revision, bound whole-document writes, structural restore; the rewrite adapter, journal origin and maintenance attribution deleted.
  - Server, context domain: 53 files, +3,931 / -1,919 — the document-link scope adapter, ahead-ref registry and arrivals, one document-address owner, the move count; the worker, redirects and holder-redirect path deleted.
  - Server, runtime, model tools, routes and projects: 52 files, +2,529 / -267 — the shown-link store, capture at accepted results, the batched ref-aware resolve endpoint, Work restore settlement.
  - Database schema: 2 files, +89 / -29 — `link_ahead_refs`, `thread_shown_links`, the reshaped `document_links`.
  - Client: 94 files, +4,377 / -1,403 — producers that assign refs, `(ref, href)` resolution through the shared rules with a settlement memo, view-owned chip and picture rendering, the gone state, clipboard refs, pictures drawn through the same resolution (#734).
  - Docs, CHANGELOG, PR assets and lockfile: 11 files, +84 / -17.

## Before / After

- **Bug fix: a label edited while its target moves keeps the old path (#729).** Before: `[Renamed t](old.md)[arget](new.md) waits.` After: `[Renamed target](new.md) waits.` in every client order and merge direction, for editor and AI edits.
- **Bug fix: an unlink racing a move links the plain suffix (#730).** Before: `[Target waits.](new.md)`. After: `Target waits.`; a partial unlink keeps exactly the words the writer left linked.
- **Renames and moves never touch linking documents.** Before: a background worker

author: rranauro
body:
Closes #46

## Gist

This PR writes down the vendoring convention, which until now existed only in `adopt-skill.sh` and the sidecars it writes. The convention is a new **Vendoring** section in `docs/companion-skills.md`, with an inventory table of every vendored skill. `scripts/lint.sh` now enforces it: a skill that declares an upstream must carry a notice and have a row in that table. A skill declares an upstream with an `UPSTREAM` sidecar or a `metadata.credits` block. There is no data structure or migration.

The plan was **designed unattended** and decided rather than confirmed. See the [`plan` comment](https://github.com/rranauro/claude-kit/issues/46#issuecomment-6085353050) for the alternatives it beat.

```text
skill declares an upstream (UPSTREAM sidecar | metadata.credits)
  must carry LICENSE (+ LICENSE-<owner> per further upstream)
  must have a row in docs/companion-skills.md "What is vendored"
```

Two existing forks were missing notices, and both now carry them:
- `visual-review` credited mattpocock/skills with no `LICENSE`.
- `visual-pr` reproduces HumanLayer's `show-me` text but carried only Matt Pocock's licence. It now also carries `LICENSE-humanlayer`.

## Acceptance Criteria

The criteria were clear. The issue left one question open, whether anything should fail when a fork lacks its notice. The plan settled it in favour of a lint check.

- **Met:** someone adding a fork can find what it must carry without inferring it from an existing fork. The doc section states it, the CLAUDE.md fork rule links to it, and the lint failure message names the doc.
- **Met:** source and point of origin are recoverable for every vendored directory. `UPSTREAM` sidecars record a sha. Credits record a URL pinned to a sha.
- **Met:** what is vendored is answerable from one place, the "What is vendored" table. Lint fails a declared fork that has no row there.
- **Met:** the carried terms are stated. They govern the directory's upstream text. They do not cover the rest of the plugin or the local changes, which fall under the root `LICENSE`.

## Evidence

- **Before:** with the check added and no notices fixed yet, `scripts/lint.sh` reported:
  `FAIL: plugins/kit/skills/visual-review credits an upstream but carries no LICENSE — see docs/companion-skills.md#vendoring`
- **Mutation check:** I deleted `grilling/LICENSE` and removed the `visual-review` row, and lint reported both:
  `FAIL: plugins/kit/skills/grilling credits an upstream but carries no LICENSE …`
  `FAIL: plugins/kit/skills/visual-review credits an upstream but has no row in docs/companion-skills.md#what-is-vendored`
- **After:** `scripts/lint.sh` → `all checks passed`.

### Screenshots

None — no visual change.

## Instructions

1. Run `scripts/lint.sh`. It should pass.
2. Move `plugins/kit/skills/visual-review/LICENSE` aside and run lint again. It should fail and name the doc. Restore the file.
3. Delete the `visual-review` row from the table in `docs/companion-skills.md` and run lint again. It should fail and name the missing row.
4. Read `docs/companion-skills.md#vendoring` as someone about to copy a skill in. It should tell you what to carry without you opening a fork.

## Reversibility

**Undo:** easy

Undoing it is a revert. The only effect outside the docs is a lint check.

**Blast Radius:** contributors

A PR that adds a forked skill without a notice or a table row now fails the required `lint` check. That is the intended behaviour change. A false positive would come from a `credits:` key nested in some other frontmatter block, and it would show up as a lint failure naming the doc.

Notes from `/simplify`:
- Three reviewers suggested generating the inventory from the sidecars and credits instead of keeping a table. The stored plan chose the doc table, so the table stays, and lint now holds each declared fork to its row instead of relying on an honour rule.
- The "carried terms govern" paragraph overlaps the text each sidecar carries. It stays because hand-vendored skills have no sidecar.

author: techrote
body:
## Summary

Completes the implementation and qualification candidate for #6 / SDVK-006.

- introduces a renderer-owned visual clock sampled only by the PF-010 MainView root
- keeps camera textures, probes, save pictures, stereo siblings and portal recursion from advancing/corrupting main timing
- defines explicit first-frame, repeated timestamp, invalid/rollback, pause/resume, load, wipe, cut and long-stall behavior
- adds UI-only render delta/accumulated time access
- adds default-off actor alpha/scale interpolation with exact endpoints and authoritative-state preservation
- extends SDVK-002 diagnostics/validation without making wall-clock pacing part of semantic corpus equality
- adds deterministic CPU/source contracts plus timing/RAG/provenance/ledger documentation

## Compatibility / simulation boundary

No gameplay timestep, tic advancement, authoritative actor state, demo/network/save semantics, TAA/history or generalized animation system is changed. `RF_DONTINTERPOLATE` remains authoritative. New interpolation flags are disabled by default.

## Context ownership

Only a PF-010 `MainView` top-level render samples the clock, once before stereo-eye fan-out. Main-root portals and later eyes consume the same snapshot. Camera textures, light-probe faces, save pictures and non-main portal descendants expose an explicit zero/invalid fallback and cannot advance or reset the next main delta.

## Donor policy

MAD-VKDoom commits `316b18a4d96b1a120c681d368ac670286234bcc8` and `7d1f2df404711986a3cc742dad1f9e6e0ac69cde` were reassessed. Only narrow concepts were adapted; the donor global clock/minimum clamp and unrelated animation systems were not transplanted.

## Verification

Focused deterministic fixture/source contracts are included. Acceptance requires the repository's full PR CI, software-Vulkan corpus/identity qualification, merge and exact post-merge master verification. Negative/failure evidence will be retained rather than waived.

Issue #6 remains open until final acceptance/post-merge verification; this implementation PR does not itself award acceptance.

Resend `auth.ordax.com.br` verificado (DKIM/SPF/Return-Path em sa-east-1); chave restrita a envio criada, não publicada no código. O Supabase `ordax-platform` possui inner gateway v11 ACTIVE. author: kaleaon
body:
Follow-up to the merged login and 403 PRs. Everything here is in `reddit/` (plus a small, backward-compatible addition to the shared `common/storykit.py`, tests, docs and the rebuilt `dist/RedditStoryFollower.zip`), tried against the real Reddit API with the user's own app credentials entered only as environment variables for the test runs. No credential is stored in the repo.

## What a real run of Out of Cruel Space (u/KyleKKent) showed, and what changed

**1.2.0 – long and renamed series.** The user's book stopped at ~190 chapters. Cause: the author renamed the series part-way ("Out of Cruel Space, Part N" for 1-999, then "OOCS, Into A Wider Galaxy, Part N"), while the Quick start filtered on the old name and the first check read only the newest 1,000 posts. Now the preset matches both names (but not the separate side stories); a first check reads back up to 30 pages and carries on at later checks until it reaches the start; editing a follow's filters re-reads the history. Real result: 1,802 chapter posts collected in ~40 s, 11 MB EPUB. Also opt-in *keep the author's own comment* under each chapter (official API; one request per chapter, fetched in batches of 300; reader comments deliberately not included).

**1.3.0 – a separate book for each post** (for subreddits of stand-alone stories by many authors, e.g. r/gayincest_stories). Flair becomes tags, "Part N" titles join Calibre series, first check takes only the newest 25, at most 50 books per check, edited posts make a fresh book. Posts whose **title states an age under 18 are skipped** (title-only heuristic, applies to this layout only; documented as imperfect). I looked at listing metadata only, not story text. Also fixes a bug the tests caught: a later check could pull in a backlog the first check had skipped on purpose.

**1.4.0 – Find stories…** Search or browse a subreddit (r/HFY by default), group posts into series by author and title name (reads `Name 14`, `Part 14`, `Chapter 14`, `(14)`, `#14`, capital Roman numerals, ignores leading `[OC]`/`[Universe]` tags), and follow a whole series: it reads the author's history for every part and previews the count and date range before adding. Checked on real HFY: *The Nature of Predators* showed 121 parts in the top list and following found 284; *Salvage* showed 86 and found 89.

**1.5.0 – optional chapter index.** A public Google Sheet (Date, Author, Chapter, Note) names chapters (`Chapter 001 – Pirates`), fixes mistitled posts (matches by number and date, then posting time), and reports chapters the index lists that Reddit lacks. The Out of Cruel Space preset includes the community's sheet. Live: 1,800 rows, all matched to a Reddit post, 65 storylines; two Reddit posts not yet in the sheet (the newest chapter and a second post numbered 726). The sheet's 2,823 total rows include other authors' side stories and fan works, which probably explains a "2,000+" count; the main series is 1,800 chapters with no gaps.

**1.6.0 – chapter titles and author's notes from the post itself.** Out of Cruel Space opens every post with its chapter title (Part 59: "The Pirates & The Bounty Hunters"), usually followed by an empty zero-width paragraph. New option *The first line of each post is its chapter title* (on in the Quick start): the line names the chapter (`Chapter 059 – The Pirates & The Bounty Hunters`, or `Out of Cruel Space, Part 59 – …` without the index) and is removed from the text; `~First~` markers are dropped; a note to readers in brackets becomes a boxed **Author's note** at the top of the chapter, and the optional author's comment a boxed **Author's comment** at the end. Empty zero-width paragraphs are now removed from every chapter. On the real series: 1,748 of 1,802 posts have a title line, 76 distinct titles, 328 posts with a bracketed note. The titles repeat (`A Scion of Many Worlds` heads 181 chapters), so they work more like a storyline name. The shared EPUB cleaner now keeps exactly two fixed classes (`author-note`, `author-note-label`) and the stylesheet gained a bordered, indented box for them (no floats); other classes are still dropped.

**1.7.0 – add the top rated series of a subreddit.** Find stories now lists results best rated first with a *Rating* column (total score of the posts found; official API only, feeds carry no scores), has a *Pages to look through* setting, and **Add top rated…** picks the highest rated real series (at least N parts found, default 3), skips series already followed, lists them for confirmation, and follows them all. Checked on real r/HFY top of all time (500 posts): *The Nature of Predators* (~834k, 139 parts seen), *Why Humans Avoid War* (~211k, 27), *A job for a deathworlder*, *The New Species*, *Jennifer is NOT an Eldritch Horror*. A series' rating counts only the posts inside the pages looked through.

## Not verified / limits

- Nothing ran inside Calibre itself; dialogs and library updates are tested under real Qt (offscreen) against a stand-in library. The boxed-note styling depends on the e-reader honouring the book's stylesheet.
- The browser login for a "personal use script" app was never exercised here (tests used the app-only grant); Reddit's treatment of it is unconfirmed.
- The Miraheze wiki for Out of Cruel Space blocks automated access (bot check), so it could not be read; the Reddit wiki index is stale (Parts 1-59, July 2021) and adds nothing. The sheet gives storylines, not unique chapter names.
- Find stories knows a series only by author and title: parts retitled midway need the *Title contains* box adjusted, tag-only titles show as pieces, and multi-author series are not joined. Top rated is a proxy (sum of scores of the posts found), so a few huge posts can outrank a longer, steadier series.
- The age guard reads titles only and errs on the side of skipping; it cannot know ages that are not in the title.
- Only the Reddit zip was rebuilt; the other plugins' zips still bundle the previous `storykit.py` until their next release (the change to it is additive).
- A note sharing a paragraph with a marker (`~First~ (note)`) stays in the text; a few early chapters have no title line and keep their `Part N` name.

## Tests

Full suite passes (PyQt6, FanFicFare, PyMuPDF, lxml installed). New: long-history backfill and resume, filter-change rescan, author-comment batches, per-post books (flair, series, age guard, first-check cap, edits), series grouping on real HFY title shapes, discovery source/order, rating and top-N selection (short, single and already-followed series skipped), index parsing/matching/typo repair/daily refresh/failure, opening-line parsing, boxed asides and class whitelist, chapter naming with and without the index, and real-Qt tests for the Add dialog, Find stories end to end, Add top rated, and the library updates.

Reddit Story Follower is now 1.7.0 (README index updated).

body:
Sub-project B of "match the MedBay report". Eumon already stored these daily series and drew them; now it says when they move, with a date and a size, so the growth plan ranks it and History records the recovery.

**Three findings** (computed at analysis time from the ledger and the crawl log, through the connector signals):
1. **"Search impressions fell N% since ⟨day⟩"** — last 7 days' average vs the best trailing week that ended a week or more earlier (120-day lookback, peak ≥ 100/day, fires at ≤ 60% of peak). When Google's indexed count fell within 7 days of the peak, the summary says so: the report's "the drop lines up with the indexed-page drop on 22 Sep".
2. **"Google's indexed count fell from A to B since ⟨day⟩"** — the imported Search Console chart when there is one, else the inspection sample (≥ 10% and ≥ 50 pages under the 90-day maximum).
3. **"At Googlebot's pace the sitemap takes N days to crawl once"** — sitemap URLs ÷ Googlebot requests/day over the last 28 days of logs (≥ 14 days of logs, > 60 days, ≥ 200 URLs), with the import's "discovered, not crawled" count when present.

Math is pure (`packages/core/src/trends.ts`); thresholds sit in one `TREND` constant with their reasons.

Spec: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-10-trend-findings-design.md` · Plan: `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-10-10-trend-findings.md`

**Ruling:** the demo's Googlebot log was slowed from ~80 to ~22 requests a day (each page about once a quarter) so the pace finding shows on the demo's 1,700-URL sitemap; the demo's rising impressions and indexed counts keep the two fall findings quiet, which the demo test asserts.

## Deploy notes
No migration, no new secret.

## Test plan
- [x] 4xx tests pass across packages; `npm run typecheck` clean.
- [x] Demo: latest analysis carries "At Googlebot's pace the sitemap takes N days to crawl once" and no fall findings.

# Vercel Web Analytics Installation Report

## Summary
Successfully installed and configured Vercel Web Analytics for the Doodle Days project.

## Implementation Details

### Project Type
This is a **vanilla HTML/JavaScript** project without a build system or package manager. It uses a single `index.html` file with inline styles and scripts, plus a service worker for offline functionality.

### Installation Method
Since this project doesn't use npm or a build system, I used the **script tag injection method** recommended by Vercel for vanilla HTML projects.

### Changes Made

**Modified:**
- `index.html` - Added Vercel Web Analytics scripts to the `<head>` section

**Scripts Added:**
1. **Analytics initialization script** - Sets up the `window.va` function and queue
2. **Analytics loader script** - Loads the analytics module from `/_vercel/insights/script.js`

**Exact insertion location:**
The scripts were inserted after the `<meta name="theme-color">` tag and before the existing inline script that handles theme initialization. This ensures analytics loads early in the page lifecycle without interfering with the app's theme detection logic.

### Code Changes

```html
<script>
window.va = window.va || function () { (window.vaq = window.vaq || []).push(arguments); };
</script>
<script defer src="/_vercel/insights/script.js"></script>
```

## Documentation Sources
- Official Vercel Analytics Quickstart: https://vercel.com/docs/analytics/quickstart
- Vercel Community forum for vanilla HTML implementation: https://community.vercel.com/t/using-vercels-analytics-with-no-framework/3194

## Verification
- ✅ HTML file is valid and can be served correctly
- ✅ Analytics scripts are properly inserted in the `<head>` section
- ✅ File structure preserved (no breaking changes)
- ✅ Existing functionality maintained

## Next Steps for User
1. Deploy the updated code to Vercel
2. Enable Web Analytics in the Vercel Dashboard (Project > Analytics > Enable)
3. After deployment, verify tracking by checking browser's Network tab for requests to `/_vercel/insights/`

## Notes
- No package manager or dependencies were needed for this implementation

author: daniel-freiermuth
body:
## Summary

Adds a **Full re-hunt** button to each repo on the Repos page, plus fixes for three scheduler bugs found while building it. Fixes come first in the history.

### Fixes

- **A failed rotation scan counts as its turn, hunts included** (`b70f64b`). Hunts were exempt from the starvation bump, so a failing hunt was re-picked every cycle (~60 s) and starved every other repo's hunt. A scan that ingested valid *and* invalid entries advanced nothing and re-ran every few seconds, a runner that returned an error skipped the bump entirely, and a hunt chain abandoned at the give-up ceiling was restarted fresh in the same selection (`744e8ce` added that bump for analysis kinds only). `attempt_failed` now mirrors the runners' success condition (`done`, an output file, no invalid entry) for every rotation kind, resumed attempts and runner errors included. A failed hunt keeps its watermark, so the retry reviews the same commits after the scan interval.
- **A resumed full re-hunt records its full hunt** (`ea00238`). A periodic full re-hunt that suspended and was resumed never set `last_full_hunt_at`, so the next cold hunt started the whole-history pass again.

### Feature (`fdd3abe`)

- `POST /api/repo/rehunt {id}` records `repos.full_hunt_requested_at` (migration 020) and wakes the scheduler.
- While a request is pending, the repo's next cold hunt reviews the complete history (`<empty tree>..<tip>`) and is never skipped as "no new commits".
- The rotation runs that hunt first until a hunt chain has started after the request. A chain already running when the request landed doesn't count, even when it finishes.
- A request is cleared only by a full-history chain that started at or after it and finished `done` with a clean ingest. Whether a chain covers the full history is recorded at its start (`jobs.full_history`) and inherited by resumes, so a suspended chain keeps its scope.
- UI: a "full re-hunt queued" badge, and the button becomes "Re-queue re-hunt" with a confirm that explains what asking again does.

Docs updated: `API-CONTRACT-WRITES.md` §8.1, `API-CONTRACT.md`, `hunter/README.md`.

## Testing

- `cargo nextest run --profile ci`: 635 passed. `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -D warnings` and `check-sql.sh` are clean.
- New regression tests in `scheduler_rotation_test.rs` and `full_rehunt_test.rs`; each fails on the code before its fix. `scheduler_resume_test::a_chain_out_of_attempts_is_retired_and_the_cycle_falls_through` now expects the fall-through to skip the abandoned hunt.
- UI: `svelte-check` (no new warnings), eslint, vitest 98 passed.
- Manual: on a local daemon, the button queues the request, the badge appears, the button turns into "Re-queue re-hunt", and the event is attributed to the logged-in user.

body: ## Summary Scanning the QR opened Alipay’s auth page and showed 「系统异常，请联系商家」 because every candidate, including the ones labeled mclient, was the same payment URL: `https://wappaygw.alipay.com/home/exterfaceAssign.htm?...`. The page also defaulted to candidate 1 with only a `1/2/3/4` control, so that was the only code anyone scanned. `cmd=3016` asked Baidu for `authInfoStr` without the `BDUSS` cookie that `activity.update` already sends. QR encoder changes are untouched. ## URLs Taken from the strings in the bundled Alipay SDK 15.8.40 (`Vendor/AlipaySDK.framework/AlipaySDK`), which is what `auth_V2` actually calls: | Segment | Host + path | Why | |---|---|---| | **m全** (default) | `https://mclient.alipay.com/home/exterfaceAssign.htm?` + full signed query | SDK string `mclient.alipay.com/home/exterfaceAssign.htm`. This is the mobile gateway that accepts an `alipay.open.auth.sdk.code.get` query, not the payment cashier. | | **m短** | same host/path, `alipay_root_cert_sn` and `app_cert_sn` removed | Shorter symbol if the server does not require the certificate serials. | | **授权** | same host/path, plus SDK auth-routing keys that are not already in the signed string: `view=wap`, `login_goal=auth`, `prod_code=WAP_FAST_LOGIN` (and `scope=kuaijie` only if missing) | SDK string next to `authWithInfo`: `view=wap&scope=kuaijie&login_goal=auth&prod_code=WAP_FAST_LOGIN`. Marks the request as account login instead of a trade. | | **网关** | `https://wappaygw.alipay.com/service/rest.htm?` + full query | SDK’s real wappaygw path is `/service/rest.htm`, not `/home/exterfaceAssign.htm`. Kept as an explicit payment-gateway fallback, labeled as such. | Not included: - `openauth.alipay.com/oauth2/publicAppAuthorize.htm` does not take this signed SDK string (it wants `app_id`, `scope`, `redirect_uri`). The in-repo note says that form returned E004. - `render.alipay.com` ulink and `alipays://` were already rejected by the scanner. Query values are percent-encoded once (`+` `/` `=` in the RSA signature). A raw `+` is a space on the cashier, which fails verification and surfaces as 「系统异常」. ## Session `cmd=3016` now sends `Cookie: BDUSS=...` and a real `User-Agent` header (the old name was `UserAgent`, which Baidu does not read). A non-zero `errno` fails instead of encoding a generic string. The same session headers are applied to `cmd=3015` and `activity.update`. ## QR page The yellow label under the title shows the active host, full/short/route variant, and path. The segmented control is labeled `m全` / `m短` / `授权` / `网关`.

author: juv4uk
body:
## Repair witness COND tree without changing any expected law

The current mainline `content_store_authority` test still observes `()` from `content-store-authority-witness`. Inspection of its parsed Lisp form shows malformed nesting: `object-relation` currently has four fields because the projection-failure clause is nested as a fourth field instead of a sibling clause; at the root level, the root-failure clause is likewise not a sibling of the root-success clause.

This one-fixture repair reconstructs the same three-level decision tree explicitly:
- root relation: yes -> inspect object relation; no -> named root-image failure;
- object relation: yes -> inspect projection relation; no -> named object-image failure;
- projection relation: yes -> pass with all three laws; no -> named projection failure.

Every COND has exactly two three-field `(query expected-result expression)` clauses. All expected-result values remain exact D1 `1`, and the same original PASS/FAIL witness payloads and data are preserved. This is strictly a parenthesis/AST ownership repair; no Rust semantics, SID, schema, D1–D10 inventory, coordinates, ratification, or T5 artifact changes.

Required: `content_store_authority`, Canon V2, and full portable/Hosted CI must pass on this exact head before merge.
