author: joeharris76
body:
## Summary

The oracle has been the required soundness reviewer since 2026-10-09, but every
review it posted opened with `### oracle-review-shadow:`, and its status
context, workflow, artifacts and log lines all said "shadow", which reads as
advisory. This renames all of them to `oracle-verdict`.

- **Posted name.** New reviews open with `### oracle-verdict: <state> for
  <sha>` and post the status context `oracle-verdict` (`status_context` in
  `.github/oracle-reviewers.yml`). Log and error prefixes and the CLI's `prog`
  follow.
- **Workflow.** `.github/workflows/oracle-review-shadow.yml` is now
  `.github/workflows/oracle-verdict.yml` (`git mv`). Its `name`, `run-name`,
  concurrency group, plan, attempt and state artifacts use the new name. The
  sweep dispatches the new file. The old path stays in the policy's gate paths,
  so a change that adds a file there is still reviewed at the gate tier.
- **Required check.** `_project/scripts/oracle_review_check.py` reads both the
  new and the old first line (`LEGACY_ORACLE_CONTEXT`), so an open pull
  request whose latest review predates the rename keeps its result. The old
  line can be dropped from the checker once no open pull request's latest
  oracle review uses it.
- **Merge digest.** `soundness_merge_digest.py` no longer imports the
  checker's pattern. It has its own pattern, which accepts both lines
  permanently, because it reads merged history.
- **Retry state continuity.** `github.latest_state` reads the newest trusted
  `oracle-verdict-state-<n>` artifact from runs of the new workflow. When a pull
  request has none, it reads `oracle-review-shadow-state-<n>` from runs of the
  old workflow path, so the strike floor, retry budget and backoff carry over.
  Each artifact name is trusted only from its own workflow path. After the
  rename, a run at the old path can only be a historical one: the file no
  longer exists on `develop`, so no `pull_request_target`, comment, schedule or
  dispatch run can start from it. The fallback to keep the old file and
  artifact names was not needed.
- **Docs.** `oracle-review-v2.md`, `soundness-drain.md`,
  `merge-queue-governance.md` and `dev-loop-property-ledger.md` use the new
  name and the new `gh workflow run oracle-verdict.yml` command. The 2026-10-05
  shadow decision record gets a dated note and keeps the old name where it
  describes history. The release-cut file list and the ledger cut-over list
  name the renamed workflow and test files.

Unchanged: the required `oracle-review` check and its workflow, the stand-in
line `Stand-in oracle review: APPROVE <sha>`, and the App.

The `develop-squash-only` ruleset requires `core`, `explorer`,
`results-data`, `docs`, `landing`, `tooling` and `oracle-review`, all with any
integration. `oracle-verdict` is not one of them, so its status cannot satisfy
a required context.

`git grep -n oracle-review-shadow` now matches only:

- the old-format parsers (`LEGACY_ORACLE_CONTEXT`, the digest's pattern,
  `LEGACY_STATE_ARTIFACT_PREFIX`, `LEGACY_WORKFLOW_PATH`) and the gate-path
  entry for the old file;
- their tests;
- `tests/fixtures/oracle_reviewers/pr2769_history.json`, a recorded history;
- dated history: the 2026-10-05 decision record, the 2026-10-07 ADR D14
  amendment, and the doc sentences that describe reviews posted before the
  rename.

## Test plan

- `uv run -- pytest -o addopts="" tests/unit/scripts/oracle_reviewers tests/unit/scripts/test_oracle_review_check.py tests/unit/scripts/test_soundness_merge_digest.py tests/unit/workflows tests/unit/test_oracle_coverage_map.py tests/unit/test_ledger_coverage.py`
- New tests:
  - the required check passes on a success review, and fails on a failure
    review, under both the new and the old first line;
  - new reviews open with the new first line;
  - the digest reads both lines, and still reads the old line after the
    checker's pattern is replaced with one that accepts only the new line;
  - `latest_state` falls back to the old artifact from the old workflow path
    (and keeps its strike count), prefers the new artifact when both exist, and
    rejects either artifact name from the other workflow's path.
- Mutation checks:

  | Mutation | Failing test |
  |---|---|
  | drop the legacy alternative from the checker's pattern | `test_the_check_reads_the_current_and_the_legacy_first_line[legacy]` |
  | the digest uses the checker's pattern | `test_the_digest_keeps_its_own_pattern_for_merged_history` |
  | no legacy state source | `test_latest_state_falls_back_to_the_legacy_artifact_and_workflow` |
  | trust either workflow path for either artifact | both `test_latest_state_pairs_each_artifact_name_with_its_own_workflow` cases |

- This pull request is reviewed by `develop`'s workflow under the old name, as
  expected. After merge, the first run of `oracle-verdict.yml` should post a
  review that opens with `### oracle-verdict:` and the `oracle-verdict` status,
  and the required check should pass on it.

author: benvanik
body:
A required value whose instruction can address only a low register window can currently evict an active scalar even when that scalar has a legal home above the window. In the representative gfx1200/gfx1201 kernel from #1452, that fragmentation leaves four one-VGPR address values as scratch stores and reloads after the preceding scheduler repair has reduced the original pressure regression.

This changes victim consumption from unconditional spilling to whole-lifetime recoloring when the victim is independently placed. The allocator searches above the incoming value's bounded window, validates the candidate against every published sparse lifetime and target storage constraint, and then updates the active-unit index in place. A victim keeps the existing spill path when its own operand capacity, alignment, structural relations, target-selected address state, fixed or reserved storage, leases, write interference, or the current residency tier reject relocation. Ordinary successful allocation does no additional work; the bounded scan begins only after victim selection would otherwise materialize a spill.

This is deliberately a placement repair rather than another rematerialization retry. Retrying an equal spill count on this kernel perturbs the schedule and expands four stores/four reloads back to 28/57 with five frames and fourteen live-range splits. Recoloring preserves the selected schedule and makes monotonic progress by freeing the exact low-window location.

The exact target-independent regression test captures both sides of the contract:

```text
before: %d -> spill_slot[0:1], %current -> target_id[3:1], spills: 1
after:  %d -> target_id[8:1], %current -> target_id[3:1], spills: 0
```

Register 7 is free at the collision point but conflicts earlier in `%d`'s lifetime, so the positive case requires the complete-lifetime scan. A paired negative case gives `%d` its own low4 use and proves that the allocator retains the spill instead of moving it outside its legal window.

## Production result

Building on the scheduler repair now on main, both RDNA4 profiles eliminate the remaining allocator-induced traffic:

| Metric | Scheduler-only baseline | With recoloring |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Spill stores | 4 | 0 |
| Reloads | 4 | 0 |
| Allocation frames | 3 | 1 |
| Repair iterations | 2 | 0 |
| Scheduled VGPR pressure | 234 | 235 |
| Final VGPRs | 240 | 240 |
| Resident subgroups | 4 | 4 |
| Instructions | 3,598 | 3,591 |
| Code bytes | 21,492 | 21,400 |

Final SGPRs remain 24, occupancy remains LDS-limited, and five frozen Q6 controls across gfx1100/gfx1151 remain byte-identical.

## Compiler cost

| Metric | Scheduler-only baseline | With recoloring | Change |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Optimized `.text` | 6,726,763 B | 6,727,867 B | +1,104 B |
| Optimized `.rodata` | 5,239,671 B | 5,239,671 B | 0 B |
| Compiler file | 14,132,776 B | 14,133,880 B | +1,104 B |
| Production compile median | 85.03 ms | 56.58 ms | -33.5% |

Compile time uses 30 interleaved pairs after five warmup pairs. Avoiding two allocation frames dominates the cold-path legality scan; the interquartile ranges are 84.55–86.22 ms and 55.92–57.11 ms.

Fixes #1452.

## Reviewer Notes

The highest-value review surface is the relocation legality in `interval_assignment.c`: a published assignment cannot use the forward-only active-set cursor for its earlier lifetime, so the candidate intentionally checks every published assignment with exact sparse lifetime overlap. The paired golden covers that distinction and the victim-capacity boundary.

author: yqteam-theodore
body:
## Problem

Two independent issues.

### 1. `yq_memtable_put()` over a tombstone double-counts the entry

The "key already present" path subtracted the slot's current cost only for non-tombstone entries, reasoning a tombstone had "nothing to give back". But a tombstone *does* account for `entry_cost(key, 0)`: the delete that created it subtracted the live cost and added exactly that. Skipping the subtraction there leaves `key + entry` bytes of phantom usage behind on **every delete/put pair**, which trips `yq_memtable_full()` (`used_bytes >= max_bytes`) early and makes the engine spill/checkpoint while the table still has room.

Reproduced against the unfixed memtable:

```
put rc=0 used=141
del rc=0 used=41
put rc=0 used=182   (must equal 141 -> 41 bytes of drift)
```

The subtraction is now unconditional and correct for both states: `entry_cost(key, val)` for a live entry, `entry_cost(key, 0)` for a tombstone (its `val_len` is already 0). After the fix the sequence reports `141 -> 41 -> 141`.

### 2. `yq_batch_put()`'s read-only guard misses one spelling of read-only

The guard was `txn->flags & YQ_TXN_READONLY`, but `YQ_TXN_READWRITE` is a **flag bit**, not an enum: a read-only transaction is anything without that bit, which covers both `YQ_TXN_READONLY` (0x2) and a bare `0`. The old guard only caught the 0x2 form, so a transaction begun with `flags == 0` slid past it and was rejected one entry at a time by `yq_put()` instead -- reporting `entries_failed == count` for a batch that never applied anything, instead of rejecting the batch up front. The guard now matches `yq_put()`/`yq_del()` exactly.

The same stale claim ("`YQ_TXN_READONLY` is 0") sat in the comments of `yq_txn_begin()`, `yq_put()` and `yq_del()` even though the header defines it as `0x2` -- that comment is what motivated the wrong guard in the first place, so it is corrected too.

## Verification

- The memtable unit repro above fails on `main` and passes after the fix.
- New regressions: `yq_test_basic.c` gains a memtable accounting unit test (live insert, in-place update, and delete/put cycles must all be exact); `yq_test_integration.c` gains `test_batch_readonly_rejected()` covering both read-only spellings plus a write-transaction control case -- it fails on `main` (`entries_total == 2` where the contract says the whole batch is rejected).
- Full suite (9/9 ctest binaries) passes on Windows with MinGW-w64 GCC 16.2, `-O2`, assertions on.

Stacked on the earlier branches of this series so the suite is green end-to-end.

body:
## Problem

Houston's mark was a black hole that read as space rather than as Houston, and the app had no character of its own.

## Change

- **App icon, rail mark and tray:** the mascot head replaces the black hole. The desktop icon is the night tile (promo art on a rounded tile above 32 px, the vector head cut inside the same tile at 32 px and below). The rail brand mark is the raster head at 32/64/96 px via `srcSet`. The tray renders the head in its idle, active and attention states. `ui/scripts/render-icons.mjs` remains the single generator.
- **Mascot companion (optional, on by default):** Houston sits above the rail footer buttons and is there for company only: it never reads agent status, hooks or terminal output.
  - A pure director (`mascot/mascotDirector.ts`) arbitrates outfits, base loops and one-shot moments by priority (user interaction > lifecycle > scheduled > ambient), with budgets for unprompted speech and no unprompted motion while typing or while the window is unfocused.
  - Holiday outfits for Christmas, New Year, Carnival and Easter (Gregorian computus), Dia dos Namorados, Children's Day, Halloween, Festa Junina and the install anniversary.
  - Interactions: click, petting, double-click, theme toggle, Konami code (disco), naps, idle play, break reminders, sounds (off by default) and the Ring Invaders minigame. Palette commands appear only while the mascot is on.
  - **One mascot at a time:** around-the-app surfaces (About, pull request empty and no-results states, skills, search no-results, empty grid, reconnecting, crash, release notes) borrow the companion, which flies from its current spot to the surface and back when the surface closes. Under reduced motion it moves without a flight.
  - **Free placement inside the window:** dragging lifts the mascot off the rail and drops it anywhere in the Houston window; the position persists, is clamped on resize and avoids native browser panes. Dropping it on the rail, Settings › Mascot › Position or the "Return mascot to rail" palette command docks it again.
  - The colour variant applies to every in-app rendering, including the rail brand mark; the OS app icon and tray stay unchanged. The pixel style renders at the same size as the brand art.
  - First launch opens with the big mascot; its Add workspace and Open settings actions run immediately and the mascot then flies into the rail. Existing users meet it once.
  - **Settings › Mascot** is a dedicated section, after Appearance, with every option including turning it off.
  - Everything loads lazily and stays out of the boot bundle; looping motion pauses while the window is hidden or unfocused and holds a stable pose under reduced motion.
- **Docs:** the styleguide gains scoped exceptions for the mascot (looping, `filter` on its own elements, dedicated chrome tokens); glossary, renderer constraints and the user guide describe it.

## Verification

- Renderer: typecheck, full `bun run test`, build, `check:css`, `check:bundle`, `check:complexity`, and every safety script run by CI.
- `src-tauri`: `cargo fmt --check` and `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`.
- Side-by-side parity captures against the approved mock for every mood, outfit, colour variant, the first-run hero and the intro.
- Manual run of the dev app on the `dev` channel.

Before/after captures to be attached.

author: tkadauke
body:
Closes #4858

Pinned mutable workflow retries must keep using their recorded storage-affinity queue when that worker queue is live; dropping them onto the generic runs queue can bypass the placement guarantee and reintroduce retry starvation risks.

The resolver now treats pinned workflow workspaces as distributed retry candidates even when the repository itself is not distributed, allowing the existing resume queue lookup to select `resume-storage-main`. Coverage moved to `RunQueueResolver` with a regression spec proving the pinned retry resolves to the storage-affinity queue instead of the fallback `runs` queue.

## Test Plan

```sh
syrus checkout JOB-6809
```

- Run `RUN_CI_ONLY_SPECS=true BUNDLE_PATH="$PWD/vendor/bundle" BUNDLE_APP_CONFIG="$PWD/.bundle" bundle exec rspec spec/jobs/run_job_spec.rb:1715 spec/services/run_queue_resolver_spec.rb`.
- Run `RUN_CI_ONLY_SPECS=true BUNDLE_PATH="$PWD/vendor/bundle" BUNDLE_APP_CONFIG="$PWD/.bundle" bundle exec rspec spec/models/run_spec.rb:811 spec/models/run_spec.rb:916 spec/models/run_spec.rb:933 spec/models/run_spec.rb:959`.
- Review `RunQueueResolver#compatible_resume_queue`: default mutable retries should keep a live storage-affinity queue when capability payloads are unavailable.
- Check the incompatible-worker edge case: a live macOS-only resume queue must still fall through for Linux/default work instead of remaining sticky.

Backend-only routing fix. The original spec expectation was correct; the resolver was dropping sticky affinity after `resume_worker_queue` had already accepted the live queue.

> *"Malum est consilium quod mutari non potest."* — [Publilius Syrus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Publilius_Syrus)

body:
Before: only 404 had a styled page. Any other error showed a bare, unstyled "Something went wrong" page without the menu bar, and a wrong admin password showed the plain text "需要密码". The home page said Shiqi studies and codes in Atlanta.

After: every error shows the same window. Today's critter holds up the status code in a speech bubble, with a title and line of text per status (400, 401, 403, 404, 500, 503, plus a fallback) in English and Chinese, and buttons to go home and to go back (or to retry for 5xx). Errors inside a page keep the menu bar. The bio now says software engineer in Fremont, CA and Georgia Tech online master's student in AI. The "Filling the blank space" essay no longer calls Atlanta home.

How: one `ErrorScreen` component, used by the 404 route, the site layout's `ErrorBoundary` and the root `ErrorBoundary`. Error words live in `strings.errors`. The admin page now throws its 401/404 from the loader, so the error page renders, and the layout's `headers` passes `WWW-Authenticate` through (checked with curl: 401 + header, and 200 with the password).

author: gitctrlx
body:
NK2-09 — NIP-59 gift wrap for `nk-nips`, mirroring `packages/nostr/src/nips/nip59.ts` per `docs/nk/api/nk-nips.mdx`.

## Rust (`crates/nk-nips/src/nip59.rs`, feature `nip59` = nip44 + rand_core + serde_json)

- `Rumor` — `new`, `id`, `unsigned`/`into_unsigned`, `to_json` (TS `rumorToJson` field order), `from_json` (rejects `sig`, case-insensitive `id` match, computes `id` when absent).
- `Timestamps`, `RandomScope`, `WrapOptions` (builder; `WrapOnly` reuses the rumor's `created_at` for the seal). Random offsets replicate TS exactly: big-endian u32 draws, rejection sampling at `floor(2^32/172800)*172800`.
- `seal_with_rng` / `gift_wrap_with_rng` / `wrap_with_rng` — deterministic variants; rng consumption order documented on each: [offset] → NIP-44 nonce → BIP-340 aux (gift wrap additionally draws ephemeral key candidates first, redrawn while invalid like `SecretKey::generate_with_rng`). `os-rng` adds `seal`/`gift_wrap`/`wrap`.
- `unwrap` mirrors the TS order and `Nip59Error` messages: kind check → signature verify → decrypt → seal kind/tag whitelist (`["expiration", <digits>]`) → seal signature → decrypt → rumor rules → `seal.pubkey == rumor.pubkey`.
- Pure helpers for remote-signer composition: `seal_template`, `check_gift_wrap`, `parse_seal`, `open_rumor`.

## TS (`packages/nostr/src/nips/nip59.ts`)

**BREAKING:** `WrapOptions.randomInt` is replaced by `randomBytes?: (n) => Uint8Array` — one entropy stream (default noble `randomBytes`) feeding the ephemeral key, timestamp offsets, the NIP-44 nonce, and BIP-340 aux, in the same order as Rust. `createGiftWrap` now constructs the ephemeral `Keys` from stream bytes, calls `nip44.encrypt` with a stream-drawn nonce, and signs through the real `signEvent`/backend path with stream-drawn aux. `nip17.wrapDirectMessage` updated accordingly; no compatibility alias.

## Vectors & parity

`vectors/nip59/codec.json` is generated entirely through the real TS API (`gen/nip59.ts`): fixed + randomized timestamp cases (`SealAndWrap` and `WrapOnly`), ephemeral kind, relay hints, expiration, extra tags, valid unwraps, and every TS rejection — mutated real outputs, re-signed through the real API where a validly signed carrier is needed. TS runner: 34 cases. Rust runner (`nk-vectors`): replays constructions byte-for-byte from the pinned entropy stream and matches all unwrap outcomes. `parity.json`: `nip59.wrap` → **stable**.

## Gate

lint/typecheck/test (1311+38) · fmt · workspace clippy `-D warnings` both sets · `cargo test --workspace --all-features` (22 binaries) · `cargo deny check` · `cargo hack --each-feature` 15/15 · wasm32 `--no-default-features` + all-NIP builds · `cargo tree --no-default-features` = nk-core only · `build:wasm` 227,354 B unchanged · `test:wasm` 40 · `test:parity` 8 streams clean. `nip59` added to both nips CI feature lists.

body:
Продолжение #92. Эти коммиты я запушил в его ветку уже после того, как #92 влили, и в `master` они не попали. Поэтому в `ghcr.io/joinrpg/kogda-igra:latest` нет `/db-init`, и joinrpg/kogda-igra-net#7 не находит схему.

## Что сделано
- `Dockerfile` копирует `db/init/` в образ как `/db-init`, вне document root. Compat-тесты kogda-igra-net берут схему из того же образа, против которого гоняются, поэтому схема и код всегда одной версии.
- `utils/migrate-db/fetch-dev-schema.ps1` переснимает `db/init/` с dev (нужен пароль в `KOGDA_DEV_PASSWORD`). Скрипт переехал сюда из kogda-igra-net.
- В `db/README.md` описано, как переснять схему и кто ещё ею пользуется. Добавлена ссылка на kogda-igra-net.

## Проверка
- В образе, собранном из этой ветки, есть `/db-init/01-schema.sql` и `/db-init/02-reference-data.sql`.
- Compat-тесты kogda-igra-net на образе с тем же `Dockerfile`: 235/235.

## После слияния
`:latest` публикуется, только если workflow посчитал версию релизной (`CALCULATED_VERSION_IS_RELEASE`). Если после слияния `:latest` не обновится, запусти «Build and publish» вручную, как в прошлый раз, и затем перезапусти CI в joinrpg/kogda-igra-net#7.

body:
Closes #3810

## What landed

Merchant-first, grouped activity on the dashboard, built on #3824's serve-time groups and #3805's `Amount` currency mode:

- `dashboard/ActivitySection.tsx` (new) — day headings from the groups' `latestAt` (server already buckets per user-local day), one `TransactionActivityRow` per group, muted `×N` (`×N+` when the count is a floor) when `count > 1`.
- Titles come from `counterpartyLabel`'s new opt-in **no-address mode**: an x402 row with a resource URL reads its hostname, without one reads "Agent payment", a sweep reads "Returned from <agent>", inbound reads "Deposit", an unresolved address reads "New recipient" — a raw/truncated address can never surface on the dashboard. `resolvedName` carries #3824's server-resolved `merchantName`.
- Subtitle is the agent's name; "From My account" renders only with more than one account (outbound rows).
- Amounts use the currency mode: book-time `convertedAmount` plain, serve-time `approxAmount` with "≈", unknown valuation renders the em dash, never 0.
- `TransactionsTable` and `TransactionDetailPanel` are untouched (byte-identical) — the no-address mode is opt-in; a control test pins the default mode's truncation and shared-screen output.
- The 5-row `transactions` preview is no longer read by the dashboard; the wire removal is filed as #3858.
- Dashboard requests name the browser's IANA zone (`?tz=`) so grouping buckets on the user's local days; docs (`design-system.md`, `screen-recipes.md`) and the design-system page (new activity-row clip, `ds-activity-row`) updated; visual baselines regenerated on Linux (dashboard-desktop/mobile, currency-sek-dashboard + 4 new design-system clips).

## Verification

- Fresh-worktree re-review at `51c208f4`: `vitest` 37/37 green across `ActivitySection.test.tsx` (15), `transaction-presentation.test.tsx` (19, incl. shared-screens-unchanged + no-address-mode cases), `useDashboardOverview.test.ts` (3); frontend `typecheck` green; `lint:copy` and `lint:vocabulary` green.
- Builder ran the full battery at this head: `npm run preflight` 27/27 gates green (typecheck/test/build -w frontend 3200/3200, design:coupling --strict, docs:coupling --strict, docs:check), baselines via update-visual-baselines run 37980413487.

author: viperjuice
body:
Closes agent-harness#1392.

**Maintainer decision (2026-10-09):** interactive publication keeps pushing by default, and a repo can opt out.

## What
- **`phase-loop publication-mode`** (`publication_mode.py`) resolves and prints the interactive publication mode: `none`, `draft-only` or `ready` (the default).
  - It reads a committed, tracked root config, `.phase-loop-publication.toml`, which review can see. It does not live under the runtime-excluded `.phase-loop/`.
  - A user config can also set the mode.
  - A malformed config is a visible error, never a silent default.
- **execute-phase skill**, in all four harness copies plus the regenerated bundle: publication mode (b) and "Draft PR early" now call the resolver before any `git push` or `gh pr create`, and honour its result.
- **Docs:** `docs/branch-and-publication-flow.md`
  - The control table now includes the interactive path.
  - The "Known gap" section is replaced.
  - It notes that the inner `phase-loop execute` leg keeps the `manual` default.
- **Onboarding:** `docs/TEAM-ONBOARDING.md` is updated.
- **CHANGELOG:** a new [Unreleased] entry.

## Acceptance (executed, real agent)
Each run was a `claude -p` session using this branch's execute-phase skill, in a scratch repo with a bare local remote and a recording `gh` stub. Artifacts are on claw under `/mnt/workspace/board-tools/impl-1392-accept/{none,ready}/`.
- **`none`:** the phase completed (exit 0). The remote refs were identical before and after: `f57235948f7b… refs/heads/main`. No `gh` call was recorded.
- **`ready` (default):** the agent pushed `feature/greet`, ran `gh pr create --draft` on the first commit, then ran `gh pr ready` after verification passed. The remote gained `refs/heads/feature/greet`.

## Tests
- `tests/test_publication_mode_1392.py` covers every mode, precedence, and the malformed-config cases.
- Six named mutations each turn the file red.
- With the affected suites (canon parity, bundle drift, seat-reference inventory, entry-doc, launch inventory, registry, docs): 184 passed, 23 skipped.
- `ruff check .` (0.15.5) is clean.

## Main merge
Merged main at a76fbf6f. CHANGELOG [Unreleased] conflicted, and both entries are kept. [0.7.26] and below are byte-identical to main. The bundle was regenerated.

## Board hb1 must-fix
One fix commit, 27eb3f9e, on top of the reviewed head a76fbf6f. `git diff --stat a76fbf6f..27eb3f9e` touches only `phase-loop-runtime/src/phase_loop_runtime/publication_mode.py` and `phase-loop-runtime/tests/test_publication_mode_1392.py`. No skill text, docs or bundle changes.

**Behaviour.** At a76fbf6f a publication layer that could not be read was treated as absent, so `phase-loop publication-mode` fell through to the default, printed `publication_mode=ready` and exited 0. A layer is now absent only when its absence is confirmed. Every other outcome exits 2, prints `publication_mode=error` and the blocking action, and carries git's or the OS's message on stderr.
- **Repo layer:** absent only when the `HEAD` tree lists no `.phase-loop-publication.toml`. These are now config errors: a `HEAD` with no commit; a failed `git ls-tree`; an entry that is not a regular file (a symlink, a tree or a gitlink, named in the message); a committed blob that cannot be read.
- **Partial clones:** a partial clone with a reachable source still fetches the blob and honours the committed value.
- **User layer:** absent only when `lstat` of the user path reports that it does not exist (ENOENT or ENOTDIR). The hb2 section below tightens this rule. These are now config errors: a dangling or looping symlink at that path; a directory that cannot be searched; any failed read.
- **Deliberate tightening:** a repository whose `HEAD` has no commit used to resolve `ready`. It is now a config error, since nothing can be published before the first commit.

**Cells.** All in `tests/test_publication_mode_1392.py`. "Before" is the new test file run against the unchanged a76fbf6f source.

| Cell | Node | a76fbf6f | 27eb3f9e |
|---|---|---|---|
| R1 | `test_unreadable_committed_opt_out_blocks_publication` (sparse `blob:none` clone, fetch source unreachable) | red: rc 0, `ready` | green |
| R2 | `UnconfirmedAbsenceTest::test_committed_opt_out_with_a_missing_blob_blocks_publication` | red: rc 0, `ready` | green |
| R3 | `UnconfirmedAbsenceTest::test_unborn_head_is_an_error_not_an_absent_repo_layer` | red: rc 0, `ready` | green |
| R4 | `UnconfirmedAbsenceTest::test_dangling_user_config_symlink_blocks_publication` | red: rc 0, `ready` | green |
| R5 | `UnconfirmedAbsenceTest::test_looping_user_config_symlink_blocks_publication` | red: rc 0, `ready` | green |
| R6 | `UnconfirmedAbsenceTest::test_unsearchable_user_config_dir_is_a_config_error_not_a_traceback` | red: uncaught `PermissionError` on Python 3.10 and 3.12; rc 0, `ready` on Python 3.14 | green |
| G1 | `UnconfirmedAbsenceTest::test_partial_clone_with_a_reachable_source_honours_the_committed_mode` | green | green |
| G2 | `UnconfirmedAbsenceTest::test_committed_config_that_is_not_a_regular_file_names_its_entry_type` | already rc 2 and blocked, but as "invalid TOML"; the new assertion that the message names the entry type is red | green |
| G3 | `UnconfirmedAbsenceTest::test_user_layer_is_absent_when_its_path_cannot_exist` | green | green |

The 14 existing tests are unchanged and green before and after. Totals for the file: 7 failed, 16 passed against the a76fbf6f source; 23 passed at 27eb3f9e. Both measured on Python 3.10, 3.12 and 3.14.

**Mutation checks.** Run against the source tree the tests import; each was restored afterwards.
- Returning "absent" when the blob read fails: R1 and R2 go red.
- Restoring the `path.exists()` gate on the user path: R4 and R5 go red (R6 too).
- Four further mutations each turn a cell red: treating a missing `HEAD` commit or a failed `git ls-tree` as absent (R3); dropping the entry-type check (G2); accepting a symlink mode (G2); treating any `lstat` error as absent (R6).

**Verification.**
- `tests/test_publication_mode_1392.py`, `tests/test_skills_canon_parity.py` and `tests/test_skills_bundle_drift.py`: 34 passed on Python 3.10, 3.12 and 3.14.
- `ruff check` (0.15.5) is clean on both files.

**Not in this commit.**
- The `source:` line for a committed file that declares no mode is unchanged.
- The follow-ups named in the board ruling are filed after merge.

## Board hb2 must-fix
One fix commit, 77fa108c, on top of 27eb3f9e. `git diff --stat 27eb3f9e..77fa108c` touches only the same two files, `publication_mode.py` and `tests/test_publication_mode_1392.py`.

**Fixed.**
- At 27eb3f9e the user layer followed the hb1 rule literally: when a parent directory of the user path was a symlink to a missing directory, `lstat` of the full path reported ENOENT and the user layer was absent. A user file reached through a symlinked directory resolved `none` while the link worked, and `ready` with exit 0 once its target was gone. That is now a config error.
- `phase-loop publication-mode` walks the user path one component at a time, from the root down to the file. The user layer is absent only where the walk ends at a directory that lacks the next component, or at a non-directory.
- A symlink on the way that does not resolve (dangling or looping) is a config error that names the component. So is a component that cannot be examined.
- A symlinked parent that resolves is followed, and the file is read through it.
- The walk covers every component, so the `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` value and the `HOME` fallback are checked the same way.

**Cells.** "Before" is the new test file run against the unchanged 27eb3f9e source. The five levels are: a directory above the config home, the config home, the `agent-harness` directory, `HOME`, and `HOME/.config`.

author: nariokeith
body:
## Summary

Restyles the renderer to match the VOX wireframes in light and dark mode, and replaces the app icon with the panther mark. Behaviour, IPC, calc, safety and the main process are unchanged.

## Motivation

The new wireframes define the look of the app: a left sidebar shell, a four-step onboarding, a chat-style log, Today/Weekly/Monthly views, Progress and Settings. Only screens and cards the app can back with real data are built. No targets, rings, macros or invented numbers are added.

## Changes

- **Design system:** Inter font and lucide icons (both bundled, pinned versions, no runtime network). Colour tokens are sampled from the wireframes, with Light, Dark and System themes chosen in Settings. Sizes are in rem with one scale knob.
- **Icons:** the app icon (`build/`, `resources/`) and the sidebar logo mark are cropped from the wireframe icon sheet. They are softer than source artwork would be, so swap them when the original files exist.
- **Shell:** the sidebar has Talk to VOX, Today · Weekly · Monthly, Progress and Settings, plus the on-device AI status chip.
- **Onboarding:** Welcome, Personal Info, Fitness Setup and Review replace the single profile form. It uses the same `ProfileInput` validation, teen and under-13 rules, disclaimer and privacy line.
- **Talk to VOX:** the log screen restyled as a chat. Confirm, discard, safety and crisis handling and their text are unchanged.
- **Today / Weekly / Monthly:**
  - stat cards and a VOX Insight card from the latest reaction
  - weekly and monthly bar cards
  - the weight trend, for adults only
  - ‹ › period navigation that never goes past today
- **Progress and Settings:**
  - Progress: weight trend and body metrics (adults), plus 30-day activity, sleep and water.
  - Settings: profile with Edit, appearance, a privacy overview with only statements that are true, and AI status.
- **Shared helpers (tested):**
  - date periods: `startOfWeek`, `monthBounds`, `periodRange`, `shiftPeriod`, `canGoNext`
  - summaries: `summarizeRange`, `weightChange`
- **Docs:** design spec in `docs/specs/`, implementation plan in `docs/plans/`.

Rules kept:
- Teen mode shows no calorie, weight or diet content.
- Energy numbers always show `~` and "estimate".
- Red is a brand accent only, never an over/under signal.
- CSP is unchanged.

## Testing

- `npm test`: 118 passed (new: `tests/dates.test.ts`, `tests/summary.test.ts`, `tests/renderer-utils.test.ts`)
- `npm run typecheck`: clean
- `npm run lint`: 0 errors. The 3 prettier warnings are already in `scripts/download-models.mjs`.
- Manual run in mock mode (`VOX_FAKE_LLM=1`) with a separate data folder and seeded demo history. Every screen was checked in light, dark and system for:
  - an adult with calories
  - an adult with calories off
  - a teen
  - under-13, which is blocked
  - the missing-model error screen

## Known gaps

- No hero illustrations until source artwork exists. They plug in through the `--banner-art` CSS variable.
- Nutrition shows "—" because `data/foods.ph.json` is still empty.
- Deferred minors:
  - no error state when `history.range` rejects
  - the tabs don't implement the full ARIA tabs pattern
  - Enter doesn't submit onboarding
  - an error message stays after Back
  - the sidebar calendar icon renders slightly small

author: bzinkan
body:
Release successor validation launched 449 separate PowerShell processes for private evidence checks. One actual preparation replay took 196.720 seconds; repeating it before publication, registration and deployment left too little room in the existing authorization and CI freshness windows.

For the single schema-5 successor, batch already-concurrent permission checks in groups of at most four. Every path still runs the official private-input assertion, including duplicates and paths after a failed check. Any failed batch rejects every waiting reader. Each invocation has its own queue, with no cached permissions; helper identity is checked before dispatch and import. Historical schema-1 through schema-4 command paths stay unchanged.

Validation:

- 182 local regressions passed, including 11 focused queue cases and real Windows protected ACL, shared ACL, reparse, helper mutation and failed-batch checks.
- The same retained preparation replay passed in 129.134 seconds with all 449 official path checks, using 143 PowerShell processes. Original native-result hashes and the exact artifact pair remained unchanged.
- Backend/frontend input inventories, the accepted binding profile, the other eight operational files and the other 178 measured scripts are unchanged. No application/image/threshold or historical evidence changes.

The new tooling still requires exact-head and resulting-main CI. The actual operational Plan must be timed before cloud mutation; this change does not extend authorization windows, refresh immutable CI receipts, publish images, register definitions or deploy services.

author: kblok
body:
Closes #236

A raw JSON array used to be valid decision state. Upstream now reads an array as an ordered list of text, file, and json parts. This ports that change. `Evaluate.EvaluateAsync` validates the state, then `DecisionState.PrepareDecisionStateAsync` normalizes it before the model call. Strings become a text part, objects become a json part, and file parts get a full media type. URL files are downloaded, and a failed download throws `DownloadError` before any model call. The start and end events keep the public state. The model call and the model-call events get the normalized parts. The `Evaluate` rename (#220) is not part of this change.

`OpenAIDecisionModel` and `GatewayDecisionModel` now read the normalized parts, as upstream does. OpenAI sends text and json parts as `input_text` and inline PNG, JPEG, WebP, or GIF files as `input_image`, and rejects other files. Gateway keeps its legacy state format and rejects files.

## Tests

Ported 7 new tests in `EvaluateTests`, and 4 in the OpenAI and Gateway decision tests (maps ordered parts to native text and images, rejects unsupported files, legacy Gateway state format, rejects files before the request). All are Covered. The OpenAI boolean-criteria test follows its upstream rename and new row. Existing OpenAI and Gateway tests now pass parts as state, as upstream does. Partial: 0.

## Report

Not ported, because the C# port has no such feature:
- `decision-language-model.test.ts` (2 tests): there is no `DecisionLanguageModel` in the port.
- `stringify-for-telemetry.test.ts` and the otel `ai.decision.state` assertions: there is no otel package.

author: tomklotzpro
body:
Tom's playtest note (PIX-250): the things to pick up off the ground came back to the same cells every day, so playing a lot meant piles of forest herbs.

## What changed

**Gathering patches move with the days.** The 41 fixed patches (`gatherSpots`, regrowing every 300 steps, which is several times a day) are gone. Now each region's ground is shuffled once into a deck (`Gathering.decks`), and each day (`DayNight`'s day, the one a night's sleep ends) deals the next few cards from it (`Gathering.patches_on`):
- **Where a patch can grow:** on the kind of tile the region's old patches stood on (`gathering.ground`, e.g. grass in the forest, ash in the Ash, snow on the pass, floor in the caves), and only:
  - in the open (all eight neighbours walkable, no statue, cave mouth or doorway next to it),
  - on bare ground, so no decor hides the patch,
  - off the roads,
  - at least 2 cells from portals, the spawn and waypoint arrivals,
  - at least 4 cells from houses, doors and villagers (so not in a village), and 4 from a pack's home (its camp),
  - not next to a chest or a fishing spot.
  The decks are read from the map before any house or prop is drawn, so they come out the same with or without the paid art.
- **Same day, same patches.** The picks come only from the day number and a seed, the same way the showers do, so nothing new is saved. Today's cells are never yesterday's, a day's patches on a map are at least 6 cells apart, and a deck takes hundreds of days to come round again.
- **A new day while you're out** swaps in the new day's patches on the spot (`MapView.refresh_patches`). A night's sleep also brings the next day's patches.
- **Picked stays picked until the next morning.** The save is unchanged: `gatheredAt` still stores the step each patch was picked on. The patch ids are the old ones (`forest_patch_1`, ...), now meaning "the region's Nth patch today", so old saves load as they were.

**Caps per material** (`combat.json` `gathering.daily`), set by the catalogue value, across all the regions that grow it:

| material | value | per day | where |
|---|---|---|---|
| forest herb | 6g | 3 | forest |
| marsh reed | 6g | 3 | marsh |
| deep root | 9g | 2 | Deepwood |
| ember shard | 10g | 2 | the Ash |
| grave moss | 10g | 2 | Mirefen |
| sea glass | 12g | 2 | 1 on the Saltmere coast + 1 in the sea cave |
| frost lily | 16g | 1 | Frostgate or the ice cave, taking turns |
| blackiron ore | 18g | 1 | the mines or the shafts, taking turns |
| old steel | 20g | 1 | Greyhold or its cellars, taking turns |

The overworld now grows 8 patches a day. Before, its 12 fixed patches each grew back every 300 steps, nearly five times in a 1440-step day. A test checks that a dearer material never grows more per day than a cheaper one, and that each day grows exactly the supply. There was no tool or level rule for picking before, and I didn't add one: the caps already make the rare materials rare, and a level gate would keep a new hero off the only patch of a material their early quests ask for.

**Dungeon floors:** each floor still has one patch in its first hall. It used to sit on the same cell and regrow every 300 steps. Now it moves to a different open cell of that hall each day (`Gathering.floor_patch`) and grows once a day, like the wild ones. `DungeonFloor.plan` returns `patch_ground` (the cells it can use) instead of a single `patch`.

**Ground treasure is unchanged.** The road's glint and the herb patch by the road are one-time finds already: they're saved in `openedChests` and never reset.

**Harness:** `--day <n>` (in `HarnessFlags.TABLE`) starts the run on the morning of day n, and the report line adds `day=` and `patches=` (the cells still to pick). `night` and `dusk` now keep that day.

## How it was verified
- GUT (all of it, headless): 750 tests, 749 passing, 1 known risky (`test_the_fountains_age_says_it_wants_the_scale`), no Parse Error or SCRIPT ERROR. The save codec tests and the frozen fixtures are untouched and pass. `test_gathering` covers:
  - every deck cell is the region's ground, off the road, open once the map is fully planned (no prop, camp or bush on it), bare, and out of the villages;
  - the same day gives the same patches;
  - the next day never repeats a cell, and a day's patches are 6 apart;
  - each day grows exactly each material's supply, with the two homes of a rare material taking turns;
  - the per-region and per-map caps over 200 days;
  - a picked patch stays picked all day and is back the next morning, with the save format unchanged;
  - a pre-PIX-250 save's `gatheredAt` loads;
  - the map deals a new day's patches mid-visit;
  - each floor's patch moves day by day.

  `test_world_maps` checks every deck cell.
- Release flows (`tools/flows.sh --quiet`): all 70 `ok` (motion skipped, it needs a window), including three new ones:
  - `patches`: overworld, day 2, eight cells
  - `regrown`: overworld, day 3, eight different cells
  - `forage`: day 2, the hero steps onto one patch and it's gone from the list
- Every wild map and the town boot headless with and without `--day`, with no SCRIPT ERROR. On day 5 the rare homes take turns: ore in the mines but not the shafts, steel in the cellars but not Greyhold, lilies in the ice cave but not the Frostgate. Floor 1's patch is at (15, 4) on day 2 and (19, 9) on day 3.
- Two windowed, muted screenshots of the same view of the marsh show day 2 and day 3 with their reeds in different places.
- `python3 tools/i18n.py --check` passes. No new player-facing strings; only string locations moved.

author: paulvers-ui2
body:
A pass on memory safety, exploit mitigations and speed, starting from what code scanning reports on `main` and the installed v0.2.13.

### Memory safety

The engine and usque are Go: bounds-checked slices, no pointer arithmetic, stacks that grow instead of overflowing. Memory can be corrupted only where code passes raw buffers to Windows (`unsafe`), or through a data race. Those are the spots this targets.

- **`win/ifbind`:** the same `GetAdaptersAddresses` buffer loop was copied four times. It is now one helper, `forEachAdapter`. Its buffer is 8-byte aligned, as Windows' adapter records need, and it stays alive while those records are read.
- **`win/owner`:** a table size Windows reports outside the buffer is refused.
- **Fuzz tests** (`fuzz_windows_test.go`) throw random input at the parsers:
  - the rule sets the app sends (`compileRules`, `decide`, `dnsVerdict`);
  - the geo-IP lookup.

  Simulate fuzzes each for 60 s on every PR.
- **Race detector:** Simulate now runs the unit tests a second time under Go's race detector.

### Exploit mitigations (`tools/check-mitigations.ps1`)

Every exe and dll the app ships must have **ASLR** (64-bit ASLR for 64-bit files) and **DEP** on. The App workflow now checks each release.

On the installed v0.2.13, everything passes except one file: electron-builder's 32-bit `resources\elevate.exe`. Nothing uses it (the app elevates through the service or PowerShell), so it is no longer packed (`packElevateHelper: false`).

CFG is reported but not required, because Go does not emit it. AuroraVPN.exe and the Electron and Wintun dlls have it.

### Electron

- **Asar integrity fuse:** the app refuses to start from a modified `app.asar`.
- **Global sandbox:** `app.enableSandbox()` puts every renderer in the sandbox.
- **Devices:** USB, HID and serial access is denied.
- **Redirects:** blocked, like navigation already was.

Context isolation, the window sandbox, deny-all permissions, CSP, IPC sender checks and the other fuses were already in place (#11).

### Speed

Every new connection copied the whole Windows TCP or UDP table to find which program opened it. This happens on the packet path, before the connection goes through.

Now a burst of connections (a browser opens many at once) shares one copy that is at most 250 ms old. A socket missing from the copy is looked up in a fresh one, so a copy never hides a new connection. `owner_windows_test.go` checks exactly that case.

### Checked

- **Mitigation script:** run against the installed v0.2.13 files, and against a copy with DEP cleared, which it fails.
- **Go and Electron changes:** CI compiles and tests them, and the packaged app's self-test covers the new fuse.

author: guillaumelauzier
body:
## Objective

StudioOS answers as a remote MCP server at `https://axal.vc/api/mcp`. ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Grok or any MCP client adds it by URL and signs in with OAuth 2.1, and a founder approves each assistant for the companies they tick, sees each grant and can revoke it. Everything is off: the flag is `"false"` everywhere, and `OAUTH_KV` is not bound yet.

Closes #1496

## Implementation

**Where this differs from #1495, so S1 can check it first:**
- **No `agents` package.** Every `agents` release (to 0.28.0) pins `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk` 1.30.0, which GHSA-6qxp-vccf-f47h covers (<1.31.0), so `npm audit` would go red.
  - `createMcpHandler` is the SDK's web-standard Streamable HTTP transport in stateless mode. This uses that transport directly from the patched SDK 1.32.1.
  - Validation uses `@cfworker/json-schema`, because the SDK's default, ajv, uses `new Function`, which Workers refuse.
- **The OAuth endpoints are `/api/oauth/{authorize,token,register}`.**
  - They sit under `/api/*`, which `run_worker_first` already covers.
  - They sit outside `/api/mcp`, because the provider demands a token for everything under its `apiRoute`.
- **`OAUTH_KV` is declared in all three blocks but commented out** (marked `OAUTH_KV-PENDING`). The owner hasn't given the id, and a binding without one breaks the deploy. The Worker treats an unbound `OAUTH_KV` as off.
- **`[env.preview]` has no `[assets]` block,** so the two `/.well-known` patterns are added in the two blocks that have one.
- **StudioOS has no password.** "Changing the password revokes every grant" is implemented as "raising the session floor revokes every grant":
  - `bumpJwtMinIat` (sign out everywhere, force re-auth, re-pairing, email revoke);
  - the post-recovery re-enrolment;
  - a deletion request.

**What a reviewer should look at:**
- **Consent goes through the SPA.**
  - The authorize endpoint checks the request, requires S256 PKCE, parks it for 10 minutes and redirects to `/connect/assistant?request=<id>`.
  - Approve and deny are signed in, single-use (with a tombstone) and re-check every company.
  - Nothing is auto-approved, and the response carries the redirect host.
- **"Companies" are projects the person owns or co-founds.** Staff pass `canAccessProject` for every project, so they are offered none.
- **Each tool call:**
  - re-reads the user: inactive, deletion requested, or a session floor raised after the grant means refused;
  - checks the company is in the grant and still writable;
  - counts against a 60-a-minute limit per grant, failing closed;
  - logs tool, company, client and outcome, with no arguments or results.
- **The read tools:**
  - `get_validate_context` reads Validate's own module records, not customer research's, which carry names. Interviews are only counted.
  - `get_interview_guide` is built by code.
- **Approve spends the request id before completing the authorization.** If completion fails, the founder starts again from the assistant. This fails closed.

## Files changed

- `cloudflare-worker/src/mcp/oauth.ts`, `server.ts`, `grants.ts`, `tools/context.ts`, and two READMEs: the provider, server, guard and read tools.
- `cloudflare-worker/src/routes/mcp_consent.ts`: consent, and the grants list and revoke.
- `cloudflare-worker/src/index.ts`: `fetch` sends the MCP and OAuth paths to the provider first, and two mounts.
- `src/auth.ts`, `src/routes/settings.ts`: revoke every grant where the session floor rises and on a deletion request.
- `src/types.ts`: `MCP_SERVER_ENABLED`, `OAUTH_KV` and `MCP_PUBLIC_ORIGIN`.
- `wrangler.toml`:
  - the flag `"false"` ×3;
  - `OAUTH_KV` pending ×3;
  - the two `/.well-known` patterns ×2;
  - `main` unchanged and no route.
- `package.json`: `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk` 1.32.1, `@cloudflare/workers-oauth-provider` 1.2.3, `@cfworker/json-schema` 4.1.1 and `zod` 4.6.5, all exact.
- `test/mcp_server_d666.test.ts` (12 tests), `test/_mem_kv.mjs`, and a `cloudflare:workers` stub in `test/_ts-loader-hook.mjs`.
- `D666.md`, `ROUTE_MAP.md`, `GOTCHAS.md` (the bearer-token consent hand-off), and the routes and src READMEs.

## Testing

- `npm run build` passes, and `npm run test:drift > drift.log 2>&1; echo EXIT=$?` gives **EXIT=0**.
- `npm audit` reports 0 vulnerabilities in the worker, including dev dependencies.
- The wrangler binding-parity guard passes, and `wrangler deploy --dry-run --env production` builds.
- The 12 tests run the real provider over an in-memory KV and SQLite D1. They cover:
  - with the flag off, or `OAUTH_KV` missing, all six paths answer 404;
  - unauthenticated calls get 401 with `WWW-Authenticate` naming the metadata;
  - discovery names `https://axal.vc/api/mcp` and S256 only;
  - PKCE is required, including from a confidential client;
  - consent refuses a company that isn't writable, a used id and an expired id;
  - staff are offered nothing, and deny carries `access_denied`;
  - a revoked token gets 401;
  - sign-out-everywhere and the session-floor backstop;
  - a tool for a company outside the grant, or one since lost, is refused;
  - the seeded interviewee's name appears nowhere in the response;
  - the log holds no argument text;
  - the toml, read from the file.
- **Mutations: 27 run, 27 caught.** Two needed work first:
  - PKCE, which the provider already enforces for public clients, was caught once a confidential-client test was added;
  - one helper-only mutation with no effect of its own was dropped.
- **Not done:** the manual check from the MCP Inspector against the preview Worker. It needs a KV namespace on the preview account. This PR stays draft until then.

## Risks

- **Production:** off. The flag is `"false"` and `OAUTH_KV` is unbound, and both are needed.
  - Every other path goes on exactly as before: `fetch` checks `isMcpPath` first and returns otherwise.
  - The production bundle grows from 2.17 MB to 2.40 MB gzipped.
- **To turn on:**
  1. `npx wrangler kv namespace create OAUTH_KV`;
  2. paste the id into the three `OAUTH_KV-PENDING` blocks and uncomment them;
  3. set the flag to `"true"` after S1's review of the OAuth flow, the scopes and prompt injection.
- **Rollback:** set the flag to `"false"`, or revert. There is no migration.
- No secret is in the diff.
- `lint:no-console` fails on `routes/esign.ts:1353`, which is identical on `main`. That lint is not part of drift or CI.

## Dependencies

- Part of #1495 (D665).
- Unblocks #1497, whose interview tools register through `registerMcpTools`, and the wiring of #1498 (PR #1502).
- Needs the owner's `OAUTH_KV` id.

## Agent

S19, claimed at the owner's request by the S02 session · Claude

## Review requested

S1, adversarially: the OAuth flow, the consent hand-off, the grant checks and the absence of `agents`.

author: victorpaleologue
body:
The ROS4HRI preset now lands a streamed viseme's `time` and `duration` along with its code.

## Why

An `hri_msgs/Viseme` carries three fields:
- `value`, the shape;
- `time`, seconds into the utterance;
- `duration`, seconds the shape is held.

The preset landed only `value`, which loses two things:
- **How long to hold the shape.** A viseme player fell back to a fixed envelope, closing the mouth under a long vowel.
- **Which viseme it is.** Two consecutive identical shapes (`PP`, `PP`) are one value on the key, so they played as one.

## The change

Each viseme lands three keys in one change, from `/tts/viseme` and `/tts/visemes` alike:

| field | key |
|---|---|
| `value` | `standard/ros4hri/viseme` (unchanged) |
| `time` | `standard/ros4hri/viseme/time` |
| `duration` | `standard/ros4hri/viseme/duration` |

On the Vizij side, `play_viseme` holds the shape for `duration`, and a new `time` starts a new run even when the shape repeats. That follows in vizij-rs once this is released.

arora-bridge-ros2 **10.1.0**: additive.

## Verified

- `ros4hri_preset_takes_a_viseme_in_either_shape`: both endpoints route the three fields to the three keys.
- `the_ros4hri_profile_fans_typed_topics_onto_face_keys` (live DDS; ignored on macOS, run here with `--ignored`): a `Viseme` and a `Visemes` each land their code, time and duration in one change.

author: coffeegoddd
body:
Rebuilding an `Alias` expression currently drops its column ID and its `Unreferencable` flag. Preserve both when replacing the child so references through derived tables continue to identify the projected column after analyzer rewrites.

For callers using `ParseTableAsColumn`, resolve a FROM relation before a previously defined SELECT alias of the same name. Doltgres gives `e::text` the output name `e`; in `SELECT e::text, e IS NULL FROM json_array_elements(...) AS e`, the second reference must read the FROM function's value. Previously it selected the first output alias and failed with `ErrMisusedAlias`. The behavior for callers without whole-row support is covered by a regression test.

Needed by https://github.com/dolthub/doltgresql/pull/3577 to address the nested JSON filtering and repeated-alias findings from Ito.

Validation:
- `go test ./sql/expression ./sql/planbuilder ./sql/analyzer -count=1`
- `go test ./enginetest -run '^Test(ColumnAliases|SetReturningFunctionQueries|TupleQueries)$' -count=1`
- Full Doltgres Go integration test package with this dependency and the corresponding column-type propagation fix.

author: matthewg119
body:
Matthew, 2026-10-09:

> i sent a bunch of keywords i wanted it to pile them keywords and generate one final prompt to run a batch of 100 variations 50 seo and 50 aeo headlines just want a final prompt to run it

The brief shipped this morning asked for **20 of each per keyword** and capped the pile at five. Wrong shape twice over: across his eleven planned pages that is 440 lines, which is not a batch anybody reads, and the cap would have split his *one final prompt* into three.

## What changed

`BRIEF_TOTAL_PER_FORMAT = 50`, and it is a **total**. The answer is 100 lines whatever the keyword count, spread across the pile. The per-keyword share is worked out and stated rather than left for the model to guess, with a floor of two per keyword and an explicit "never skip one" so the spread cannot collapse onto the first three.

For his real eleven:

```
THE 11 KEYWORDS. One page per keyword. Every one of them gets lines:
THE SIZE OF THE JOB: 50 AEO H1s and 50 SEO title tags, 100 lines in total,
spread across those 11 keywords. That is about 5 of each per keyword.

PART A. 50 AEO H1s IN TOTAL, across every keyword above.
PART B. 50 SEO TITLE TAGS IN TOTAL, across every keyword above.
```

`BRIEF_MAX_KEYWORDS` 5 to 15. At twenty per keyword the cap was protecting him from the size; with totals the size is fixed, so it only has to clear his eleven with room. It is still a cap, because a hundred pasted phrases would spread two lines each and be worth nothing.

The chat prompt now says to pass **every** keyword he named in **one** call, since "one final prompt" is the request and calling it per keyword is the failure mode the old wording invited.

## Verification

The probe pins both halves: the totals in the part headings **and** the wording that says they are totals, so a revert to per-keyword fails by name. It also checks the single-keyword case still asks for the full fifty, and that eleven keywords stay one brief inside the cap.

`tsc --noEmit` clean but the pre-existing Stripe error. All 26 gated probes pass.

author: boxysean
body:
## What this is

The first step in extending the Jaffle Logistics dataset **backwards in time**: 2023 and 2024 are added
to the operational backbone, so 2025 stops being the only year in the data and becomes the third year of
a company with a visible history.

**Append-only. Zero deleted lines** across every seed touched — all existing 2025 rows are byte-identical.

| seed | before | after | factor |
|---|---|---|---|
| `seeds/shipments.csv` | 2,009 | 6,027 | 3.00× |
| `seeds/routes.csv` | 3,629 | 10,887 | 3.00× |
| `seeds/incidents.csv` | 174 | 384 | 2.21× |
| `seeds/drivers.csv` | 50 | 56 | 1.12× |
| `seeds/vehicles.csv` | 40 | 44 | 1.10× |

Also: `scripts/generate_history.py` (the deterministic, seeded generator that produced the rows) and a
new `docs/history.md` page wired into the mkdocs nav, stating the expanded timeline.

## The story the numbers tell

2023 and 2024 are the **quiet, healthy years** — deliberately generated as a baseline, not uniformly at
random:

- Whole-book on-time delivery (**`delivered` = on time**): **97.5% in 2023, 97.2% in 2024** — at or above
  the 97% contractual target, against **93.3% in 2025**.
- Jaffle Equipment (`CLI-0042`): **98.1% in 2023 and 98.1% in 2024** — a healthy account before its 2025
  decline.
- **No 2025 signal starts early**: no storm-scale event, no repeated handling-damage cluster at `HUB-CMH`,
  no bay-3 pattern in the prior years. Every analysis already written about 2025 still holds, and now has
  something to be measured against.

## Date discipline

Every added row is dated inside the past, never the future:

- `shipments.created_at` max **2025-12-31**
- `routes.service_date` max **2025-12-31**
- `incidents.occurred_at` max **2025-12-31**
- `shipments.delivered_at` max **2026-01-03** — a late-December delivery completing a few days into
  January, exactly as the pre-existing data already did before this change.

## Verification (run locally, duckdb — no warehouse, no AI spend)

```
dbt build --target duckdb --vars '{ai_functions_enabled: false}'
→ PASS=239  WARN=0  ERROR=0
```

Plus independent checks of the invariants above: row counts per file, `git diff --numstat` showing zero
deletions, per-year on-time rates, and min/max date bounds of the added rows.

The eight source cards (CRM notes, support tickets, dispatch notes, incident reports, legal docs,
Slack threads, call transcripts, fleet work orders + HR docs) depend on this branch landing — their new
rows cite the shipments, routes and incidents added here.

author: teseo-bot
body:
⛔ **Mergear este PR despliega el compiler a producción.** El código no cambia; sólo se añade un `.sql`. La migración se aplica a mano como `postgres`.

**Qué se midió.** El 2026-10-09, después de aplicar la 016 en producción, `kdb_compiler` tenía `UPDATE` y `DELETE` sobre `casos_exito_versiones`, aunque la 016 sólo le concede `SELECT` e `INSERT`. Una consulta de diagnóstico de sólo lectura encontró la causa en los privilegios por defecto del Cold-Tier:

```
pg_default_acl: postgres → kdb_compiler=arwd/postgres
kdb_compiler_es_miembro_de: (ninguno)
compiler_borra_versiones: t · compiler_vacia_versiones: f
```

Toda tabla que crea `postgres` le da esos cuatro permisos a `kdb_compiler`, y un `GRANT` no quita lo que ya llegó por defecto.

**Qué cambia.** La 017 revoca `UPDATE`, `DELETE` y `TRUNCATE` sobre `casos_exito_versiones`. Sobre `casos_exito` se mantienen los cuatro, que la autoría necesita. Así se cierra el borrado de versiones no vigentes, que la FK no cubría; el trigger de la 016 ya impedía reescribirlas.

**Probada** en local reproduciendo esos privilegios por defecto:
- Después de la 016: `UPDATE` y `DELETE` en `t`, como en producción.
- Después de la 017, aplicada dos veces: `UPDATE` y `DELETE` en `f`, con la cabeza intacta.
- Un `DELETE` como `kdb_compiler` da `permission denied`.

author: skalaliya
body:
## What and why

The pipeline names flaky tests and shard times on each run, but nothing kept them:
- A flake seen on `integration` had to be noticed and filed by hand, although the flaky test policy asks for an issue the same day.
- The time target (`ios` within 22 minutes at the median) had no data behind it.
- The runner queueing seen on #186 (16–19 minutes) could not be measured.

This PR adds:
- **`flaky-issues`**, a new job that runs on pushes to `integration` and `main` and on the nightly, never on a pull request ([`flaky_issues.py`](scripts/ci/flaky_issues.py)):
  - For each flaky test it opens an issue titled `Flaky test: <test>`, labelled `bug` and `flaky` as the policy asks. If that issue is already open, it comments on it instead, with the run, the commit and the first failure's message.
  - It handles at most 10 tests a run and never closes an issue.
  - It is the only job with `issues: write`. `ios` does not need it, so tracking never decides the check.
- **`ci-timings`**, a new job that runs whenever the iOS gates ran ([`ci_timings.py`](scripts/ci/ci_timings.py), `actions: read` only):
  - It records each job's minutes running and minutes queued, and how many minutes `ios` took from the attempt's start, and keeps them as the 90-day `ci-timings` artifact.
  - A job kept from an earlier attempt by a re-run gets no queued time. The API dates its creation to the re-run but its start to the earlier attempt.
  - It warns when a test shard ran over 20 minutes. Only a slow UI shard is told to rebalance.
- **Shard balance advice** in `ios-report`'s summary ([`rebalance_shards.py`](scripts/ci/rebalance_shards.py)): the UI classes' times on this run, and a `test_shards.json` to use when moving classes would shorten the slowest UI shard by more than 10%. It is advice only and never fails.
- **`xcresult_report.py --flaky-out`** writes the flaky tests for the issue job.
- **Review follow-up from #186:** the shard balance figures in the testing strategy and in `test_shards.py` now cite the run they were measured on (37984144377: 742, 689 and 785 seconds in tests) instead of unsourced estimates.
- **`docs/working-memory.md`** tracks the text-editing flake left after #187 ([#188](https://github.com/Algorythmos-AI/pdf-algo-pro/issues/188)).

## How it was tested

- **`uv run --with pytest==8.4.2 pytest -q scripts`:** 211 passed, 16 of them new. The new tests cover:
  - the flaky reporter's JSON;
  - issue planning: commenting on an open issue or creating one, each test handled once, the cap, a message unable to break out of its code block, a dry run that never calls `gh`, and the policy labels;
  - timings from API pages and job lines, the slow-shard warning, and a re-run's kept jobs;
  - the balance proposal and its rewrite of `test_shards.json`.
- **Local checks:** `check_docs.py`, `invariants.py` and actionlint are clean.
- **Green CI run on the head (34b1856):** [38005892731](https://github.com/Algorythmos-AI/pdf-algo-pro/actions/runs/38005892731).
  - `ci-timings` reported its table, with `ios` at 32.2 minutes after the run started.
  - `flaky-issues` was skipped, as it should be on a pull request.
  - `ios-report` printed the balance summary.
  - The inventory ran 821 of 821 tests.
- **Re-run bug, caught and fixed:** the earlier run [38000339542](https://github.com/Algorythmos-AI/pdf-algo-pro/actions/runs/38000339542) went green after one re-run of ui-3, which had run no test because github.com was unreachable while it fetched packages. That re-run exposed the negative queued times fixed in 34b1856.
- **Still to check:** `flaky-issues` first runs for real on the `integration` push after the merge, and I'll check that run.

## Pillars and platforms

Engineering foundations (CI); no app code.

## Privacy

Privacy policy impact: none, because this changes CI scripts, workflow jobs and docs only. The issues it opens hold test names and failure messages from synthetic fixtures.

## Checklist

- [x] One focused change; the branch targets `integration`
- [x] Tests added or updated for changed behaviour
- [x] Every new or changed test has passed in a CI run on this branch ([38005892731](https://github.com/Algorythmos-AI/pdf-algo-pro/actions/runs/38005892731)), and this branch does not start from another unmerged branch
- [x] No secrets, credentials, personal data or real documents in the diff
- [x] Docs and `docs/working-memory.md` updated (quality gates, testing strategy)
- [x] Accessibility: no UI change
- [x] No new third-party dependency

author: lkiesow
body:
Profile limits reached an existing key only when its owner opened the
dashboard, because the dashboard pushed them to the gateway on every page
view. Admin changes were written only to the database. This caused three
problems:

- **Admin changes were not enforced** for anyone who only uses the API.
  Downgrading a user or cutting a profile's budget had no effect until that
  user opened the portal.
- **A failed profile lookup removed every limit.** If the dashboard could not
  load the profile (a busy database, or no default profile), it pushed empty
  limits, and the gateway reads empty limits as "unlimited".
- **Every page view wrote to the gateway**, even when nothing had changed.

Pushing inline when an admin saves is no fix: one key update is three gateway
calls, so a change to a profile with 5,000 users takes about 25 minutes.

## What changes

**Pending updates are recorded in the database.** Each profile gets a
revision number that goes up when its limits change (models, TPM/RPM, quota
windows). Renaming a profile or changing its description or key validity
doesn't count. Each key records the profile and revision it last received.
A key is out of date when its owner's current profile, their own or the
default, differs from that record. One rule covers every way limits can
change:

- a profile is edited,
- a user is moved to another profile,
- another profile becomes the default,
- a time-limited assignment runs out.

**A background sync pushes out-of-date keys.** Admin saves start it right
away; the admin's request does not wait. It also runs at startup and on an
interval to retry failures.

- There is no queue. A key always gets what its profile says when the key is
  updated, so if a profile is saved twice in quick succession, keys not
  reached yet only ever see the second version.
- A key whose push fails keeps the error and is tried once per run, so a
  gateway outage does not turn into a retry loop.
- A key whose owner has no profile at all is never pushed empty limits; it is
  reported as failed.

**The admin panel shows the progress** to every admin in an "API Key
Updates" card: how many keys are waiting, whether a run is going on, which
keys failed and why, and when the last run finished. The profile table shows
how many keys are waiting per profile.

**The dashboard only reads**, and no longer hides what it could not load:

- Profile not loaded: it says so, leaves out the model list and the extension
  date, and hides Extend and Regenerate, which would fail. Delete still works.
- Key not loaded: it says so instead of "You don't have an API key yet", and
  offers no Generate button.
- Usage not readable from the gateway: it says the figures may be incomplete,
  instead of claiming "no usage limit" or "no usage recorded".

**The profile-expiry job** only switches the profile in the database and
starts the sync. Assignments that end by deleting the key work as before.

**A new command, `ai-self-service -resync-limits`,** marks every key as out
of date, to undo changes made directly in the gateway. It needs only
`DB_PATH`, pushes nothing itself, and can run from cron through
`docker exec` or `kubectl exec`.

## Configuration

| Variable | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `LIMIT_SYNC_WORKERS` | `1` | Key updates sent to the gateway at once |
| `LIMIT_SYNC_INTERVAL` | `5m` | How often failed updates are retried |

## Deploying

- **Migration 20240010** adds `profiles.limits_rev` and four `api_keys`
  columns.
- **The first run after the upgrade updates every key once,** because no
  existing key has a record yet. With one worker that's about 25 minutes per
  5,000 keys, and the admin card shows the progress. This also moves keys
  issued before #26 onto the per-user allowance.
- This relies on the SQLite concurrency change already on `main` (WAL mode),
  so `-resync-limits` can write while the server runs. Keep the database on a
  local disk, not NFS.

## Testing

- New tests cover the out-of-date query, the sync (failures, retries, edits
  during a run, keys without a profile, parallel workers), the admin card,
  the dashboard error states, the expiry job and `-resync-limits`.
- The tests that checked the dashboard's pushes are replaced by one that
  checks it makes none.
- `go test -race ./...` and `go vet ./...` pass.
- Checked by hand against the OIDC mock with an unreachable gateway: the
  admin card (pending, failed, all up to date), the dashboard warnings, and
  `-resync-limits` running alongside the server.

The commits are ordered so that each one builds and passes the tests on its
own; reviewing them one at a time may be easier than the full diff.

author: g-eskayo
body:
Closes #385 (Pipeline scans overlap: a busy scan lock is ignored after 120 s)
Closes #386 (A PR repaired seconds earlier still gets sent back for a full rebuild)
Closes #387 (The hold label doesn't stop the pipeline (dispatch and send-back ignore it))

**What happened (2026-10-09):** PR #358 (ticket #102) had its merge conflict repaired automatically and pushed at 21:39:53. A second scan was running alongside it, working from a list of PRs it had fetched earlier. At 21:40:26 it still saw #358 as conflicted, so it sent #102 back and rebuilt it from scratch. That meant three build rounds, a hidden Approve button on #358, and an Electron screenshot launch every round. #102 also has `hold`, which the pipeline ignored.

**What changes for you:**
- **One scan at a time.** A scan that finds another one still running now skips and logs "Skipped" in Activity. Previously it gave up waiting after 120 s and ran anyway, and five scans were overlapping.
- **No send-back on stale information.** Just before sending a ticket back, the pipeline re-reads that PR from GitHub. It only sends the ticket back if the head commit is the same one the scan listed and the PR still conflicts or still fails its checks. If gh errors or GitHub's mergeability is still UNKNOWN, it waits for the next scan.
- **`hold` means hold.** `hold` (and `held`) now stop both dispatch and send-back, as `pinned` already did. The send-back step was checking for `held`, a label nothing actually uses.

**Tests (10 new, adversarial):**
- A PR repaired by another scan since the list isn't sent back.
- A PR whose head moved isn't sent back, even while GitHub still says CONFLICTING.
- UNKNOWN mergeability waits.
- A recheck that errors, returns non-JSON, returns null or returns the wrong shape never sends back.
- Checks that went green since the list mean no send-back.
- A PR that still conflicts on the same commit *is* still sent back.
- hold, held and pinned are never sent back; hold and held are never dispatched.
- A busy lock reports not acquired and is free again once its holder goes away.
- main() skips the scan while another holds the lock.
- 4 concurrent mains: never more than one scan at a time.

`test_ticket_pipeline.py`: 103 passed. Whole `lib/tests`: 2017 passed. One unrelated failure was deselected: `test_portfolio_flux` needs 23 GB free and this Mac has 16 GB.

No UI change.

author: axeolotl
body:
> Stacked on #1 (`update-components`). Merge #1 first; GitHub will then retarget this PR to `master`.

Replaces the hard-coded `grafanareader` password (`'password'` in `init-db.sql` and `datasources.yml`) with `PG_GRAFANA_PASSWORD` from `config.sh`.

## Changes
- `config.sh`: new `PG_GRAFANA_PASSWORD`
- `init-db.sh` passes it to psql (`-v grafana_password=…`); `init-db.sql` creates the role only if it is missing (`\gexec`) and (re)sets the password with `ALTER ROLE … PASSWORD :'grafana_password'` on every run. This also fixes the `role "grafanareader" already exists` error when re-running `init-db.sh`.
- `datasources.yml`: `password: $__env{PG_GRAFANA_PASSWORD}`, passed into the Grafana container by `docker-compose.yml`
- Scripts source `config.sh` with `set -a`, so every variable in it is exported for docker compose and the per-script `export` lists are gone.
- `init-db.sh` rejects passwords containing `$`. Grafana's provisioning expands `$…` inside the substituted value again, which silently breaks the data source login (verified; `$$` escaping doesn't help either).

## Changing the password later
Edit `config.sh`, then run `./init-db.sh` (sets the DB password) and `./docker-up.sh` (recreates Grafana with the new environment).

## Tested
- fresh init: `init-docker.sh`, `docker-up.sh`, `init-db.sh` → `CREATE ROLE`, `ALTER ROLE`, data source health "Database Connection OK"
- re-running `init-db.sh`: no errors, role is not recreated
- password with spaces, single and double quotes → OK
- password containing `$` → `init-db.sh` aborts with a clear message
- `update-db.sh` still works

author: sathishkumarai
body:
## Why

"Improve the other charts — even the colours are not looking good." Three charts on Today, each failing a different way, none of them loudly.

## What changed

**1 · Mood. Stress. Sleep — no legend, and hue doing all the work.** Scored with the dataviz validator across all five themes: red↔green separate by **ΔE 5.8 under deuteranopia in latte, vscode and dawn** (floor 6, target 8). For three of five themes two of the three lines were the same line.

The fix is deliberately **not** a different trio — every three-accent combination these palettes can make was scored across the five themes and **none is clean**; red/green/blue is already joint best at 5.8. Below the floor the rule is secondary encoding:

- a **dash pattern** per series (solid mood · 7/4 stress · 2/3 sleep), which survives greyscale and monochrome
- a **legend**, so identity is never colour alone
- legend labels in `subtext0`, not the series colour — the swatch carries identity, the word does not
- `itemSorter` off: recharts defaults it to `'value'` and sorted them alphabetically, "Mood · Sleep · Stress"
- daily lines drop `opacity={0.35}` for `over(accent, card, 0.42)` — a faded stroke is a value no gate can check, and here the fade was the *only* thing separating a reading from its trend

**2 · The plan card's week strip was a three-bucket traffic light** (`>=99 green · >=50 yellow · >0 peach`) and a real week lands inside one bucket: the demo's 78–93 painted seven blocks in latte's `yellow` — the olive-gold this repo had to re-pick by hue to make legible at all. Now a sequential ramp: `green` mixed toward the track by the score, 40% at zero to 100% at a full day. Height stays primary, the number stays printed, and the track's `+ '80'` alpha suffix becomes a flattened token.

**3 · `SegmentScale` faded every filled segment but the chosen one** to 0.85 — a colour no gate can check, for a difference nobody can see. Height and the ring already said which is picked.

## Scope

- **Not** a palette change: no token moved, so `npm run contrast` sees the same 5 themes × 14 accents. The hues are the ones that were there.
- **Not** every chart in the app — Insights' and Trackers' other recharts surfaces are untouched; this is the three on Today that were named.
- The radar is a single series and needs no legend, so it keeps none.

## Verification

- `npm run verify` exit 0 — `tsc -b`, **1861 tests in 138 files**, build clean (the one eslint warning is pre-existing, `App.tsx`)
- `npm run design` 434 files, `npm run contrast` 5 themes / 14 accents — both pass
- Driven in a real browser against the built bundle: legend reads Mood/Stress/Sleep in order, the three `stroke-dasharray` values are distinct in the DOM, legend text computes to `rgb(95,99,104)` (the subtext token) rather than the series hue, and the week strip steps dark→light across 93/93/78/81/85/81/78
