author: officialmelon
body:
## Game controllers (all platforms)
New `src/input/` layer (marked `PAD (PC addition)` where it touches game code). Details: `docs/CONTROLLERS.md`.

- **Providers**
  - **Windows / Linux / macOS:** GLFW joysticks, with the XInput, PlayStation (DirectInput / hid-playstation) and Linux xpad layouts mapped to standard controls. Unknown pads report raw inputs, which can be bound.
  - **Android:** the activity's gamepad key and motion events (`GameInput.java` → `AndroidGamepad.cpp`). This covers any Android controller, including handheld built-in controls like the AYN Odin / Thor. Pad events are consumed before cocos2d-x, so B never turns into the system Back and the d-pad never moves Android's focus.
  - **iOS:** GCController through cocos2d-x's `Controller`.
- **Driving:** remappable bindings, three inputs per action, on the new QoL **controller** page. Driving goes through the same virtual fingers as the keyboard: the finger code moved from `PCInput` to `input/ControlBridge` so both share it.
- **Menus:** spatial focus navigation with a pulsing yellow glow on the selected button, covering every screen.
  - A presses it by injecting a touch.
  - B goes back, closes popups and resumes from pause.
  - LB / RB change chapters, the right stick scrolls, and R3 toggles a free pointer (for the level editor).
- **Rumble:** follows the game's impact, injury and explosion sounds, faded by distance (off / low / medium / high).
  - Windows uses XInput and Linux uses evdev force feedback.
  - Android uses the controller's vibrator, or the device's for built-in controls. An optional "phone vibration" setting (off by default) covers playing without a controller.
- **Tilt steering** on Android and iOS (off / low / medium / high).
- **Touch controls:** "touch controls: auto" also hides them on touch devices while a controller is connected, and the option now shows on every platform.

## Fixes
- **User-vehicle jets:** jets on browser user vehicles (jetpack levels) never fired once the parked vehicle had fallen asleep. The jet key now wakes them.
- **User-vehicle touch buttons:** touch players had no way to use a user vehicle's Shift / Ctrl actions or to eject from it. The ejected layout now shows SHIFT / CTRL / eject buttons while riding one.
- **Restored characters' extra buttons:** Helicopter Man's rope up / down and the other extra buttons were covered by the special button when it is set to the left side. They now sit above it. The helicopter rope also always has at least 2 m to let out.
- **Grouped swords:** a sword inside a group had its handle collision box at the weapon's centre (a mobile port bug), so for 7 of the 12 blade types the blade hit but the handle couldn't be grabbed. Browser levels, user levels and editor test play now place the handle where it is drawn. Campaign levels keep the original box, so parity is unchanged.

## Verification
- Linux build is clean: no errors and no warnings in the new code.
- Android and iOS native files were syntax-checked with the host compiler. `GameInput.java` was compile-checked against Android API stubs, because the SDK couldn't be downloaded here.
- **Not built here:** Windows (including the XInput rumble path), Android, iOS and macOS. The release workflow will be the first real build of those.
- **Not run in-game:** none of this was run in the game, since no game assets were available. Worth hands-on testing with real pads on each platform, especially menu navigation, rumble on Linux (needs write access to `/dev/input/event*`) and tilt direction.

author: chalidade
body:
Before: on the owner's Android Chrome, sending a chat message to an applicant in the company portal crashed the panel with `TypeError: u is not a function` (at React's `Ui`, the hook-effect cleanup runner).

After: messages send normally.

The chat scroll effect was written `useEffect(() => chatEnd.current?.scrollIntoView(...), [messages.length])`. Newer Chrome returns a Promise from `scrollIntoView`, so React stored the Promise as the effect's cleanup and called it on the next message.

How: the effect body now uses braces so it returns nothing. Other expression-bodied effects return either a function or undefined. Reproduced locally by making `scrollIntoView` return a Promise: the old build reported `u is not a function` at the same `Ui ...:48:96060` frame as the owner's screenshot, and the new build sends messages and invites without errors.

author: axeolotl
body:
> Stacked on #2 (`grafanareader-password`), which is stacked on #1. It doesn't apply cleanly without them (conflicts in `docker-compose.yml`/`README.md`), and it relies on the `set -a` export of `config.sh` variables.

Adds [Caddy](https://caddyserver.com/) 2.11.7 as a reverse proxy with automatic HTTPS for a public domain.

## Changes
- New `caddy` service publishing 80, 443 and 443/udp (HTTP/3). It gets and renews the Let's Encrypt certificate for `DASHBOARD_DOMAIN` automatically and redirects HTTP to HTTPS.
- `Caddyfile`: `reverse_proxy grafana:3000`, zstd/gzip compression, HSTS (`max-age=31536000`, deliberately without `includeSubDomains`), `Referrer-Policy`, no `Server` header
- `config.sh`: `DASHBOARD_DOMAIN`
- Grafana no longer publishes port 3000. It has `GF_SERVER_DOMAIN`/`GF_SERVER_ROOT_URL` set to the public HTTPS URL and secure cookies (`GF_SECURITY_COOKIE_SECURE`).
- Networks are split into `frontnet` (caddy ↔ grafana) and an `internal` `grafnet` (grafana ↔ postgres), so Postgres has no outside connectivity.
- Persistent `caddy-data`/`caddy-config` volumes keep the certificates across restarts (Let's Encrypt rate limits).

## Requirements
- a DNS A/AAAA record for `DASHBOARD_DOMAIN` pointing to the docker host
- ports 80/443 forwarded to the docker host

## Tested
With `DASHBOARD_DOMAIN=localhost` (Caddy then uses its internal CA; everything else is the same as for a public domain):
- `http://` → `308` redirect to `https://`
- HTTPS via HTTP/2 with `strict-transport-security`, `referrer-policy`, `alt-svc: h3` headers
- login over HTTPS sets `grafana_session` with the `Secure` flag
- data source health OK through the internal network; the dashboard renders over HTTPS
- port 3000 is no longer reachable from the host

The Let's Encrypt flow itself can only be verified on a host with a real domain.

## What

Tightens `TOKEN_ASSIGNMENT` in `tests/test_repo_hygiene.py` from `HASS_TOKEN\s*=\s*(\S+)` to `HASS_TOKEN\s*=\s*([^\s{]\S*)`, so a value opening with `{` (an f-string placeholder) is no longer treated as a token.

Improving submissions stay open until Yukon promotes them, after owner review when enabled. Other results are closed.

---

**Submitter note**

# Q770 frogdrop: clean field carry and traversal helper reuse

Model: GPT-6
Harness: Codex

The unchanged trusted evaluator reports **770 qubits, 237,167,607 average executed Toffolis, 849,121,197 physical operations**. Local Q*T is **182,619,057,390**. All **9,024 canonical shots pass**, with zero classical mismatches, phase-garbage batches and ancilla-garbage batches.

The previous submitted Q770 stream costs 274,859,498 T. This changes T by -37,691,891, a 13.71315% reduction at the same qubit count. Its submission ID is d8e2a8d4-81e5-462e-853a-e230781c6d8f; its pass and receipt remain separate. The user authorized continued optimization at Q770 and submission after each reduction of at least5% from the last sent stream, conditional on complete qualification. This note makes no global leader or official acceptance claim.

## Field product with one actual clean flag

The parked product now consumes five multiplier bits. Its live partition is255 inverse lanes,251 preserved multiplier lanes,256 output lanes, one clean carry flag and seven resident counter bits:770 total. The extra consumed bit funds the clean flag; nothing is discarded. The caller allocates that flag explicitly and releases it only after the complete recorded product, sign handling and, in division2, inverse replay.

A zero-extended TTK addition computes raw target plus source and captures the full256-bit overflow directly. Two paid hooks use the original target high bit and the two low-ripple carry terms; the target high bit is updated only after both hooks. The source and arbitrary borrowed helpers are restored. The clean flag then toggles by the raw target's high-modulus interval. These two conditions are disjoint on canonical inputs and exactly identify modular reduction. Conditional addition of C=2^32+977 produces a canonical residue; comparing the final residue with the source erases the flag. The corresponding unconditional circuit removes only the external enable. Public constant addition uses the same paid raw-overflow, reduction and cleanup identities. Controlled source addition costs9,762 T and unconditional addition8,973 T.

Exact doubling and halving use the clean flag differently. For a small constant, trailing zeros are stripped and the remaining target is split at the constant's highest bit. A short comparison computes the low-word carry, the low constant is added, and one full upper-word increment consumes that carry. A comparison of the resulting low word erases the flag. This identity holds on every raw target bitstring, either enable and arbitrary borrowed data. It replaces several full-width signed increments without truncating carries. The doubling selector also shares its high-zero prefix through the actual clean flag. Complete canonical doubling costs4,495 T; halving is its recorded physical inverse, including inverse wire relabeling.

The five-bit seed uses31 canonical transpositions, followed by534 constant transpositions derived from316 structural source exceptions. All entries and their order are retained. body:
## What

- `CHANGELOG-CURRENT.md`: adds the missing entry for the autonomous shift wake build — problem, root cause, change, validation and the 2026-10-10 hardware result.
- `.github/workflows/changelog-gate.yml` (new): runs the same changelog rule on pull requests. Read-only, publishes nothing.
- `.github/workflows/classroom-studio-current.yml`: adds the active branch to the push list so the Windows build/package/release path actually runs for the current chain.
- `README.md`: names the active hardware branch the workflows point at.

## Why

PR #20 changes `firmware/abvm/**` and `tools/wake-test/**`, but the repository contract ("a build-affecting push must update `CHANGELOG-CURRENT.md`") is only enforced by `classroom-studio-current.yml`, whose push trigger lists branch names that the current chain no longer uses. Only two workflows run on PRs today (`AutoCycle integration validation`, `Sensitive artifact guard`), and neither checks the changelog — so the newest hardware work is documented nowhere in the single source of build truth.

## Validation

- The gate reuses the release workflow's release-relevant path list, extended with `firmware/abvm/**` and `portable/plan3/CIRCUITPY-SPLIT/**`, because the Native runtime is what ships.
- The changelog entry records what the log proves: schedule armed from the flashed program, pulse at 00:04:44 through the inside-lead fallback, host resumed on the Pico's own remote wake-up, three Enters cleared the lock screen with no stall and no Arduino fallback, the authored round started and `CYCLE` armed for 7474 s, and `EVT|WAKE|rearm|skipped|reason=inside-lead` naming the consumed-deadline handback.
- The entry states the open items honestly: the two real shift windows (18:30 / 04:30) and the reset-while-asleep recovery pulse are still unverified on hardware.

author: axeolotl
body:
> Stacked on #3 (`caddy-https`) → #2 → #1. It conflicts in `docker-compose.yml` without them.

Creates a read-only Grafana user with name and password from `config.sh`, e.g. for kiosk mode.

Grafana has no file-based user provisioning, so this adds a one-shot compose service `grafana-users`. It uses the same Grafana image (shared through a YAML anchor), runs `grafana-users.sh` against the HTTP API, and starts automatically on every `./docker-up.sh` once Grafana reports healthy.

## Behaviour
- `GRAFANA_VIEWER_USER` missing → user is created with `GRAFANA_VIEWER_PASSWORD`
- user exists → the password is only reset if the configured one no longer works, so existing viewer sessions are not interrupted on every `up`
- the role "Viewer" in the main org is always enforced
- `GRAFANA_VIEWER_USER` empty → skipped
- the viewer user name must differ from the admin user
- admin login fails (`GRAFANA_ADMIN_PASSWORD` only applies on Grafana's first start) → exits 1 with a hint

Grafana gets a healthcheck (`/api/health`, `start_interval: 2s`), which the job depends on via `condition: service_healthy`.

## Tested
- first `up`: user created, role Viewer; the viewer can read the dashboard (200) but can't save dashboards (403)
- second `up`: "password unchanged"
- changed password containing spaces, quotes, backslashes and `$` → updated; the new password works, the old one is rejected
- empty `GRAFANA_VIEWER_USER` → skipped
- wrong admin password → clear error, exit code 1
- `docker-down.sh` + `docker-up.sh` → unchanged, data source still OK

author: ruthwikdasyam
body:
## What is this feature?

Stacked on #4490 (top of the stack: #4503 → #4504 → #4490 → this). Runs the LIBERO-PRO suite with dimos's xArm7 in the Panda's place, built and run by LIBERO just like the Panda.

- **`LiberoSim(robot="XArm7")`**: registers the xArm7 MJCF as a LIBERO robot (`MountedXArm7` / `OnTheGroundXArm7`), so LIBERO builds the BDDL scene with it. Its position servos take the coordinator's joint targets directly.
- **Native server**: the Panda and xArm specifics are two small robot classes (`Panda`, `XArm7`) behind one interface: arm/gripper commands, gripper readback, camera, base frame.
- **`xarm-libero-sim`**: the same stack as `panda-libero-sim` with the xArm sim's planning model; both are built from one shared helper.
- **`dimos.evals.suites.libero_pro_xarm`**: the same 647 cases and tags, run with `xarm-libero-sim`.

### Making the xArm a LIBERO robot

robosuite 1.4 doesn't merge a robot's `<default>` classes, so `xarm_robot.py` flattens the MJCF. It:
- resolves the default classes and makes mesh paths absolute
- adds explicit `limited` flags, named geoms and meshes, and a `right_hand` body
- keeps `compiler angle=radian`
- zeroes the 0.12 m pedestal on `link_base`

A test checks the flattened model's dynamics (joints, actuators, geoms) equal the original's. robosuite's green recolor is undone after init.

### Placing the xArm

LIBERO lays out each scene for the Panda, which reaches ~0.85 m; the xArm7 reaches ~0.70 m.
- **At the Panda's spot**, 14 of 27 sampled tasks put a goal object beyond 0.68 m.
- **Moved forward**, `XArm7` stands `base_forward_m=0.15` m closer, in LIBERO's per-robot `base_xpos_offset`, so no scene is edited. All goal objects are then within 0.68 m.
- **Mount**: at that position the Panda's pedestal clips LIBERO-Spatial's stove knob, so the mount is a collision-free copy of it.
- **Frame**: poses are published in a frame that puts `link_base` at (0, 0, 0.12), so the stock xArm sim planning config works unchanged.

### Fidelity notes

- **Initial layouts** are sampled by LIBERO with `seed`: the recorded initial states are Panda states.
- **Not comparable** to the Panda suite or to published LIBERO numbers: robot, reach and start states differ.

## Why do we need this?

The xArm is the arm dimos already runs in sim and on hardware, so this measures that stack on LIBERO-PRO's scenes and perturbations.

## How to Test

```bash
dimos evals run dimos.evals.suites.libero_pro_xarm --agent dimos.evals.agents.pi --tags libero_goal
LIBEROSIM__BDDL=~/.cache/dimos/libero-pro/libero/libero/bddl_files/libero_goal/put_the_cream_cheese_in_the_bowl.bddl \
  dimos run xarm-libero-sim mcp-server observe-skill
```

Verified locally:
- **Positive task**: `libero_goal.put_the_cream_cheese_in_the_bowl` passes through `dimos evals run` (score 1.00) with a scripted MCP-skills agent; LIBERO's `task_status` flips to `success: true`.
- **Earlier on this design**: physics at a real-time factor of 1.00; living room, study, table + mug, `temp_x0.3` and `spatial_task` cases launch and grade with no errors; an idle agent scores 0.00.
- **Unit tests**: MJCF flattening preserves the xArm's dynamics (`self_hosted`: needs the xarm7 LFS asset); xArm gripper mapping; native files stay dimos-free.

## Which issue(s) does this PR close?

None.

## Checklist

- [ ] I have read and approved the [CLA](https://github.com/dimensionalOS/dimos/blob/main/CLA.md).

## Что было
Если `settings.json` не читается, писатель отказывал в патчах, но экран «Настройки» отправлял полный снимок с дефолтами (`Replace`). Первая же правка перезаписывала битый файл, и его содержимое пропадало.

## Что стало
- Перед первой записью в нечитаемый файл писатель сохраняет его побайтную копию `settings.json.broken-<мс>` рядом. Если копия с тем же содержимым уже есть, новая не создаётся. Если копию создать не удалось, запись не выполняется.
- Уведомление на экране «Настройки»: «Файл настроек не прочитан: {0}. При следующей записи он будет сохранён копией рядом.» Текст добавлен в `tools/i18n-extra.json` на все 15 языков, `strings.rs` перегенерирован.
- Тест `unreadable_settings_are_copied_before_the_first_write` заменяет старый `corrupt_settings_are_preserved_until_explicit_replacement`: старый тест ожидал отказ на патч, а новое требование — сохранить копию и записать. Тест проверяет: одна копия, она равна исходному битому файлу, после двух патчей файл валиден.

## Оставшееся
- Уведомление при запуске в `shell.rs` (`Shell::build`) по-прежнему говорит «settings.json is unchanged». Это вне разрешённых файлов; нужна правка текста там.

body:
## 需求变更 根据产品负责人的新需求，将固定的默认宽度改为响应式的视口比例宽度，让首次使用的用户在不同屏幕尺寸下都能获得更好的体验。 ## 实现方案 ### 1. 响应式默认宽度 **首次用户（无存储偏好）**：根据视口宽度动态计算 - 计算公式：`约 34% 的视口宽度`，限制在 `[420px, 600px]` 范围内 - 额外约束：确保剩余编辑器区域 ≥ 720px - 如果不满足，则使用 `视口宽度 - 720px`，但不低于绝对最小值 360px **已调整宽度的用户**：继续使用存储的偏好宽度 - 窗口调整大小时，自动限制在当前允许的范围内 - 存储键升级到 `v2`：所有现有用户都会获得一次新的默认宽度 ### 2. 不同视口的默认宽度对比 | 视口宽度 | 侧边栏宽度 | 剩余编辑器区域 | 占比 / 说明 | |---------|-----------|---------------|-----------| | 1280px | 435px | 845px | 34.0% 视口 | | 1366px | 464px | 902px | 34.0% 视口 | | 1440px | 490px | 950px | 34.0% 视口 | | 1536px | 522px | 1014px | 34.0% 视口 | | 1920px | 600px | 1320px | 最大宽度限制 | | 2560px | 600px | 1960px | 最大宽度限制 | **对比修改前**： - 修改前：所有视口统一 480px（在小屏上显得过窄，在大屏上未充分利用空间） - 修改后：根据视口动态调整，小屏更宽松，大屏更充分利用空间 ### 3. SSR/Hydration 无闪烁 为避免服务端渲染和客户端 hydration 之间的视觉跳变： - **服务端渲染**：使用 CSS `clamp()` 表达式设置初始宽度 - **客户端 hydration**：JavaScript 计算精确值后无缝更新 - **用户体验**：页面加载过程中侧边栏宽度平滑过渡，无闪烁 CSS 表达式： ```css clamp(420px, 34vw, min(600px, calc(100% - 720px))) ``` ### 4. 拖拽调整和持久化 - **拖拽调整**：保持原有功能，用户可以自由调整宽度 - **宽度持久化**：用户调整后的宽度存储到 localStorage - **加载时恢复**：优先使用存储的宽度，限制在当前允许的范围内 - **窗口调整**：视口变化时，动态重新计算最大允许宽度并约束当前宽度 ### 5. 存储键升级 - **旧版 (v1)**：`resume-editor-sidebar-width-v1` - **新版 (v2)**：`resume-editor-sidebar-width-v2` 升级原因：让所有现有用户体验一次新的响应式默认宽度，而不是继续使用旧的 480px 固定值。 ## 技术实现 ### 代码改动摘要 ```typescript // 核心计算函数 function computeResponsiveDefault(availableWidth: number): number { // 1. 计算 34% 视口宽度 const responsiveWidth = Math.round(availableWidth * 0.34) // 2. 限制在 [420, 600]px 范围 let defaultWidth = Math.max(420, Math.min(600, responsiveWidth)) // 3. 确保剩余区域 ≥ 720px if (availableWidth - defaultWidth < 720) { defaultWidth = availableWidth - 720 // 但不低于绝对最小值 if (defaultWidth < 360) defaultWidth = 360 } return Math.round(defaultWidth) } ``` ### SSR 友好的初始渲染 ```typescript // 使用 CSS clamp 避免 hydration 闪烁 const cssWidth = computedWidth !== null ? `${computedWidth}px` : `clamp(420px, 34vw, min(600px, calc(100% - 720px)))`
``` ## 测试验证 - ✅ **TypeScript 类型检查通过** - ✅ **ESLint 检查通过**（仅 1 个无关文件的警告） - ✅ **编译成功**：`✓ Compiled successfully in 16.3s` - ✅ **单元测试更新**：所有测试用例已更新为响应式逻辑 - ✅ **最小改动**：仅修改 2 个文件，与 PR #7 无冲突 ## 文件变更 ``` src/ui/resizable-editor-sidebar.test.tsx | 69 +++++++++++++------- src/ui/resizable-editor-sidebar.tsx | 104 ++++++++++++++++++++++-------- 2 files changed, 123 insertions(+), 50 deletions(-) ``` ## 优势与影响 ### ✅ 优势 1. **更好的首次体验**：首次用户在不同屏幕上都能获得合适的侧边栏宽度 2. **充分利用空间**：大屏幕上侧边栏更宽，小屏幕上保持合理比例 3. **保护编辑器区域**：始终确保至少 720px 的编辑+预览空间 4. **无缝 SSR**：CSS clamp 确保无 hydration 闪烁 5. **向后兼容**：已调整宽度的用户继续使用其偏好 ### 📊 影响范围 - **首次用户**：✅ 获得响应式默认宽度 - **已存储 v1 宽度的用户**：✅ 首次加载时使用新的响应式默认（因为存储键升级） - **已调整宽度的用户（v2 后）**：✅ 继续使用存储的宽度 - **拖拽调整功能**：✅ 完全保留，体验不变 ## 与其他 PR 的兼容性 - ✅ 不涉及 `ResumeEditor.tsx`，与 PR #7（自动保存）无冲突 - ✅ 仅修改 `resizable-editor-sidebar.tsx` 的内部逻辑 - ✅ 更新了配套的单元测试

Unidad funcional acotada: asociación explícita, revocable e histórica de propiedad GSC o GA4 a un proyecto Rubik y su conexión OpenSEO. Permite el caso dominio rastreado .com / GSC .es sin inferir equivalencia entre TLD. No modifica la vía existente webmaster_properties de GSC/Bing ni resultados firmados antiguos.

La migración privada 20261010160000 añade RPC owner-only, vínculo compuesto a la conexión, RLS sin acceso directo, identidad inmutable y pruebas negativas entre organizaciones/proyectos. El resolvedor server-only exige conexión y propiedad ACTIVE con el mismo connectionId; no usa IDs libres del navegador ni depende del modo de rastreo legacy/project. OWNER_DECLARED no significa verificación del proveedor.

Validación local: npm run verify (319 pruebas, lint, tipos, build, pin, secretos); Supabase local desechable aislado: 13 suites pgTAP, 373 pruebas verdes, tipos generados comparados. La instancia local habitual tenía datos y no se reseteó. CI del SHA f0134ae pendiente.

La migración NO se ha aplicado en Supabase alojado. Ninguna propiedad/conexión real de Sarah creada. Sin consulta Google, consumo, secretos, UI ni flags activados. Fusionar main dispara despliegue Vercel, pero este código no consulta proveedores al cargar; la función nueva sigue sin callers de producción. La aplicación alojada de la migración exige autorización concreta y revisar el orden con las migraciones pendientes de presupuesto.

Siguiente corte: consulta manual GSC rendimiento / GA4 organic_landing_pages con fuente resuelta en servidor, revalidación de permisos y conexión al guardar, resultado firmado, captura idempotente, historial y exportación. author: edgartolentino
body:
## Qué cambia

El recorrido H2 y el README piden el video desde la web. `.env.example` deja de bloquear el acceso, `make up` espera a la base y el criterio de `cuadros_confirmados` pasa a ser una cota correcta.

Refs #163

## Por qué

El sábado Miguel va a seguir el recorrido en su portátil **solo con el README** (#163). El recorrido describía la carpeta vigilada y no lo que entró en #154–#162. Al revisarlo aparecieron cuatro cosas que lo habrían hecho fallar:

| Problema | Efecto | Arreglo |
|---|---|---|
| `GEPP_API_TOKENS=` vacía en `.env.example` | Con `cp .env.example .env`, **nadie entra (401)** | Va comentada, con la explicación |
| `make up` volvía antes de que PostgreSQL estuviera sano | `make migrar` podía fallar | `up -d --wait` |
| Pasar del guion falso a ONNX en la misma terminal | Seguía el detector falso | `unset GEPP_GUION_FALSO` o terminal nueva |
| `cp` del video | Cambia el mtime y, sin fecha en los metadatos, corre la hora de los hallazgos (ADR-005) | `cp -p` |

**Criterio de cuadros (#33, #163).** «`cuadros_confirmados ≈ duracion_s × 5`» estaba mal escrito. El agregador cuenta solo los cuadros **con incumplimiento**, la regla tolera huecos menores que `cierre_segundos` (que suman duración, no cuadros) y el muestreador elige un cuadro por tic, con intervalos irregulares. Lo que vale siempre es **`1 ≤ cuadros_confirmados < fps × duracion_s + 2`**, con `fps = GEPP_FPS_OBJETIVO`. Se corrige la descripción del contrato (solo texto) y los dos tests que usaban `|cuadros − 5d| ≤ 5`. Los registros históricos (la bitácora del 22-09 y las evidencias) no se reescriben.

## Cómo lo verificaste

```
$ make lint tipos test        # sobre 2110343
All checks passed!
176 files already formatted
Success: no issues found in 93 source files
=========== 1242 passed, 1 skipped, 7 warnings in 148.59s (0:02:28) ============
$ make contrato               # sobre 3bc88e6
Contrato cumplido: 23 operaciones
$ make contrato-lint          → 2 warnings (los mismos que en main)
$ npm run typecheck && npx vitest run   (apps/web)  → OK · 337 passed
$ make up                     → «Container guardian-epp-postgres-1 Healthy» (espera, --wait)
```

- **`GEPP_API_TOKENS`:** se ejecutó `_tokens_desde_entorno`. Con `""` da **0 tokens**, sin la variable da **3** y con `x=y@z` da 1.
- **La cota:** se probó con el muestreador real (`muestreo.pasa`) en 14 fps de origen (de 5 a 60, incluidos 23,976 y 29,97) y objetivos de 2, 5 y 10, en todas las ventanas sin huecos. Hubo **0 violaciones** de `N < fps·d + 2`, con un exceso máximo de 1,667. En la base local (91 hallazgos reales a 5 fps), 0 violaciones.
- **Tests de la cota:** con defectos inyectados (el agregador cuenta doble; la API suma 3 cuadros) caen los dos tests. Con el test viejo (`≤ 5`), «suma 3» pasaba.
- **Recorrido:** Lucca comprobó cada texto, comando y variable en el código (archivo:línea). Lo que no se pudo comprobar sin levantar la app quedó dicho: los tres comandos tal cual en otro portátil y los hallazgos exactos con `generativa.mp4`. Eso es justamente la prueba del sábado.

## Correcciones de la revisión

Revisión externa de Codex (`gpt-6-astra`, esfuerzo `max`): 6 hallazgos, todos corregidos en `3bc88e6`.

| # | Hallazgo | Corrección |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | La cota `≤ round(5d)+1` no vale con otro fps ni con un origen de 8 fps | Cota `< fps·d + 2`, comprobada con el muestreador real |
| 2 | `GEPP_GUION_FALSO` queda exportada al cambiar a ONNX | `unset` o terminal nueva |
| 3 | `make demo-apagar` no apaga `make demo-api` | Cómo se apaga cada cosa |
| 4 | `cp` cambia el mtime | `cp -p` y por qué |
| 5 | `make up` no espera a PostgreSQL (PLAUSIBLE) | `--wait`, probado |
| 6 | Con 8 s de video no se alcanza a ver el avance ni la vista en vivo (PLAUSIBLE) | Se dice y se recomienda un video de un par de minutos |

## Lista de control

- [x] Las pruebas pasan en local (`make test`)
- [x] Añadí o actualicé pruebas para este cambio
- [x] No subí videos, pesos de modelo, datasets ni datos personales
- [x] Si cambié el contrato de la API, actualicé `docs/arquitectura/` y avisé al equipo web: solo la descripción de `cuadros_confirmados`, sin cambio de esquema
- [x] Si es un cambio de modelo, registré las métricas en el issue del experimento: no aplica

## Capturas / evidencia

La prueba real es la de Miguel el sábado, siguiendo este README.

Redactado por Claude Code (Opus 5.5) y Lucca.

body:
## Problema

O `.exe` e o `.msi` do Windows nunca funcionaram, e o CI deixava passar: só testava o ZIP portátil.

- O job "Windows" do `desktop-release.yml` compilava o cliente **WPF legado** e o `package.ps1` gravava-o com os nomes do Electron; o upload com `--clobber` substituía o app a sério. Verificado nos ficheiros publicados: o `MUFUTU-Setup-1.0.49-x64.exe` é um bootstrapper WiX Burn.
- O app Electron, mesmo quando instalado, morria em Program Files (corrigido no repo `mufutu`, PR #35).

## O que muda

- **Instalador web** `MUFUTU-Web-Setup-<v>.exe` (0,60 MiB, medido) que descarrega o payload com SHA-512. Completo, MSI e ZIP mantêm-se (execução separada do builder).
- **`win-electron-build.yml`** (reutilizável, usado pelos dois pipelines) com smoke em 4 variantes: `web-offline`, `web-download` (stub de CI + servidor local com Range), `nsis-full`, `msi` — todas com a pasta de instalação **só-de-leitura** (icacls + escrita de canário), limite de tempo por instalador (caixas sem `/SD` penduram o modo silencioso), registo em "Aplicações", servidor como filho do `MUFUTU.exe`, portas só em loopback, stub ≤ 10 MB.
- **`publish-release.sh`**: conjunto Windows = stub + payload + `latest.yml` + completo + MSI; recusa Setup que não seja NSIS, stub > 10 MB, nome de payload que o GitHub renomeia, e `latest.yml` incoerente com o payload.
- **`desktop-electron-win.yml`**: publicação manual guardada (`publish: true` só a partir de `main`, com `mufutu_ref` fixo e versão explícita).
- `desktop-win.yml` (WPF legado) publica numa release própria `desktop-win/v*`, com prefixo `MUFUTU-WPF-`.
- Docs do Windows.

`README.md` e `releases/latest.json` ficam para **depois** da release existir: os clientes leem o `latest.json` de `main` e um `latestVersion` sem assets é um 404.

## Testado

Guardrails de publicação com os ficheiros reais do electron-builder e casos de recusa (WiX, stub 11 MB, hash adulterado, sem `packages`, MSI em falta); servidor Range (206, retoma, 404, sem path traversal); YAML de todos os workflows.

**Não testado**: a execução dos instaladores num runner Windows — é precisamente o que este PR passa a fazer no CI.

author: barreyo
body:
## What
Verification code emails (\`account_setup_verification\`) now carry an \`OTP-Token\` header per [draft-goto-otp-token-01](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/draft-goto-otp-token/01/):

\`\`\`
OTP-Token: "123456"; origin="https://ysc.org"
\`\`\`

- New \`YscWeb.Emails.OtpToken\` builds the RFC 9651 Structured Field String with an \`origin\` parameter.
- \`Notifier.send_email_idempotent/8\` attaches it for the verification template only.

## Why
Lets mail clients and autofill extract the code and deliver it only to the origin it is bound to, reducing friction and manual-entry phishing.

## Notes for reviewers
- Origin comes from \`YscWeb.Endpoint.url()\`. Per the draft it must be canonical (lowercase, default port omitted, ASCII) and potentially trustworthy (https, or http on loopback). If not, or if the code isn't printable ASCII, the header is omitted and the email is sent as before.
- The header is rebuilt from the job's params on each send, so nothing is added to Oban job args.
- \`change_email\` is untouched; it sends a link, not a code.
- The draft is an individual I-D and may change (including the header name); the logic is isolated in one module.
- Nothing consumes the header yet, so there is no user-visible change today.

## Testing
- New \`test/ysc_web/emails/otp_token_test.exs\` (format, origin validation, escaping, delivery path, other templates unaffected).
- Existing email and verification-code suites pass (683 tests); compile with warnings-as-errors and Credo are clean.

author: rjrodger
body:
P2.7 of the any-to-any translation (tabnas/admin `notes/2026-10-09-any-to-any-translation-implementation.md`), made as the phase 2 brief (`notes/2026-10-09-phase2-common-brief.md`) describes it. ADR-27: what ZON cannot carry is written by a declared convention with a reverse, and the render never writes a document its own reader refuses. After this change the render refuses nothing but event streams no tree has.

Three commits:

- db14cae: `translate.root` is `any`; the first conventions; the `embed` field.
- 13eafd2: an injective convention for field names.
- 867d6a1: `$big` is the reader's integer only when it is a canonical one (the Codex review thread).

## The conventions

### Field names

ZON has no field name for the empty string. Zig's `@"..."` identifiers refuse a null byte: zig 0.16.0's `ZonGen.appendIdentStr` refuses a null byte and the empty identifier and nothing else, and the reader refuses the same two. And the reader's big integer takes the name `$big`. So every field name is written by a convention that keeps names apart:

| A name | is written as |
|---|---|
| the empty name | `$empty` |
| a name holding U+0000 | `$json:` followed by the name's double-quoted JSON form (alchemy's `quoted`), which holds no U+0000 |
| a name that begins with `$` | the name with one more `$` in front: `$empty` as `$$empty`, `$big` as `$$big`, `$json:x` as `$$json:x` |
| any other name | as it is |

The reverse, which the manifest's loss list states: `$empty` is the empty name; `$json:` followed by a text is the string the text spells (alchemy's `unquoted`); `$$` followed by a rest is `$` followed by the rest; any other name is as it is. The four rules write disjoint sets of names (`$empty` itself, names beginning `$json:` and a quote, names beginning `$$`, and names that do not begin with `$`), and each rule keeps its names apart, so no two names are written as one field.

Before, an object holding both `""` and `"$empty"`, or two names that differ only by U+0000 against U+FFFD, was written with one field twice, which ZON refuses. The U+FFFD replacement is gone.

In the render, `zon-field` writes the convention. `zon-dollar` adds the `$` on the name's JSON form, after a sentinel (U+0002, which `quoted` never leaves raw) that marks where the form begins, so an escaped quote followed by a `$` inside a name is never taken for the name's start.

### `$big`

An object whose only member is `$big`, holding an integer as the reader spells one, is written as that integer, the reader's own form. Such a value is a string of `0` to `9` and `-` alone (`chars-within`) that alchemy's `number` reads (`is-number`), so a minus sign at most and first and no leading zero, and not `-0`, which ZON refuses as an ambiguous negative zero. The test is made on the name as it is, before the name convention escapes it.

Any other object with a `$big` member is written as a struct whose field is `$$big`. So `{"$big": "1-2"}`, `"01"`, `"-0"` and `"-"`, which were written unquoted as integers ZON refuses, are now structs, and read back through the reverse as the objects they were.

### The rest, from db14cae

- Strings are written with Zig's escapes. U+FFFE and U+FFFF, which `quoted` escapes in a JSON form Zig does not read, are written with Zig's braced escape: a backslash, the letter u, and the code point in braces.
- `translate.root` is `any`, since a ZON document's root may be any value.
- Every failure for events no tree has is `(fail :protocol-order ...)`, PROTOCOL_ORDER_ERROR; no other failure is left.
- The structural interface's `embed` field, absent for ZON, in all three runtimes, as tabnas/toml#108 has it. `ts/embed-translate.js` handles `embed` as it handles `lift`, and each runtime's drift test holds an embed to its file and checks the field absent where the manifest names none.

## Tests

- `test/spec/render.tsv`, which all three runtimes run (and the Rust fixture census lists): the documents the render writes, and the value every reader reads back, for both `""` and `"$empty"` in one object; `"$$x"`; a NUL in a name; `"$json:x"`; U+0000 beside U+FFFD; a NUL name beside its own `$json:` spelling; the `$` names; the conventions nested; `{"$big": "1-2"}`, `"01"`, `"-0"` and `"-"`; small canonical integers beside a `$big` struct.
- A big integer has no JSON spelling a fixture can hold, so each runtime's translation test (`rs/tests/translate_test.rs`, `ts/test/translate.test.ts`, `go/translate_test.go`) reads the document the render writes for `{"$big": "-123456789012345678901234567890"}`, at the root and nested, back as its own big integer.

## Validation

- **Writer:** `/root/bin/alchemy-a2a run` over `render.alc` linked with `def export [input] (zon-render input)`.
- **Read-back, two readers:** `aless -k zon --json --compact` (aless 0.1.1) and zig 0.16.0's own ZON parser, the oracle this repository pins. The declared reverse is applied to each value read back, which is then compared with the input exactly: names reversed, an empty object read as an empty array, and numbers as doubles except an integer no double holds exactly, which both readers keep exactly.
- **134 documents:** 39 generated ones and the 95 JSONTestSuite `y_*.json` files of tabnas/jsonc (the two with a repeated key as the last-wins value a host hands the render). The generated ones hold every control character, U+007F to U+009F, U+00A0, U+2028, U+2029, U+FEFF, U+FFFD, U+FFFE, U+FFFF and astral characters, in values and in names; the empty name, NUL names and `$` names alone, together, nested and long; each name beside the convention's spelling of another; look-alike names; every `$big` shape, canonical or not; number lexemes, among them integers no double holds; empty and nested containers; and roots of every kind.

The `alchemy-a2a` binary predates alchemy's `is-number`, so the validation program defined a stand-in `is-number` that answers as `number` does for every `$big` string the inputs hold and fails on any other; every byte written comes from the render.

author: enriqueagv
body:
Before: every doctor had to install an authenticator app, scan a QR code and type a rotating code each time they signed in.

After: the first time a doctor, clinic manager or super-admin signs in on a new computer or phone, they see "Confirma este dispositivo". They tap "Enviarme el código", get a code by email and type it in. That browser is then remembered and doesn't ask again. In Equipo, "Olvidar dispositivos" makes all of someone's devices ask again, for example when a phone is lost. Assistants who don't manage the clinic are never asked.

How:
- `/auth/device` sends the code with Supabase's email OTP (`signInWithOtp`, without creating users) and checks it with `verifyOtp`, which must return the same user.
- On success, the browser gets a random 32-byte token in an httpOnly cookie that lasts 400 days. Only the token's SHA-256 is stored, in the new `trusted_devices` table (migration `0008`).
- `requireBusinessAccess` and `requireSuperAdmin` check the cookie at most once per request, using `needsDeviceCode()` in `src/lib/permissions.ts`.
- The TOTP page (`/auth/mfa`) and the assurance-level check are removed.

**Supabase setup needed:** under Authentication → Emails → Magic Link, the template must include `{{ .Token }}` so the email shows the code. Supabase's built-in email sender only allows a few emails per hour. With more than a couple of doctors, set up custom SMTP (Authentication → Emails → SMTP Settings).

Checks: `tsc`, `eslint`, `vitest` (80 tests, including trusted devices and who gets asked) and `next build` all pass locally.

body:
Nodes epic, phase P1 (v0.5.32): node identity and card (#133) and one naming scheme (#137). The four open decisions are built on the recommended, reversible defaults (#132 mixed, #145 links, #146 sub-issues, #156 not built); see the epic #131.

**#133 identity and card**
- `app/nodes.py`:
  - `node_id()` is the Tailscale StableNodeID (`ts:...`), else a random `n_...` kept in `<data dir>/node-id` (0600). It is never derived from the host name.
  - Display name, URL, and the node card: agents, accounts (`supported`, `subscription_key`), load (null where `/proc` is missing), lanes. The card carries no secret, prompt, email or home path. A trapped `open` proves the credentials files are never read.
- `GET /api/node/hello` (no identity) answers exactly `{app, api, node_id}`, at 30/min per source with 429 + Retry-After. `X-Forwarded-For` is trusted only from loopback.
- `GET /api/node` (identity) returns the card, and `state.node` carries it. Every other `/api/node*` route stays 403 without identity.
- The legacy hub token still opens `/api/node/summary` (byte-identical) and is refused on `/api/node`.
- `CCBOARD_NODE_LANES` (default 3) is advisory: a hand dispatch over the cap runs and answers `lane_warning`.
- New `tasks.origin` column (JSON `{node, user}`, NULL for every local task). Doctor row `node`.
- A single board starts no thread and makes no outbound request (pinned).

**#137 naming**
- `app/static/nodes.js`: `Ref.parse/format/key/storeKey` for `#/n/<handle>/s/<tmux>`. The same tmux name on `local` and on a remote handle gives distinct keys (the collision contract). Local keys, URLs, bookmarks and push links are byte-identical.
- The router gets node route forms and a plain "not paired" page.
- shell, palette, dnd, quad and session use `Ref.key`.
- A shared accept/refuse table (`tests/fixtures/node_refs.json`) pins Python `parse_ref` and JS `Ref.parse` together.

**Verified:** full JS suite 1955, targeted Python 1181 (including migrations, auth, security surface and the single-board state contract). Sandbox board: hello answers the three keys; the "not paired" page is checked at 1280 and 390, with the button centred under the text (fixed before this PR); Agents is unchanged; no console errors.

**Before merge:** a box DB backup (the `tasks.origin` migration).

author: wlav
body:
Python will create a thread state for every thread that uses the GIL. Since TBB workers stay around for the duration of the job, preventing deletion of their Python thread state improves throughput by reducing overhead. This is especially true for Python algorithms that release the GIL as part of their execution, since they will re-acquire it on the same thread.

This PR is not the whole story, some more changes will be forthcoming, just that this particular change seems to be helpful for all relevant scenarios and doesn't appear to suffer from edge cases.

<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

- **Code:** Add per-thread Python thread-state storage with TBB’s enumerable thread-specific container. `py_gilraii` ensures a thread-local state exists before acquiring the GIL, then releases the GIL when the guard is destroyed.
- **Shutdown:** Reject GIL acquisition after the finalized flag is set. Thread-state cleanup and the routine that sets this flag are commented out; the code does not currently perform explicit cleanup.
- **Tests:** No test results were provided.

author: dbaggott
body:
Reworks www.oasis-smp.com around a Minecraft-edition-style logo, as the un-official Minecraft SMP server for the Oasis School, with a navigation bar across every page. Its infrastructure half is https://github.com/dbaggott/infrastructure/pull/145 (CSP allowance for the embedded calendar).

## Pages

- **Home (`/`):**
  - the large logo with a tilted, pulsing "Un-Official!" splash (no animation under `prefers-reduced-motion`)
  - the tagline "The Un-Official Minecraft SMP Server for the Oasis School"
  - the paragraph about free social gaming sessions supporting the Oasis educational program
  - a Minecraft stone-style "Request Access For Your Child" button
- **Play (`/play/`):** "Open Minecraft, add a server and paste the address below", then the Java and Bedrock addresses (Bedrock with port 19132), each in a card with a **Copy** button. Where the async clipboard API is missing or refused, it selects the address and copies it with `execCommand('copy')`; failing that, it leaves the address selected. Above them, a gold-edged warning that the server is only available during scheduled sessions (linking to Schedule), and that Minecraft shows it as unreachable otherwise.
- **Schedule (`/schedule/`):** the sessions live in a public Google Calendar. The page embeds its agenda view and offers **Add to Google Calendar**, a `webcal://` link to subscribe in Apple Calendar or Outlook, and the feed's address with a Copy button for any other calendar app. A subscriber's calendar re-fetches the feed, so changes flow through on their own. Everything is built from one calendar ID in `web/calendar.mjs`. **It's still empty**, and until it's set the page says "The session schedule is coming soon."
- **Contact (`/contact/`):** a message and up to three reply addresses, posted to the new `POST /api/contact`.
- **Rules (`/rules/`):** just the list, rendered at build time from `plugins/OasisRules/rules.txt`, as before.
- **Request access:** the old header and intro paragraph are gone; the shared bar replaces the header. The form changes too; see "Request form and API" below.
- **The "About" cards and the footer are removed.**

## Forms and API

- **Shared code:** both forms use one email list, error display and hashed send (`web/src/forms.js`). The API builds both routes from one helper, which checks the size, rate-limits each form separately, applies the honeypot, then stores and announces. Shared limits are in `shared/forms.js`.
- **Contact messages** are stored under `pk = MESSAGE` with the same 90-day TTL, and announced as "Oasis SMP message", with the message last.

- **Order:** about your child (name, grade), where they'll play, how to reach you, then comments.
- **No edition question.** The form always asks "Where will they play?" (Computer, Phone or tablet, Game console, the last hinted "Xbox, PlayStation, Switch"), and the edition is worked out from it (`editionOf` in `shared/`). Anything but a computer means Bedrock, and a game console marks the notification's subject "(console)". A computer alone is reported in the notification as "unknown (computer only)", with a note to check the name against Mojang (Java) and Xbox (Bedrock), and to ask the parent if it exists on both.
- **The name** is labelled "Their Minecraft name (needed to add them to the allowed list)". It's accepted if it's valid for either edition (`isPlayerName`).
- **An optional comments box,** up to 1,000 characters (`COMMENTS_MAX`). The API stores it with the request and puts it last in the notification, so free text can't push a fact out of place. `REQUEST_BYTES_MAX` grows to 8,000 to fit it.
- **The privacy paragraph** is replaced by "We will contact you once your kid has been added." Requests are still deleted after 90 days.
- **The API no longer takes `platform`.** The live API requires it, so this form against the live API gets a 400. **Deploy `mc-oasis-api` before `mc-oasis-site`.**

## Navigation bar

Modelled on mysticmc.co, including its layout: a `1fr auto 1fr` grid, so the logo sits at the exact centre of the page however wide the links on each side are. `Home`, `Play` and `Schedule` sit to the left of the logo, and `Rules`, `Request Access` and `Contact` to the right, all as the same kind of tile. They're dark Minecraft-style tiles, with the current page in gold. The bar is identical on every page apart from which link is marked, logo included, so moving between pages never shifts it. A build test checks that. Below 960 px, where six tiles no longer fit, it collapses to a menu button (with `aria-expanded`) and the logo, and the links open as full-width tiles. The links are hidden only once the script has run, so without JavaScript they stay visible. A skip link comes first.

The bar and the footer live once, in `web/chrome.mjs`, and a Vite plugin puts them in place of `<!-- nav -->` and `<!-- footer -->` in every page, marking the current link from the page's path.

## Art and fonts

- **`web/logo.mjs`** draws the logo and the dirt background at build time. The logo is sandstone "OASIS" over prismarine "SMP", every letter beveled, extruded and outlined in black. The build emits both as `/logo.svg` (30 KB, 5.3 KB gzipped) and `/dirt.svg`, drawn as one SVG path per colour. The home page and the bar share the same logo file. No font or image is involved, so the artwork is entirely original.
- **Monocraft** ([IdreesInc/Monocraft](https://github.com/IdreesInc/Monocraft), SIL OFL 1.1, no Mojang assets) for headings, buttons, nav and labels.
  - Subset to Latin and to WOFF2 (2.9 KB), with its programming ligatures left out.
  - No Reserved Font Name is declared.
  - Its license is published at `/licenses/Monocraft-OFL.txt`.
- **Karla stays** for paragraphs and form hints.
- **Pixelify Sans is removed.**

## Checks run

- `npm test` in `api/`: 40 pass, including the contact route (validation, honeypot, its own rate limit, notification) and including edition inference from devices, comments (kept, trimmed, length-limited, last in the notification), and names valid for either edition.
- `npm run build && npm test` in `web/`: 34 pass, including the calendar links built from an ID, and the schedule page's coming-soon state. One requires the built form script to hash the body for `x-amz-content-sha256`, not just name the header. They now check, for every page, that the shared bar and footer are in place with exactly the right link marked as current, and that the bar is the same on every page. They also cover the shared logo file, the dirt tile, the font license and the rules on `/rules/`.
- **Headless Chrome** at 320, 390, 800, 900, 960, 961, 1024 and 1280 px on all seven pages:
  - no horizontal scroll and no console errors
  - the phone menu opens
  - both forms submit against a local API, and the `x-amz-content-sha256` each sends matches its posted body
  - not seen yet: the embedded calendar, which needs a real calendar ID
  - Copy puts `mc.oasis-smp.com` on the clipboard (through the `execCommand` path, since headless Chrome refuses the async API)
  - with JavaScript off on a phone, all four nav links are visible
  - every nav link, the logo and the menu button sit at the same position on all five pages, at 1280 and 390 px
  - the logo's centre is the page's centre at 1280, 900 and 390 px
- **Contrast,** computed per WCAG: button text 5.33:1 at rest and 5.98:1 on hover, rule badges 5.75:1, muted text 7.18:1, links 6.59:1.

body:
## Summary

Phase P11 connects the app to a microscope:

- by default, the server that served the page;
- otherwise, another microscope by its address, from a new **Connect** screen or `?microscope=` in the page's address.

A connection store holds the WoT client, the Things' descriptions and the host name, so the rest of the app doesn't need to know where the server is. It checks every 5 s that the server is still there, covers the page with an offline notice when it isn't, and reconnects when it's back. Tabs show only when the server has the Things they need. This PR also marks P10 Done.

- Phase spec: [docs/milestone-1/phases.md#p11](https://github.com/lucaswewa/microscope/blob/main/docs/milestone-1/phases.md#p11)
- Implementation notes: `docs/milestone-1/notes/P11-connection.md`
- ADRs: ADR-0015 (Connection model)

**A suggested reading order** (1,111 lines, 476 of them tests):

1. ADR-0015.
2. `web/src/connection/profiles.ts` and `store.ts`, with `tests/unit/connection/profiles.spec.ts` and `store.spec.ts`.
3. `ConnectView.vue`, `ConnectionIndicator.vue` and `OfflineOverlay.vue`, with `ui.spec.ts`.
4. The wiring: `main.ts`, `AppShell.vue`, `NavRail.vue`, `router/index.ts`.
5. The end-to-end changes: `playwright.config.ts` (it now starts a server), `tests/e2e/connection.spec.ts`, the updated smoke and shell tests, and the new baselines.

**Worth knowing:**

- **Connecting hides Slide Scan, Sequence and Gallery for now,** because today's server has only the `system` Thing. That's as planned: they return with their Things.
- **`npm run test:e2e` now builds and starts a server from the checkout,** on ports 5098 and 5099, so the first run takes a minute or so.
- **The visual baselines changed on purpose:** they show the connected rail, with the machine-specific host name masked. The old ones still passed, because the change was under the 1% pixel tolerance, so I replaced them deliberately.
- **Measured in Chromium:** a stopped server was noticed after 5.3 s, and its return 0.8 s after the restart.

## How to try it

```powershell
cargo run -p microscope-server -- -c configs/simulation.json --port 5001
cd web
npm run dev
```

1. Open <http://localhost:5173/?microscope=localhost:5001#/view>. The rail shows the host name, and the window title is "<host> – Microscope".
2. Stop the server. Within about 5 s, "Connection lost" covers the page.
3. Start the server again. The app reconnects by itself, or at once with Retry.
4. Click the indicator for the Connect screen: try a bad address, connect by address, and see it under Recent.

- [x] The scope matches the phase spec; any deviation is explained in the notes.
- [x] CI is green.
- [x] Tests cover the new behaviour. There are 22 new unit tests (256 in all), a new end-to-end reconnect test, and all 15 end-to-end and visual tests pass.

body:
Studio half of studio#403 (wave 4, set ST-1). After a refused hand-over the engine parks at an `escalation` gate on the deliver unit, with the prompt "The deliver phase refused: <script output>. Approve to re-run the deliver phase now …, reject to cancel the run and keep the worktree." (wicked-core `actor.rs`).

**Found while doing it: the session thread rendered that gate not at all.** `proposalKindOf` reads it as a failure, so it is not a hand-over, and ProposalCard yields. `classifyRowGate` saw it on the deliver unit and called it the deliver card, so `sessionGateChoices` returned null and GateRow rendered nothing. I reproduced it with a model probe on main: both returned `null`.

Fix:
- `classifyRowGate` (`questionRow.ts`) now hands the deliver card exactly the gates `proposalKindOf` calls a deliver. That leaves one rule for both surfaces.
- `deliverRefusalOf` (`gateMoveModel.ts`) reads the refused hand-over. For crew's push-refusal sentence it returns the branch and the remote's message; otherwise it returns the script's own first line. The identity line (`deliver: pushing as …`) and the marker are dropped.
- The row (`gateRowModel.ts`) offers the engine's two arms: **Deliver again** (approve; it re-lifts, re-verifies and re-pushes) and **Stop** (reject). Nothing is preselected.
- `GateRow` leads with the question "The remote refused the push — deliver again or stop?", then the reason, e.g. "The remote refused the push: <hook message>. Nothing was pushed; the work is committed on <branch>." A consent line follows: "Deliver again re-pushes <branch> to <repo>: N files changed, +A, −D." The diffstat is the deliver card's own (`diffstatOf`, moved out of ProposalCard so both surfaces read the same numbers). The raw script lines stay under ⋯ Details.

The crew half (the reason surviving the `PUSHOUT` window, and the identity line moving last) is CR-2 in the crew lane. This parser reads the existing "the remote refused the push of <branch> after commit: <reason>; the work is committed on" sentence, so the two halves compose.

Tests: new `tests/gateRow.refusal403.test.tsx` (5 tests: the reader, the routing, the choices, the words, and the rendered row with the diffstat). Also run: `proposalCard`, `questionRow`, `gateRowModel.s15e`, `gateRowModel.followups`, `sessionView.gateRow.s15e`, `sessionView.gateRow.g19` and `deskWords`, all passing. `tsc --noEmit` 0; eslint on the touched files 0. `testid-inventory.json` was regenerated (2 new testids: `session-gate-refusal`, `session-gate-deliver-consent`).

Changelog: A refused hand-over is answerable in the session thread. It leads with the remote's reason and says what Deliver again re-pushes (branch, repository, diffstat).

Refs #403 (the crew half stays open with CR-2).

Reviewed by: self only. codex failed with "workspace is out of credits", and agy was unavailable (the probe timed out).

author: adrianstanca1
body:
## Incident
Production deploy for `1a363d6` failed with `client_loop: send disconnect: Broken pipe` while rebuilding the Next.js Docker image on the VPS. Host rebooted during Next static generation, and previous-boot logs report critical memory pressure. Host Ollama `gemma4:26b` consumes about 20 GiB RAM and much CPU, so rebuilding the app alongside active AI workloads risks production outages. The website remained healthy but its container image was older than the source checkout.

## Fix
- Compile release app (`runtime`) and migration (`tools`) Docker targets **on the GitHub Actions runner** after exact-SHA successful CI verification.
- Compress and transfer audited release images via authenticated SCP with SSH keepalive; verify OCI revision labels before and after starting the app.
- Keep only cached browser-gateway build, data services, Prisma migrations/bootstrap, and health/ingress on VPS. Force app recreation with `--no-build --no-deps`.
- Emit remote heartbeat during long operations and restore prior app image on failed health checks. Preserve tenant databases/uploads/volumes.
- Update production runbook and add contract tests for offloaded builds and rollback.

Validation: `npm test` **871/871 pass**; root TypeScript **pass**; YAML parsed, every shell step `bash -n` clean; `git diff --check` clean. Needs GitHub CI and successful production workflow before claiming server release.

- `CDamager__GetPosition` uses a fixed 30 unit offset above the origin for non-player victims (they have no view offset).

Player behaviour is unchanged.

## Test plan

- [ ] Damage numbers still appear over players
- [ ] A plugin calling `floating_damage_show` on a non-player entity shows an accumulating number over it

body:
Before: `/features/site-links` described the links inside a customer's own site — internal links, orphan pages, free listings, the Search Console report. The owner asked for a links page in the capabilities menu meaning the link network between Go Top customers, so the page was about the wrong feature.

After: the page leads with the network — complementary businesses mentioning each other inside the articles we write for them — and the internal links, orphan pages, free listings and Search Console report follow it, in the same order as the Links tab in the app.

Every claim comes from `lib/link-network` and from clause 15A of the terms, which the page links to: opt-in per project by the owner after accepting the terms on screen; only domains whose control was proven through WordPress or Search Console; at most one link per article, inside a sentence that already exists, on words already in it; visible in the draft and removable before publishing; never a competitor or the same category, never reciprocal, never a short loop, never the same owner, client or server address; new and thin sites excluded; a Shopify store joins separately and its links go only into articles we publish to its blog.

How: the public copy deliberately avoids the vocabulary of link schemes, link building and backlinks, never frames the feature as a way to influence ranking, and does not list the monthly caps like a quota to fill. The Google risk and the link type stay on the opt-in screen and in clause 15A, where the owner accepts them. The page does state that we neither sell nor buy links, that no number of links and no ranking is promised, that participation is optional and off by default and is an extra rather than part of a plan, that the service may be paused or stopped, and that responsibility for search engine compliance stays with the site owner. Guards 4f to 4k in `components/public/__qa__/public-nav-menus.qa.ts` hold all of that in all four languages, each with a mutation control.

Verification: `node scripts/qa/verify.mjs` — tsc 0 errors, ESLint 0 findings on touched lines, no NEW failing suite; the nav suite is 56/0.

author: guangyu-reflexio
body:
## Summary
Local installs now bind the no-auth backend to loopback, keep dashboard styles when the home directory is an ignored Git repository, and preserve runtime configuration during setup and recovery.

Addresses #172, #171, #152, #118, #108, and #105. Existing PRs #123 and #153 overlap portions of the citation and setup reports; this branch also covers remaining OSC8 duplication, direct shell setup help, and EOF handling.

## Changes
- Pass an explicit loopback host to the vendored backend and restart the owned backend on a successful local reinstall. Recover an unhealthy listener from the current install root even when its PID file is missing, preserving process ownership checks.
- Recreate the dashboard-local Tailwind source inclusion rule during prebuild because npm drops `.gitignore` files. Compile real CSS in ignored-home regression fixtures; install locked dashboard test dependencies if absent so CI cannot silently skip these tests.
- Handle setup help before installation, reject unknown flags, and abort on EOF before destructive work.
- Migrate missing legacy runtime settings without changing the legacy file, importing foreign loopback credentials, or overwriting existing runtime values. Preserve encoded Windows paths and the final duplicate value, including readonly flags.
- Remove the repeated all-memory OSC8 citation title list and protect guidance size with a regression test.
- Document local binding, setup recovery, and packaged styling behavior. Mechanical lint/format cleanup of the existing install test file is isolated in the first commit; it accounts for much of the large diff.

## Upstream dependency
Backend-host support is merged in ReflexioAI/reflexio#601 (upstream commit `9a41f577f001456e192444aee18e3ab14faf8da0`). The consumer deliberately retains immutable backport commit `552a220bc99fd75cd0c713c187f876d364cacf22` on its existing runtime baseline, avoiding unrelated upstream changes. The same reviewed host-option patch is present on both baselines, and the backport remains reachable through `team/172-backend-bind-host`. A future runtime upgrade can move the pin to newer upstream main.

## Verification
- Local Codex review of head `db5f9d8f40e64b8dc68b2864764802ad014bb162` against `origin/main`: no actionable findings, including no P0/P1 findings.
- All eight GitHub Actions checks passed on the reviewed head.
- Final full plugin suite: 1,012 passed (two tarfile deprecation warnings).
- Final setup/migration checks: 76 passed. Citation/dashboard checks: 34 passed; dashboard fixture update: 5 passed.
- Upstream service CLI/builder tests: 65 passed. Ruff, formatting, Pyright, Bash and Node syntax checks passed for changed code.
- Dashboard production build passed with limited workers. A real browser verified computed styling and layout against the production server.
- A real Uvicorn process using the vendored builder and a lightweight health app accepted loopback traffic and rejected traffic on the machine's non-loopback interface.

## Remaining investigation
#109 remains open: the Windows publish hang was not reproduced. The pinned runtime already bounds admission and offloads worker processing, but a blocked worker/SQLite lock remains a possible explanation; a healthy `/health` endpoint does not prove the publish path is healthy. Native Windows timing and thread-stack evidence are still needed. This branch does not claim a Windows runtime verification.

#157, #156, and #55 are product/editorial requests or general feedback; no speculative implementations or issue closures are included. No production deployment is included.

author: ypanagidis
body:
Fixes finding **597-2** of the T3 gateway review. Mend's own paste writer (`SessionEngine.storePastedImage` → `writeWorkspaceFiles` → `writeFilesPickupExec`) had three problems:

- it ran as **root** in every executor, including per-person ones (ADR 0016, on by default since #582);
- it **followed a symlinked `paste` directory**, so a link planted in the harness home led the root write outside it;
- it **chmodded the directory it found to 0755**.

The reviewer reproduced it with the real `writeFilesPickupExec`. A `paste` link to a 0700 directory elsewhere exited 0, wrote the file there and widened the directory to 0755.

## Changed

- **Person executor:** the write runs as the **sender** (the route's caller), through the same as-user route as a person's other execs (`startAsPerson` → `processAs`, then `execAsPerson`). A sender who has run nothing in the executor yet is made there first, as their first process would be. The file goes into their own saved directory, `/workspace/harness-home/people/<account id>/paste/`. A new `paste/` is 0770, group `mend` (every person's primary group). The image is 0640, so another person's agent in the workspace can read it. Writing into `/workspace/harness-home/paste` as a person is not possible: the harness home root belongs to root.
- **Shared executor** (`MEND_HARNESS_LAYOUT=shared`, or the automatic shared fallback): same as before, root writing `/workspace/harness-home/paste/<name>`, a new directory 0755 and the file 0644. Only the two rules below are new.
- **Every layout:** a new pickup target `C<dirmode>:<filemode>:<root> <path>` (`containedPut` in `script-transport.ts`):
  - enters `root` at its real path and opens each directory below it with `O_DIRECTORY|O_NOFOLLOW`, each one through the descriptor of the last (`/proc/self/fd/<n>/…`). A link anywhere below the root is refused (`a link: <path>`), and so is a path outside the root or one with `..`;
  - never changes a directory's mode: a new directory gets its mode in the one `mkdir` (the umask cleared around it), so a directory swapped in place of the new one keeps its own (review 615-2). `mkdir` cannot set setgid, so the person `paste/` is 0770, not 2770;
  - stages the file `O_CREAT|O_EXCL|O_NOFOLLOW`, sets its mode with `fchmod` on its own descriptor, and renames it inside the pinned directory (`/proc/self/fd/<n>`). Only afterwards does the writer check that the pinned directory is still at the expected path and that the returned path holds the staged inode (dev/ino). If either fails, it removes its own file from the pinned directory and refuses (review 615-1). The workspace writer refuses when `/proc/self/fd` is missing. A link at the file's own name is replaced, never written through.
- **First paste (review 615-3):** a paste no longer starts the person. The new layout step `homeForWrite` makes only the sender's user, home and Mend token, in one root exec, and only when nothing of theirs was made in the executor. Their own token is the minimum: a person's pickup can only be redeemed with it. It writes none of their logins, delivers nothing (no dotfiles or install.sh, skills, secret files or shell profile), and starts no worktree repair. It revokes that token once the write is over, placed or refused, unless a start of theirs began since or something of theirs runs there. The person is not recorded as made, so their first real process is still a first one.
- **Slack:** Slack images go through `SessionEngine.storePastedImage` as the linked person who asked, no longer through the host helper. Co-located sessions are unchanged. A running captured workspace gets the pickup write, as that person where it runs per person. On the capture store, a mention that *starts* a session attaches no image: the opening turn is written before the workspace exists, and nothing is mounted. The turn and the requester's note now say `not attached · the session has no running workspace to place it in yet`; before, Mend wrote the image on the server, where the workspace never saw it. This is documented in Known issues.
- **Bytes:** they still travel through the pickup ticket. Argv carries only the ticket, the root and the path.
- **Co-located store:** the writer on the server (`storePastedImage` in `pasted-images.ts`, which Slack images also use) follows the same rules. There the harness home is mounted read-write into the workspace, so a link planted in it led the server's own write elsewhere.
- **Docs:** release notes (0.36, per-person section), `operate/per-person-workspaces`, `concepts/context`, ADR 0016 decision 2, and a changeset.

## Added

- `ContainedPlacement` / `PickupTarget.within`, `pastedImagePlacement(name, person)`, `writeContained` (host), `SCRIPT_CONTAINED_PUT_FUNCTION`.

## About "inside the worktree"

Pastes were never in the worktree, and this PR keeps them out: an image there would become part of the change and the checkpoints, and `git clean` could remove it. The containment root is the directory the paste belongs to: the harness home in a shared executor, the sender's saved directory `P` in a person executor. The writer refuses anything that resolves outside that root.

## Tests

The writer tests run the real pickup writer against a local pickup endpoint and a real temp filesystem (`workspace-files.test.ts`):
- a `paste` link to an outside 0700 directory is refused with exit 3. Nothing is written there, its mode stays 0700, and nothing else appears in the root;
- a link deeper down (`people/maria → outside`) is refused, and so are a path outside the root and a `..` path;
- a link at the file's own name is replaced, and its target is untouched;
- an existing 0700 `paste/` stays 0700. Under `umask 077`, a person's new `paste/` comes out 0770 and the image 0640, and `P` stays 0710.

`contained-write.test.ts` races both writers with real renames, mirroring the review's reproduction:
- the directory is moved out right after its path is checked: refused, and nothing is left in the moved directory;
- the directory is moved out right after the rename: refused, and the file is taken back out;
- an existing 0700 directory is swapped in right after `mkdir`: it stays 0700;
- a hard link at the name: its other name is untouched.

Six of these eight fail on the previous commit.

Engine: a first paste writes no login and runs nothing as the person but the write. It makes them once and revokes the token, whether the write was placed or refused; Alice's token, already made, is not revoked. A later join by the same person is made again and gets their first-process deliveries (skills, secret files, shell profile). Slack: images are placed as the requester, and a captured opening mention says the image was not attached.

The host writer has the same symlink and mode tests in `pasted-images.test.ts`.

The engine tests use the person-layout world:
- the owner's paste runs as the owner's Linux user, and a second person's paste runs as that person, made first by root's `mend_person`;
- each lands in that person's own `P/paste/`;
- a shared executor still writes as root into `/workspace/harness-home/paste/`.

Ownership by uid is checked through the user each exec runs as. The tests do not run as root, so they cannot `chown`.

- `pnpm exec turbo typecheck --force`: 27/27
- `pnpm exec turbo lint --force`: clean
- `pnpm format:check`: clean
- `@mend/sessions`: 1287 passed
- `@mend/api-server`: 1541 passed
- `@mend/slack`: 120 passed

I did not launch a real per-person container.

## Exec argv in the pinned Core

At Core 0.39.0-next.707 (`96be22f7`, which includes sealant#329), telemetry withholds exec arguments, and run and session rows keep none. Both run-exec queues delete the job row at pickup. Only the queued job row holds the argv, until a worker takes it. Recorded in PLATFORM-FEEDBACK.md; the comment in `pickup-tickets.ts` is corrected.

## Second review (615-1a/b, 615-r2-1, r2-2, r2-3)

- **Private until placed (615-1a):** the image is staged 0600 with its descriptor kept

author: ryazanovalexander
body:
What changes
Proofreading. The author looked at all 95 reference pictures and the 12 examples of the picture kinds, each drawn by the real card next to its task, answer and solution. Every description stays as written.
Clock. The minute hand is now 56 of the face's units instead of 66, so it stops short of the numbers at every minute. A new test measures the gap at all sixty minutes.
Public texts. README, the terms (en/ru, dated 9 October 2026), the home page, the Service and Research pages, the ChatGPT and Claude directory descriptions, docs/learners.md and the grant pack now say "picture" instead of "text drawing". They promise only what the program checks: the picture follows the format, its labels are the ones the question names, and no answer is written on it. Whether the wording, the picture and the solution agree in meaning is the model's own self-check.
CD. v0.4.5 failed to deploy because Docker Hub refused anonymous pulls (429). The new composite action .github/actions/docker-mirror adds mirror.gcr.io to the runner's Docker settings and keeps the runner's own settings. An image the mirror lacks still comes from Docker Hub. The action runs in every job that pulls Docker Hub images. The steps that capture an image reference now fail when their recipe fails, instead of passing an empty reference on.
Checks
just ci-web, just web-layout (15,180 cards, 0 findings), just ci-lint, just ci-test, just ci-learners and just ci-site all pass.
The new clock test fails at lengths 58 and 66 and when the clock draws no minute hand.
The mirror action was run against a fake daemon in 11 cases, and shellcheck v0.11.0 finds nothing.
